countdown.q: What should you do first this week?
options: Sort licences and buy the scope
countdown.why: Deer tags can take time to get and the rifle must be zeroed before you can hunt deer.

countdown.q: You zeroed with Brand A. The store is out, so you buy Brand B. What now?
options: Check the zero again with Brand B
countdown.why: Different loads hit different spots. Confirm the zero with the exact ammo you will hunt with.

countdown.q: Why pattern the shotgun before duck season?
options: To see where and how tight your shot hits with your load and choke
countdown.why: Patterning shows if the gun shoots where you look and how the shot spreads at real distances.

licences.q: Do you need to carry a hunter number card?
options: No. Carry photo ID and know your FWID number
licences.why: BC replaced the card with the FWID. Carry photo ID and be able to give the number.

licences.q: You hunt deer in 10 days. How do you get the species licence?
options: Order online, it prints at home
licences.why: Species licences cannot be printed at home and online orders are mailed, about 14 days.

licences.q: What do you need to shoot a mallard?
options: BC hunting licence and the federal Migratory Game Bird Hunting Permit
licences.why: Ducks are federal. You need the BC hunting licence plus the federal permit.

licences.q: Can an unlicensed friend carry your rifle on the walk in?
options: No. Having a firearm while out after game can count as hunting
licences.why: Under the Wildlife Act, searching for wildlife while in possession of a firearm is hunting. They would need a licence.

shotgun-guide.q: Which choke is the safe general choice for steel shot over decoys?
shotgun-guide.why: IC is open and steel safe in most guns. Most makers say nothing tighter than Modified with steel.

shotgun-guide.q: How many shells may your shotgun hold for ducks?
shotgun-guide.why: The Migratory Birds Regulations limit the gun to 3 shells, with a one piece plug.

shotgun-guide.q: Why is a gas semi auto a good beginner duck gun?
options: It spreads recoil, so heavy steel loads kick less
shotgun-guide.why: The gas system softens felt recoil. You still must keep it clean.

shotgun-guide.q: Where should you try a shotgun for fit?
options: In a T shirt at the counter
In the jacket you will hunt in
shotgun-guide.why: A thick jacket makes the stock feel longer. Fit it the way you will hunt.

scope-guide.q: Why might your T3x Arctic need high rings?
options: High rings are always more accurate
The scope must clear the tall rear drum sight
scope-guide.why: The rotary drum peep sight sits on the receiver. Owners report high rings are needed to clear it with a 40 to 44 mm scope.

scope-guide.q: Your scope has a 30 mm tube. Which rings fit?
scope-guide.why: Ring size must match the tube diameter.

scope-guide.q: What does second focal plane mean?
options: The crosshair stays the same size when you zoom
scope-guide.why: In SFP the reticle size does not change. Simple for beginners.

scope-guide.q: How tight do ring screws go?
options: To the ring maker's torque number with a torque wrench
scope-guide.why: Each maker lists a torque. Too tight can damage the tube; too loose lets the scope move.

sighting-in.q: Your 3 shot group at 100 m is 6 cm low. Scope is 1/4 MOA per click. About how many clicks UP?
sighting-in.why: One click is about 0.73 cm at 100 m. 6 divided by 0.73 is about 8.

sighting-in.q: Why shoot 3 shot groups before adjusting?
options: One shot can be a flyer. The group centre is the truth
sighting-in.why: You adjust from the centre of the group, not from one shot.

sighting-in.q: At what distance do you pattern a shotgun for the standard percent?
sighting-in.why: The classic test is the percent of pellets inside a 76 cm (30 in) circle at 40 yd.

sighting-in.q: 82 of 138 pellets land in the circle. What does the gun act like?
sighting-in.why: 82 divided by 138 is about 59%, close to the 60% Modified benchmark.

ammo-guide.q: Which shot is legal for ducks?
ammo-guide.why: Ducks, geese, coots and snipe need non toxic shot: steel, bismuth, tungsten or tin.

ammo-guide.q: You change .308 brands the night before the hunt. What now?
options: Re zero with the new load before hunting
ammo-guide.why: Each load hits a different spot. Zero with the load you hunt with.

ammo-guide.q: Can you shoot quail with your .22?
options: No. In BC a .22 is allowed only for grouse, ptarmigan and turkey among game birds
ammo-guide.why: Synopsis page 13, note 2: rimfire is allowed for grouse, ptarmigan or turkey only. Quail are not on the list.

ammo-guide.q: What steel size is the all round duck choice?
ammo-guide.why: Steel #2 or #3 balances pellet count and energy for most ducks.

what-to-wear.q: Which layer do you put on when you stop to sit?
what-to-wear.why: Carry the puffy on the walk in so you do not sweat. Put it on when you stop.

options: It holds water and chills you
what-to-wear.why: Wet cotton loses warmth. Wool and synthetics stay warmer when damp.

what-to-wear.q: What does a wader belt do?
options: Slows water rushing into the waders if you fall
what-to-wear.why: Cinched at the waist, it slows water filling the legs and helps you get out.

what-to-wear.q: Is blaze orange required for deer in BC?
options: No. The Synopsis has no orange rule, but wear it anyway
what-to-wear.why: The 2026 to 2028 BC Synopsis contains no hunter orange requirement. Ontario requires it. Orange is still a strong safety choice.

options: Trip planning, Training, Taking the essentials
pack-kit.why: Plan the trip, know your skills, and carry the 10 essentials.

options: 5 to 8 cm above the wound, not on a joint
pack-kit.why: Above the wound on the limb, tightened until bleeding stops. Note the time.

pack-kit.q: Why keep meat out of cooler meltwater?
options: Wet meat spoils faster and loses quality
pack-kit.why: Keep meat cold and dry: a rack, bagged ice, and the drain open.

pack-kit.q: Your phone has no signal in the hills. What still calls for help?
pack-kit.why: Satellite messengers send SOS and texts with no cell coverage, if the plan is active.

first-duck-hunt.q: When can you take your first shot at ducks?
first-duck-hunt.why: Migratory bird hours are half an hour before sunrise to half an hour after sunset. Deer and quail are 1 hour.

first-duck-hunt.q: A duck drops in deep water and you have no waders, boat or net. What went wrong?
options: You took a shot you could not fetch. The law says you need a way to retrieve birds with you
first-duck-hunt.why: You must have a way to retrieve birds before you hunt, and must retrieve them as soon as you can.

first-duck-hunt.q: Which shot can you carry while duck hunting?
first-duck-hunt.why: Lead shot is banned for most migratory game birds in Canada, even in your pocket.

first-duck-hunt.q: Where should the open landing pocket be in a J hook?
options: In front of you, 20 to 25 m out, where ducks land into the wind
first-duck-hunt.why: Ducks land into the wind and like an open hole. Put it where you want to shoot.

first-duck-hunt.q: A flock comes in while you are in the 10 ft boat with your brother. What do you do?
options: One shooter, seated, motor off and boat stopped
first-duck-hunt.why: Stay seated in small boats. One shooter at a time. Never hunt from a boat moving under power.

first-deer-hunt.q: Your brother's house is on the property. How close to it can you shoot?
options: Anywhere on his land with his OK
No closer than 100 m to an occupied house or farm building
50 m if the shot is away from it
first-deer-hunt.why: BC bans hunting and shooting within 100 m of an occupied dwelling or farm building. His permission does not change that.

first-deer-hunt.q: On the ATV, when may a round be in the magazine attached to the rifle?
options: Always, if the chamber is empty
Never. A loaded magazine attached counts as a loaded firearm
first-deer-hunt.why: Loaded means a round in the chamber or in an attached magazine. No loaded firearm in or on a motor vehicle, ATV included.

first-deer-hunt.q: The deer bounces away on all 4 feet with a thin black tipped tail. Which licence?
first-deer-hunt.why: Stotting and a rope tail with a black tip are mule deer signs. Check the mule deer rules for your MU.

first-deer-hunt.q: It is a cold late afternoon. Which way is air moving on the slope?
first-deer-hunt.why: Cooling air sinks. Evening thermals flow downhill, so deer below you can smell you.

first-deer-hunt.q: You shot a deer 8 km in. What must you bring out?
options: The edible meat: neck, ribs, 4 quarters and loins
first-deer-hunt.why: BC requires the edible portions to be removed. Plan 2 trips or bone it out.

first-quail-trip.q: What do you need to hunt quail as a BC resident?
first-quail-trip.why: Residents need no species licence for quail. The BC hunting licence covers it.

first-quail-trip.q: A quail flushes low between you and your partner. What do you do?
options: Quick shot before it gets away
No shot. Gun up, safety on
Shoot once it passes your partner
first-quail-trip.why: Never swing through your partner, and never shoot low birds. Let it go.

first-quail-trip.q: The orchard is not fenced or posted. Can you hunt it?
options: No. Cultivated land needs the owner's or occupant's permission
first-quail-trip.why: BC requires consent to hunt cultivated land, posted or not.

first-quail-trip.q: Can you hunt quail on your brother's land at Heffley Creek this October?
options: No. Region 3 has no quail season
Yes, private land has no seasons
first-quail-trip.why: The Region 3 table on page 34 has no quail row. No open season means no quail hunting, private land included.

legal-to-shoot.q: Sunrise is in 40 minutes. A buck and a flock of ducks show up. What is legal right now?
options: The buck only. Duck hours start 30 minutes before sunrise, which is 10 minutes away
legal-to-shoot.why: Deer hours start 1 hour before sunrise. Duck hours start 30 minutes before sunrise. At 40 minutes before, only the deer is legal (if its season is open).

legal-to-shoot.q: You think it is a 4 point buck but can only see one side. What now?
legal-to-shoot.why: Step 4: you must be 100% sure of species, sex and antler points before the shot.

legal-to-shoot.q: A deer stands 80 m from your brother's house. He says go ahead. Can you shoot?
options: No. Inside 100 m of an occupied dwelling
Yes if the backstop is safe
legal-to-shoot.why: The 100 m rule protects occupied houses. Owner permission does not lift it.

legal-to-shoot.q: What happens if any one answer is no?
legal-to-shoot.why: Every step must be yes. One no ends it.

after-the-shot.q: The deer is down. What is the first legal step?
options: Notch the species licence before you handle it
after-the-shot.why: The licence must be cancelled immediately after the kill and before handling the animal.

after-the-shot.q: Why not wrap the carcass in a tarp for the drive?
options: It holds heat and the meat can spoil
It hides the evidence of sex
after-the-shot.why: Plastic and tarps trap heat. Meat needs to drop below 4°C fast.

after-the-shot.q: Your friend drives your deer home while you stay at camp. What does he need?
options: A Record of Receipt from you
after-the-shot.why: Anyone carrying wildlife killed by another person needs a Record of Receipt.

after-the-shot.q: Using the gutless method, what must you take out?
options: Neck, ribs, all four quarters and the loins
after-the-shot.why: Those are the legal edible portions of big game. Leaving them is wastage.

know-your-mus.why: An MU number is region, dash, unit. 3-27 is unit 27 in Region 3 Thompson.

know-your-mus.q: Which MU holds Heffley Creek and Sun Peaks?
know-your-mus.why: Both are in MU 3-27. Kamloops is in 3-20, and 3-28 is west across the North Thompson River.
Mission is in MU 2-8. Abbotsford and Chilliwack, south of the Fraser, are in MU 2-4.
Region 8 is Okanagan. Oliver and Osoyoos are in its MU 8-1.

know-your-mus.q: Why does the MU matter before you hunt?
options: Seasons and limits are set by MU
know-your-mus.why: The synopsis season tables list dates and limits by MU. Find your MU, then read that row in the Rule Book.

firearm-safety.q: What does the S in ACTS stand for?
options: See that the firearm is unloaded: PROVE it safe
firearm-safety.why: The Vital Four ACTS end with: See that the firearm is unloaded, PROVE it safe.

firearm-safety.q: Your magazine is in the rifle but the chamber is empty. Is it unloaded for transport?
options: No. A cartridge in an attached or inserted magazine means loaded
Only if the safety is on
firearm-safety.why: The federal definition of unloaded covers the chamber and any magazine attached to or inserted in the firearm.

firearm-safety.q: A deer runs between you and your partner walking side by side. What do you do?
options: Hold fire. It is outside both arcs
firearm-safety.why: The space between two hunters walking abreast is a no shot zone. Never swing past your arc.

firearm-safety.q: Crossing a barbed wire fence alone, what comes first?
options: Hold the rifle high and step over
Unload and PROVE it, then pass it under the fence muzzle away
Put the safety on and climb
firearm-safety.why: Never cross an obstacle with a loaded firearm. Unload, lay it through, cross away from the muzzle.

firearm-safety.q: You and your brother both carry rifles. What do you agree before the walk?
options: Who covers left, who covers right, and a stop signal
firearm-safety.why: Agreed arcs and a stop signal keep each muzzle off the other hunter.

water-safety.q: What does the first 1 in the 1 10 1 principle warn about?
options: About 1 minute of cold shock: control your breathing
water-safety.why: Phase one is cold shock. Gasping and fast breathing last about a minute. Calm your breathing before you act.

water-safety.q: Where should your PFD be while the boat is moving?
options: Under the seat, easy to reach
water-safety.why: In cold water you will not manage to put one on. Only a worn PFD helps.

water-safety.q: Can you carry a loaded shotgun while motoring to the blind?
options: Yes if the safety is on
No. BC bans a loaded firearm in a boat while the motor pushes it, and you may not hunt ducks from a moving motor boat
water-safety.why: BC's Firearm Violence Prevention Act bans a loaded firearm in a boat. The hunting exemption applies only while the motor is not propelling the boat. Federal rules ban hunting migratory birds from a moving boat with a motor.

water-safety.q: You capsize 200 m from shore in October. Best first move after the gasp?
options: Stay with the boat and climb onto the hull
Take off your boots and PFD
water-safety.why: Stay with the boat and get as much of your body out of the water as you can. Swimming in cold water drains you fast.

bush-safety.q: You realize you do not know where the truck is. First step?
bush-safety.why: AdventureSmart teaches STOP. Pushing on is how most people get more lost.

bush-safety.q: Which iPhones can use Emergency SOS via satellite in Canada?
options: iPhone 14 or later, with iOS 16.1 or later
bush-safety.why: Apple lists iPhone 14 or later, all models, with iOS 16.1 or later in Canada.

bush-safety.q: Your brother stops shivering but is confused and stiff. What does that mean?
bush-safety.why: Shivering that stops with confusion and stiffness is a sign of severe hypothermia. Call for help and rewarm gently.

bush-safety.q: A black bear stalks you quietly at dusk and closes in. What do you do?
options: Spray, stand big, fight back if it attacks
bush-safety.why: Parks Canada: a predatory attack means spray and fight back. Playing dead is only for a defensive attack once contact is made.

bush-safety.q: When do you use a tourniquet?
options: Life threatening bleeding from an arm or leg when direct pressure fails
bush-safety.why: Direct pressure first. A tourniquet goes on a limb when bleeding is life threatening and pressure is not working.

atv-rules.q: Rifle in the rack on the quad. Chamber empty, loaded magazine clipped in. Legal in BC?
options: No. A loaded magazine attached to the firearm makes it loaded, and a quad is a conveyance
Yes if the engine is off
atv-rules.why: The synopsis (page 3, 2 October 2026 edition) defines loaded to include a detachable magazine attached to the firearm. Item 28 bans a loaded firearm in or on a motor vehicle or other conveyance.

atv-rules.q: You ride an FSR to the trailhead. What must you have?
options: Registration copy, plate, helmet, driver's licence and $200,000 liability insurance
atv-rules.why: The ORV Act requires registration, plate and helmet on Crown land. On a Forest Service Road the synopsis adds a driver's licence and $200,000 third party liability insurance.

atv-rules.q: Region 3, above 1,700 m, the trail fades into open meadow. What now?
options: Ride across, it is open country
Stop. Above 1,700 m vehicles may only use existing roads and trails
atv-rules.why: Region 3 bans all motor vehicles except snowmobiles above 1,700 m except on existing roads and trails.

atv-rules.q: How often do you pay the ICBC ORV registration fee?
options: Once, $48, as long as you own the quad
Every time you cross a highway
atv-rules.why: ICBC says the combined plate and registration fee is a one time fee of $48, valid as long as the same person owns the vehicle.

atv-rules.q: Can a licensed and insured quad cross Highway 5 at a stop sign without a police permit?
options: No, every road use needs a permit
atv-rules.why: ICBC: a licensed and insured ORV may cross a highway at an intersection controlled by a stop sign or traffic light without an operation permit.

bc-rules.q: Rifle in the truck: chamber empty, full magazine clipped in. Is it loaded in BC?
options: Yes. Live rounds in an attached magazine count as loaded
Only if the safety is off
bc-rules.why: BC defines loaded as live ammunition in the breech or the magazine. An attached clip counts as the magazine.

bc-rules.q: A buck stands 60 m from a farmhouse with people home. Can you shoot?
options: No. Inside 100 m of an occupied dwelling or farm building
bc-rules.why: No hunting or shooting within 100 m of an occupied dwelling, farm or ranch building.

bc-rules.q: Ducks in your brother's boat. When can you shoot?
options: Any time the motor is idling
Only when the boat is beached, anchored or tied off, not moving under motor
bc-rules.why: Federal rules ban hunting migratory birds from a moving boat with a motor or sail.

bc-rules.q: What must stay on a duck until it is preserved at home?
options: One fully feathered wing or the fully feathered head
bc-rules.why: Officers use the wing or head to identify the species and count your bag.

bc-rules.q: Which deer parts must you take out as edible portions?
options: Neck, ribs, all four quarters and the loins
bc-rules.why: The synopsis defines edible portions for big game as neck, ribs, four quarters and loins.

maps-terrain.q: On a 1:50,000 map, 1 cm on paper is how far on the ground?
maps-terrain.why: 1:50,000 means 1 cm equals 50,000 cm, which is 500 m, half a kilometre.

maps-terrain.q: The contour V shapes point uphill toward the peak. What is it?
maps-terrain.why: V shapes pointing uphill mark a draw, a small valley. Ridges point the other way.

maps-terrain.q: Five lines in one centimetre with a 20 m interval. How steep?
maps-terrain.why: Five lines is 100 m of rise over 500 m of ground, which is 20 percent.

maps-terrain.q: Two sets of closed loops with an hourglass of lines between them. What is the hourglass?
maps-terrain.why: A saddle is the low point on a ridge between two highs. Deer cross ridges there.

maps-navigation.q: Declination is 15 degrees east. The map bearing to the saddle is 90. What do you set on the compass?
maps-navigation.why: Declination east, magnetic least: subtract. 90 minus 15 is 75.

maps-navigation.q: What does red in the shed mean?
options: The needle is boxed inside the orienting arrow
maps-navigation.why: The orienting arrow is the shed. When the red needle sits inside it, the bearing at the index line is true for your direction of travel.

maps-navigation.q: Which UTM zone is Heffley Creek in?
maps-navigation.why: Heffley Creek is west of 120 degrees west, so zone 10U. East of that line, around Sun Peaks, it is 11U.

maps-navigation.q: No cell signal on the bench. Does your phone GPS still work?
options: Yes, but only on maps you downloaded first
maps-navigation.why: GPS satellites need no cell network. Map tiles do, so download offline maps at home.

maps-navigation.q: Your bearing out was 40. What is the back bearing?
maps-navigation.why: Add 180 to a bearing under 180. 40 plus 180 is 220.

maps-land-status.q: A great bench sits on a First Nations reserve. What do you need?
options: Permission from the local band office to hunt on or cross it
maps-land-status.why: The synopsis: Indian Reserves are private land. Permission must be obtained from the local Indian business office to hunt on or across these lands.

maps-land-status.q: Crown land, cattle grazing on it, no fence. Can you hunt?
options: Not without the lease holder's consent while livestock are on it
maps-land-status.why: The Wildlife Act bans hunting on Crown land under a grazing lease while livestock occupy it, without the consent of the lessee or occupant.

maps-land-status.q: A river is the MU boundary. Which bank is the line?
options: The right bank as you face downstream
maps-land-status.why: The Management Unit Regulation says a river boundary follows the right hand bank as you face downstream.

maps-land-status.q: Where do you check if an FSR near Kamloops is closed?
options: The resource road safety page for the Thompson Rivers district
maps-land-status.why: FSR closures are posted by Natural Resource District on the resource road safety page. DriveBC covers highways.

maps-land-status.q: You want to drive to a lake at 1,800 m in Region 3. Allowed?
options: Only on an existing road or trail
maps-land-status.why: Region 3 bans motor vehicles above 1,700 m except on existing roads and trails.

map-scouting.q: You found a perfect south facing bench on imagery. What do you check first?
options: Land status: Crown land or not
map-scouting.why: If it is private land, a reserve, a park or a lease with cattle on it, nothing else matters. Land first.

map-scouting.q: Region 3, 15 November. Which mule deer can you take in MU 3-27 under the general season?
map-scouting.why: Page 34: 1 November to 10 December is 4 point bucks only in 3-12 to 3-20, 3-26 to 3-44 and 3-46.

map-scouting.q: Your road climbs to 1,800 m in Region 3. Can you ride the ATV there?
options: Only on an existing road or trail
map-scouting.why: Page 33: motor vehicles, except snowmobiles, are banned above 1,700 m in Region 3 except on existing roads and trails.

map-scouting.q: Early snow fell last night. Where do you start glassing?
map-scouting.why: Snow and cold push mule deer down toward winter range. Drop your search band.

map-scouting.q: Morning hunt. Where should your glassing point be?
options: Directly below the bench, wind at your back
Across or beside the bench, with rising air carrying scent away
Anywhere, scent does not matter at 500 m
map-scouting.why: Morning thermals rise uphill. Glass from across or to the side so your scent goes up and away from the deer.

wind-thermals.q: Which way do thermals usually move on a sunny morning?
wind-thermals.why: The sun warms the slope and the warm air rises uphill.

wind-thermals.q: Evening hunt on a calm day. Where do you set up?
options: Directly downhill in the deer's path, wind at your back
wind-thermals.why: Evening air sinks downhill. Sitting below or to the side means your scent sinks away from the deer.

wind-thermals.q: Your milkweed drifts left, then curls back to you. What is happening?
options: A swirl. Your scent is going everywhere
wind-thermals.why: Curling and doubling back is a swirl. No setup is safe in a swirl.

wind-thermals.q: Wind on hunt day is wrong for your planned spot. Best move?
options: Go to your B spot that fits this wind
wind-thermals.why: Plan an A and B spot for each wind. Forcing a bad wind educates deer.

glassing.q: What should you look for when glassing?
options: A whole deer standing in the open
Parts: a horizontal back, legs, an ear flick, a white rump
glassing.why: Deer are usually partly hidden. Look for pieces and movement that do not belong.

options: Steady glass and less fatigue, so you see small movement
glassing.why: A steady view shows a tail flick or ear twitch you miss with shaky hands.

glassing.q: How do you glass a hillside with the grid method?
options: Slow strips with overlap, corner to corner, then repeat
glassing.why: Slow overlapping strips leave no gaps. Glass it again because deer move and light changes.
Deer are most active around dawn and dusk. Be glassing at first light.

still-hunting.q: What is the difference between still hunting and stalking?
options: Still hunting is slow walking to find a deer. Stalking is closing in on a deer you have seen
Stalking is done from a blind
still-hunting.why: Still hunting searches. Stalking closes the gap on a deer you already spotted.

still-hunting.q: Which sound most likely spooks a deer?
options: A zipper or Velcro rip close by
still-hunting.why: Deer hear high pitch well, better than people. Zippers, Velcro and metal clinks are sharp high sounds.

still-hunting.q: A deer lifts its head and stares your way. What do you do?
still-hunting.why: Deer pick up movement. Freezing gives it nothing to react to.

still-hunting.q: A good still hunting pace looks like?
options: A couple of steps, then a long stop to look
still-hunting.why: Look much more than you walk. Short moves, long looks.

weather-moon.q: What did the Penn State collar study find about deer before winter storms?
options: No real change before the storm. They slowed during it
weather-moon.why: Thirty storms, collared does: no statistical or biological effect before storms. Deer moved less during the storm itself.

weather-moon.q: Which has the strongest evidence for moving Interior mule deer?
weather-moon.why: Snow and cold trigger the move to winter range. Moon evidence is near zero and pressure evidence is mixed.

weather-moon.q: Full moon next weekend. Your brother says skip it. Best answer?
options: Go. Collar studies show the moon effect is near zero
weather-moon.why: The MSU study of 48 bucks found moon effects inside the GPS error. Hunt the days you have.

weather-moon.q: Can you start hunting deer earlier on a bright moon morning?
options: No. Not until 1 hour before sunrise
weather-moon.why: Synopsis page 12: no hunting game, except migratory birds, from 1 hour after sunset to 1 hour before sunrise. The moon does not change it.

field-first-aid.q: Your brother is hit in the thigh and blood is pooling. First move after making the scene safe?
options: Look for the bullet hole on the other side
Firm direct pressure, and call for help
field-first-aid.why: Life threatening bleeding comes first. Press hard right away and get help coming. A tourniquet follows if pressure fails on a limb.

options: Above the wound on the heart side, not on a joint
field-first-aid.why: Between the wound and the heart, off joints. Sources differ on the distance: 5 to 8 cm or 5 to 10 cm. Ask your instructor.

field-first-aid.q: The tourniquet is on, the bleeding has stopped. Now what?
options: Lock the rod, write the time, leave it for the medics
Take it off once he feels better
field-first-aid.why: Current Red Cross and Stop the Bleed guidance: do not loosen or remove it yourself. Write the time for the medical team.

field-first-aid.q: A deep cut in the armpit will not stop with pressure. What do you do?
options: Pack the wound with gauze until full, then press on top for at least 3 minutes
field-first-aid.why: A tourniquet cannot go on the armpit. Packing fills the wound so pressure reaches the bleeding vessel.

field-first-aid.q: How much water should flush a dirty knife cut?
options: At least 1 litre of drinkable water, under pressure
field-first-aid.why: The Wilderness Medical Society recommends at least 1 litre, with drinkable water as the preferred fluid.

cold-injuries.q: Which is the best sign that hypothermia has become serious?
options: Shivering slows or stops and the person gets drowsy
cold-injuries.why: Strong shivering is mild hypothermia. Shivering that slows or stops with drowsiness is moderate or worse: an emergency.

cold-injuries.q: Your brother is alert, shivering hard and fumbling. What do you do?
options: Shelter, pad under, dry layers, heat packs on the trunk, warm sweet food, rest 30 minutes
Rub his arms and legs hard
cold-injuries.why: That is mild hypothermia. Insulate, warm the trunk, give food since he is alert, and rest at least 30 minutes.

cold-injuries.q: Why warm the trunk first and handle a cold person gently?
options: To avoid afterdrop: cold limb blood rushing to the core
cold-injuries.why: Warming or moving limbs can return cold blood to the core and upset the heart rhythm.

cold-injuries.q: Frostbitten toes, and a 3 hour walk out in the snow. Thaw them now?
options: No, keep them frozen if they could refreeze on the way
cold-injuries.why: Thawing then refreezing does the most damage. Rewarm only when refreezing can be prevented.

options: As hot as you can stand
cold-injuries.why: Wilderness Medical Society: 37 to 39 °C, about 30 minutes, until the skin is soft and red or purple.

lost-survival-kit.q: You realize the ridge does not look right and the sun is setting. First move?
lost-survival-kit.why: STOP first. Pushing on is how most people get more lost.

lost-survival-kit.q: Why does staying put help searchers?
options: It keeps the search area small near your trip plan
lost-survival-kit.why: Staying put reduces time and search area. Double the distance you wander and the area is 4 times bigger.

lost-survival-kit.q: No bars from your own carrier. Is 911 worth trying?
options: Yes, a phone can reach 911 through any carrier tower in range
lost-survival-kit.why: BC Search and Rescue Association: 911 can connect through any tower in range.

options: A V or SOS at least 3 m long, high contrast
lost-survival-kit.why: BC Search and Rescue Association: a V or SOS at least 3 metres, big and high contrast.

lost-survival-kit.q: Where should the whistle and lighter live?
options: In your pockets, so they go where you go
At the bottom of the pack
lost-survival-kit.why: Hunters drop packs to stalk. Pocket kit is with you when the night surprises you.

fire-wet-weather.q: What is the size limit of a Category 1 campfire?
fire-wet-weather.why: BC Wildfire Service: one pile no larger than 0.5 metres high and 0.5 metres wide.

fire-wet-weather.q: What must be on hand while your campfire burns?
options: At least 8 litres of water or a hand tool
fire-wet-weather.why: The brochure says at least 8 litres of water or a hand tool at all times while it is lit.

fire-wet-weather.q: It is raining. Where do you find dry fuel?
options: Wood lying in the wet grass
Standing dead wood, dead twigs under big spruce, the split core of a log
fire-wet-weather.why: Dead, off the ground, and split. Green wood bends and will not burn well.

fire-wet-weather.q: Your tinder flared and died. Most likely reason?
options: Not enough small kindling ready, so the tinder burned out before the wood caught
fire-wet-weather.why: Have 2 big handfuls of every size before lighting. The ladder has to be ready.

options: When the ashes are cool to the touch after drowning and stirring
fire-wet-weather.why: Drown, stir, feel, repeat. Hot coals under ash can reignite.

shelter-night-out.q: Clear dry night, little time. What do you build first?
options: A thick bed off the ground
shelter-night-out.why: The ground pulls heat by conduction all night. Insulate under you first.

shelter-night-out.q: Best place to spend the night?
options: The valley bottom by the creek
A sheltered bench part way up, near trees and fuel, not under dead trees
shelter-night-out.why: Cold air pools in valley bottoms at night and ridge tops are windy.

shelter-night-out.q: Which way does the low edge of the tarp face?
options: Into the wind, pinned to the ground
shelter-night-out.why: The windward edge goes down and gets pinned. The open side faces away from the wind.

shelter-night-out.q: What is a foil blanket weak at?
options: Stopping heat loss into the ground
shelter-night-out.why: The thin film does little against conduction. You still need a bed or pad.

shelter-night-out.q: Your shelter is deep in thick timber. Searchers may miss you. Fix?
options: Put blaze orange and bright gear out in the nearest opening
shelter-night-out.why: Shelter keeps you warm; visibility gets you found. Do both.

water-safe-drinking.q: How long should you boil creek water at 1,200 m?
options: At least 1 minute at a rolling boil
water-safe-drinking.why: HealthLink BC: at least 1 minute. Above 2,000 m, at least 2 minutes.

options: A certified filter with pores of 1 micron or smaller
water-safe-drinking.why: HealthLink BC: NSF certified, 1 micron or less. Jug filters do not remove Giardia.

water-safe-drinking.q: Cold, cloudy creek water and bleach. What do you do?
options: Strain and settle, then 4 drops a litre and wait 1 to 2 hours
water-safe-drinking.why: Cloudy or below 10 °C: clarify, double the bleach, wait 1 to 2 hours. And chlorine is weak on Giardia, so boiling or filtering is better.

water-safe-drinking.q: You drank untreated water on the hunt. When might beaver fever show up?
water-safe-drinking.why: HealthLink BC: symptoms usually appear 1 to 3 weeks after infection.

water-safe-drinking.q: A pond has green scum. Will boiling make it safe?
options: No, boiling does not remove toxins or chemicals
water-safe-drinking.why: The CDC says boiling and disinfecting cannot make water with toxins or chemicals safe. Find other water.

bear-cougar-encounters.q: A black bear 40 m away has not noticed you. What do you do?
options: Leave quietly the way you came, watching it, spray ready
bear-cougar-encounters.why: WildSafeBC: an unaware bear, leave quietly the way you came and keep it in sight.

bear-cougar-encounters.q: A bear woofs, pops its jaw and bluff charges, stopping short. Best move?
options: Speak calmly, back away slowly, spray ready
bear-cougar-encounters.why: These are signs of a stressed, defensive bear. Give it room. Most bluff charges stop short.

bear-cougar-encounters.q: A bear quietly follows you and keeps coming closer at dusk. What kind of attack is this?
bear-cougar-encounters.why: A bear that stalks and keeps coming may be predatory. Spray and fight back with everything.

bear-cougar-encounters.q: How far from the gut pile should you move the meat, per Alberta's guidance?
bear-cougar-encounters.why: Bears often go to the gut pile first. Separate the meat by at least 200 m and hang it 3.5 m up.

bear-cougar-encounters.q: A cougar attacks. What do you do?
options: Fight back, aiming at the face and eyes
bear-cougar-encounters.why: WildSafeBC: always fight back against a cougar. Never run, never play dead.

wildfire-smoke-heat.q: The evacuation order for a burned area was lifted, but an area restriction order remains. Can you hunt there?
options: No, you may not enter without written authorization
wildfire-smoke-heat.why: Area restriction orders under section 11 of the Wildfire Act cover all purposes, including hunting, and can outlast evacuation orders.

wildfire-smoke-heat.q: A fire is below you on the slope. Which way do you go?
options: Down and across the slope, toward burned ground, rock, water or a road
wildfire-smoke-heat.why: Fire races uphill. Escape down and sideways, out of its path.

wildfire-smoke-heat.q: The AQHI is 10+. You planned a hard climb. What do you do?
options: Avoid or reschedule the strenuous effort
Wear a cotton mask and climb
wildfire-smoke-heat.why: At 10+ the air is extremely poor. The BC Centre for Disease Control says reduce or reschedule strenuous outdoor activity, and higher risk people should avoid it.

wildfire-smoke-heat.q: Your partner is hot, red and confused after a September climb. First move?
options: Call 911, shade, soak with cold water and fan
wildfire-smoke-heat.why: Those are heat stroke signs. HealthLink BC: call 911, move to shade, cool the whole body with water and fanning.

wildfire-smoke-heat.q: How do you report a wildfire from a cell phone?
wildfire-smoke-heat.why: The BC Wildfire Service line is 1 800 663 5555 toll free, or *5555 on a cell.

avalanche-hunters.q: Which slope angles produce most avalanches?
avalanche-hunters.why: Avalanche Canada: the vast majority start on slopes between 30 and 45 degrees.

avalanche-hunters.q: You hear a loud whumpf as the snow drops under you. What does it mean?
options: A buried weak layer collapsed: a sign of instability. Leave avalanche terrain
avalanche-hunters.why: Whumpfs are a classic sign of instability. Stay off and out from under steep slopes.

avalanche-hunters.q: Why is a gully a terrain trap?
options: Snow from a slide piles up much deeper there
avalanche-hunters.why: Steep sided gullies and creek beds trap moving snow so even a small slide buries you deep.

avalanche-hunters.q: What rescue gear does each person need?
avalanche-hunters.why: Avalanche Canada: all three, everyone, and training to use them.

avalanche-hunters.q: Your partner is fully buried. Why not run for help first?
options: Survival drops sharply after about 15 to 20 minutes, so companion rescue is the best chance
avalanche-hunters.why: Over 90 percent survive the first 15 to 20 minutes, then survival falls fast. You are the rescue.

ice-cold-water.q: How thick should clear blue ice be for one person to walk on, per the Canadian Red Cross?
ice-cold-water.why: Red Cross: 15 cm to walk alone, 20 cm for a group, 25 cm for a snowmobile, on clear blue ice. Floating ice is never 100 percent safe.

ice-cold-water.q: White, opaque ice compared with clear blue ice?
ice-cold-water.why: Lifesaving Society: white snow ice is about half as strong. Double the thickness.

ice-cold-water.q: You go through the ice. Which way do you turn?
ice-cold-water.why: The ice you just walked on held you. It is probably the strongest.

ice-cold-water.q: You are out of the hole. Now what?
options: Stay flat and roll away from the hole
ice-cold-water.why: Lying flat spreads your weight. Roll several body lengths before standing.

ice-cold-water.q: Your brother falls through 20 m out. First moves?
options: Call 911, shout encouragement, reach or throw from shore
Wait for him to get out
ice-cold-water.why: Call 911, then preach, reach, throw, row. Going out yourself is the last resort.

rifle-mechanics.q: What does lifting the Tikka bolt handle do?
options: Unlocks the lugs and cocks the firing pin
rifle-mechanics.why: Lifting turns the locking lugs out of the receiver and moves the cocking piece back, which cocks the firing pin (Tikka manual).

rifle-mechanics.q: On your Tikka, the red dot is showing. What does it mean?
rifle-mechanics.why: Tikka manual: red dot visible means the safety is disengaged and the rifle is ready to fire.
The second number is the inches of barrel for one full turn. Lower number, faster spin.

rifle-mechanics.q: You press the trigger: click, no bang. First?
options: Keep it pointed safe and wait at least one minute
rifle-mechanics.why: Tikka's manual says wait at least one minute, then unload with extreme care. A slow ignition can still fire.

rifle-mechanics.q: Which rifle lets you open the bolt with the safety ON?
rifle-mechanics.why: CZ's manual lists pulling the bolt with the safety engaged as a feature. The Tikka two position safety locks the bolt closed.

cartridge-anatomy.q: What are the four parts of a cartridge?
cartridge-anatomy.why: Hunter education: the case holds everything, the primer ignites the powder, the powder becomes gas, the bullet flies. CPPB.

cartridge-anatomy.q: Before loading, what three stamps should match?
cartridge-anatomy.why: Hunter education says compare the barrel stamp, the box and the stamp on each cartridge.

cartridge-anatomy.q: Can you hunt deer in BC with full metal jacket ammunition?
options: No. Full metal jacketed non expanding bullets are unlawful for hunting with a rifle
cartridge-anatomy.why: The Rule Book bans full metal jacketed non expanding, tracer, incendiary and explosive bullets for hunting.

cartridge-anatomy.q: Which bullet design keeps the core glued to the jacket?
cartridge-anatomy.why: Bonded bullets fuse the core to the jacket so they hold together through bone.

cartridge-anatomy.q: A box of .308 is 12 years old. Tikka says:
options: Do not fire ammunition over 10 years old
Fire it at the range only
cartridge-anatomy.why: The Tikka manual says do not fire old ammunition, over 10 years, because primers, powder, cases and bullets can deteriorate.

ballistics-deep.q: Why does the bullet cross the line of sight twice?
options: The bore points slightly up because the scope sits above it
ballistics-deep.why: The scope is about 3.8 cm above the bore, so the bore tilts up to meet the aim point at the zero. The bullet climbs through the line, then falls back through it.

ballistics-deep.q: Deer at 250 m slope distance, 30 degrees uphill. Hold for about:
ballistics-deep.why: Flat distance = 250 × cos 30 = 217 m. Gravity works over the flat distance. Holding for 250 m hits about 10 cm high.

ballistics-deep.q: Wind blowing from 1 o'clock (target at 12) counts as about:
ballistics-deep.why: Wind 30 degrees off the line of fire gives about half of the full crosswind drift. 3 and 9 are full value.

ballistics-deep.q: How much does a 20 km/h full crosswind push a 150 gr .308 at 250 m?
ballistics-deep.why: About 27 cm, more than a deer's vital zone. Close the distance or pass.
A milliradian is one thousandth of the distance: 10 cm at 100 m. One MOA is 2.9 cm at 100 m.

judging-distance.q: Your rangefinder reads 64 m on a deer you think is 200 m away. Most likely?
options: The beam hit brush in front
judging-distance.why: A reading much shorter than expected usually means a branch or grass in the beam. Find a gap and range three times.

judging-distance.q: A 0.46 m deer chest covers 2 mils. Range?
judging-distance.why: 0.46 × 1,000 ÷ 2 = 230 m. Remember the deer size is lore, so use it as a check.

judging-distance.q: Looking across a bright, snowy cutblock, the deer will look:
judging-distance.why: Canadian Army fieldcraft: bright light and looking over snow or a uniform surface make objects seem nearer.

judging-distance.q: Past what distance does the unit of measure method stop being accurate?
judging-distance.why: The fieldcraft manual says it is not accurate beyond 400 m.

judging-distance.q: A rangefinder box says 1,800. On deer expect about:
judging-distance.why: The big number is reflective range. One maker lists 900 yd on deer for its 1800 model.

field-positions.q: Your crosshair keeps drifting right of the deer when you relax. Fix?
options: Move your body around a pivot until it settles on target
field-positions.why: That drift is your natural point of aim. Move the body, not the rifle, so the relaxed position points at the target.

field-positions.q: You rest the barrel directly on a rock. The shot will tend to go:
field-positions.why: Hunter education: a barrel on a hard surface fires higher than normal. Pad under the forend.
Sitting is steadier than kneeling, and sticks add support. Offhand is the least steady.

field-positions.q: Shooting down a steep slope, a good choice is:
options: Sitting facing downhill, heels dug in
field-positions.why: Facing downhill, the slope puts your knees at bench height. Prone pointing steeply down is awkward.

field-positions.q: When does the safety come off?
options: When the crosshair is settled and you are ready to shoot
field-positions.why: Safety stays on until you are ready to fire. Finger to the trigger last.

season-practice.q: What is the first shot of every range day for?
options: A cold shot that tells you what a deer would get
season-practice.why: A deer gives you one cold shot. Logging the first shot each day tells you your true field accuracy.

season-practice.q: Dry fire set up, step one:
options: All ammunition out of the room
season-practice.why: Dry fire is only safe with zero ammunition in the room. Then prove the rifle and chamber a snap cap.

season-practice.q: A week before the hunt you find a cheaper .308 load. Best move?
options: Keep your zeroed load. Try the new one after the season
season-practice.why: Every load hits differently and needs a new zero. Freeze your setup before the season.

options: Cheap rounds for positions and trigger work
season-practice.why: About 15 to 17 cents a round versus over $2 for .308. Positions and trigger habits carry over. It is not legal for deer.

season-practice.q: Where can you shoot a field course?
options: A range or land where shooting is lawful and safe
season-practice.why: Discharge rules, No Shooting Areas and safe backstops apply. A club range is the simple answer.

shotgun-mastery.q: About what share of pellets does a modified choke put in a 76 cm circle at 40 yd, lead shot?
shotgun-mastery.why: The common chart: cylinder 40, IC 50, modified 60, full 70 percent. A starting point only.

shotgun-mastery.q: Why not shoot big steel through a tight, non rated choke?
options: Choke creep: hard steel can deform the choke and lock it in
shotgun-mastery.why: Steel does not squeeze like lead. Use chokes your maker rates for steel.

shotgun-mastery.q: A duck crosses at 30 m. You miss. Most likely you were:
shotgun-mastery.why: Most misses are behind. The shot takes about 0.1 second and the bird keeps going. More lead, keep the gun moving.

shotgun-mastery.q: How many steel #2 pellets in 1 1/8 oz?
How do you find your dominant eye?
options: Hand triangle at arm's length, pull back to the face
shotgun-mastery.why: Hunter education: the triangle ends at your dominant eye. Aim with that eye.

rimfire-22.q: Which bird can you legally hunt with the CZ 457 .22?
rimfire-22.why: Rule Book note 2: rimfire is allowed for grouse, ptarmigan or turkey only among game birds. Ducks need a shotgun; quail are not on the rimfire list.

rimfire-22.q: With a 50 m zero, where does the bullet hit at 100 m?
rimfire-22.why: The model shows about 19 cm low at 100 m. Inside 55 m it stays within about 1.5 cm.

rimfire-22.q: A grouse sits on a high branch with sky behind it. Rifle shot?
options: Yes, it is a small bullet
No. No backstop: a .22 can carry well over a kilometre
rimfire-22.why: Every rifle shot needs earth behind it. A .22 bullet carries far.

rimfire-22.q: How do you clean the CZ 457 bore?
options: From the chamber end, brush all the way through before reversing
rimfire-22.why: CZ's manual: rod and brush from the chamber to protect the muzzle, and do not reverse the brush inside the bore.

rimfire-22.q: Can you open the CZ 457 bolt with the safety on?
rimfire-22.why: The CZ manual lists pulling the bolt out with the safety engaged as a safe handling feature. The Tikka two position safety locks the bolt.

firearm-care.q: Tikka says corrosion can begin how soon after use if not cleaned?
firearm-care.why: The manual says corrosion can begin within 24 hours, even on all weather and stainless models.

firearm-care.q: Which way does the cleaning rod go?
options: Breech to muzzle, in the bullet direction, with a guide
firearm-care.why: Tikka and CZ both say from the chamber end. It protects the crown.

firearm-care.q: Your rifle got soaked. Tonight you:
options: Leave it in the soft case
Take it out of the case, dry it warm, then clean and oil
firearm-care.why: Tikka: dry it in a warm, dry place without a protective cover. Fabric and leather cases hold moisture.

firearm-care.q: Hunting at minus 25 C, the CZ manual says:
options: Remove oil from accessible parts or use a cold rated lubricant
firearm-care.why: Thick oil can slow parts in deep cold. CZ says remove it or use a lube made for those conditions.

firearm-care.q: You slip and the muzzle goes into snow. Before the next shot:
options: Unload, bolt out, look through the bore
firearm-care.why: Firing with an obstruction can cause serious injury. Check the bore; an obstruction is a gunsmith job.

optics-mastery.q: What is the exit pupil of a 10x42 binocular?
optics-mastery.why: Objective ÷ power: 42 ÷ 10 = 4.2 mm. An 8x42 gives 5.25 mm.

optics-mastery.q: Which is better in thick timber?
optics-mastery.why: Lower power gives a wider, steadier, brighter view. Vortex calls 7x or 8x adequate for woodland.

optics-mastery.q: You set the binocular diopter. After that you focus with:
optics-mastery.why: The diopter balances your two eyes once. Note the number and use only the centre focus wheel.

optics-mastery.q: Can you carry a thermal monocular on a BC hunt if you do not use it?
options: No. Infrared optics are banned on the trip, even in the pack
optics-mastery.why: The Rule Book bans thermal scopes and monoculars, even unused.

optics-mastery.q: Why not glass a hillside with your rifle scope?
options: Your muzzle points wherever you look
optics-mastery.why: Never point a firearm at anything you do not intend to shoot. Binoculars look; the rifle aims.

topo-deep-dive.q: Contour lines bend into a sharp V where a creek crosses them. Which way does the V point?
topo-deep-dive.why: The V points upstream into the hill. Water flows out through the open end of the V.

topo-deep-dive.q: A closed ring has small ticks on its inside edge. What is it?
topo-deep-dive.why: Ticks point down into the low spot. A plain ring with no ticks is a top.

topo-deep-dive.q: From the top of a slope the lines are wide apart near you and tight further down. Can you see the bottom?
options: No. It is convex and rolls away, leaving dead ground
topo-deep-dive.why: Wide to tight is convex. The roll hides the bottom. Great for stalking, bad for glassing from the top.

topo-deep-dive.q: The map uses 20 m contours. Could a 15 m cliff go missing?
options: Yes. It can fit between two lines
topo-deep-dive.why: Anything smaller than the interval can hide between lines. Check satellite view and your eyes.

topo-deep-dive.q: 20 m contour lines sit 50 m apart on the ground. About how steep is it?
topo-deep-dive.why: 20 m rise over 50 m run is 40 percent, about 22 degrees. Hard going with a pack.

compass-mastery.q: You take a bearing off the map. What do you do with the needle?
options: Box it in the shed first
Ignore it while on the map
compass-mastery.why: On the map only the ring's north lines and the map's north lines matter. The needle comes in when you lift the compass to walk.

compass-mastery.q: The truck is on a long east to west road to the north of you. Best plan?
options: Aim off to one side, hit the road, turn toward the truck
compass-mastery.why: Aim off on purpose so you know which way to turn when you hit the road.

compass-mastery.q: Your compass has no declination set. The map bearing is 70. What do you walk near Heffley Creek?
compass-mastery.why: Declination east, magnetic least: subtract about 15. 70 minus 15 is 55.

compass-mastery.q: For a good triangulation, the two landmarks should be...
options: Close together in the same direction
compass-mastery.why: Lines that cross near a right angle give a sharp fix. Nearly parallel lines give a long smear.

compass-mastery.q: You walked 1 km with a 5 degree error. About how far off are you?
compass-mastery.why: Each degree is about 17 m per km, so 5 degrees is about 87 m.

gps-phone-battery.q: No cell signal at the bench. Will the phone still show your dot on the map?
options: Yes, if the map area was saved offline first
gps-phone-battery.why: GPS satellites need no cell network. The map tiles do, so save the area in Offline Maps at home.

gps-phone-battery.q: It is minus 6°C. Where should the phone ride?
gps-phone-battery.why: Apple designs iPhones for 0 to 35°C. Body heat keeps it in range so it does not shut off early.

gps-phone-battery.q: Your phone and power bank are both frozen. Best move?
options: Warm both inside your jacket first, then charge
gps-phone-battery.why: Lithium ion should not be charged below freezing. Warm first.

gps-phone-battery.q: What keeps the screen awake all day in the Hunt Map?
options: Recording a track with Go & Track
gps-phone-battery.why: iPhone web apps cannot record with the screen off, so Go & Track keeps it awake. Waypoints cost almost nothing.

gps-phone-battery.q: What does iPhone satellite SOS need?
options: iPhone 14 or later and a clear view of the sky
gps-phone-battery.why: It works only outside cell and wifi coverage, with a clear view of the sky and horizon, on iPhone 14 or later.

hunt-map-pro.q: Where do you turn on the private land and MU layers?
hunt-map-pro.why: Hunt Map Layers holds Land status, Hunting, Habitat and migration, Access and Spots.

hunt-map-pro.q: A slope shows red in Slope steepness. What angle is it?
hunt-map-pro.why: Red is 30 to 45 degrees: very steep, and avalanche terrain in snow.

hunt-map-pro.q: What does What can I see from here leave out?
hunt-map-pro.why: It works from bare ground height only. In timber you will see less than the pink shows.

hunt-map-pro.q: Fastest way to drop a waypoint right where you look on the map?
options: Press and hold the map, Drop waypoint
hunt-map-pro.why: Press and hold opens This spot with Drop waypoint, Range rings, Measure from here, Scent cone and Insights.

hunt-map-pro.q: Which Offline Maps detail saves every trail and contour?
hunt-map-pro.why: Most saves zoom 14, every trail and contour. Less is about a third of the size.

route-planning.q: 3 km off trail and 400 m of climb. About how long by Naismith with Aitken's off trail speed?
route-planning.why: 3 km at 4 km an hour is 45 minutes; 400 m at 600 m an hour is 40 minutes. Total about 85 minutes, a minimum.

route-planning.q: On 15 October 2026 near Heffley Creek, when does legal light end for deer?
route-planning.why: Big game legal hours end 1 hour after sunset. Sunset is about 18:08, so about 19:08.

options: A clock time set at home, worked back from dark with a buffer
route-planning.why: Work back from when you want to be at the truck, minus the walk, minus a buffer, and keep it.

route-planning.q: Going over a 300 m hill or around it on one contour. What does Naismith say the climb costs?
options: About 30 minutes for the climb alone
route-planning.why: 600 m of climb is an hour, so 300 m is about 30 minutes, plus a slow descent. Around can win.

route-planning.q: Which is the fastest slope to walk on by Tobler's curve?
options: A gentle downhill of about 5 percent
route-planning.why: Tobler's speed peaks at about 6 km an hour on a 5 percent downhill. Steep is slow both ways.

night-navigation.q: Legal light ends and you are 2 km from the truck. First thing?
options: Unload, then walk out on your planned route
night-navigation.why: Hunting ends 1 hour after sunset and hunting with a light is unlawful. Unload and walk out.

night-navigation.q: How long do your eyes need to adapt to the dark?
night-navigation.why: Rhodopsin builds over 20 to 40 minutes, and a few seconds of bright light breaks it down.

night-navigation.q: Best night route back to a truck on a road?
options: Walk to a creek handrail, follow it to the road, aim off
night-navigation.why: Handrails and a catching feature are hard to get wrong in the dark. Aim off so you know which way to turn.

options: Line from Merak through Dubhe, about 5 times the gap
night-navigation.why: The Big Dipper's pointer stars lead to Polaris. It marks north and sits at about your latitude in height.

night-navigation.q: Phone dead, unsure where you are, 19:30. Best move?
options: STOP, try the compass to a handrail, and if still lost stay put and call
night-navigation.why: Stop and think first. A known handrail may save you. If not, stay put; your trip plan brings help.

field-weather.q: At evening glassing you see a ring around the sun and the sky turning milky. What is likely?
options: A warm front: rain or snow within about a day
field-weather.why: A halo comes from thin cirrostratus, often ahead of a warm front. Plan for wet weather.

field-weather.q: A puffy cumulus keeps growing taller through the afternoon and spreads a flat top. What is it?
field-weather.why: The anvil top marks cumulonimbus, the thunderstorm cloud. Get off ridges.

field-weather.q: Stand with your back to the wind. Where is the low pressure?
field-weather.why: Buys Ballot's law, northern hemisphere: back to the wind, low on the left.

field-weather.q: 8°C at the truck at 400 m. About how warm on a 1,400 m ridge?
field-weather.why: Standard air cools about 6.5°C per 1,000 m. Dress for the top.

field-weather.q: You hear thunder while glassing. What do you do?
options: Keep glassing under a lone tree
Get to the truck and wait 30 minutes after the last thunder
field-weather.why: When thunder roars, go indoors. A hard topped vehicle counts. Wait 30 minutes after the last thunder.

wind-mastery.q: Clear October morning. Which slope switches to upslope wind first?
options: East face, when the sun hits it
wind-mastery.why: Upslope begins soon after the sun strikes a slope, so east faces start first.

wind-mastery.q: It is 10 am in thick shady timber. Which way can your scent creep along the ground?
options: Downhill, in a thin cool layer under the canopy
wind-mastery.why: Upslope flow can rise above the treetops while a shallow downslope flow persists under the canopy shade.

wind-mastery.q: The forecast says 20 km/h. About what do you feel at head height in the open?
wind-mastery.why: Forecast and Beaufort speeds are at 10 m. At 2 m the wind may be only 50 to 70 percent.

wind-mastery.q: Wind blows over a ridge from the west. Where is a bad place to sit?
options: Just over the crest on the east side
In the open on the windward side
wind-mastery.why: The lee side just over the crest can tumble and even blow back uphill. Scent goes everywhere.

wind-mastery.q: When is swirl most likely on a calm day?
options: At the switch times, around sun arrival and shade arrival
wind-mastery.why: Between upslope and downslope there is a brief calm. Weak, changing air means scent pools and swirls.

stay-unseen.q: Which colour is the worst choice for hunting clothes, from a deer's point of view?
stay-unseen.why: Deer likely see blue well. Orange, red and green look like dull browns and greys to them.

stay-unseen.q: A deer lifts its head and stares your way. What do you do?
options: Freeze until it drops its head
stay-unseen.why: Movement is what deer catch best. Freeze. Move when the head is down or behind cover.

stay-unseen.q: Where should you sit to glass a basin?
options: Below the crest with hillside behind you, in shade if you can
In the open in full sun
stay-unseen.why: Below the crest kills your silhouette, and shade kills shine and your shadow.

stay-unseen.q: What matters more than camo colour, according to the deer vision research summary?
stay-unseen.why: The NDA summary says scent and movement matter far more than clothing colour or UV brighteners.

stay-unseen.q: You and your brother are stalking. Best way to move?
options: One moves while the other watches, then swap
stay-unseen.why: Two moving shapes are twice as easy to see. One watches the animal and signals.

stalking-footwork.q: In the fox walk, which part of the foot touches first?
options: The outside edge of the ball
stalking-footwork.why: Set the outside of the ball of the foot down lightly, roll in, then lower the heel, then shift weight.

stalking-footwork.q: When do you put your full weight on the front foot?
options: Only after it is set and quiet
stalking-footwork.why: Weight back until the foot has found any sticks. The crack comes from weight.

stalking-footwork.q: Why avoid a steady step, step, step rhythm?
options: It sounds like a person; deer move in uneven bursts
stalking-footwork.why: Animals walk in irregular bursts. A steady beat is a human signature.

stalking-footwork.q: Wind is gusting through the timber. Best time to move?
stalking-footwork.why: Wind noise covers footsteps. In calm air, slow right down.

stalking-footwork.q: A log lies across your path. What do you do?
options: Step on it, it is solid
stalking-footwork.why: Dry bark cracks under weight. Step over, never on.

hunt-fitness.q: Your first hunt is in 10 days. Best fitness move?
options: Cram hard: big pack hikes every day
Walk most days with hills, boots on, light pack, sleep well
hunt-fitness.why: You cannot build 12 weeks of fitness in 10 days. Steady walking, broken in boots and sleep help now without injury. Start the full plan and it pays off for the late season and next year.

hunt-fitness.q: On a training hike you can talk but not sing. What intensity is that?
hunt-fitness.why: The talk test: moderate means you can talk but not sing. Vigorous means only a few words before you need a breath.

hunt-fitness.q: When does the heavy pack come into the plan?
options: Week 1, so you get used to it
After the base is built, from week 5, in small steps
hunt-fitness.why: Coaches build the aerobic base first, then add load. Small steps and easy weeks lower injury risk.

hunt-fitness.q: How many strength sessions a week do the Canadian guidelines suggest?
hunt-fitness.why: Muscle strengthening using major muscle groups at least twice a week (CSEP).

hunt-fitness.q: You are out of breath at the top of a climb and a buck stands up. What now?
options: Breathe, settle, and only shoot if you are steady with a clear vital shot
hunt-fitness.why: The synopsis ethics code says do not shoot unless you have a clear shot of a vital part. Fitness buys you a steady hold; patience does the rest.

packs-carrying.q: Where should the middle of the hip belt sit?
options: On top of your hip bones
packs-carrying.why: The hip bones (iliac crest) are the shelf that carries most of the weight. Too low and the shoulders take it all.

packs-carrying.q: Where do the heaviest items go?
options: In the middle, close to your spine
packs-carrying.why: Heavy and close to your back keeps the load from pulling you backward. Light and bulky goes at the bottom, quick items on top.

packs-carrying.q: What order do you tighten the straps?
packs-carrying.why: Hips first so the hip belt takes the weight, then shoulders, then load lifters, then the sternum strap. Hungry Sheep Like Salt.

packs-carrying.q: You must lift a 30 kg meat pack from the ground. Best way?
options: Bend at the waist and swing it onto one shoulder
Sit into the straps, buckle the hip belt, roll to a knee and push up
Twist and heave it up fast
packs-carrying.why: Swinging and twisting loads the back. Sitting in and standing with your legs follows the safe lifting rules: load close, legs lift, no twist.

packs-carrying.q: You weigh 80 kg. About how heavy should an overnight pack be?
packs-carrying.why: About 20% of body weight is a common guideline for a loaded backpacking pack (REI). 20% of 80 kg is 16 kg.

fsr-vehicles-radio.q: You drive past kilometre sign 6, then 8. What direction do you call?
fsr-vehicles-radio.why: Kilometre numbers rising means you call up. Falling numbers means down.

fsr-vehicles-radio.q: Where do you get the radio channel for a resource road?
options: The sign at the road entry
fsr-vehicles-radio.why: The BC government says the radio channel signage in the field governs over maps at all times.

fsr-vehicles-radio.q: You have no road radio and the road is an active haul road. Best move?
options: Wait at the start and follow a vehicle with a radio
Use your FRS handheld to call the trucks
fsr-vehicles-radio.why: The BC Forest Safety Council guide says wait and follow a radio equipped vehicle, pulling over when it does. FRS radios do not reach the trucks.

fsr-vehicles-radio.q: Your rifle's magazine is full but the chamber is empty. Can it ride in the truck like that?
options: No. A live round in an attached magazine counts
fsr-vehicles-radio.why: Synopsis item 28: live ammunition in the breech or in an attached magazine, in or on a motor vehicle, is unlawful.

fsr-vehicles-radio.q: You want to stop and glass a slope. Where do you park?
options: On the curve with the best view
In a pullout on a straight with clear sight both ways
In the middle of the road with flashers on
fsr-vehicles-radio.why: Stop in a pullout or a straight, visible section wide enough for others to pass. Never on a curve or hill crest.

hunting-camp.q: Where do your granola bars and toothpaste spend the night?
options: In the tent, in a zipped pocket
Locked in the truck or hung with the food
hunting-camp.why: WildSafeBC: never take food into your tent, not even a snack. Toothpaste and soap are attractants too. Lock them in the vehicle or hang them.

hunting-camp.q: The night wind usually flows down the valley. Where goes the tent?
options: Upwind of the kitchen and food
hunting-camp.why: Smell drifts downwind and a bear follows it. With the tent upwind, the smell trail leads to the food and kitchen, not to you.

hunting-camp.q: What does a Category 1 campfire need?
options: 8 L of water or a hand tool, a fuel break, someone watching, max 0.5 m by 0.5 m
hunting-camp.why: BC Wildfire Service: no larger than 0.5 m high by 0.5 m wide, a fuel break, at least one person watching with a hand tool or 8 L of water, and fully out before you leave.

hunting-camp.q: It is minus 8 °C. Can you run the propane heater in the tent if you open the flap?
options: Yes, the flap lets the fumes out
No. Opening the flap is not enough to stop carbon monoxide
hunting-camp.why: Camping heaters and stoves are not made for indoor use, and opening flaps does not prevent dangerous carbon monoxide build up.

hunting-camp.q: Which sleeping bag number should you shop by?
options: Limit for warm sleepers, Comfort for most
Whatever is lowest on the tag
hunting-camp.why: Extreme is survival only. Comfort is relaxed sleep. Limit is curled up for 8 hours. Most people should buy for Comfort, with a buffer for real conditions.

hunt-food-water.q: Which gives the most energy per gram to carry?
hunt-food-water.why: Fat has about 9 kcal per gram; carbohydrate and protein about 4 (FAO factors).

hunt-food-water.q: You fill a bottle from a creek in cattle country. Bleach method?
options: 2 drops per litre, wait 30 minutes; double if cold or cloudy
No need, it is running water
hunt-food-water.why: HealthLink BC: 2 drops of household bleach per litre, cover, wait 30 minutes. Cloudy or colder than 10 °C: double it and wait 1 to 2 hours. Boiling is the most effective.

hunt-food-water.q: After a 3 hour training hike you weigh 1 kg less and you drank 1 L. About how much did you sweat?
hunt-food-water.why: 1 kg lost is about 1 L not replaced, plus the 1 L you drank: about 2 L in 3 hours.

hunt-food-water.q: When should you eat on a long hunt day?
options: A little every 2 to 3 hours, before big climbs
hunt-food-water.why: By the time you feel hungry you are behind. Small and often keeps energy and warmth steady.

hunt-food-water.q: Leftover chili sat in the warm truck all afternoon, about 5 hours. Eat it?
options: No. Over 2 hours in the 4 to 60 °C danger zone
hunt-food-water.why: HealthLink BC: do not leave cooked leftovers out more than 2 hours. Germs grow fast between 4 and 60 °C, and smell is not a safety test.

hunting-partner.q: You and your brother walk side by side. A deer runs between you. What do you do?
options: Hold fire. The middle is a no shot zone
hunting-partner.why: Each hunter shoots only in their own zone, about 45 degrees straight ahead. The gap between you and behind you are no shot zones.

hunting-partner.q: What does three whistle blasts mean?
hunting-partner.why: Signals in threes are the distress signal (BC Search and Rescue Association). Keep your own codes to one or two blasts.

hunting-partner.q: You shoot a buck but your deer licence is in the truck. Can your brother cancel his licence for it?
options: Yes, it is the same family
No. The person who kills it must cancel their own licence, and licences cannot be used by others
hunting-partner.why: Synopsis item 1: the person who kills big game cancels their own species licence immediately. Item 2: using another person's licence is unlawful. Carry your licences.

options: Big fir on the saved pin at 12:00, wait 30 minutes, then the truck
hunting-partner.why: A landmark both know, a clock time, a wait window and a plan B make it work.

hunting-partner.q: On a push, where can the stander shoot?
options: Only in a zone that never points toward the cover the pusher walks
hunting-partner.why: The pusher is in that cover. Agree a zone that points away from the pusher's line before you start.

ethics-fair-chase.q: What does the BC synopsis say about shots?
options: Any shot in range is fine
Do not shoot unless you have a clear shot of a vital part
Shoot running animals to stop them
ethics-fair-chase.why: Synopsis page 77: do not shoot unless you have a clear shot of a vital part of the animal. You can't pull the bullet back.

ethics-fair-chase.q: You hit a buck and lose the trail. What does the law require?
options: All reasonable effort to locate, dispatch, retrieve and include it in your bag limit
ethics-fair-chase.why: Synopsis page 12, Retrieval: all reasonable effort to locate, dispatch, retrieve and include it in your bag limit.

ethics-fair-chase.q: You realise the buck you shot has too few points for the season. What do you do?
options: Stop, do not hide it, and report it promptly to an officer
Tag it with your brother's licence
ethics-fair-chase.why: Honesty is the path: report promptly (item 18 covers accidental kills; my reading is the wrong animal is handled the same way, VERIFY with the officer). Using another person's licence is unlawful.

ethics-fair-chase.q: Can you scout with a drone the morning of your hunt?
options: Yes, if you land it first
No. Drone information from less than 6 hours before or during a hunt is banned
ethics-fair-chase.why: Synopsis item 36: no drone on a hunting expedition, and no use of drone information obtained during or less than 6 hours before it.

options: Lawful and sporting, and the animal has a reasonable chance to escape
ethics-fair-chase.why: Boone and Crockett: ethical, sportsmanlike and lawful pursuit without an improper or unfair advantage; unfair means the game has no reasonable chance of escape.

season-planning.q: When do BC hunting licences expire?
season-planning.why: The licence year runs 1 April to 31 March. Everything expires 31 March.

season-planning.q: Can you use a wireless trail camera for hunting deer on 15 August in Region 3?
options: No. Not from 1 August to 10 December, except Region 1
season-planning.why: Synopsis item 30: no wireless camera for hunting from 1 August to 10 December, except in Region 1.

season-planning.q: What does the app's Plan a hunt give you?
options: Legal and open check, odds, a day by day plan and a checklist
season-planning.why: Pick animal, place and dates; the plan has four parts: legal and open, odds for big game, day by day, checklist. Always read your MU row too.

season-planning.q: It is 2 November. Which Region 3 mule deer buck season applies?
season-planning.why: Any buck runs 1 to 31 October; then 4 point bucks from 1 November to 10 December in Region 3 (check your MU row).

season-planning.q: Best time to buy and test new boots?
options: Spring, then break them in all summer
season-planning.why: Nothing new on the hunt. Buy early and test on training hikes.

daylight-weather-bc.q: 15 November near Heffley Creek, sunrise about 8:15. When can you start hunting deer?
daylight-weather-bc.why: Big game: from 1 hour before sunrise. 8:15 minus 1 hour is 7:15. BC stayed on UTC minus 7, so the sunrise is near 8:15 on the clock.

daylight-weather-bc.q: Do BC clocks fall back on 1 November 2026?
options: No. BC stays on UTC minus 7 all year
daylight-weather-bc.why: The BC government release says the March 2026 spring forward was the last change; clocks that would usually turn back on 1 November stay the same.

daylight-weather-bc.q: Duck hunting in Mission on 31 October, sunset 17:52. Last legal shooting time?
daylight-weather-bc.why: Migratory game birds: until half an hour after sunset. 17:52 plus 30 minutes is 18:22.

daylight-weather-bc.q: Average November low at Kamloops A?
daylight-weather-bc.why: 1991 to 2020 normals: average daily minimum minus 1.1 °C, with about 16 nights at or below 0 °C. Records go much colder, so pack for it.

daylight-weather-bc.q: Which place is by far the wettest in October and November?
daylight-weather-bc.why: Abbotsford averages 144 mm in October and 233 mm in November, about 6 to 9 times Kamloops or Osoyoos.

tracks.q: A track has 4 toes, no claw marks, and a big heel pad with 3 lobes on the back edge. What made it?
tracks.why: Cats keep their claws in and have a big 3 lobed heel pad. Wolves show claws and have a small triangular pad. Bears have 5 toes.

tracks.q: Groups of 4 prints close together, with 3 m gaps between groups. What happened?
tracks.why: Stotting leaves tight groups of 4 with gaps of about 2.4 to 4.6 m. That deer was alarmed, probably by you.

tracks.q: Which way did the deer go?
options: Toward the round end of the heart
You cannot tell from a hoof print
tracks.why: The pointed tips of the two toes lead. The round heels trail.

tracks.q: Frost crystals have grown inside a deer print. When was it made?
options: Before the frost formed, last night or earlier
tracks.why: Frost grows after the print was made. A print made this morning would cut through the frost crust instead.

tracks.q: Bear track: toes in a nearly straight row, claw marks far ahead of the toes. Which bear?
options: You cannot tell from a track
tracks.why: Long claws and toes above the toe line say grizzly. Black bears have short claws and the outer toe drops below the line.

sign.q: You find a deer carcass covered with leaves and sticks in thick cover. What do you do?
options: Uncover it to see what killed it
Back out, talk loudly, and leave the area
Sit nearby and wait for deer to come and feed
sign.why: A covered carcass is a cougar or bear cache. The owner is close and will come back. Leave.

sign.q: A twig is cut clean at 45 degrees. Who ate it?
sign.why: Hares have sharp upper teeth and cut clean. Deer have no upper front teeth and tear twigs, leaving a ragged end.

sign.q: A pawed bare oval of dirt under a branch about 1.3 m up. What is it and who likely made it?
options: A scrape, a white tailed buck
sign.why: Bare pawed dirt under a chewed licking branch is a scrape. White tails scrape; mule deer rarely do. Most scraping is mid October to mid November.

sign.q: Every twig on a shrub is eaten up to about 1.2 m. Above that it is untouched. What made the line?
sign.why: Deer reach to about 1.2 m. Elk lines run 1.5 to 1.8 m and moose up to 2.4 m. Cattle graze grass and do not make a neat shrub line.

sign.q: A tube of scat full of deer hair and bone chips, about 3 cm across and tapered at one end. Most likely?
sign.why: Over 2.5 cm across with deer sized hair and bone says wolf. Coyote scat is thinner and holds mouse and hare hair.

funnels.q: Where do deer most often cross a ridge?
options: At the highest point, for the view
At a saddle, the low dip between high points
funnels.why: A saddle is the easiest and most hidden crossing. Bucks cruise saddles between doe groups in November.

funnels.q: Morning sit on a hillside trail. Where do you set up?
options: Above or beside the trail, so rising air carries your scent away
funnels.why: Morning thermals rise. Sit above or to the side so your scent climbs away from deer moving up to bed.

funnels.q: Which of these is a pinch point?
options: A creek crossing with low banks where several trails meet
funnels.why: A pinch point is the narrowest spot deer must pass. Crossings, gaps, gates and field corners are classics.

funnels.q: Your planned stand faces the wrong wind today. Best move?
options: Sit anyway, deer are not that smart
Use your B spot for this wind
Walk through the feed to a new spot
funnels.why: Plan an A and a B spot for each wind. Forcing a bad wind educates deer and ruins the spot.

funnels.q: A wireless trail camera on a funnel in October in Region 3?
options: Illegal for hunting from 1 August to 10 December, and all year in Region 1
funnels.why: The synopsis bans wireless cameras for hunting from 1 August to 10 December in every region except Region 1, where wireless cameras for hunting are banned all year (page 20). Use a memory card camera.

food-water-cover.q: What takes over a mule deer's diet near Kamloops in December and January?
food-water-cover.why: The Kamloops stomach study found grass under 10% until spring. Douglas fir peaks in December and January, with shrubs.

food-water-cover.q: A cold snap with 60 cm of snow up high. Where are the deer?
options: South and west facing Douglas fir slopes down low
food-water-cover.why: Deer avoid snow over about 50 cm. Snow and cold push them to warm aspect winter range with old Douglas fir.

food-water-cover.q: Dry October, the feed is brown. Which spot becomes worth an evening sit?
food-water-cover.why: When green feed dries, deer need surface water and visit it at dawn and dusk.

food-water-cover.q: A field of alfalfa regrowth next to cottonwood brush. Which deer?
food-water-cover.why: White tails live on farm edges and bottoms. Mule deer use fields less, mostly in hard weather and the rut.

food-water-cover.q: Can you hunt a farmer's hayfield without asking?
options: Yes if there is no sign
No, cultivated land needs the owner's consent
food-water-cover.why: The synopsis says you may not hunt cultivated land without the consent of the owner, lessee or occupant.

the-rut.q: When does the mule deer rut peak in BC?
the-rut.why: Mule deer rut from mid November to mid December with the peak in mid November. Elk and moose are earlier.

the-rut.q: Bottled deer urine from an American farm, poured on a scrape in Region 3. Legal?
options: No, it is a cervid derivative from outside BC
Yes, if it is under 100 ml
the-rut.why: Synopsis item 51 bans using any part or derivative of deer, elk, moose or caribou from outside BC for hunting. It is a CWD safeguard.

the-rut.q: Can you use an electronic deer call?
options: No, electronic calls are only allowed for listed predators and Schedule C birds
the-rut.why: Item 41 bans recorded or electronic calls except for wolf, coyote, cougar, lynx, bobcat and Schedule C birds.

the-rut.q: Which rut comes first in the fall?
the-rut.why: Elk rut in September, moose late September into October, deer in November.

the-rut.q: Peak rut. You found a group of does at dawn. What next?
options: Stay and watch; the bucks will come to the does
Walk into the timber to find the buck
the-rut.why: In the rut, bucks follow does. Sit on the does with the wind right and be patient.

snow-tracking.q: Loose snow crumbs around a print still fall apart when you poke them. What does that tell you?
snow-tracking.why: Disturbed snow bonds into a crust within hours. Loose crumbs mean the track is recent.

snow-tracking.q: You shot a deer through the lungs and it ran into timber. How long do you wait?
snow-tracking.why: A heart or lung hit deer dies fast. Give it about 30 minutes so you do not push it. Gut hits need hours.

snow-tracking.q: The buck track turns downwind toward thick timber. What do you do?
options: Loop around so you approach the likely bed from downwind
snow-tracking.why: Walking the track downwind sends your scent to the bed first. Loop and come in with the wind in your face.

snow-tracking.q: Legal light ends and you are on a fresh track of an unwounded buck. Next?
options: Mark it, go home, come back at first light
snow-tracking.why: Hunting after one hour past sunset is unlawful and so is hunting with a light. Mark the track and return.
