snow-tracking.q: Backtracking a deer trail teaches you
options: Where the deer is right now
Where it fed, crossed and bedded
snow-tracking.why: Backtracking shows the deer's routine. Following is how you try to catch up with it.

sign-drill.q: Best time of day for the sign walk?
options: Mid morning, when deer are bedded and you are not hunting
sign-drill.why: Mid morning you can read sign without bumping deer off their feed or spooking them at the edge.

sign-drill.q: You find a big bed in timber at 11 am. What is the right move?
options: Sit in it to see the view
Measure, photograph from the edge, and leave quietly
Walk deeper to find more beds
sign-drill.why: Bedding areas are sacred. Record from the edge and leave before you evict the deer.

sign-drill.q: A photo of a track with nothing for scale is worth
sign-drill.why: Without a ruler or a known object you cannot measure it later, and size is half of track identification.

sign-drill.q: Lac du Bois grassland inside Kamloops city limits:
options: Good for a sign walk, no firearm discharge
sign-drill.why: The Region 3 synopsis bans discharge of firearms and bows on that part of Lac du Bois and Crown land inside the city boundary. Walking and scouting are fine.

sign-drill.q: You carry the rifle on the drill. What must be true?
options: Nothing, it is just a walk
Licences on you, season open in that MU, legal hours, firearm unloaded in the truck
sign-drill.why: With a firearm in the field you are hunting under the Wildlife Act. All the hunting rules apply.

habitat-deer.q: Where do Kamloops mule deer usually bed on a warm fall day?
options: In the middle of the open grass
In the timber beside the grass edge
habitat-deer.why: Deer feed on the grass at dusk and dawn and bed in the shade of the Douglas fir beside it.

habitat-deer.q: A twig ends in a ragged, torn tip. Who ate it?
habitat-deer.why: Deer have no top front teeth, so they tear twigs. Hares and beavers cut them clean.

habitat-deer.q: Which shrub has tiny wedge shaped leaves with 3 teeth and grows on dry slopes?
habitat-deer.why: Bitterbrush is the grey green dry slope shrub, a key mule deer browse.

habitat-deer.q: Deer pellets are shiny, dark and soft. How old are they?
habitat-deer.why: Fresh pellets are moist and shiny. They dull and harden over days.

habitat-deer.q: Which plant tells you that you are in coast black tailed deer country around Mission?
habitat-deer.why: Salal covers the wet coast forest floor and is a main fall and winter food for black tailed deer.

habitat-ducks.q: On a windy morning, where on the pond will the ducks most likely sit?
options: The middle of the open water
habitat-ducks.why: Ducks get out of the wind in the lee of a point or a reed bed.

habitat-ducks.q: How do mallards and pintails feed?
options: They dive to the bottom of deep lakes
They tip up in shallow water and feed in fields
habitat-ducks.why: They are dabbling ducks: shallow water and wet fields.

habitat-ducks.q: Which plant has a brown sausage shaped head and marks a marsh?
habitat-ducks.why: Cattail heads stand above the marsh and are easy to see from far away.

habitat-ducks.q: You see a pile of corn put out near a slough. When can you hunt waterfowl within 400 m of it?
options: Only after it has been bait free for at least 7 days
habitat-ducks.why: The synopsis bans hunting migratory birds within 400 m of bait unless the place has been bait free for at least 7 days.

habitat-upland.q: How far from thick cover do California quail usually go?
habitat-upland.why: Quail rarely leave the safety of brush, so you hunt the brushy edges.

habitat-upland.q: What do ruffed grouse eat in winter?
habitat-upland.why: Aspen buds are a main winter food, so aspen stands hold grouse.

habitat-upland.q: You find a hole in the snow with wing marks beside it. What happened?
options: A grouse roosted under the snow and flew out
habitat-upland.why: Ruffed grouse roost under soft snow and burst out, leaving wing prints.

habitat-upland.q: Where would you look for spruce grouse?
options: Spruce and pine forest, often high up
habitat-upland.why: Spruce grouse are conifer specialists that eat pine and spruce needles.

habitat-big-game.q: Which plants are top winter food for moose?
habitat-big-game.why: Moose winter on willow, red osier dogwood, aspen, birch and cottonwood browse.

habitat-big-game.q: You find a track about 14 cm long by a beaver pond. Most likely?
habitat-big-game.why: Moose tracks are about 13 to 15 cm, more than twice a deer track.

habitat-big-game.q: A muddy pit in a wet meadow, smelling strong, in September. What is it?
habitat-big-game.why: Bull elk dig and roll in wallows in the rut, mid September.

habitat-big-game.q: What does berry filled bear scat on a trail tell you?
options: A berry patch nearby is in use
habitat-big-game.why: Bears fatten on berries in late summer and fall, so a patch nearby is being fed in.

habitat-big-game.q: Where do moose gather in winter on the plateaus?
options: River valleys, burns, logged areas and wetlands
habitat-big-game.why: The BC moose account names river valleys, burns, logged areas and wetland complexes.

migration.q: Early November: 40 cm of new snow up high near Heffley Creek. Where do you look for mule deer?
options: Subalpine basins where you saw them in August
Lower slopes and south and west facing winter range
migration.why: Snow and cold push migrants down. Deer struggle above about 30 cm and leave a slope by about 50 cm. October to December is the move.

migration.q: Which bird moves UP the mountain for winter?
migration.why: Dusky grouse leave open breeding ground in fall and winter in dense conifers, usually uphill, eating needles. Quail and ruffed grouse are residents.

migration.q: In which month do snow geese leave the Fraser delta for Wrangel Island?
migration.why: They return to the Fraser estuary mid March to mid April and leave in April. They arrive back in early October.

migration.q: Where is a California quail covey in January?
options: On the same small brushy range near farms and orchards, below about 750 m
migration.why: Quail do not migrate. A covey holds a range of roughly 7 to 18 hectares all winter and stays within 15 to 30 m of cover.

migration.q: About how long do interior black bears stay in the den?
migration.why: The BC account says 5 to 7 months in the interior and 3 to 5 on the south coast. A study just south of BC had dens entered mid October to mid November.

landforms-101.q: Contour Vs point uphill and a blue line runs down the middle. What is it?
landforms-101.why: In a draw the contour Vs point uphill toward its head, and water runs down the middle. Ridges and spurs point the other way.

landforms-101.q: Two sets of closed rings with an hourglass of lines between them. Why might deer use it?
options: It is the lowest crossing of the ridge
landforms-101.why: The hourglass is a saddle, the low point between two tops. Animals cross ridges there to save climbing and stay off the skyline (hunter observation).

landforms-101.q: Tight lines, then a wide gap, then tight lines again on a slope. What is the gap?
landforms-101.why: A wide gap between tight lines is a flat step on the slope: a bench. Deer often bed and travel on benches.

landforms-101.q: Why might a 15 m rock band not show on the Hunt Map contours?
landforms-101.why: In metres the Hunt Map draws a line every 20 m. A 15 m band can fit between two lines. Check 3D, satellite and your eyes.

landforms-101.q: On the Hunt Map Slope steepness tool, how does a bench on a steep face look?
options: An uncoloured strip between coloured slopes
landforms-101.why: Slopes under 15 degrees get no colour, so a flat bench shows as a gap between yellow, orange or red slopes.

slope-aspect.q: A slope is 30 degrees. What is that in percent?
slope-aspect.why: Percent is tan of the angle times 100. tan 30 degrees is about 0.58, so 58 percent. 45 degrees is 100 percent.

slope-aspect.q: Mid October noon near Kamloops. Which slope gets the strongest sun?
slope-aspect.why: The sun is about 30 degrees up from the south. A south face tilted toward it meets it nearly head on; a 30 degree north face gets almost none.

slope-aspect.q: On the Hunt Map, 3 contour lines cross 100 m of ground. About how steep?
slope-aspect.why: Each line is 20 m of height. 3 lines is about 60 m up in 100 m along: about 60 percent, roughly 31 degrees.

slope-aspect.q: A cold, clear October morning. Where do you glass first?
options: The valley floor in the cold air
slope-aspect.why: On cold mornings deer often bed or feed where the first sun hits (Tip). Warm aspects also hold mule deer later in the fall.

slope-aspect.q: Which slope angles start most avalanches?
slope-aspect.why: Avalanche Canada: the vast majority start on 30 to 45 degree slopes. The Hunt Map colours that band red.

elevation-snowline.q: The valley is 5°C. About how warm is a ridge 1,000 m higher on an average day?
elevation-snowline.why: Air cools about 6.5°C per 1,000 m on an average day: 5 minus 6.5 is about minus 1.5°C. Clear calm nights can flip this.

elevation-snowline.q: A big storm left 60 cm of fresh snow up high. Where do mule deer go?
options: Down to shallower snow on warm aspects
Into the deepest north timber at the top
elevation-snowline.why: Mule deer generally avoid snow over 50 cm and move to lower, warmer faces where the snowpack is lower.

elevation-snowline.q: Where does the snowline sit lowest on one mountain?
elevation-snowline.why: Shady north faces hold snow lower and longer. Sunny south faces melt first.

elevation-snowline.q: Clear, calm night. Where is it coldest at dawn?
elevation-snowline.why: Cold air drains down at night and pools low: an inversion. The valley floor gets frost and fog.

elevation-snowline.q: Region 3, 1,800 m, no road. Can you drive the ATV across the meadow?
options: No, above 1,700 m stay on existing roads and trails
elevation-snowline.why: Region 3 bans operating motor vehicles other than snowmobiles above 1,700 m except on existing roads and trails. Study aid only: the official regulations are the law.

water-on-land.q: A dry October. A lone clump of aspen sits on an open grass slope. What might it mean?
water-on-land.why: Aspen, willow and dogwood need wet roots. A lone green clump in dry grass often marks a seep.

water-on-land.q: On the Hunt Map Topo, a creek is drawn as a dashed blue line. What does that tell you?
options: It may be dry part of the year
water-on-land.why: The Hunt Map dashes intermittent waterways: they may hold only pools or nothing in a dry fall.

water-on-land.q: Where do trails gather along a creek with steep cut banks?
options: At a low bank with a firm bottom
water-on-land.why: Animals cross where it is easy and safe. One good crossing can collect trails from a whole slope.

water-on-land.q: It just rained hard for two days. Your water stand?
options: Less useful: water is everywhere now
water-on-land.why: After a big rain, every puddle holds water, so a single source loses its pull. Hunt food and cover.

water-on-land.q: A ranch dugout full of ducks. What comes first?
water-on-land.why: Most dugouts are on private land or leases. You need permission, and no hunting or shooting within 100 m of an occupied dwelling or farm building. Study aid only: the official regulations are the law.

options: Where two or more cover types meet
edges.why: Edge is the juncture of two or more different cover types, like timber and grass.

edges.q: Which spot on a timber edge usually holds the most travel?
options: The middle of a long straight edge
An inside corner or a point of timber
edges.why: Corners and points bunch animals as they step out or cut across. Hunter observation (Tip).

edges.q: BC mule deer ratings want security cover within about how far of feed in spring?
edges.why: The BC habitat account lists security and thermal cover near forage habitat, within 200 m.

edges.q: A soft edge, or ecotone, is:
options: A sharp line of tall timber
A blended band of shrubs and young trees between two types
edges.why: An ecotone is a transitional edge where forest and open blend through shrubs and small trees.

edges.q: You plan an evening sit on a timber edge. Where should the wind go?
edges.why: Animals step out of the cover. The wind must carry from them to you, not your scent to them.

bedding-cover.q: Mule deer security cover, by the BC rating, hides how much of a deer at what distance?
bedding-cover.why: The BC habitat account: the most effective security cover hides 90% of the animal at 60 m or less, in patches 180 m or more across.

bedding-cover.q: Which stand catches the most snow before it reaches the ground?
options: Tall closed conifers, over 10 m with over 60% crown cover
bedding-cover.why: Canopy closure in stands over 10 m tall with over 60% crown completeness has the most effect on snow interception.

bedding-cover.q: A cold, clear morning. Where would you glass first for bedded deer?
options: Sunny faces, below rock, out of the wind
bedding-cover.why: On cold days deer pick sun exposed, sheltered spots; rock gathers heat by day. Hot days push them to shade.

bedding-cover.q: Why do deer often bed just below a crest rather than on top?
options: View below, wind and thermals from below, no skyline
bedding-cover.why: Below the crest they see down, smell what comes up on the morning thermal, and stay off the skyline (hunter observation).

bedding-cover.q: Does thermal cover always make elk fatter or healthier?
options: Not proven: one study found no benefit
bedding-cover.why: Cook and others 1998 found thermal cover did not improve elk condition in the Blue Mountains. Elk may use those stands for food or safety.

escape-terrain.q: A coyote comes. Which deer usually heads up slope into rough ground?
escape-terrain.why: Lingle 2002: mule deer moved to and up slopes; white tails moved down and away.

escape-terrain.q: Mountain goats usually stay within about how far of escape terrain?
escape-terrain.why: BC Mountain Goat Management Plan: usually reluctant to go more than 400 to 500 m from escape terrain, often less in winter.

escape-terrain.q: A bighorn ram feeds on grass above a 50 m cliff. Shoot now?
options: No: wait until it moves to safe ground
escape-terrain.why: An animal shot above a cliff can fall: lost meat and a dangerous retrieval. Wait for safer ground (Tip).

escape-terrain.q: Why does steep ground far from roads often hold more game in season?
escape-terrain.why: Hunter density drops with distance from roads and with slope, so pressured animals end up there.

escape-terrain.q: Quail flush wild. Where do they go?
escape-terrain.why: California quail seldom go more than 15 to 30 m from cover and run or fly to thorny brush.

options: The narrowest spot in a funnel
pinch-points.why: A funnel narrows the routes; the pinch point is the narrowest spot in it, where most travel passes.

pinch-points.q: A steep draw cuts across a slope. Where do trails usually cross it?
options: Around the head of the draw
pinch-points.why: Animals avoid dropping into and climbing out of steep draws; they go round the top (hunter observation).

options: A wide flat with one trail
A saddle, a timber strip and a creek crossing in one line
pinch-points.why: Stacked funnels concentrate travel most. Two or three features in a line beat one.

pinch-points.q: Where should you sit relative to a pinch?
options: 100 to 150 m off it, downwind, with a clear lane
pinch-points.why: Off the trail and downwind keeps you out of the animal's path and nose, with a lane to shoot.

pinch-points.q: A fence gap on a farm looks perfect. First step?
options: Get permission and check the 100 m rule
pinch-points.why: Most farm fences are on private land: permission first, and no hunting or shooting within 100 m of a dwelling or occupied farm building. Study aid only: the official regulations are the law.

habitat-islands.q: In the Pennsylvania study, how far from a road did hunters get on average, at their farthest?
habitat-islands.why: GPS units showed an average maximum distance of 0.84 km from a road open to vehicles, much less than hunters reported.

habitat-islands.q: On a 2 lane public road, how wide is the road allowance for shooting?
options: 15 m each side of the middle of the road
habitat-islands.why: Rule Book: for roads with less than three lanes it extends 15 m on either side of the middle, or to private or cultivated land. Study aid only: the official regulations are the law.

habitat-islands.q: A thicket 80 m from an occupied farmhouse holds a deer. Can you shoot it there?
options: No: within 100 m of an occupied dwelling
habitat-islands.why: No hunting or shooting within 100 m of a dwelling or occupied farm building. Permission does not change that.

habitat-islands.q: Why do small patches near roads sometimes hold animals in season?
options: Hunters skip them for bigger, farther spots
habitat-islands.why: Hunters tend to skip spots that look too small, too close or too awkward (Tip), and pressured animals use any cover that is left alone.

habitat-islands.q: Can you glass for deer from your parked truck with your rifle inside?
options: No: searching for wildlife with a firearm is hunting, and hunting from a motor vehicle is unlawful
habitat-islands.why: Hunting includes searching for wildlife while in possession of a firearm, and item 22 bans hunting from a motor vehicle. Glass from away from the truck, or without a firearm (my reading of the Rule Book).

read-land-truck-map.q: What comes first in the 10 minute map read?
read-land-truck-map.why: Law first: if the ground is closed, private or out of season, nothing else matters. Wind is checked last for the seat and approach.

read-land-truck-map.q: Fresh tracks cross a dirt road in three places after rain. What do you do?
options: Waypoint each with its direction; look for the trail and a pinch nearby
read-land-truck-map.why: Fresh crossings mark live trails. Two or three close together often point to a pinch nearby.

read-land-truck-map.q: You see a deer from the truck. Your rifle is cased in the back seat. What does the law allow?
options: Get out, walk away from the truck and out of the road allowance before loading, if all else is legal
Load in the cab, then get out
read-land-truck-map.why: No hunting from a motor vehicle, no loaded firearm in it, and no shooting within the road allowance. Study aid only: the official regulations are the law.

read-land-truck-map.q: Best time to drive and scout?
read-land-truck-map.why: Animals move most at dawn and dusk. Drive and scout at midday, hunt the edges of the day (Tip).

read-land-truck-map.q: How do you put a height on the snowline you see from the road?
options: Centre the Hunt Map on the snow edge and read the elevation
read-land-truck-map.why: The readout at the top left shows the ground height under the map cross.

bec-zones.q: You read IDFxh2 on the zone map. What does xh tell you?
bec-zones.why: The first small letter is moisture (x is very dry) and the second is temperature (h is hot).

bec-zones.q: Going uphill in the southern Interior, which order do you meet the zones?
bec-zones.why: Big Pines In Many Elk Areas: Bunchgrass, Ponderosa pine, Interior Douglas fir, Montane spruce, Engelmann spruce and subalpine fir, then Alpine tundra.

bec-zones.q: Why is Kamloops so much drier than Mission?
options: It sits in the rain shadow of the Coast Mountains
bec-zones.why: Pacific air drops its rain on the coast side of the mountains. The Interior valleys behind them are in the rain shadow.

bec-zones.q: It is late November with deep snow up high. Which zones should you scout for mule deer near Kamloops?
options: Low PP and IDF south slopes
bec-zones.why: Deer struggle in snow deeper than about 30 cm and winter on low, south facing PP and IDF slopes.

bec-zones.q: You stand in a young lodgepole pine stand. Is it the lodgepole pine zone?
options: Not necessarily. Lodgepole pioneers after fire in many zones, so look for old trees and ground plants
bec-zones.why: Lodgepole pine and aspen come in after fire or logging in many zones. The old trees and the plants underneath tell the true zone.

grassland-country.q: You glass a Kamloops grassland at noon in October and see no deer. Where should you look?
options: Further out on the open grass
In the brushy draws and along the timber edge
grassland-country.why: Deer feed on the open grass at dawn and dusk and spend midday in draws and timber edges, where there is shade, cover and green feed.

grassland-country.q: A slope has lots of sagebrush, cheatgrass and prickly pear cactus. What does it tell you?
grassland-country.why: The zone book says overgrazing raises sage, cheatgrass and cactus at the expense of bunchgrass.

grassland-country.q: Can you hunt a grazing lease on Crown land while cattle are on it?
options: Only with the consent of the lessee or occupant
grassland-country.why: Page 9: no hunting on a grazing lease while livestock are on it without consent. Leased land is also under the Trespass Act.

grassland-country.q: It is late October in the Thompson. How worried should you be about rattlesnakes?
options: Very: they are most active now
Low: virtually all are back in their dens by mid October, but watch rock piles on warm days
grassland-country.why: The BC account says virtually all rattlesnakes have returned to dens by mid October.

grassland-country.q: What is the safest backstop for a shot on open grassland?
grassland-country.why: A bullet that misses with only sky behind it can travel a long way. Shoot only with earth behind the animal.

dry-forest-country.q: You pick up a pine needle bundle: 3 needles, each about 15 cm long. Which tree?
dry-forest-country.why: Ponderosa pine needles come mostly in threes and are 12 to 20 cm long. Lodgepole has 2 short needles; Douglas fir needles are single and 2 to 3 cm.

dry-forest-country.q: Why were many dry pine and fir forests open and park like?
options: Frequent low ground fires that killed small trees but not thick barked old ones
dry-forest-country.why: The zone book says ground fires were common and favoured thick barked mature trees with open canopies.

dry-forest-country.q: Which 3 jobs make old Douglas fir on a south slope good winter range?
options: Catches snow, drops food, sun on the slope
Hides hunters, blocks roads, grows grass
dry-forest-country.why: Big crowns intercept snow, litterfall gives forage, and the south aspect gets the most sun.

dry-forest-country.q: It is noon on a warm October day in open IDF forest. Where are the deer most likely?
options: Feeding on the open pine flats
Bedded on benches, in shady draws or under big fir
dry-forest-country.why: Deer feed at dawn and dusk and bed through midday in cover and shade (Tip).

dry-forest-country.q: Which grouse is linked to old Douglas fir and open pine forest in the zone book?
dry-forest-country.why: The tables list blue grouse, now called dusky grouse, in PP parkland and IDF old forest.

wet-forest-country.why: The BC zone map reads CWHdm3 (Coastal Western Hemlock, dry maritime) at Mission.

wet-forest-country.q: Why does a dense 25 year old second growth stand hold so little deer food?
options: The crowded trees have overtopped and shaded out the shrubs and herbs
wet-forest-country.why: In the pole and sapling stage, dense trees overtop the shrub and herb layers, so the floor is dark and bare.

wet-forest-country.q: What do coast black tailed deer eat in winter?
options: Douglas fir, redcedar, red huckleberry, salal, deer fern and tree lichens
wet-forest-country.why: That is the winter list in the BC Ministry of Environment deer brochure.

wet-forest-country.q: How do old forest crowns help deer in a snowy winter?
options: They intercept snow so it is shallower underneath, and drop branches and lichen to eat
wet-forest-country.why: Old growth intercepts snow and provides forage from broken branches and the lichens on them.

wet-forest-country.q: In thick coast cover, where is the best place to sit at dusk?
options: Deep in the darkest young forest
On the edge where timber meets a cutblock or opening, wind to you
wet-forest-country.why: Deer feed in openings and edges at dusk and slip back to cover. The edge is the hunt (Tip).

wetland-country.q: A wooded wetland with at least a quarter of its area under trees or tall shrubs is a...
wetland-country.why: Swamps are wooded wetlands with 25% or more cover of trees or tall shrubs. Marshes are herb covered; bogs are moss peat.

wetland-country.q: What do moose eat most in a BC winter?
wetland-country.why: Moose in BC depend primarily on willows for winter food. Pondweeds and other water plants are summer food.

wetland-country.q: Why is there a strip of standing trees along a fish stream in a cutblock?
options: Forestry law sets reserve and management zones along fish streams
wetland-country.why: Section 47 of the Forest Planning and Practices Regulation sets riparian widths, for example a 30 m reserve on S2 streams.

wetland-country.q: You see ducks tipping up in a shallow pondweed bay. What kind of ducks are they?
wetland-country.why: Dabblers tip up in shallow water to feed. Divers go right under in deeper water.

wetland-country.q: You drop a duck in the middle of a cold lake with no dog and no boat. What is the right plan?
options: Do not shoot over water you cannot retrieve from; plan the retrieve first
wetland-country.why: Plan the retrieve before you shoot. Cold water is deadly; never swim for a bird (Tip).

burn-country.q: A burned hillside has knee to chest high shrubs and aspen suckers under scattered snags. Roughly how old is the burn?
burn-country.why: Shrubs and aspen root suckers fill in a few years after the fire. That is often the peak browse stage.

burn-country.q: Which part of a burn did moose use most in the Mount McAllister study?
options: Only the high severity black areas
Low and medium severity patches, especially wet sites
burn-country.why: The study found moose used low and medium severity patches and recommended prescribed burns aim for that.

burn-country.q: Where should you park your truck in a burn?
options: Under the tallest snag for shade
In the open, more than a tree length from any snag
burn-country.why: Danger trees fall without warning. Keep a tree length of open ground around you (Tip).

burn-country.q: Why can a burn be dangerous long after the fire is out?
options: Hidden hot ash pits, falling trees, floods and slides after rain
burn-country.why: BC Wildfire Service lists ash pits, danger trees, floods, debris flows, unstable soil and rockfall, lasting 2 years or more.

burn-country.q: What should you check before hunting near a recent fire?
options: BC Wildfire Service area restrictions and in season closures in the Rule Book
burn-country.why: Big fires can bring area restrictions and even hunting closures, as in the 2017 Cariboo fires.

cutblock-country.q: A cutblock has young trees about twice your height, thick willow and aspen. Which animal is it most likely feeding?
cutblock-country.why: Tall shrub blocks about 10 to 30 years old were the ones moose selected in a BC study, and moose eat willow and aspen.

cutblock-country.q: What is BC's pole and sapling stage like for deer food?
options: Dark and bare: dense trees overtop the shrubs and herbs
cutblock-country.why: Stage 4 is dense trees over 10 m tall that overtop the shrub and herb layers, so little food grows.

cutblock-country.q: Where should you sit to hunt a 6 year old cutblock at dusk?
options: In the middle of the block
On the timber edge, downwind of where deer come out
On the road blocking the gate
cutblock-country.why: Deer feed in the block near cover and slip back into timber. Sit the edge with the wind in your favour (Tip).

cutblock-country.q: You ride an ATV on a Forest Service Road. What do you need?
options: A valid driver's licence and at least $200,000 third party liability insurance
cutblock-country.why: Page 9 of the synopsis: ATV operators on a Forest Service Road need a driver's licence and $200,000 liability insurance.

cutblock-country.q: Why does the province worry about new logging roads in moose country?
options: More access can lead to over harvesting moose
cutblock-country.why: BC Ministry of Environment says access roads in moose habitat need control because they could lead to over harvesting.

farm-country.q: Can you hunt an Okanagan orchard without asking if nobody is there?
options: Yes, if it is not fenced
No. Orchards are cultivated land and need the owner's consent
farm-country.why: Page 9: no hunting on cultivated land without the consent of the owner, lessee or occupant.

farm-country.q: A deer is 80 m from an occupied farmhouse. Can you shoot?
options: No. It is unlawful to hunt or shoot within 100 m of an occupied dwelling or farm building
farm-country.why: Page 10: no hunting or discharge within 100 m of a dwelling house or occupied farm or ranch building.

farm-country.q: Where do field deer usually step into a field?
options: At the corner or gap nearest thick cover, with the wind in their favour
farm-country.why: Field deer tend to come out the same corner most nights from the nearest cover (hunter lore, Tip).

farm-country.q: What was the most common waterfowl group in Delta winter field surveys?
options: Mallard, American wigeon and snow goose
farm-country.why: The 2021 to 2022 surveys found mallard, American wigeon and snow goose most common.

farm-country.q: How tall should a woven wire orchard deer fence be?
options: At least 2.4 m with 15 cm mesh
farm-country.why: The BC Tree Fruit Production Guide gives at least 2.4 m with 15 cm mesh, secured close to the ground.

browse-plants.q: A shrub has opposite leaves, bright red young stems and white berries. What is it?
browse-plants.why: Red osier dogwood: opposite leaves with veins curving to the tip, red stems and white berries.

browse-plants.q: What is the main winter food of moose in BC?
browse-plants.why: The BC Ministry of Environment says moose depend primarily on willows for winter food.

browse-plants.q: A grey green shrub on a dry Okanagan slope has small wedge shaped leaves with 3 teeth at the tip. What is it, and who eats it?
options: Bitterbrush, a key mule deer winter food
browse-plants.why: Antelope brush (bitterbrush) has wedge leaves with 3 teeth and is a key mule deer winter browse.

browse-plants.q: A twig end is cut clean at 45 degrees, like pruning shears. Who did it?
browse-plants.why: Hares cut twigs clean. Deer, elk and moose have no upper front teeth, so they tear twigs and leave a ragged end.

browse-plants.q: How high can a moose reach to browse?
options: About 2.5 m, and it breaks stems down for higher tips
browse-plants.why: Moose reach twigs up to about 2.5 m and often break down branches with their jaws.

berries-mast.q: It is early October. Where are you most likely to find ripe huckleberries?
berries-mast.why: Fruit ripens later the higher and shadier the site. A high huckleberry patch may not peak until August or September and lasts later up high.

berries-mast.q: Why do bears spend nearly all day eating berries in fall?
options: Berries are very high in calories
They need up to 20,000 calories a day and berries are low in calories per kilogram
berries-mast.why: Bears in hyperphagia eat up to about 20,000 calories a day; at about 366 calories per kg, that is around 55 kg of huckleberries.

berries-mast.q: Which fruits hang on into winter for grouse and other wildlife?
berries-mast.why: Snowberry fruits persist through winter, and rose hips and kinnikinnick berries also hang on.

berries-mast.q: What do ruffed grouse eat in winter?
options: Buds and catkins of aspen, birch and alder
berries-mast.why: Ruffed grouse rely on buds and catkins of aspen, poplar, birch and alder in winter.

berries-mast.q: You see a bear with a shoulder hump in a berry patch. What do you do?
options: Do not shoot: treat it as a grizzly. There is no open season for grizzly bears in BC
berries-mast.why: A shoulder hump points to a grizzly. There is no open season for grizzly bears in BC. If in doubt, do not shoot.

rs-track-measuring.q: What is a stride in this app?
options: One print to the next print
The same foot to the same foot, which is 2 steps
rs-track-measuring.why: A step is print to print. A stride is the same foot to the same foot. Always write down which one you measured.

rs-track-measuring.q: Where do you measure a print in soft snow?
rs-track-measuring.why: Soft ground pushes the rim out and makes the print look bigger. Measure the floor, and leave out claws.

rs-track-measuring.q: A canid front print is 10.5 cm long without claws. What does the Washington rule say?
rs-track-measuring.why: Front 10 cm or more (4 inches), or hind 9 cm or more (3.5 inches), without claws: likely wolf. 82% of dogs have smaller feet, but big breeds overlap.

rs-track-measuring.q: The trail gets a longer stride and a narrower straddle. What happened?
options: The animal sped up, from a walk to a trot
rs-track-measuring.why: Trotting makes a longer stride and a narrower trail than walking.

rs-track-measuring.q: Groups of 4 prints with gaps of 3 m. Which deer and what mood?
rs-track-measuring.why: Mule deer stot with gaps of about 2.4 to 4.6 m. It saw, heard or smelled something.

rs-track-aging.q: There are rain pits inside a deer print and on the ground around it. When was it made?
rs-track-aging.why: Rain pitted the inside of the print, so the print was there first.

rs-track-aging.q: A crisp print in mud looks very fresh. Why be careful?
options: Mud ages slowest and can look fresh for days
rs-track-aging.why: Mud is the slowest aging ground. Make a control print and look for other clues.

rs-track-aging.q: At sunrise you see a dark line through silver, dewy grass. What does it mean?
options: An animal walked through after the dew formed
It is an old game trail from last week
rs-track-aging.why: The animal knocked the dew off, so it passed after the dew formed: in the night or this morning.

rs-track-aging.q: What is the best single tool for aging a track?
options: Your own boot print beside it, in the same ground
rs-track-aging.why: Your print is minutes old in the same ground and light. Compare, and revisit it to learn how that ground ages.

rs-track-aging.q: Deer pellets are light brown. A friend says that means old. What do you say?
options: Colour depends on diet; check moisture, shine and the inside
rs-track-aging.why: Colour varies with diet; North Dakota Game and Fish even says fresh deer scat can be light brown and darken in a day or two. Moisture and shine are better clocks.

rs-droppings.q: Segmented scat with blunt ends, full of deer hair, in a scraped pile of needles. Who?
rs-droppings.why: Cats leave segmented scat with blunt ends, often in a scratched out spot, sometimes covered. Deer hair says a big cat.

rs-droppings.q: Twisted rope scat under 2.5 cm across, full of mouse hair. Who?
rs-droppings.why: Coyote scat is thinner than about 2.5 cm and holds small mammal hair. Wolf scat is thicker with deer sized hair.

rs-droppings.q: Why wear gloves for coyote, fox or wolf scat?
options: It can carry a tapeworm dangerous to people
rs-droppings.why: Echinococcus multilocularis eggs are shed in canid feces. It is rare in people but serious. Gloves, a stick and soap.

rs-droppings.q: A big pile of deer pellets next to a flattened oval in the grass means...
options: A deer bedded or stood here
rs-droppings.why: Piles form where a deer bedded or stood. Pellets scattered along a trail mean it was moving.

rs-droppings.q: Curved droppings with a white cap, piled under a fir. What is it?
rs-droppings.why: The white cap is dried urine products: a bird. A pile of grouse droppings marks a roost.

rs-beds.q: Which two things mattered most for mule deer summer day beds in the 2004 study?
rs-beds.why: Germaine and others found site temperature and canopy closure were the most influential. Beds are about comfort and cover.

rs-beds.q: Tracks leaving a bed in tight groups of 4 with long gaps. What happened?
options: The deer walked off to feed
rs-beds.why: Stot or gallop groups mean an alarmed exit. Walking tracks mean it left on its own.

rs-beds.q: Hot October afternoon. Where do you look for bedded deer first?
options: Open south slope in full sun
Shade: conifers, north slopes, cool draws
rs-beds.why: Temperature drives bed choice. On hot days deer seek shade and thermal cover.

rs-beds.q: What is the beginner lean for hunting a bedding area?
options: Ambush the trail between bed and feed at first and last light
Sit in the middle of the beds
rs-beds.why: Ambushing the trail keeps the bedding area undisturbed and gives safer, calmer shots.

rs-beds.q: You put your hand in a bed and it is warm. What now?
options: Freeze and glass ahead and to the sides
rs-beds.why: Warm means minutes. The deer is likely close and may be watching you.

rs-rubs-scrapes.q: Which tells you more about buck size: rub height or tree size?
rs-rubs-scrapes.why: Young bucks rub big trees too. A rub centred 75 cm or higher suggests a mature buck (60%).

rs-rubs-scrapes.q: The rubbed side of 4 trees faces the bedding cover. What does it suggest?
options: He walked from the beds toward the feed
He walked from the feed toward the beds
rs-rubs-scrapes.why: The rubbed side usually faces where he came from. He was walking away from the beds, out to feed.

rs-rubs-scrapes.q: In the Georgia camera study, what share of buck scrape visits were at night?
rs-rubs-scrapes.why: 85% of buck visits and 75% of doe visits were at night. Hunt scrapes near cover at first and last light.

rs-rubs-scrapes.q: Can you use store bought deer urine to hunt in BC?
options: No, not if it came from outside BC, which it almost always does
rs-rubs-scrapes.why: Synopsis item 51 bans using deer, elk, moose or caribou parts or derivatives from outside BC for hunting. It can carry CWD.

options: A branch the buck rubs with his antlers to the ground
An overhanging branch above a scrape that he chews and rubs with face glands
rs-rubs-scrapes.why: Bucks chew and rub the licking branch, about 1.2 to 1.5 m up, and paw the scrape below.

rs-bird-sign.q: You find a ring of feathers on a stump with whole quills pulled clean and the breastbone left. Most likely?
options: A bird of prey plucking spot
rs-bird-sign.why: Raptors pluck, leaving whole quills, often in a ring, and leave the breastbone. Mammals bite, cutting shafts. It is a field rule, not proof.

rs-bird-sign.q: Many small round bowls 7 to 15 cm across in dry soil near a rose thicket. What are they?
options: Quail dust bowls, a covey bathed
rs-bird-sign.why: Quail bathe together in small bowls 7 to 15 cm across. A grouse makes one bigger bowl about 20 cm.

rs-bird-sign.q: A pile of curved droppings with white caps under a Douglas fir. What is it?
rs-bird-sign.why: White caps mark bird droppings. Piles form where birds roost overnight.

rs-bird-sign.q: What do Migratory Birds Regulations, 2022, s. 42 require if you wound a duck?
options: Ensure it is killed and retrieved as soon as circumstances permit
rs-bird-sign.why: s. 42 requires adequate means to retrieve and that a wounded bird be killed and retrieved as soon as circumstances permit.

rs-bird-sign.q: Fresh green goose droppings and grazed shoots across a stubble field. What does it tell you?
rs-bird-sign.why: Geese drop often while feeding. Fresh green droppings mean a recent feed. Get permission and plan your setup.

rs-predator-sign.q: A deer carcass is neatly covered with needles in thick cover, with a drag mark leading to it. What is it and what do you do?
options: A cougar cache; back out the way you came, talking loudly
A bear den; climb a tree
rs-predator-sign.why: Cougars drag kills to cover and cover them. The cat stays close and feeds for days. Leave.

rs-predator-sign.q: A carcass in the open, many canid tracks, big bones cracked and remains spread around. Most likely?
rs-predator-sign.why: Wolves feed at the kill, crack big bones and scatter remains. Cougars are tidy and cover; bears rake a mound.

rs-predator-sign.q: How high should you hang meat in bear country, by the Alberta guidance?
options: At least 3.5 m up and 1.5 m from trees
On the ground under a tarp
rs-predator-sign.why: At least 3.5 m up and 1.5 m from trees, in plain view, 200 m from the gut pile and 100 m from camp.

rs-predator-sign.q: You come back to your hung deer and the carcass has been pulled down and partly buried. What now?
options: Do not approach; leave and report
Wait beside it with the rifle
rs-predator-sign.why: A bear may have claimed it and will defend it. Leave the site and report. Meat is replaceable.

rs-predator-sign.q: Why does the Alberta guide say approach your kill from upwind?
options: So the bear cannot smell you
So a bear can smell you coming and is not surprised
rs-predator-sign.why: Coming in from upwind, glassing first and making noise warns a bear early, which avoids a close surprise.

rs-blood-hair-tissue.q: At the hit site you find pink frothy blood and small bits of spongy pink tissue. Most likely?
rs-blood-hair-tissue.why: Light coloured, bubbly blood with soft light tissue points to the lungs.

rs-blood-hair-tissue.q: Thin blood mixed with green plant matter and a sour smell. What do you do?
options: Back out and wait hours, longer than for a lung hit
rs-blood-hair-tissue.why: That is a gut hit. Pushed early, a gut hit deer runs far. Wait, then trail quietly.

rs-blood-hair-tissue.q: Blood drops on a rock each have a small tail on one side. What does the tail tell you?
options: The direction the deer was moving
rs-blood-hair-tissue.why: A drop landing at an angle forms a tail on the far side, so tails point the way the animal went.

rs-blood-hair-tissue.q: The blood trail stops after 50 m. What is the most common reason?
options: Clotting, fat plugging the hole, or bleeding inside
rs-blood-hair-tissue.why: Clotting is the most common reason. No blood does not mean no hit; switch to tracks and disturbed ground.

rs-blood-hair-tissue.q: Where do wounded deer usually head?
options: Downhill, into thick cover, toward water
Straight back to where they were shot
rs-blood-hair-tissue.why: Wounded deer often go downhill, to thick cover and water, often on a game trail.

rs-track-following.q: Where should your eyes be most of the time while following a fresh track?
options: Ahead, 40 to 100 m, with quick glances down
rs-track-following.why: The animal is ahead, not at your feet. Glance down for the next print, then look ahead.

rs-track-following.q: You lose the trail. What do you do first?
options: Walk on in the same direction
Go back to the last clear print, flag it, and circle about 10 m out
rs-track-following.why: Wandering ahead stamps out the next print. A circle from the last known track must cross the trail.

rs-track-following.q: The track shows the deer slowing to feed, with nibbled twigs and short wanders. What now?
options: Slow right down and glass every direction
rs-track-following.why: Feeding means it is close and likely to bed soon. Slow down a lot and scan ahead.

rs-track-following.q: The trail turns and heads downwind. What is the Tip?
options: Leave the trail and loop around so your scent does not reach the deer
rs-track-following.why: Walking downwind on the trail sends your scent to the deer. Loop around and come in with the wind right.

rs-track-following.q: What does a track stick do?
options: Uses step and stride bands to show where the next print should be
rs-track-following.why: Set bands at step and stride on clear prints, then sweep an arc from the last track to find the faint next one.

rs-sign-substrates.q: Which snow gives the best print detail?
options: A thin layer of wet snow
rs-sign-substrates.why: Wet snow captures a print well. Powder leaves holes with little detail, and crust or wind leaves almost nothing.

rs-sign-substrates.q: A snow print looks huge and round after 4 sunny days. What is the trap?
options: Melt out makes prints grow; measure only fresh prints
rs-sign-substrates.why: Sun melts snow prints bigger and rounder. Use shape clues and fresh prints.

rs-sign-substrates.q: A deer print sits on top of a tire tread in a dusty road. What does it tell you?
options: The deer passed before the truck
The deer passed after the truck
rs-sign-substrates.why: Whatever mark is on top was made last. If you know when the truck passed, you know the deer came after.

rs-sign-substrates.q: Why can a crisp mud print fool you about age?
options: Mud ages slowest and keeps a fresh look for days
rs-sign-substrates.why: Mud holds detail and ages slowly. Look for water seeping in and a shiny rim, and use other clues.

rs-sign-substrates.q: In dry leaf litter with no prints, what do you look for?
options: Flipped leaves, scuffed moss, pressed duff, moved stones
rs-sign-substrates.why: Litter shows disturbance, not prints. Crouch low toward the light and read what moved.

fronts-and-movement.q: What did Penn State find when collared does faced 30 winter storms?
options: They fed hard the day before
No real change before; they moved less during the storm
fronts-and-movement.why: Their data showed no statistical or biological effect of oncoming storms. The deer slowed during the storms.

fronts-and-movement.q: A cold front passes at noon. What usually happens to the wind?
options: It swings from south to west or northwest
It always blows from the east
fronts-and-movement.why: Ahead of a cold front the wind is usually southerly; behind it, westerly or northwesterly. Your scent cone swings with it, so have a second seat.

fronts-and-movement.q: Which weather fact has the strongest evidence for moving Interior mule deer in fall?
fronts-and-movement.why: Snow and cold trigger the move to winter range (Monteith 2011; Wyoming collars 2016 to 2018). Pressure evidence is weak and the moon is near zero.

fronts-and-movement.q: What best explained duck numbers in the Missouri weather study?
options: A cumulative index of cold days and snow cover
fronts-and-movement.why: The cumulative weather severity index (temperature, runs of freezing days, snow depth and snow cover days) had the most support. Cold costs energy; ice and snow hide food.

fronts-and-movement.q: A storm is on and the wind is howling. A sound plan?
options: Glass sheltered lee slopes from a sheltered seat, then glass hard in the first calm
Walk the open ridge top fast
fronts-and-movement.why: Deer move less in storms but they do not vanish. Lee slopes and the calm after are the tip. Keep warm and dry.

pressure-push.q: In the Pennsylvania aerial survey, what share of hunters were within 0.5 km of a road?
pressure-push.why: 73% were within half a kilometre, and the average farthest point from a road was 0.84 km. Large areas farther out had little or no hunting.

pressure-push.q: What did collared mule deer bucks in Wyoming do in rifle season?
options: Moved onto the best feed near roads
Selected security habitat away from motorized routes
pressure-push.why: Bucks chose security cover away from motorized routes. Does stayed on better feed. Weather, not hunting, set migration timing.

pressure-push.q: Oregon mule deer in hunting season were on average how far from closed roads versus open roads?
pressure-push.why: Deer stayed much closer to roads closed to vehicles. Gated roads are worth walking at first light.

pressure-push.q: It is 15 October in MU 3-28. Can you ride the ATV up a Forest Service road to hunt?
options: No. ATVs for hunting are closed in 3-28, 3-29 and 3-30 from 1 September to 10 December
pressure-push.why: Synopsis page 33. Use the truck on open roads, then walk. The quiet is good for you.

pressure-push.q: Opening morning, crowded road. Best plan?
options: Walk the road edge with everyone
Sit the trail between the crowd and the nearest thick, steep timber, before light
Drive the roads to push deer
pressure-push.why: Pushed deer head for cover. Sitting the link between pressure and refuge uses the crowd. Driving at wildlife to herd it is unlawful.

bc-migration-routes.q: In the Southern Interior Mule Deer Project, what share of collared deer that could migrate did migrate?
bc-migration-routes.why: 74% on the current project page, 78% in the 2020 update. Some deer stay low all year.

bc-migration-routes.q: What sets the timing of the fall mule deer move?
bc-migration-routes.why: Monteith 2011 and the Wyoming collar study both point to weather: snow and temperature.

bc-migration-routes.q: Which goes down from the high country last?
bc-migration-routes.why: The BC moose account says moose stay on high ranges much longer than elk, deer or sheep, and handle snow to about 40 cm with little trouble.

bc-migration-routes.q: What ends most Interior duck migration in BC?
bc-migration-routes.why: Ducks Unlimited: fall migration largely concluded by late November, with freeze up.

bc-migration-routes.q: Do mule deer use a new route each fall?
options: No. Most choose nearly the same path both ways, year after year
bc-migration-routes.why: SIMDeer collars showed nearly the same path. Find the route once and it pays for years.

winter-range-legal.q: What does a BC Ungulate Winter Range order mainly control?
options: Forest practices like timber harvest and roads, to keep snow interception cover
winter-range-legal.why: Order u-3-003 sets rules for primary forest activities (harvest, silviculture, roads) and requires snow interception cover. Hunting rules come from the synopsis.

winter-range-legal.q: Are there approved UWR polygons right around Heffley Creek?
options: No. The layer query found none in that box; the nearest mule deer ones are south toward Merritt and on the North Okanagan side
winter-range-legal.why: Near the base, use the habitat rule: low south and west slopes, shrubs, old fir.

winter-range-legal.q: 15 November, Region 3, a 3 point mule deer buck on winter range. Legal?
options: No. From 1 November a mule deer buck needs 4 points
Yes, if you are on foot
winter-range-legal.why: Synopsis page 34: 4 point bucks only from 1 November to 10 December in your MUs.

winter-range-legal.q: Cattle are grazing on a Crown grazing lease below a winter range slope. Can you walk in to hunt?
options: Not without the consent of the lessee or occupant
winter-range-legal.why: Page 9: no hunting on a grazing lease occupied by livestock without consent. Leased land also falls under the Trespass Act.

winter-range-legal.q: Why glass winter range from across a draw instead of walking it?
options: Each disturbance costs deer energy and feeding time, and you push deer you cannot see
Glassing is faster to shoot from
winter-range-legal.why: Agency fact sheets: disturbance burns reserves. Glassing finds deer without pushing them (Tip).

waterfowl-daily-flights.q: Louisiana mallards moved how far between day and night sites?
waterfowl-daily-flights.why: Link and others 2011: 3.1 to 15.0 km depending on land type. Draw a 15 km circle around a roost to find the fields.

waterfowl-daily-flights.q: When do Canada geese usually fly to fields?
options: Early morning and late afternoon, more all day in storms
waterfowl-daily-flights.why: The Illinois study: morning and late afternoon feeding flights, with more flying through the day when stormy.

waterfowl-daily-flights.q: Where should the wind be when you set up on water?
options: At your back, blowing out over the decoys
waterfowl-daily-flights.why: Ducks land into the wind. With it at your back they come in facing you, into the hole in front.

waterfowl-daily-flights.q: Sunrise at Heffley Creek is 7:22. When can you first shoot a duck?
waterfowl-daily-flights.why: Migratory birds: from half an hour before sunrise. Deer would be 6:22.

waterfowl-daily-flights.q: You found the roost. Best way to hunt it over a season?
options: Hunt the feeding area and rest the roost, hunting it every few days at most
Fly over it in the boat to count birds
waterfowl-daily-flights.why: Pressure on a roost moves birds off. That is a tip. Using a boat to herd birds is unlawful.

upland-daily-pattern.q: How far from cover do California quail usually feed?
upland-daily-pattern.why: CDFW: seldom more than 15 to 30 m from cover. Walk the brush edges.

upland-daily-pattern.q: Where are chukar most likely at 1 pm on a warm day?
options: Out on open grassy slopes feeding
In shade, draws, dust bowls or near water
upland-daily-pattern.why: WDFW: morning feeding on slopes, then shady slopes, draws, dusting sites and water holes midday.
They usually run uphill. Get above them and hunt down.

upland-daily-pattern.q: At what height are ruffed grouse most common in BC?
upland-daily-pattern.why: BC Breeding Bird Atlas: highest abundance at 750 to 1,250 m.

upland-daily-pattern.q: It is 15 October. Can you hunt California quail near Heffley Creek in Region 3?
options: No. Quail seasons are in Region 8 MUs, not Region 3
upland-daily-pattern.why: The quail season is in Region 8 (MUs 8-1 to 8-15 and 8-21 to 8-26), 1 October to 30 November. No quail row in Region 3.

build-hunting-map.q: Which layer do you build first?
options: The legal base: MU and land status
build-hunting-map.why: Law first. A perfect bench on private land or in a No Shooting area is no use.

build-hunting-map.q: What distance ring belongs round every occupied house and barn on your map?
build-hunting-map.why: No hunting or shooting within 100 m of a dwelling or occupied farm or ranch building (page 10). 15 m is the road rule.

build-hunting-map.q: Can you use photos from a cell trail camera to plan a hunt on 20 October in Region 3?
options: No. Wireless cameras may not be used for hunting from 1 August to 10 December outside Region 1
build-hunting-map.why: Page 11, item 30. A card only camera is not a wireless camera.

build-hunting-map.q: Your month layer says deer should be high, but you found fresh tracks heading down to a south slope. What wins?
build-hunting-map.why: Month layers are a general pattern (60%). Fresh sign is what deer did last night.

build-hunting-map.q: What should change on your map on 1 November?
options: Region 3 mule deer bucks now need 4 points
build-hunting-map.why: In your MUs, October is any buck; 1 November to 10 December is 4 point bucks only.

land-drill-heffley.q: On 24 October in MU 3-27, which mule deer are legal?
land-drill-heffley.why: Any buck from 1 to 31 October. From 1 November, 4 points only. Antlerless mule deer are LEH only.

land-drill-heffley.q: Sunrise is 7:37. When does legal deer hunting start?
land-drill-heffley.why: Big game from 1 hour before sunrise. Ducks would be 30 minutes before.

land-drill-heffley.q: Can you shoot inside the developed part of a recreation site?
options: No. No firearm on or into the developed portion, which includes a 100 m buffer
land-drill-heffley.why: Forest Recreation Regulation section 11. Walk well clear before you load.

land-drill-heffley.q: Morning, sunny slope, deer bedded above you. Which way does the thermal carry your scent?
land-drill-heffley.why: Morning thermals rise as the slope warms. Come in from the side or from above.

land-drill-heffley.q: Tracks with points leading uphill, shiny pellets, a fresh rub. Best story?
options: A buck fed below and went up to bed recently
land-drill-heffley.why: Points lead the way, shiny pellets are fresh, rubs are buck sign. Sit below at last light (Tip).

moon-and-daylight.q: How big was the moon effect on buck movement in the Mississippi State collar data?
options: About 4 m an hour, inside GPS error
Bucks stopped moving at full moon
moon-and-daylight.why: About 4 m an hour, within the collar error. The rut nearly doubled buck travel.

moon-and-daylight.q: What sets the timing of the deer breeding season?
moon-and-daylight.why: Shortening days change melatonin and hormones. Deer are short day breeders.

moon-and-daylight.q: Bright full moon, 15 October. When can you start hunting deer at Heffley Creek?
moon-and-daylight.why: Item 38: game only from 1 hour before sunrise. The moon changes nothing.

moon-and-daylight.q: About how much daylight is lost each day in mid October at Heffley Creek?
moon-and-daylight.why: About 3.8 minutes a day by calculation. Late November days are about 8.3 hours long.

moon-and-daylight.q: When are deer moving most, by the Penn State October data?
options: Dawn and dusk, 120 to 140 m an hour
moon-and-daylight.why: Dawn and dusk dwarf any moon effect. Be glassing at first light.

land-in-weather.q: A track has small rain pits inside it. When was it made?
land-in-weather.why: Rain pitted the print, so the print was there first. A clean print on spattered ground came after.

land-in-weather.q: Snow stopped at 5 am. You find tracks on top of the new snow at 8 am. What do you know?
options: They were made in the last 3 hours
land-in-weather.why: On top of the new snow means after it stopped. That is fresh sign.

land-in-weather.q: A gale is blowing over the ridge. Where do you glass first?
options: Sheltered lee slopes and timber edges
land-in-weather.why: A tip from experience: animals use shelter in strong wind. The wind studies are mixed, so change where you look, not whether you go.

land-in-weather.q: It is 4 °C, raining and windy. Your brother starts fumbling with his zipper and talking oddly. What now?
options: Keep going, it is above freezing
Stop, dry layer and food, and turn back together
Leave him and finish the stalk
land-in-weather.why: Hypothermia does not need frost. The umbles are an early warning. Turn back together.

land-in-weather.q: Cold, still, clear morning. A crisp deer track sits in shaded snow. Fresh?
options: Maybe not: cold still air keeps tracks crisp for days
It is a week old for sure
land-in-weather.why: Crisp does not always mean fresh in the cold. Compare with your own boot print and look for other clues.

mule-deer.q: A deer bounces away with all 4 feet hitting the ground together. What is it?
mule-deer.why: That bounce is called stotting. It is a mule deer trademark. White tails gallop with the tail up like a flag.

mule-deer.q: When should you be on your glassing spot in late October?
options: At noon when deer are bedded
mule-deer.why: The morning peak is about 04:00 to 09:00. Arrive early, in the dark, and be still when light comes.

mule-deer.q: In a 4 point season, which buck is legal?
options: 3 tines plus a brow tine on one side
4 tines on one antler, not counting the brow tine
Any buck with 4 points total on both antlers
mule-deer.why: The brow tine does not count. You need 4 or more tines on one antler, each at least 2.5 cm long and longer than it is wide (synopsis pages 3 and 4). In MU 3-27 and 3-28 the 4 point rule applies 10 to 30 September and 1 November to 10 December (page 34).

mule-deer.q: What mostly triggers mule deer to move down to winter range?
mule-deer.why: Studies show snow and cold drive the move. The rut comes later, mid November.

mule-deer.q: What do mule deer near Kamloops mostly eat in fall?
mule-deer.why: A Kamloops stomach study found grass under 10% until spring. Fall diet is forbs and shrub browse.

white-tailed-deer.q: A deer runs into the willows with a wide white tail held straight up. What is it?
white-tailed-deer.why: The raised white flag and smooth gallop are white tail signs. Mule deer have a thin black tipped tail and bounce.

white-tailed-deer.q: Where is the best place for your stand?
options: In the middle of the hayfield
On the trail between bedding cover and the field, downwind
white-tailed-deer.why: Deer travel that trail at dusk and dawn. Downwind keeps your scent off them. Walking into bedding brush pushes them out.

options: A pawed bare patch of dirt under a low branch
white-tailed-deer.why: Bucks paw the ground and work the branch above with their face and antlers. Bark stripping is a rub.

white-tailed-deer.q: How close to an occupied house or farm building may you shoot?
white-tailed-deer.why: The synopsis, page 10, bans hunting or shooting within 100 m of a dwelling house, or a farm or ranch building occupied by people or domestic animals.

white-tailed-deer.q: When does rattling work best for white tails?
options: Cool, calm mornings near the rut in early November
white-tailed-deer.why: Response was best on cool, calm, overcast mornings near the rut. Mid October is early for it.

deer-mind.q: Which sense can you never fully beat?
deer-mind.why: Smell is a deer's strongest sense. Only the wind protects you.

deer-mind.q: It is 08:30, sun on the slope. Which way does your scent drift?
deer-mind.why: Sun warms the slope and warm air rises, so scent drifts uphill. Approach from above or the side.

deer-mind.q: A deer stares at you and stamps a hoof. What do you do?
deer-mind.why: The stamp is a test to make you move. Freeze until it looks away or relaxes.

deer-mind.q: What gives a hunter in blaze orange away?
deer-mind.why: Deer have no red cone, so orange looks dull. They catch motion and shape very fast.

deer-mind.q: What is the top cause of death for southern Interior mule deer?
deer-mind.why: In the southern Interior mule deer project, cougars were first and coyotes second.

moose.q: In the Region 3 general open season, which moose is legal?
moose.why: All three Region 3 rows read spike fork bulls, bag limit 1. Cows, calves and bigger bulls need an LEH authorization or are closed.

moose.q: How many tines may a spike fork bull have on one antler?
options: At least 3 on the brow palm
moose.why: Synopsis page 3: no more than two tines on one antler, brow palm tines included. Three on the brow palm is a tripalm; ten is a 10 point.

moose.q: You bought a moose licence but never went hunting. What must you do?
options: Submit a Mandatory Hunter Report by 31 March
Return the licence for a refund
moose.why: Every moose licence buyer reports by 31 March, hunt or no hunt. Skip it and you cannot buy next year's licence until it is filed.

moose.q: What must travel with your moose species licence after the kill?
options: The antlers, naturally attached to part of the upper skull
moose.why: Antlers must accompany the species licence and stay attached to part of the skull, available for inspection, until home, the meat cutter or cold storage.

moose.q: A bull stands chest deep in a lake. Can you shoot?
options: No. Hunting big game while it is swimming is unlawful
moose.why: Synopsis page 11, item 26. It is also the surest way to lose 150 kg of meat on a lake bottom.

elk.q: What makes a bull a 6 point under BC rules?
options: 6 tines on both antlers added together
At least 6 tines on one antler, brow tine included
6 tines not counting the brow tine
elk.why: Synopsis page 3: at least six tines on one antler. Unlike the deer 4 point rule, the brow tine counts for elk.

elk.q: Is there a general open season for elk in Region 3 Thompson?
options: No. Only an LEH draw could open elk there
elk.why: The Region 3 table on page 34 has no elk row. LEH seasons are open only to hunters who drew an authorization.

elk.q: When is the Region 8 rifle season for 6 point bulls?
elk.why: Page 68: 6 point bulls, 10 September to 20 October in MUs 8-1 to 8-15 and 8-21 to 8-26, plus bow only 1 to 9 September.

elk.q: You held an elk licence this year. What is due by 31 March?
options: Nothing unless you killed an elk
elk.why: From 2026 the Mandatory Hunter Report replaces compulsory inspection and reporting for elk. Every licence buyer files one, kill or no kill.

elk.q: When do bull elk bugle most?
elk.why: The rut runs early September to mid October, with bugling possible into November. June is calving time.

black-bear.q: A big brown bear feeds on a slope. What do you check before anything else?
options: Shoulder hump, face profile and ears
black-bear.why: Colour is not reliable. Interior black bears are often brown. A hump, a dished face and small round ears mean grizzly, and there is no open season on grizzlies in BC.

black-bear.q: What is the Region 3 fall black bear season in MUs 3-12 to 3-20 and 3-26 to 3-44?
black-bear.why: Synopsis page 34: Sept 1 to Nov 30, bag limit 2. MU 3-46 opens later, on 20 September.

black-bear.q: A bear is feeding with a smaller bear nearby. Can you shoot the big one?
options: Yes, if it is the bigger one
No. A bear under 2 and any bear in its company are closed
black-bear.why: Synopsis page 11, item 14. The smaller bear is likely a cub or yearling, and the sow with it is protected too.

black-bear.q: Which is legal when hunting black bear in BC?
options: Using a 20 gauge shotgun with No. 1 buck
black-bear.why: Baiting bears is unlawful. Rimfire is not allowed for black bear. A shotgun of 20 gauge or larger with No. 1 buck or larger is on the methods table, page 13.

black-bear.q: How do you make bear meat safe from trichinosis?
options: Cook it to an internal 71 C (160 F) and check with a thermometer
black-bear.why: The bear species of Trichinella survives freezing. Only heat kills it. Use a thermometer, because colour does not show doneness.

ducks.q: A duck patters along the water to take off and has wings set far back. What is it?
ducks.why: Divers run along the surface to get airborne and carry their wings far back. Puddle ducks jump straight up. The bufflehead is the exception that can jump.

ducks.q: Which puddle duck has a white wing patch?
ducks.why: The gadwall is the only puddle duck with a white speculum. The mallard is blue with white bars, the pintail green with a white trailing edge.

ducks.q: You have 2 goldeneyes and 3 mallards. A goldeneye hen comes in. What now?
options: No shot. Goldeneyes are limited to 2 a day, Barrow's and common combined
Shoot only if it is a Barrow's
ducks.why: The daily limit for goldeneyes is 2 in aggregate inside the 8 duck limit. Once you have 2 you may not hunt them that day.

ducks.q: When do ducks open near Kamloops in District No. 3?
ducks.why: Schedule 3, Part 10 of the Migratory Birds Regulations, 2022: District No. 3 ducks run September 8 to December 23. District 2 opens 10 October 2026 and District 8 opens 23 September.

ducks.q: What must stay on an unpreserved duck in your truck and your fridge?
options: One fully feathered wing or the fully feathered head
ducks.why: Section 52 of the federal regulations. The wing or head lets an officer identify the species and count your bag. BC says the same on page 15 of the synopsis.

geese.q: A small goose with a stubby bill and a yelping call lands with Canada geese. How does it count?
options: It is a separate species with its own limit of 5
Canada and cackling geese are combined: 10 a day together
geese.why: The federal table lists Canada Geese and Cackling Geese, combined, with one daily limit of 10 in every BC district.

geese.q: You plan a Kamloops goose hunt on 25 September. Is District 3 open for Canada geese?
options: No. The first period ends 20 September and the next opens 1 October
geese.why: District No. 3 Canada and cackling goose periods are September 8 to 20, October 1 to December 23, and March 1 to 10. White fronted and snow geese stay open through that gap.

geese.q: What do you need to hunt geese inside the district of Mission beyond the normal licences?
options: The Fraser Valley Special Area licence and $1,000,000 liability insurance
geese.why: Map B10 in the Region 2 synopsis: all of the district of Mission is in the Fraser Valley Special Licence Hunting Area. The licence is $10 and insurance is required.

geese.q: Which steel pellet is the all round choice for large Canada geese over decoys?
geese.why: BB is the standard goose pellet in steel, with BBB or T for longer range. Pattern it: 60 pellets in a 30 inch circle at your longest range.

geese.q: Where should geese be on your morning hunt, and why?
options: In the field they fed in yesterday afternoon
geese.why: Geese usually return to the previous afternoon's feeding field. Scout the evening before, mark the spot, and hide there before light.

grouse.q: A dark grouse with a red comb over the eye sits on a branch and will not fly. What is it?
grouse.why: Spruce grouse are dark, the male has a red eye comb and a black breast edged in white, and they are famously tame. A ruffed grouse has a crest and a banded fan tail.

grouse.q: In Region 3 you have 5 ruffed grouse. Can you shoot a dusky grouse?
options: Yes. The limit is 5 of each species and 10 in total a day
grouse.why: Region 3, page 34: 5 each (15 each), with a daily aggregate of 10 and possession of 30. In Region 8 the aggregate is only 5.

grouse.q: Which bird may you hunt with a .22 rimfire in BC?
grouse.why: Page 13 of the synopsis: rimfire for upland game birds is Yes with note 2, grouse, ptarmigan, or turkey only. Quail, chukar, partridge and pheasant are shotgun, air gun or bow.

grouse.q: A grouse sits on the gravel shoulder of a two lane public road. What is legal?
options: Get out, walk 15 m or more off the road, load, and shoot only with a safe backstop
Shoot from the road once the engine is off
grouse.why: No shooting from a motor vehicle, no loaded firearm in it, and no hunting or shooting within the road allowance, 15 m either side of the middle of a road under three lanes.

grouse.q: Where is sharp tailed grouse open in Region 3?
options: MUs 3-30 and 3-31 only, with part of 3-30 closed
grouse.why: Page 34: open in 3-30 and 3-31, 10 September to 30 November, 5 a day, 10 in possession, and closed in the part of 3-30 south of the Scottie Creek FSR, Map C18.

upland-birds.q: Can you hunt California quail near Heffley Creek in Region 3 this fall?
options: Yes, 10 a day like the Okanagan
No. The Region 3 table has no quail row, so there is no open season
upland-birds.why: Quail rows exist in Region 8 (10 a day) and Region 1 (5 a day). Region 3 has chukar, partridge and pheasant rows but no quail.

upland-birds.q: Which firearm is legal for chukar?
upland-birds.why: Page 13: rimfire and centrefire rifles are allowed for upland birds only for grouse, ptarmigan or turkey. Quail, chukar, partridge and pheasant are shotgun, air gun or bow.

upland-birds.q: What are the Region 8 limits for chukar and grey partridge?
upland-birds.why: Region 8, page 68: chukar 5 a day, 15 in possession; grey (Hungarian) partridge 3 a day, 9 in possession. Both open 1 October to 30 November.

upland-birds.q: A long tailed brown bird flushes from a Mission hedgerow in MU 2-8. Shoot?
options: No. Only cocks are legal, and a brown bird with no ring is a hen
Yes if you have the special licence
upland-birds.why: The Region 2 row is PHEASANT (Cocks). A hen is never legal. In Mission you also need the Fraser Valley Special Area licence and insurance before any hunt.

upland-birds.q: An orchard has no fence and no sign. Can you walk it for quail?
options: No. Cultivated land needs the consent of the owner or occupant
Yes if you stay 100 m from the house
upland-birds.why: Page 9 and item 53 on page 12: no hunting on cultivated land without consent. The 100 m rule from occupied buildings applies on top of that.

mountain-sheep.q: For a full curl bighorn ram, where does the legal line run?
options: From the eye to the tip of the nose
From the centre of the nostril to the lowest back edge of the horn base
Along the top of the skull
mountain-sheep.why: The synopsis definition on page 4 draws the line through the centre of the nostril and the lowest hindmost portion of the horn base. A horn tip must rise above it.

mountain-sheep.q: A thinhorn ram's horn tip does not clear the nose bridge line. Can he still be legal?
options: Yes, if he is 8 years old by true horn rings, confirmed by the regional manager or designate
mountain-sheep.why: The full curl thinhorn definition has two tests: 8 years by true annuli, or the horn tip beyond the nose bridge plane. The synopsis warns not to age rams by rings in the field.

mountain-sheep.q: You kill a ram on October 20. By when must it be inspected?
options: Within 30 days and before December 5, whichever comes first
Before the end of the licence year
mountain-sheep.why: Sheep and goats must be inspected within 30 days and before December 5 of the year of the kill. Book the appointment early; no drop ins.

mountain-sheep.q: Which weapon is NOT legal for mountain sheep in BC?
options: Air gun of .35 calibre or larger
mountain-sheep.why: Page 13 lists rimfire as No for mountain sheep. Shotguns are also not allowed.

mountain-sheep.q: Which Region 3 MUs have a general open season for full curl bighorn rams?
mountain-sheep.why: Page 34 lists MUs 3-31 and part of 3-32 for full curl rams, Sept 10 to Oct 20, with part of 3-32 closed (Map C21). A portion of 3-17 is open for mature rams.

mountain-goat.q: Which goat is illegal to shoot in BC?
options: A female goat in a group that has a kid in it
Any goat with horns under 25 cm
mountain-goat.why: Page 11 says it is unlawful to hunt a female mountain goat accompanying a kid or in a group with one or more kids. A lone nanny is legal but a poor choice.

mountain-goat.q: A group of 12 goats with several small ones is feeding on a slope. What are the adults most likely to be?
mountain-goat.why: Groups with kids and yearlings are almost always nannies. Billies are alone or in groups of 2 or 3 without young, except in the rut.

mountain-goat.q: Can you hunt mountain goat near Heffley Creek under a general open season?
options: No, Region 3 goats are LEH only
Yes, but only with a bow
mountain-goat.why: The Region 3 general open season table on page 34 has no goat row. Region 3 goat hunts are LEH, with Kamloops zones running Sept 1 to Nov 30.

mountain-goat.q: What must you bring to a goat compulsory inspection?
options: The horns and evidence of sex
mountain-goat.why: Page 17 lists the horns plus a testicle or part of the penis for males, or a portion of the teats or mammary gland for females.

caribou-bison.why: Caribou are the only deer family animal where females also grow antlers. Antlers alone never make it a bull.

caribou-bison.q: Is there a general open season for caribou in BC?
options: No, every caribou hunt is LEH
caribou-bison.why: The Region 6 and 7A tables print LIMITED ENTRY HUNTING ONLY, and Regions 5 and 7B offer caribou only through the LEH synopsis. Region 3 has no caribou season.

caribou-bison.q: What is the bison rifle rule?
options: A 175 grain or heavier bullet with at least 2,712 joules at 100 m
caribou-bison.why: Page 13 note 7 and the LEH synopsis set the 175 grain and 2,712 joule (2,000 ft lb) at 100 m rule.

caribou-bison.q: What must a caribou hunter submit for compulsory inspection?
options: The incisor tooth and the antlers, plus the hide with evidence of sex if no main beam is over 60 cm
caribou-bison.why: Page 17 lists the incisor tooth, the antlers, and the hide with evidence of sex for a caribou without a main beam over 60 cm. A Mandatory Hunter Report is also due by March 31.

wild-turkey.q: What class of turkey is legal in the Region 8 spring season?
wild-turkey.why: Page 68 lists Bearded for Apr 15 to May 15. A bearded hen is legal; a beardless tom is not.

wild-turkey.q: You shot a bearded bird in May. What must stay on the carcass?
options: One feathered wing and the beard
wild-turkey.why: Page 15: a game bird must keep one feathered wing attached, and a turkey taken in a bearded only season must keep the beard too.

wild-turkey.q: Which firearm is NOT legal for turkey in BC?
wild-turkey.why: Page 13 note 2 allows rimfire for grouse, ptarmigan or turkey. Note 3 limits centrefire to grouse or ptarmigan only.

wild-turkey.q: How many turkeys may you take in Region 8 in a year?
options: 2, one in spring and one in fall
wild-turkey.why: The Region 8 footnote on page 68 and the bag limit note on page 67 say the aggregate is 2, one per season. Region 4 allows 3.

predators.q: In which Region 3 MUs is there no closed season for wolf?
predators.why: Page 34 lists MU 3-17 and MUs 3-26 to 3-44 as No closed season with no bag limit. MUs 3-12 to 3-16 and 3-18 to 3-20 run Sept 10 to June 15 with a limit of 3.

predators.q: Which of these may NOT be hunted with a .22 rimfire?
predators.why: Page 13 lists rimfire as No for cougar and wolf. Bobcat, lynx, wolverine and coyote allow rimfire.

predators.q: You kill a lynx in Region 3. What paperwork follows?
predators.why: Page 17: lynx in Regions 3, 6, 7A or 7B need a Compulsory Report within 30 days. Cougar is the predator that needs Compulsory Inspection.

predators.q: Which predator's meat must you take home by law?
predators.why: The edible portions definition on page 3 excludes wolf, lynx, bobcat and wolverine, but not cougar. Cook cougar thoroughly because of Trichinella.

predators.q: A cougar with spots crosses the road. Legal?
options: No, it is a kitten and protected, and so is any adult with it
predators.why: A cougar kitten is any cougar with spots or under one year. You may not hunt a kitten or any cougar in its company.

small-game.q: Which of these counts as small game in BC law?
small-game.why: Page 4 lists fox, raccoon, coyote, skunk, snowshoe hare and game birds. Red squirrels are furbearers for trappers, and Nuttall's cottontail is protected.

small-game.q: What is the Region 3 snowshoe hare season and limit?
small-game.why: Page 34: MUs 3-12 to 3-20 and 3-26 to 3-44, Aug 1 to Apr 30, 10 daily.

small-game.q: Where may you hunt Columbian ground squirrels in Region 3?
options: Private land only, with the landowner's permission
small-game.why: The page 34 note restricts the ground squirrel season to private land with permission.

small-game.q: What does the BC tularemia fact sheet tell trappers and hunters?
options: Freeze the meat for a week
Do not skin animals found dead, and handle carcasses with gloves
small-game.why: The fact sheet says trappers should not skin animals found dead and should handle dead animals with gloves. Hares, rabbits and rodents are the usual carriers.

sea-ducks.q: Where and when is brant open in BC?
options: All coastal MUs, October to January
sea-ducks.why: The federal table for District 2 lists Brant March 1 to 10 only in MU 2-4, 3 a day and 9 in possession. Every other district says no open season.

sea-ducks.q: Besides the hunting licence and the MGBHP, what does MU 2-4 require?
options: The Fraser Valley Special Area licence and $1,000,000 liability insurance
sea-ducks.why: Map B10's note requires the Fraser Valley Special Area Hunting Licence and $1,000,000 public liability and property damage insurance for MU 2-4 and parts of MU 2-8.

sea-ducks.q: How many harlequin ducks may you take in a day?
sea-ducks.why: The 8 duck aggregate caps harlequins at 2 a day and 6 in possession, with the same caps on goldeneyes.

sea-ducks.q: When may you shoot a duck from a boat with a motor?
options: Any time the motor is running slowly
Only when the boat is not moving, for example beached, anchored or tied off, and not gliding from the motor
sea-ducks.why: Page 11 item 24: it is unlawful to hunt migratory birds from or by using a moving boat that is equipped with a motor or sail. A boat still gliding from its motor counts as moving.

all-bc-species.q: Which bear has no open season anywhere in BC?
all-bc-species.why: Page 19 and page 80: there is no open season for grizzly bears in BC. Cinnamon is a legal black bear colour; white and blue phases are closed.

all-bc-species.q: You are a BC resident hunting coyote in Region 3. Which licence?
all-bc-species.why: Coyote is small game. Page 8: no species licence is required for small game. You still need the basic licence.

all-bc-species.q: What extra permit do you need for snipe?
options: The federal Canada Migratory Game Bird Hunting Permit
all-bc-species.why: Page 3 lists snipe as a migratory game bird, which needs the federal permit on top of the BC licence.

all-bc-species.q: You bought a cougar licence today. When can you use it?
options: 2 days after the date of issue
