all-bc-species.why: Page 8: cougar, bobcat, lynx, caribou, goat, sheep and wolverine licences are not valid until 2 days after issue.

all-bc-species.q: Is there a general elk season in Region 3?
options: No general season row in the Region 3 table
all-bc-species.why: Page 34 has no elk row. Any elk hunt would be LEH only, and that is a separate draw.

gallery-deer.q: From behind you see a white rump and a thin white tail with a black tip, held down. What is it?
gallery-deer.why: A thin rope tail with a black tip, held down even when running, is the mule deer mark. A white tail has a wide tail raised like a flag.

gallery-deer.q: A buck's antler has one main beam with three tines rising off it. Which species does that suggest?
gallery-deer.why: White tail tines grow up off one main beam. Mule and black tailed deer antlers fork, then fork again.

gallery-deer.q: A mule deer buck has 3 tines plus a brow tine on his best antler. Is he a 4 point buck?
options: No. The brow tine does not count, so he has 3
Yes, if the brow tine is over 2.5 cm
gallery-deer.why: Page 4: a 4 point buck has at least four tines on one antler, excluding the brow tine.

gallery-deer.q: A deer bounces away with all four feet leaving the ground together. What is that called?
gallery-deer.why: That pogo stick bounce is stotting, a mule deer habit. White tails gallop with the tail up.

gallery-deer.q: Which deer does the law treat as a mule deer?
gallery-deer.why: The synopsis definitions say Mule (Black tailed) Deer. The 4 point rule applies to black tailed bucks too.

gallery-waterfowl.q: A brown hen duck shows a white square on the back of the wing. Mallard or gadwall?
gallery-waterfowl.why: Gadwall is the only puddle duck with a white speculum. A mallard hen shows a blue purple patch edged in white.

gallery-waterfowl.q: A diving duck has a white face patch shaped like a crescent, not a round spot. Which goldeneye?
gallery-waterfowl.why: Barrow's drake has a crescent. Common goldeneye drake has a round spot.

gallery-waterfowl.q: How many goldeneyes may be in your daily duck bag?
gallery-waterfowl.why: Page 12: not more than 2 goldeneyes, Barrow's and common in aggregate, inside the bag of 8.

gallery-waterfowl.q: A big all white bird with no black wing tips flies over. What should you do?
options: Shoot, it is a snow goose
Do not shoot. It is likely a swan
Shoot only if it is alone
gallery-waterfowl.why: Snow and Ross's geese have black wing tips. All white and bigger than a goose means swan. Do not shoot.

gallery-waterfowl.q: A duck runs across the water before it lifts off. What kind of duck is it?
gallery-waterfowl.why: Divers patter along the surface to take off. Puddle ducks jump straight up.

gallery-upland.q: A grouse flushes from aspen with a long fan tail and a wide dark band near the tip. What is it?
gallery-upland.why: The banded fan tail in aspen and birch is the ruffed grouse mark, in both grey and red phases.

gallery-upland.q: A small white ptarmigan in winter has black tail feathers. Which one is it NOT?
gallery-upland.why: The white tailed ptarmigan has a white tail all year. Willow and rock ptarmigan have black tails.

gallery-upland.q: A quail has a straight plume and broad white bars on red sides. May you shoot it?
options: Yes, it is a California quail
No. It is a mountain quail, no open season
gallery-upland.why: California quail have a curled teardrop plume. Mountain quail have a straight plume, and the synopsis says no open season on mountain quail.

gallery-upland.q: A big grouse displays with a spiky fanned tail and a white chest. What should you do?
options: Shoot it, it is a sharp tail
Do not shoot: it is a sage grouse, no season in BC
gallery-upland.why: That is a greater sage grouse. No season row exists in the synopsis, so it has no open season.

gallery-big-game.q: A brown bear in a berry patch has no shoulder hump, a straight face and tall ears. What is it?
options: Black bear in a brown colour phase
gallery-big-game.why: Shape, not colour. No hump, straight face and tall ears mean black bear. Black bears can be brown, cinnamon or blonde.

gallery-big-game.q: Which mark is the elk signature from behind?
options: White tail with a black tip
gallery-big-game.why: Elk show a large pale straw coloured rump patch, framed by darker legs.

gallery-big-game.q: A lone black bear walks out. Two minutes later a small bear follows. What does the law say?
options: Neither: no hunting a bear under 2 or any bear in its company
gallery-big-game.why: Page 11, item 14: it is unlawful to hunt a black bear less than 2 years old or any bear in its company.

gallery-big-game.q: White animal on a cliff with short black horns. Sheep or goat?
gallery-big-game.why: Mountain goats have short black dagger horns. Sheep horns are amber or brown.

gallery-big-game.q: A canid has tall pointed ears and a narrow pointed muzzle. Coyote or wolf?
gallery-big-game.why: Coyotes have a slim pointed muzzle and tall ears. Wolves have a broad muzzle and shorter, rounder ears.

shooting-skills.why: Prone has both elbows and your whole body on the ground. Hunter education ranks it steadiest, then sitting, then kneeling, then standing.

shooting-skills.q: How much breath do you hold for the shot?
shooting-skills.why: Draw a deep breath, let about half out, hold while you squeeze. Held too long, your pulse moves the rifle: start over.

shooting-skills.q: What goes in the chamber for dry fire on the Tikka?
shooting-skills.why: The Tikka manual says long term dry firing may damage the bolt and tells you to use a snap cap with a spring loaded primer.

shooting-skills.q: You pass the 20 cm test at 150 m but miss one shot at 200 m. Your max ethical range?
shooting-skills.why: The last distance where all 3 cold shots hit is your max. One miss and you go back to the previous distance.

ballistics-308.q: 100 m zero, 150 gr Power Shok. About how low is the bullet at 200 m?
ballistics-308.why: Federal's table gives 3.9 in low at 200 yd. Read at 200 m that is about 12 cm. At 300 m it is about 47 cm.

ballistics-308.q: A 20 km/h full crosswind at 250 m moves the 150 gr bullet about how far?
ballistics-308.why: About 27 cm, more than a deer's vital zone. That is why the lean is no shots past 200 m in a real wind.

options: The range where the bullet stops
The farthest distance you can hold centre of the vitals and still hit them
ballistics-308.why: Maximum point blank range: hold dead centre from the muzzle out to that distance and the bullet stays inside the vital zone.

ballistics-308.q: Your 20 inch barrel versus the 24 inch test barrel: roughly?
options: About 3% slower, 1 to 3 cm more drop by 300 m
ballistics-308.why: Rifleshooter measured about 70 to 105 fps lost between 24 and 20 inches. That is about 3%, a small change in drop.

ballistics-308.q: Does the 150 gr load have 1,000 ft lb at 300 m?
ballistics-308.why: Federal lists 1,341 ft lb at 300 yd. The rule of thumb is not your limit inside 300 m. Placement and your range test are.

shot-placement.q: A deer stands broadside. Where is the spot?
options: Straight up the back of the front leg, one third up the chest
shot-placement.why: That line and height puts the bullet through both lungs and the top of the heart. Hunter education teaches it for deer, elk, moose and bear.

shot-placement.q: Deer quartering away. Where do you aim?
options: Behind the near shoulder, same as broadside
Farther back, so the bullet exits the far shoulder
shot-placement.why: Picture the far front leg and aim on the near side at the spot that sends the bullet there. Aiming at the near crease can clip one lung.

shot-placement.q: What is wrong with the Texas heart shot?
options: No vitals in reach, guts and hams in the way, ruins meat
It is only illegal in Texas
shot-placement.why: A shot at a walking away animal goes through paunch and hindquarters first. Hunter Ed says never take it.

shot-placement.q: Black bear broadside, near leg forward. Where is the spot?
options: Halfway up the body, tight behind the shoulder, through both lungs
High on the shoulder to break it down
shot-placement.why: The heart sits low and the lungs reach well back. Shoulder and head shots are not recommended: heavy bone, sloped skull, lost bears.

shot-placement.q: Dark red blood, no bubbles, the deer hunched and trotted off. What now?
options: Mark the spot, back out, wait hours
shot-placement.why: That is a liver hit. The deer will bed and die if not pushed. Every source says hours; how many differs (2 to 10 hours, your call: see Blood trailing). Pushed early, it can go a long way.

shotgun-skills.q: Which lead method does hunter education teach beginners first?
shotgun-skills.why: Swing through: start behind, swing faster than the bird, fire as the muzzle passes its head, keep swinging.

shotgun-skills.q: You lift your head to watch the duck fall. Where did the shot go?
shotgun-skills.why: Your eye is the rear sight. Lifting it is like raising a rifle's rear sight. You shoot high.

shotgun-skills.q: Why is 40 yd the edge for steel on ducks?
options: Pattern density runs out: you need about 100 pellets in a 30 in circle for a big duck
shotgun-skills.why: Steel pellets have energy past 40 yd, but the pattern thins. Without enough pellets in the circle you cripple birds.

shotgun-skills.q: Roughly how much lead for a duck crossing at 30 m?
shotgun-skills.why: The shot takes about a tenth of a second to get there and a duck covers 1.4 m in that time at 50 km/h. Let the swing make the lead.

blood-trailing.q: Dark red blood, no bubbles, the deer walked off hunched. What now?
options: Follow right away before it gets far
Back out and wait hours, much longer than for a lung hit
Fire a shot in the air to make it run
blood-trailing.why: Dark blood with no bubbles points to the liver, and a hunched walk points to the paunch. Every source says wait hours; how many differs (2 to 12 hours, your call). Pushed, they run for kilometres.

blood-trailing.q: Light is gone and the trail leads into timber. You take the rifle and a headlamp to finish the track. Legal?
options: No. Following wildlife with a firearm is hunting, and hunting after hours or with a light is unlawful
Yes if you do not shoot
blood-trailing.why: The synopsis defines hunting to include following the trail of wildlife while in possession of a firearm. Hours and the light rule then apply.

blood-trailing.q: The blood crosses a fence with a No Trespassing sign. What is the right move?
options: Cross quietly, it is only for a few minutes
Stop, find the owner and ask, or call a conservation officer
Shoot from your side if you see it
blood-trailing.why: Enclosed land is presumed off limits without consent. There is no tracking exception in the Trespass Act.

blood-trailing.q: You lose the blood trail. First step?
options: Walk straight ahead in the direction it was going
Return to the last flagged blood and circle out from there
Give up and come back next weekend
blood-trailing.why: Last blood is your anchor. Circles at 20 m and 40 m, then lanes 10 m apart. Walking ahead tramples the sign.

tagging-legal.q: When must the species licence be cancelled?
options: Before you leave the kill site
Immediately after the kill and before handling the animal
When you get to the truck
tagging-legal.why: The synopsis says immediately after the kill and before handling the big game killed, following the instructions on the licence.

tagging-legal.q: A buck is down in Region 3 in October. What must stay attached as evidence of sex?
options: The unskinned tail and a testicle or part of the penis
tagging-legal.why: For deer the rule is the unskinned tail AND a testicle or part of the penis. Antlers are not a substitute.

tagging-legal.q: Do you have to report a Region 3 mule deer kill to the province?
options: No. Deer are not on the inspection or compulsory reporting lists
tagging-legal.why: Compulsory inspection covers goat, sheep, caribou, cougar and Haida Gwaii bears. Compulsory reporting covers lynx, wolverine, bobcat, wolf and feral pig. Deer are on neither list.

tagging-legal.q: Your brother takes your deer to the butcher without you. What travels with it?
options: Your Record of Receipt, and you keep a part with the evidence of sex
tagging-legal.why: Anyone transporting wildlife another person killed needs a Record of Receipt, and the hunter keeps a portion with the sex parts attached.

tagging-legal.q: You bought a moose licence but never went. What do you owe by March 31?
tagging-legal.why: All individuals who purchase an elk, moose or caribou species licence must submit a report by March 31, hunt or no hunt.

field-dressing.q: Gutless method on a deer. The hind quarters are off. What must you still take out?
options: Nothing, the quarters are the meat
Backstraps, tenderloins, neck and rib meat
field-dressing.why: BC edible portions are the neck, ribs, four quarters and the loins. The loins include backstraps and tenderloins. All must come out.

field-dressing.q: Why do you open the belly with the blade edge up and two fingers inside?
options: The fingers lift the skin away from the paunch so the blade cannot cut the stomach
field-dressing.why: A punctured stomach puts gut contents on the meat. Fingers under the skin guide the blade and keep the guts away from the edge.

field-dressing.q: Gut contents got on a hind quarter. What now?
options: Wash that spot with clean water and dry it immediately
field-dressing.why: Alaska Fish and Game: wash the contaminated area and dry it at once. Otherwise do not wash, the blood glaze slows bacteria.

field-dressing.q: It is a cold evening. Can you leave a gutless carcass with the guts in overnight?
options: Yes, below zero the meat is safe
No. The gut cavity holds heat and the meat spoils regardless of air temperature
field-dressing.why: Alaska Fish and Game says do not use the gutless method if the animal will sit overnight. Gut it instead.

meat-care.q: Target temperature for the carcass, and how soon?
options: Below 4°C as fast as possible, ideally in a cooler the same day
meat-care.why: Washington Fish and Wildlife: cool game to under 40°F (4°C) as quickly as possible, ideally in a cooler on the day of the kill.

meat-care.q: Which deer should you not age?
options: A mature buck chilled fast in cold weather
A doe shot on a warm day and trailed for hours
Any deer with the hide on
meat-care.why: Warm weather without rapid chilling, hard running, long trailing, heavy damage and dirt all mean spoilage, not aging.

meat-care.q: Is a bear roast safe after three weeks in the freezer?
options: No. Wild Trichinella resists freezing. Cook bear to at least 71°C
Yes if it was salted first
meat-care.why: The Canadian Food Inspection Agency says most Trichinella in wildlife resist freezing and curing, drying and smoking are not reliable. Cook to 71°C.

meat-care.q: It is raining on your hanging quarters. Best fix?
options: Wrap each quarter in a garbage bag
A tarp above as a roof with an air gap, meat in game bags
Lay them on the ground under a tree
meat-care.why: Moisture and trapped heat spoil meat. A roof keeps the rain off while air still moves. Plastic traps heat and sweat.

packing-out.q: The deer is down inside an ATV for Hunting Closed Area. Can you ride in to fetch it?
options: No. Using a motor vehicle to transport wildlife is banned there
Yes if you unload the rifle
packing-out.why: A Motor Vehicle for Hunting Closed Area bans using a motor vehicle to hunt, to transport wildlife, or to carry hunters or hunting gear. Pack it out on foot.

packing-out.q: Which parts of a moose may legally stay on the mountain?
options: The ribs and neck if the pack is heavy
Bones, hide, head and guts, as long as neck, ribs, four quarters and loins come out
packing-out.why: Edible portions are the neck, ribs, four quarters and loins. Boning out is fine. Bones and guts can stay or go to a landfill.

packing-out.q: What do you need to ride an ATV on a Forest Service Road?
options: A valid driver's licence and at least $200,000 third party liability insurance, plus registration and a helmet
packing-out.why: The synopsis quotes the ORV rules: driver's licence and $200,000 liability insurance on an FSR, mandatory registration, helmet on ride astride ORVs.

packing-out.q: Roughly how much boneless meat from an average field dressed deer?
options: About 48%, so 24 kg from a 49 kg deer
packing-out.why: Ohio Department of Natural Resources weighed 115 deer: average 49 kg field dressed gave 24 kg of venison, a 48% yield.

cwd.q: You shoot a mule deer near Heffley Creek. Must you submit it for CWD testing?
options: Yes, it is mandatory everywhere in BC
No, Region 3 is outside the zone, but the province asks you to and it is free
cwd.why: Mandatory testing applies in MUs 4-1 to 4-8 and 4-20 to 4-25. Elsewhere it is voluntary and encouraged.

cwd.q: What can you bring back to BC from an Alberta deer?
options: The whole deer in the truck
Meat of the quarters, loins, neck and ribs, plus hide, antlers and skull plate cleaned of all tissue
cwd.why: Synopsis number 50: only edible meat of the four quarters, loins, neck and ribs, or hide, antlers and skull plate cleaned of all tissue.

cwd.q: How much neck stays on a head for testing?
options: At least three inches, about 8 cm, to keep the throat tissues
cwd.why: The lymph nodes and tonsils at the back of the throat are the test tissue. Three inches of neck keeps them.

cwd.q: Does cooking make meat from a CWD positive animal safe?
options: No. Cooking does not destroy prions. Health Canada says do not eat it
cwd.why: BC Centre for Disease Control: cooking temperatures cannot destroy the prion. The advice is not to eat meat from an infected animal.

butchering.q: What must a butcher record when you drop off a deer?
options: Your FWID, species licence number, species, sex and the MU it came from
butchering.why: Meat cutters must record the species, sex and MU, and your receipt must show your FWID, licence number, species and sex.

butchering.q: Which cut should never go into the grinder?
butchering.why: The backstraps are the loins, the tenderest big muscles on the deer. Shank and neck are the classic grind and braise cuts.

butchering.q: At minus 18°C, how long does well wrapped venison keep its quality?
butchering.why: Penn State Extension: properly handled game stored at 0°F (minus 18°C) lasts up to a year or so.

butchering.q: What is the main source of a waxy, strong taste in venison burger?
options: Deer fat and silver skin left in the grind
butchering.why: Venison fat is waxy and goes rancid. Trim it and the silver skin before grinding.

cooking.q: Minimum safe internal temperature for bear meat?
options: At least 71°C in every part of the cut
Any temperature if it was frozen for a month
cooking.why: The Canadian Food Inspection Agency: all wild game to at least 71°C. Freezing, curing, drying and smoking do not reliably kill wild Trichinella.

cooking.q: Which cut is wasted if you braise it for 3 hours?
cooking.why: Backstrap is lean and tender. It wants a hot pan and a short time. Shank and neck want the long braise.

cooking.q: You breast out a mallard at the truck. What must stay with the breasts until home?
options: One fully feathered wing or the feathered head
cooking.why: Migratory birds in possession or transport must keep one feathered wing or the feathered head attached.

cooking.q: Most common cause of strong gamey flavour?
options: Slow dressing, poor cooling and fat left on
cooking.why: North Dakota State University: inadequate bleeding, delayed or careless dressing and slow cooling. Trim the fat too.

trophy-care.q: Where does the ring cut go for a shoulder mount?
options: Right at the base of the neck
Well behind the front shoulders, leaving 20 to 30 cm of hide
trophy-care.why: The taxidermist needs the whole neck, both shoulders, the brisket and extra hide behind the shoulder in one piece.

trophy-care.q: A 4 point buck from the November season. Can you saw a tine off for the pack?
options: No. Antlers from a restricted season must stay naturally attached and untampered until the carcass is home and butchered or inspected
Yes if you keep the piece
trophy-care.why: Tampering with antlers from an antler restricted season is unlawful until the carcass reaches a meat cutter, cold storage, home butchering or inspection.

trophy-care.q: What must you give a taxidermist with the head?
options: FWID, species licence number, species, sex and date of kill
trophy-care.why: Taxidermists are required by the Wildlife Act to record these details. Without them the animal can be seized.

trophy-care.q: Best way to whiten a cleaned skull?
options: Leave it in the sun for a month
trophy-care.why: Bleach weakens bone and keeps flaking. Peroxide whitens gently. Sun bleaches antlers too.

bc-calendar.q: When do BC hunting and species licences expire?
bc-calendar.why: The synopsis fee page says all hunting and species licences expire March 31 of each year. The licence year is 1 April to 31 March.

bc-calendar.q: What was the 2026 main LEH draw deadline?
bc-calendar.why: The LEH synopsis cover reads: applications must be submitted by 11:59 pm Tuesday, June 23, 2026.

bc-calendar.q: In Region 3, when can you shoot any mule deer buck, not just a 4 point?
bc-calendar.why: The Region 3 table shows Bucks for Oct 1 to Oct 31. September and November to December are 4 point bucks only.

bc-calendar.q: Who must file a Mandatory Hunter Report by 31 March?
options: Anyone who bought an elk, moose or caribou species licence
bc-calendar.why: Page 16 of the synopsis: all individuals who purchase an elk, moose or caribou species licence must report by March 31, whether or not they hunted.

bc-calendar.q: How do you find out if you won an LEH authorization?
options: A letter comes in the mail
Log in to WILD and check your FWID profile
bc-calendar.why: LEH results are not mailed. Authorizations are posted to your profile in WILD. An email notice is a courtesy, not the authorization.

leh-strategy.q: A hunt shows odds of 22.4:1. What does that number mean?
options: About 22 first choice applicants per authorization last year
leh-strategy.why: The LEH synopsis says the odds are a measure of the number of people who applied for each authorization available in the previous year. They are a guide, not a guarantee.

leh-strategy.q: You drew an antlerless mule deer tag last year. Your odds this year?
options: Unchanged. Deer has no enhanced odds penalty
leh-strategy.why: Enhanced odds apply to all species except deer, black bear and turkey.

leh-strategy.q: You and your brother apply as a shared group of two for moose and win. How many moose may the group take?
leh-strategy.why: A shared group of two is authorized to take one moose. A group of three or four may take two.

leh-strategy.q: What is the LEH application fee in the 2026 to 2027 synopsis?
leh-strategy.why: The synopsis states the fee is $6.30 including taxes and is not refundable. $15.75 is the Special Mountain Sheep draw fee.

leh-strategy.q: Which hunts can be applied for as a regular group?
options: Not elk in Regions 1 and 2, moose, bison or black bear
leh-strategy.why: Group hunt applications cannot be submitted for elk in Regions 1 and 2, moose, bison, or black bear. Moose and bison use shared hunts instead.

top-areas.q: Which Region 3 MU had the largest average mule deer harvest, 2020 to 2024?
top-areas.why: MU 3-30, the Cache Creek and Clinton country, averaged about 502 resident mule deer a year from about 2,050 hunters. 3-27 and 3-19 tied for second at about 327.

top-areas.q: Where do the harvest numbers in this session come from?
options: The BC Hunter Sample Survey, published on the BC Data Catalogue
top-areas.why: Resident harvest and effort are estimated from the annual Hunter Sample Survey and published by the province. They are estimates with error ranges.

top-areas.q: You want to ride an ATV to hunt deer in MU 3-29 in October. Allowed?
options: No. ATVs for hunting are closed in 3-28, 3-29, 3-30 and part of 3-17 from 1 September to 10 December
top-areas.why: The Region 3 access list closes ATVs for hunting in those MUs during the main deer seasons.

top-areas.q: Which Region 8 MU carries nearly all the quail harvest?
top-areas.why: MU 8-1 averaged about 249 quail a year from 39 hunters. Every other MU reported a handful of birds.

top-areas.q: What is the MU for Mission and Stave Lake?
top-areas.why: Point checks on the official MU layer put Mission, Stave Lake and Deroche in MU 2-8. Harrison Mills is 2-18 and Delta is 2-4.

etiquette.q: You find a ranch gate open on a Crown land road. What do you do?
options: Close it to keep cattle in
Leave it open, as you found it
etiquette.why: The Region 3 notice and the ethics code both say leave gates and fences as they are found. Open stays open, shut stays shut.

etiquette.q: A friend wants to buy a package of your deer meat. Legal?
options: No. Trafficking in wildlife meat is an offence
Yes with a Record of Receipt
etiquette.why: It is unlawful to traffic in wildlife meat or offer to. Give it away, with a Record of Receipt if it travels without you.

etiquette.q: You posted a buck photo with the FSR kilometre sign in the frame. Problem?
options: Yes. You just gave away the spot and invited pressure on the landowner and the road
etiquette.why: Opinion, but hard earned: a spot shared online is a spot lost. The ethics code also asks you not to display kills where it may offend.

etiquette.q: What does an ATV rider need to ride a Forest Service Road?
options: A valid driver's licence and $200,000 third party liability insurance, plus registration
etiquette.why: Page 9 of the synopsis: on a Forest Service Road, ATV operators must hold a valid driver's licence and carry a minimum of $200,000 third party liability insurance. ORVs must be registered.

indigenous-respect.q: Whose territory is Kamloops and Heffley Creek on?
indigenous-respect.why: The City of Kamloops and TRU both place the city on Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc territory within the unceded lands of the Secwépemc Nation.

indigenous-respect.q: You want to cut across reserve land to reach Crown land behind it. What do you need?
options: Nothing, you are not hunting on it
Permission from the band office, because reserves are private land
A note from a conservation officer
indigenous-respect.why: The synopsis says Indian Reserves are private land and permission must be obtained to hunt on or across these lands.

indigenous-respect.q: What did section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982 do?
options: Recognized and affirmed existing Aboriginal and treaty rights
Banned Indigenous hunting out of season
indigenous-respect.why: Section 35(1) reads: the existing aboriginal and treaty rights of the aboriginal peoples of Canada are hereby recognized and affirmed.

indigenous-respect.q: In the Sparrow case, what comes first when a resource is limited?
options: Conservation, then Indigenous food, social and ceremonial harvest
indigenous-respect.why: The Court said subsistence fishing by Aboriginal people should be given priority after conservation requirements.

indigenous-respect.q: How is Stó:lō pronounced, per the BC guide?
indigenous-respect.why: The 2018 BC pronunciation guide gives staw-low. The community is the final authority.

landowner-permission.q: A fenced field with no signs. Can you hunt it without asking?
options: No. A lawful fence makes it enclosed land and you are presumed to have no consent
Only if it is not cultivated
landowner-permission.why: Enclosed land includes land surrounded by a lawful fence. A person found on enclosed land is presumed not to have consent.

landowner-permission.q: Crown land under a grazing lease, cattle grazing on it. Hunt?
options: Only with the consent of the lessee or occupant
landowner-permission.why: The Wildlife Act bars hunting on leased Crown land while it is occupied by livestock without the consent of the owner, lessee or occupant.

landowner-permission.q: The rancher said yes last October. This October?
options: Ask again. Permission once does not carry over unless they said so
landowner-permission.why: The synopsis ethics code: unless explicitly stated, permission granted once does not entitle you to access the property on subsequent occasions.

landowner-permission.q: An occupier asks your name and address while you are on their land. You refuse. Problem?
options: Yes, refusing is an offence under the Trespass Act
landowner-permission.why: The Trespass Act requires a person reasonably believed to be trespassing to give their correct name and address on demand of the occupier.

grandpas-rules.q: Which of these is actually law, not just Grandpa's wisdom?
options: Glass twice as long as you think you need to
Cancel your species licence before you handle the deer
grandpas-rules.why: Page 11, item 1: any person who kills big game must immediately after the kill and before handling it cancel the species licence. The other two are opinion.

grandpas-rules.q: A deer is hit and runs into thick timber. Grandpa's rule 37 says?
options: Chase it before it gets away
Wait 20 minutes, longer on a gut shot
grandpas-rules.why: A pushed deer runs. A deer left alone lies down. Waiting is wisdom; making every reasonable effort to retrieve it is also law.

grandpas-rules.q: Rule 46 says share the meat, never sell it. Why never?
options: Trafficking in wildlife meat is an offence under the Wildlife Act
grandpas-rules.why: Page 11, item 7: it is unlawful to traffic in wildlife meat or offer to do so, except as authorized by permit.

hunt-journal-guide.q: You hunted all morning and saw nothing. Do you log it?
options: Yes. Blank days show where deer are not
Only if you fired a shot
hunt-journal-guide.why: Blank days are data. Over a season they show which spots are dead and which are worth the drive.

hunt-journal-guide.q: What does 'west wind' mean in your journal?
hunt-journal-guide.why: Winds are named for where they come from. A west wind blows from west to east.

hunt-journal-guide.q: You bought a moose species licence. By when must you file the Mandatory Hunter Report?
options: Only if you killed a moose
hunt-journal-guide.why: Synopsis page 16: anyone who buys an elk, moose or caribou species licence reports by 31 March, hunt or no hunt.

options: Only on your phone. Export CSV to back it up
hunt-journal-guide.why: Hunt Mentor keeps your data in local storage on the phone. Export CSV after trips so a lost phone does not lose your seasons.

mastery-levels.q: Are these mastery levels a BC rank?
options: No. They are Hunt Mentor's opinion
mastery-levels.why: The ladder is a learning aid. BC gives no such ranks. Only the legal lines cite the synopsis.

mastery-levels.q: To supervise an initiation licence hunter, how many prior licence years do you need?
options: At least 3 of the licence years before this one
mastery-levels.why: Synopsis page 6: the supervisor must have held a hunting licence in not fewer than 3 of the preceding licence years, plus other conditions.

mastery-levels.q: A friend offers you $200 to take him deer hunting. Can you?
options: Yes, if you are a good hunter
No. Guiding for compensation needs a guide licence
Yes, if you split the meat
mastery-levels.why: Synopsis page 11: acting as a guide for compensation or reward without a licence is unlawful.

mastery-levels.q: When should you tick a checklist box?
options: After doing it in the field
mastery-levels.why: The ladder is about field skill. Reading is the start, not the tick.

mentoring.q: Your 25 year old friend never held a BC hunting licence and has no CORE. Can he hunt this fall?
options: Yes, on an initiation licence, supervised at all times
Yes, alone on an initiation licence
mentoring.why: Page 6: a resident 18 or older who never held a BC licence can get a once in a lifetime initiation licence, no training needed, but must be supervised at all times.

mentoring.q: Your friend shoots a deer on an initiation licence. Whose bag limit is it?
mentoring.why: Page 6: wildlife taken under an initiation or youth licence counts in the supervising adult's bag limit.

mentoring.q: What must happen before each day of initiation hunting?
options: The supervisor signs the supervision form
mentoring.why: Page 6: the supervising hunter signs a form acknowledging the conditions, before starting to hunt each day.

mentoring.q: How many initiation licence hunters can one supervisor take at once?
mentoring.why: Page 6: no more than two youth, two initiation, or one of each at one time.

mentoring.q: Youngest age to hunt in BC?
mentoring.why: Page 6: no one under 10 may hunt, and allowing it is an offence.

local-heffley.q: It is 20 October. You are in MU 3-28 across the river from Heffley Creek. Can you use the ATV to get to a glassing spot and hunt?
options: No. ATVs for hunting are closed in 3-28, 3-29 and 3-30 from 1 Sept to 10 Dec
local-heffley.why: Synopsis page 33: ATV for Hunting Closed Areas from Sept 1 to Dec 10 in MUs 3-28, 3-29, 3-30 and part of 3-17. Walk or use the truck on open roads.

local-heffley.q: A forkhorn mule deer buck steps out on 3 November in MU 3-27. Legal?
options: Yes, bucks are open to 10 December
No. From 1 November a mule deer buck needs 4 points on one antler
local-heffley.why: The any buck season ends 31 October. November 1 to December 10 is 4 point bucks only in 3-12 to 3-20 and 3-26 to 3-44.

local-heffley.q: Where can you legally shoot ducks near Kamloops without asking anyone?
options: Tranquille marsh at the head of Kamloops Lake
Lac du Bois grassland ponds north of the city boundary
local-heffley.why: Tranquille and McQueen are No Shooting areas. BC Parks says hunting is permitted in Lac du Bois outside the City of Kamloops boundary.

local-heffley.q: What does the City of Kamloops bylaw allow for hunters inside city limits?
options: Nothing. No person shall discharge a firearm within City boundaries, and there is no hunting exemption
local-heffley.why: Bylaw No. 24-49 bans discharge inside the city. The exemptions are peace officers, farmers protecting crops or destroying predators on their own land, the airport, school archery and permit holders.

local-heffley.q: You shoot a deer in MU 3-20. What extra step does Region 3 ask for?
options: Submit the head for bovine tuberculosis testing
A 48 hour report to the CO
local-heffley.why: Synopsis page 32 asks hunters to submit deer, elk and moose heads from MUs 3-12, 3-19 and 3-20 for bovine tuberculosis testing.

local-mission.q: You want to shoot ducks on the Fraser bar below Silverdale, inside Mission. What do you need beyond the usual licences?
options: The Fraser Valley Special Area Hunting Licence and $1,000,000 liability insurance
local-mission.why: Map B10: hunting in the Mission portion of MU 2-8 requires the special licence and the insurance. The bylaw also limits you to a shotgun with shot there.

local-mission.q: A doe black tail stands in a cutblock north of Stave Lake on 25 October. Legal?
options: Yes, bag limit is 2 with one antlerless
No. The general season in 2-8 is bucks only
local-mission.why: Page 28: mule (black tailed) deer in 2-8 is Bucks Sept 10 to Dec 15. Antlerless needs a draw or a listed special season.

local-mission.q: Where in Mission may you fire a rifle while hunting?
options: Only in bylaw Area D, west of Stave Lake and north of Cannell Lake
local-mission.why: Bylaw section 11(c): rifle or shotgun only in Area D. Area B is shot only, Area C is shotgun with shot or slug.

local-mission.q: The Chehalis Fleetwood FSR is inside a No Shooting Area. Can you hunt grouse along it?
options: Yes. Map B33 says discharge of firearms for the purpose of hunting is permitted
local-mission.why: These 400 m road closures stop plinking, not lawful hunting.

local-okanagan.q: How many quail may each of you carry home from a 2 day trip?
options: Up to 30 each in possession, no more than 10 taken per day
local-okanagan.why: Region 8 quail: 10 (30). Daily bag 10, possession 30, per hunter.

local-okanagan.q: The Osoyoos Oxbows sign says No Shooting or Hunting. It is 25 October. What applies?
options: The closure runs 1 March to 30 September, so hunting is open, but vehicles stay on established roads
local-okanagan.why: Map J1: no shooting or hunting from Mar 1 to Sept 30 in the restricted area. Motor vehicles are restricted to the established roads all year.

local-okanagan.q: Can you use your .22 rifle on a quail that holds tight?
options: Yes, rimfire is fine for small game
No. Rimfire is for grouse, ptarmigan or turkey only. Quail is shotgun, air gun or bow
local-okanagan.why: Page 13 legal methods: rimfire note 2 says grouse, ptarmigan or turkey only.

local-okanagan.q: You are inside Vernon city limits on a friend's acreage. Can you shoot quail there?
options: No. Vernon Bylaw 5399 bans discharging a firearm within the city, with no hunting exemption
local-okanagan.why: The bylaw exempts only bylaw officers and farmers protecting crops or livestock.

trip-yukon.q: You and your brother want a Yukon moose. What is the cheapest legal route?
options: Buy big game licences and go
A Yukon resident friend wins a special guide licence and guides you for free
Hire a BC guide to come along
trip-yukon.why: Non resident Canadians must be guided by a registered Yukon outfitter or a Yukon resident holding a special guide licence. The special guide may not be paid.

trip-yukon.q: Can you hunt mule deer in Yukon with an outfitter?
options: No, deer and elk are for Yukon residents only
trip-yukon.why: Yukon limits deer and elk hunting to Yukon residents.

trip-yukon.q: You shot 30 kg of grouse and ptarmigan meat. Any paperwork to leave Yukon?
options: Ask for a wildlife export permit at an Environment office
trip-yukon.why: Yukon requires a wildlife export permit before wildlife parts leave the territory. The permit is free. The 20 kg exception is written for processed big game meat, so ask.

trip-alberta.q: You and your brother want to shoot ducks near Brooks. Who must come along?
options: Nobody. Game birds need no host or outfitter
trip-alberta.why: Alberta's host or outfitter rule applies to big game, wolf and coyote. Game birds are not on the list.

trip-alberta.q: What does your Alberta friend need before hosting you on a deer hunt?
options: A WIN card and a Hunter Host Licence
trip-alberta.why: A hunter host must be an adult Alberta resident with a WIN card and a Hunter Host Licence, and may host at most 2 hunters a year.

trip-alberta.q: Which deer parts may cross into BC from Alberta?
options: Whole carcass if under 24 hours old
Meat of the four quarters, loins, neck and ribs, plus hide, antlers and skull plate cleaned of all tissue
Anything if the head was tested
trip-alberta.why: BC Synopsis page 12, item 50. The brain and spine stay in Alberta.

trip-saskatchewan.q: A BC resident wants a Saskatchewan white tailed deer licence. How?
options: Buy it over the counter from August 1
Enter the Canadian Resident draw by the last Thursday in May, buy the licence if drawn
Book an outfitter, it is the only way
trip-saskatchewan.why: Saskatchewan residents buy over the counter. Canadian residents enter the draw in May and buy from August 1 if successful.

trip-saskatchewan.q: What must you wear to hunt deer with a rifle in Saskatchewan?
options: A vest of scarlet, bright yellow, blaze orange or white, or a CSA class 2 or 3 garment
trip-saskatchewan.why: The summary requires a high visibility vest in those colours when hunting big game with a rifle.

trip-saskatchewan.q: Which of these is legal to carry into BC from your Saskatchewan buck?
options: The whole head for a mount
Boned out meat and a skull plate cleaned of all tissue
trip-saskatchewan.why: BC Synopsis page 12, item 50 allows only the edible meat of four quarters, loins, neck and ribs, plus hide, antlers and skull plate cleaned of all tissue.

trip-manitoba.q: Does a BC resident need an outfitter to hunt white tailed deer in Manitoba?
options: No. The guide rule is for non Canadian residents. Canadian residents buy a deer licence for listed GHAs
trip-manitoba.why: Manitoba's outfitter and guide requirement applies to non Canadian residents. Canadian residents may buy a Canadian resident deer licence valid in listed Game Hunting Areas.

trip-manitoba.q: What orange does Manitoba require for a deer hunter?
options: A completely orange head covering plus 2,580 square cm of hunter orange above the waist, visible from all sides
trip-manitoba.why: General Hunting Regulation M.R. 351/87 requires both the orange head covering and 2,580 square cm of hunter orange above the waist.

trip-manitoba.q: Your brother carries no rifle and just helps drag. Does he need orange?
options: Yes. The rule covers anyone accompanying a big game hunter or retrieving game
trip-manitoba.why: The regulation names anyone who hunts, dresses or retrieves big game, or guides or otherwise accompanies such a person.

trip-alaska.q: You are a Canadian citizen living in BC. Can you hunt Alaska black bear with just your brother?
options: Yes, black bear needs no guide
No. Nonresident aliens need an Alaska licensed guide for every big game animal
Yes if you have a locking tag
trip-alaska.why: The guide rule for US nonresidents covers only brown bear, sheep and goat. For nonresident aliens it covers all big game, black bear included.

trip-alaska.q: What is the first step to get your rifle into Alaska?
options: Show your PAL at the US border
Buy the Alaska hunting licence, then file ATF Form 6NIA weeks ahead
Mail the rifle to the guide
trip-alaska.why: ATF needs a copy of a valid US state hunting licence with the 6NIA application, and processing takes about 4 to 6 weeks.

trip-alaska.q: Which Alaska caribou parts can you drive home to Heffley Creek?
options: Whole head and cape for the taxidermist
Boned out meat and a skull plate with antlers cleaned of all tissue
Anything, CWD is not in Alaska
trip-alaska.why: BC Synopsis page 12 item 50 applies to any cervid killed outside BC. Yukon has a matching import ban on the drive through.

named-areas.q: Which named place near Kamloops is closed to shooting?
options: Tranquille Wildlife Management Area at the head of Kamloops Lake
named-areas.why: Synopsis Map C17 marks Tranquille as No Shooting. The BC Parks pages for Bonaparte and Tunkwa say firearms are permitted for hunting in open season.

named-areas.q: On which days may you hunt ducks in the marked parts of Pitt Addington Marsh Wildlife Management Area?
options: Saturdays, Sundays and Wednesdays in the general waterfowl season
named-areas.why: The Fraser Valley Special Area brochure allows waterfowl hunting only on those three days, only in the marked parts, with blinds removed each day.

named-areas.q: Why are the quiet spots not on this list?
options: A public name brings hunters. Quiet spots come from the map's candidate spots and your own scouting
named-areas.why: Everything here is named in public sources, so expect company. The candidate spots are built from land status, roads, closures and habitat.

named-areas.q: It is 20 October. Can you hunt quail in the Osoyoos Oxbows?
options: No, it is closed all year
Yes, the no hunting period is 1 March to 30 September; vehicles stay on established roads
named-areas.why: Map J1 on synopsis page 69 closes shooting and hunting from 1 March to 30 September and limits vehicles to established roads. Town bylaws and private land still apply.

named-areas.q: How long may you camp in one spot on Crown land?
options: Up to 14 consecutive days, then be gone 72 hours to reset
named-areas.why: The Crown land Permission policy allows up to 14 consecutive calendar days; the count resets only after 72 hours away with your vehicle and gear.

local-harrison-deer.q: 20 November, MU 2-19 west of Harrison Lake. A black tailed doe steps out at 60 m. Legal?
options: Yes, the Region 2 limit allows 1 antlerless
No. The 2-19 general season is bucks only
Yes, if your brother cancels his licence
local-harrison-deer.why: Page 28: 2-19 is in the Bucks row, 10 September to 15 December. The page 27 limit of 2 with 1 antlerless is a ceiling, not a season. And only the shooter cancels a licence.

local-harrison-deer.q: Sunset is 4:25 p.m. What is the last legal minute to shoot a deer?
local-harrison-deer.why: Page 11, item 38: no hunting game except migratory birds from 1 hour after sunset to 1 hour before sunrise. 4:25 plus 1 hour is 5:25 p.m.

local-harrison-deer.q: Which licence does a black tailed buck use?
local-harrison-deer.why: The synopsis lists them as mule (black tailed) deer, and the page 8 fee table puts black tailed deer under the deer licence. Each hunter needs a hunting licence plus their own species licence.

local-harrison-deer.q: You are on the Weaver Lake FSR, inside the 400 m band of Crown land. May you shoot at a legal buck during the season?
options: No, it is a No Shooting Area for everyone
Yes. The band bans discharge unless you are lawfully hunting; target shooting is out
local-harrison-deer.why: Page 27: unless lawfully hunting or trapping, discharge is prohibited within 400 m of these roads. Lawful hunting is allowed (90%, my reading with Schedule 5.1). Still check for houses, roads and posted signs.

rb-definitions.q: Your rifle has an empty chamber, but the detachable magazine clipped into it holds three rounds. Loaded?
options: Yes. Ammunition in a detachable magazine inside or attached to the firearm makes it loaded
Only if the safety is off
rb-definitions.why: Page 3: a firearm is loaded with ammunition in the chamber, a fixed magazine, a hinged floor plate magazine, or a detachable magazine inside or attached to the firearm, even if it cannot fire for the moment.

rb-definitions.q: You walk a cutblock with a rifle looking for deer and never fire. Were you hunting?
options: Yes. Searching for wildlife while in possession of a firearm is hunting
Only if you saw a deer
rb-definitions.why: Page 3: hunting includes searching for, stalking or lying in wait for wildlife while in possession of a firearm or other weapon, whether or not anything is killed.

rb-definitions.q: A mule deer buck has 3 tines plus a brow tine on his best antler. Is he a 4 point buck?
options: No. The brow tine is excluded, so he has 3
Yes if the brow tine is over 2.5 cm
rb-definitions.why: Page 4: a four points or greater buck has at least four tines, excluding the brow tine, on one antler. Elk and moose definitions count the brow tines; the mule deer definition does not.

rb-definitions.q: How long must a branch of antler be to count as a tine?
options: Any length, if it is pointed
At least 2.5 cm, and longer than it is wide
rb-definitions.why: Page 4: a tine is a branch of an antler longer than its breadth and at least 2.5 cm (1 inch) long, with the width measured at least 2.5 cm down from the tip.

rb-definitions.q: A bull moose has 2 points on the left antler and 6 on the right. Spike fork?
options: No, both sides must be a spike or fork
Yes. The definition asks for no more than two points on one antler
No, a fork is never legal
rb-definitions.why: Page 3: a spike fork bull has no more than two tines on one antler, counting brow palm tines, and is not a calf. The definition names one antler. That is this app's reading of the wording; the synopsis diagram shows small symmetric antlers.

rb-licences-fees.q: You buy a mule deer species licence online on 1 September for a 10 September hunt. What does the synopsis say happens?
options: It prints at home right away
It is mailed, subject to Canada Post delivery times. In person you get it immediately
It appears on your FWID profile like the hunting licence
rb-licences-fees.why: Page 5 and page 8: species licences bought online are mailed. Bought in person, you obtain them immediately. Only the hunting licence and a few others are electronic.

rb-licences-fees.q: Which of these species licences is not valid until 2 days after it is issued?
rb-licences-fees.why: Page 8 marks bobcat, caribou, cougar, lynx, mountain goat, mountain sheep and wolverine with the 2 day wait. Deer, moose, elk, black bear and bison have no wait.

rb-licences-fees.q: A Conservation Officer stops you. What must you be able to do?
options: Know or produce your FWID number and show photo ID, and show every species licence bought this year
Nothing, it is all on their app
rb-licences-fees.why: Page 5: the hunting licence is electronic, but you are legally required to know or produce your FWID number and photo ID on request, and you must carry all species licences, cancelled and uncancelled.

rb-licences-fees.q: A 15 year old on a youth licence shoots a deer. Whose bag limit does it count against?
rb-licences-fees.why: Page 6: a youth licence provides no personal bag limit. Wildlife taken under a youth or initiation licence is included in the bag limit of the supervising licensed adult.

rb-licences-fees.q: A non resident from Alberta has an unrestricted BC licence. Can he hunt moose on his own?
options: No. Big game always needs a guide outfitter, assistant guide or a permit to accompany holder
rb-licences-fees.why: Page 7: non residents must be accompanied at all times when hunting big game, regardless of licence type. The unrestricted licence only lets them hunt small game alone.

rb-where-you-can-hunt.q: You want to shoot a grouse with a shotgun 200 m off the Coquihalla, Hwy 5 between Hope and Kamloops. Legal?
options: No firearm of any kind within 400 m
Yes, outside the road allowance. Within the 400 m band only single projectiles are banned; shot is allowed
rb-where-you-can-hunt.why: Page 10: on the listed routes a firearm using a single projectile is banned within 400 m of the road allowance. The discharge of a shotgun using shot only is permitted. The road allowance itself stays closed to all shooting and hunting.

rb-where-you-can-hunt.q: How wide is the road allowance on a 2 lane numbered highway with no private land nearby?
options: 15 m on either side of the middle of the road
rb-where-you-can-hunt.why: Page 10: for a road with less than three lanes the road allowance extends 15 m on either side of the middle of the road, or to the boundary of private or cultivated land, whichever comes first.

rb-where-you-can-hunt.q: A Crown grazing lease has no cattle on it today. Can you hunt it without asking?
options: Yes, the consent rule only applies while livestock are present
No. Page 9 now notes that leased land is subject to the Trespass Act whether or not livestock are present
Yes, Crown land is always open
rb-where-you-can-hunt.why: Page 9: hunting a grazing lease needs consent while it is occupied by livestock, and the new green note says leased land is subject to the Trespass Act regardless of whether livestock are present.

rb-where-you-can-hunt.q: Your quail cover is 80 m from an occupied farmhouse. The farmer is your friend and says go ahead. Legal to shoot there?
options: No. The 100 m rule has no permission exemption for hunting
rb-where-you-can-hunt.why: Page 10: it is unlawful to hunt or discharge a firearm within 100 m of a dwelling house or occupied farm building. The only exemption is the owner, occupier or employee slaughtering livestock.

rb-where-you-can-hunt.q: A No Shooting Area sits along your deer route. Can you hunt it with a crossbow?
options: Yes, unless that region specifically restricts bows
rb-where-you-can-hunt.why: Page 10: No Shooting Areas are open to the use of bows, including crossbows, unless specifically restricted in the regional sections. A No Hunting Area is different: no hunting at all.

rb-unlawful-acts.q: You cut the motor and your boat glides toward a flock of mallards. Can you shoot while it still glides?
options: No. A boat still moving from motion its motor gave it counts as a moving boat
Yes, if the motor is tilted up
rb-unlawful-acts.why: Item 24, page 11: no hunting migratory birds from a moving boat equipped with a motor or sail. Hunting Regulation section 17(1.2) adds that a boat is moving if it continues to move because of motion imparted by its motor or sail.

rb-unlawful-acts.q: Your deer is down. When must you cancel the species licence?
options: Immediately after the kill and before handling the animal
rb-unlawful-acts.why: Item 1, page 11: anyone who kills big game must immediately after the kill and before handling it cancel the species licence as the licence instructs.

rb-unlawful-acts.q: Your thermal monocular stays in the pack all hunt, never used. Legal?
options: No. Item 39 bans using or possessing infrared optics on a hunting expedition
rb-unlawful-acts.why: Item 39, page 11: it is unlawful to use or possess infrared optics on a hunting expedition. Having it with you is enough.

rb-unlawful-acts.q: Which call is legal for hunting ducks?
options: A mouth or hand call you blow yourself
rb-unlawful-acts.why: Item 41 bans recorded or electronic calls except for wolf, coyote, cougar, lynx, bobcat and Schedule C birds, and item 42 bans recorded bird calls for game birds. A call you blow is neither.

rb-unlawful-acts.q: You shoot a deer in Alberta. Which can you bring back into BC?
options: The meat of the quarters, loins, neck and ribs, plus a hide, antlers and skull plate cleaned of all tissue
The head with the cape on
rb-unlawful-acts.why: Item 50, page 12: it is unlawful to possess any part of a deer, elk, moose or caribou killed outside BC other than that edible meat, or the hide, antlers and skull plate cleaned of all tissue before entering BC.

rb-legal-methods.q: You want to take a deer with your 12 gauge. Which load is legal?
options: No. 1 Buck or larger, or slugs
Any shell, it is a shotgun
rb-legal-methods.why: Page 13, note 1: for deer a shotgun must be 20 gauge or larger and use shells of shot size No. 1 Buck or larger. Page 12 allows single projectiles (slugs) where shotguns are allowed for big game.

rb-legal-methods.q: Can you shoot a ruffed grouse with a .22 rimfire?
options: No, rimfire is never legal for birds
Yes. Note 2 allows rimfire for grouse, ptarmigan or turkey only
rb-legal-methods.why: Page 13: upland game birds show Yes for rimfire with note 2, grouse, ptarmigan or turkey only. Quail, pheasant and partridge are not on that list.

rb-legal-methods.q: On a duck hunt you carry a box of lead grouse loads in the truck vest. Problem?
options: No, as long as you shoot steel at ducks
Yes. Note 4 bans possession or use of shot other than non toxic shot for migratory game birds, except pigeons or doves
rb-legal-methods.why: Page 13, note 4: possession or use of shot other than non toxic shot is prohibited when hunting migratory game birds, except for pigeons or doves.

rb-legal-methods.q: How many shells may your pump shotgun hold when you hunt ducks?
options: As many as the tube takes
3: a plug limits the magazine to 2, plus 1 in the chamber
rb-legal-methods.why: Page 12: a pump, repeating or auto loading shotgun must have a plug so the magazine holds no more than 2 cartridges. The unplugged exception is only for slugs on big game.

rb-legal-methods.q: Your dog will help you track a deer. What is the rule?
options: Dogs are allowed, but on a leash for deer
rb-legal-methods.why: Page 12: dogs may be used for all game, but must be on a leash when used to hunt deer, elk, moose, mountain sheep, mountain goat and caribou.

rb-bag-limits.q: You shoot a mule deer buck near Heffley Creek in Region 3. Can you shoot another mule deer buck in the Okanagan, Region 8, the same licence year?
options: Yes, it is a different region
No. Only 1 mule deer buck may come from Regions 3, 4, 5, 6, 7A, 7B and 8 combined
Yes, if you buy another licence
rb-bag-limits.why: Page 14: only 1 of your 3 deer may be a mule (black tailed) deer buck from Regions 3, 4, 5, 6, 7A, 7B and 8 combined.

rb-bag-limits.q: A regional table shows deer 2(1). What does it mean?
options: 2 for the season, 1 of which may be antlerless
rb-bag-limits.why: Page 12: an entry such as 2(1) for ungulates means the season bag limit is two animals of that species, one of which may be antlerless.

rb-bag-limits.q: You have 24 ducks in your home freezer from earlier hunts. Can you shoot 8 more today and bring them home?
options: Yes, the freezer does not count
No. The migratory bird possession limit is 3 times the daily limit at all times, home included
rb-bag-limits.why: Page 12: the possession limit for all migratory game birds at all times, including at a residence, is three times the daily limit. 3 times 8 is 24.

rb-bag-limits.q: Your friend drives your deer meat home for you. What must travel with it?
options: A Record of Receipt showing the date and place, both names, your FWID, the licence number, species and sex
rb-bag-limits.why: Page 15: anyone possessing or transporting meat of an animal taken by another person must have a Record of Receipt with those details. Page 14 prints the form.

rb-after-the-kill.q: You are driving your mule deer home whole from the Thompson. What must stay naturally attached?
options: The unskinned tail, and the testicle or part of the penis for a buck
rb-after-the-kill.why: Page 15: for deer, the unskinned tail AND, for a male, a testicle or part of the penis (for a female, a portion of the udder and teats) must stay naturally attached until home and butchered, at the meat cutter, or inspected.

rb-after-the-kill.q: You bought a moose licence and never saw a moose. Do you file the Mandatory Hunter Report?
options: Yes, by 31 March. Every elk, moose or caribou licence buyer must report
rb-after-the-kill.why: Page 16: all individuals who purchase an elk, moose or caribou species licence must report their hunting activity by March 31. Missing it is an offence and blocks next season's licence and LEH application.

rb-after-the-kill.q: You shoot a doe by mistake in a bucks only season. What is the first step?
options: Immediately cancel your species licence and mark in ink that you intend to self report
Tag it with a friend's licence
rb-after-the-kill.why: Page 18: immediately cancel your species licence and mark in ink on it that your intention is to self report, then call RAPP or field dress and get to a phone.

rb-after-the-kill.q: Your 4 point buck goes to a taxidermist. Which paper must you bring?
options: Your hunting and species licences with the cancelled species licence, plus any LEH authorization or inspection sheet that applies
rb-after-the-kill.why: Page 16: when a hunter takes parts of an animal to the business, the person must have the hunting and species licences with the appropriately cancelled species licence, and the LEH authorization and Compulsory Inspection Data Sheet where required.

rb-after-the-kill.q: A deer is shot in MU 4-3, inside the CWD Management Zone. What may not leave the zone?
options: The brain tissue and spinal column, vertebrae included, but not the tail
rb-after-the-kill.why: Page 15: a person who kills a deer, elk or moose in MUs 4-1 to 4-8 or 4-20 to 4-25 must not transport the brain tissue or spinal column, including vertebrae and nervous tissue but not the tail, outside the zone.

rb-region-3.q: 2 November, MU 3-27. A forked mule deer buck, 2 points a side, walks out. Legal?
options: Yes, deer season runs to 10 December
No. From 1 November to 10 December only 4 point bucks are open
rb-region-3.why: Page 34: mule deer Bucks (any buck) only 1 to 31 October. 1 November to 10 December is 4 point bucks in 3-12 to 3-20, 3-26 to 3-44 and 3-46.

rb-region-3.q: 20 October, MU 3-28. Can you use your quad to haul your deer to the truck?
options: No. ATVs are closed for hunting, including hauling game, 1 September to 10 December in 3-28
rb-region-3.why: Page 33: ATV for Hunting Closed Areas, 1 September to 10 December in 3-28, 3-29, 3-30 and part of 3-17. Page 10 counts transporting wildlife as a hunting use.

rb-region-3.q: How many dusky, ruffed and spruce grouse may you take in one day at Heffley Creek?
options: Up to 5 of each but no more than 10 together
rb-region-3.why: Page 34: 5 each a day, and the daily aggregate bag limit for the three is 10, with 30 in possession.

rb-region-3.q: You put out apples for deer 50 m from your house near Heffley Creek. Legal?
options: No. In Region 3 it is unlawful to bait or feed ungulates within 200 m of a dwelling, school yard or playground
rb-region-3.why: Page 33, It's Unlawful, new in this edition: no intentional baiting or feeding of ungulates within 200 m of a dwelling, school yard or playground in Region 3.

rb-region-3.q: When is the general moose season in MUs 3-27 and 3-28, and what is legal?
options: 1 to 15 November, spike fork bulls only
15 October to 15 November, cows and calves
rb-region-3.why: Page 34: MUs 3-12 to 3-14, 3-18 to 3-20, 3-26 to 3-30 and 3-39, spike fork bulls, 1 to 15 November, bag 1.

rb-region-2.q: 25 October, MU 2-8 in the Stave Lake hills. A black tailed doe walks out. Legal?
options: Yes, the Region 2 limit is 2 with one antlerless
No. The 2-8 season is bucks only; the antlerless seasons are in 2-16 and the Pemberton zone
rb-region-2.why: Page 28: 2-8 is in the Bucks row, 10 September to 15 December. Antlerless rows exist only for 2-16 and part of 2-11. The page 27 limit is a ceiling, not a season.

rb-region-2.q: You want to hunt ducks on the Fraser inside the Mission city limits. What do you need on top of your usual licences and federal permit?
options: The Fraser Valley Special Area licence and $1,000,000 liability insurance
rb-region-2.why: Map B10, page 29: all of MU 2-4 and the parts of 2-8 inside Maple Ridge, Pitt Meadows, Mission and Coquitlam need the special licence and the insurance.

rb-region-2.q: Can you hunt wolves near Mission in MU 2-8?
options: No. The Region 2 wolf rows cover only 2-5, 2-6 and 2-11 to 2-16
rb-region-2.why: Page 28: wolf, 2-5, 2-6, 2-11 to 2-16, 10 September to 31 March and 1 April to 15 June. No row means no season in 2-8.

rb-region-2.q: When is pheasant open near Mission this fall, and what may you shoot?
options: 10 October to 30 November 2026, cocks only, 2 a day, 6 in possession
rb-region-2.why: Page 28: PHEASANT (Cocks), MUs 2-4 and 2-8, Oct 10, 2026 to Nov 30, 2026, bag 2(6).

rb-region-2.q: A road north of Mission is on the FVRD no shooting map. Can you shoot a grouse within 400 m of it during the season?
options: No, it is a No Shooting Area for everyone
Yes. The ban is on discharge unless lawfully hunting or trapping
rb-region-2.why: Page 27: Unless lawfully hunting or trapping, the discharge of firearms is prohibited within 400 m of select FVRD roads. Target shooting is out; lawful hunting is allowed.

rb-region-8.q: 15 October, MU 8-1 near Oliver. How many quail may you shoot today, and how many may you have in your cooler?
rb-region-8.why: Page 68: quail, MUs 8-1 to 8-15 and 8-21 to 8-26, 1 October to 30 November, 10 (30). The first number is the daily limit, the second the possession limit (page 12).

rb-region-8.q: You have 3 ruffed grouse and 2 dusky grouse today in Region 8. Can you shoot a spruce grouse?
options: No. Region 8 is 5 grouse a day of the three kinds together
rb-region-8.why: Page 67 and the page 68 footnote: the daily aggregate bag limit for dusky, spruce and ruffed grouse is 5, possession 15. Region 3 is different.

rb-region-8.q: 20 October. Can you hunt quail inside the Osoyoos Oxbows area on Map J1?
options: Yes. The no shooting or hunting period is 1 March to 30 September; vehicles stay on established roads
rb-region-8.why: Map J1, page 69: no shooting or hunting from 1 March to 30 September. The motor vehicle closure has no end date. The ecological reserve beside it stays closed.

rb-region-8.q: You flush a rooster and a hen pheasant together in MU 8-9 in November. What is legal?
options: The rooster only. The season is cocks only
Neither, pheasant is closed in November
rb-region-8.why: Page 68: PHEASANT (Cocks), 1 October to 30 November, 2 (6). Hens have no season.

rb-region-8.q: What is the rule on Skaha Lake, south of Penticton?
options: Firearms using shot only. No slugs or rifle bullets
rb-region-8.why: Map J10, page 69: Skaha Lake Firearms Using Shot Only Area. Kaleden and Okanagan Falls beside it are No Shooting Areas.

rb-migratory-birds.q: 6 October 2026. You want to shoot mallards near Mission. Legal?
options: Yes, if you are in MU 2-4
rb-migratory-birds.why: Table 1, item 2: ducks open the Saturday after the first Monday in October. In 2026 that is 10 October. District 3 at Heffley Creek opened 8 September.

rb-migratory-birds.q: Which district is Heffley Creek in?
rb-migratory-birds.why: Heffley Creek is MU 3-27 or 3-28. District No. 3 means MUs 3-12 to 3-20 and 3-26 to 3-44.

rb-migratory-birds.q: You have 3 pintails and 4 mallards. A pintail and a mallard come in together. What may you shoot?
options: One of them, either one, because the next duck is your 8th
Neither, you are at your pintail limit
rb-migratory-birds.why: Daily limit is 8 ducks, not more than 4 pintails. You have 7. One more duck of either kind makes 8, then you stop under s. 44. Shooting both would make 9.

rb-migratory-birds.q: You cut the outboard and glide toward a flock. Can you shoot before the boat stops?
options: No. A boat still moving from its motor's push counts as moving
Yes, if the motor is tilted up
rb-migratory-birds.why: s. 41(4) and BC Hunting Regulation s. 17(1.2): a boat is moving if it continues to move because of motion imparted by its motor or sail. The old BC tilted motor exception ended 1 October 2026.

rb-migratory-birds.q: Three weekends of ducks sit plucked but unfrozen in your fridge. How many can you hold?
options: 24, because unpreserved birds count toward possession everywhere
rb-migratory-birds.why: s. 46(1): unpreserved birds count toward the possession limit in any area at any time. A bird is preserved once plucked and frozen away from the hunting area (s. 1).

rb-region-1.q: You hold no LEH draw. Where can an adult take an antlerless black tailed deer in Region 1 in a general season?
options: Only in the Special Areas on Maps A1, A10, A13, A14, A19, A20 and A32
Only on Vancouver Island north of Campbell River
rb-region-1.why: Page 20: no open season for antlerless mule (black tailed) deer where rifles are permitted, except LEH in part of MU 1-15 and youth hunters. Page 21: antlerless Special Areas, Maps A1, A10, A13, A14, A19, A20, A32.

rb-region-1.q: What is the season for fallow deer in MUs 1-1 to 1-7?
options: No Closed Season, no bag limit, no species licence
rb-region-1.why: Page 21: FALLOW DEER, 1-1 to 1-7, either sex, No Closed Season, NBL. Footnote: species licence not required for fallow deer.

rb-region-1.q: May you use a wireless trail camera to hunt deer in Region 1 in July?
options: Yes, the ban runs 1 August to 10 December
No. Region 1 makes it unlawful to use a wireless camera for hunting, with no dates
rb-region-1.why: Page 20, It's Unlawful: 'To use a wireless camera for the purpose of hunting in region 1.' The province wide line on page 11 points to page 20 for Region 1.

rb-region-1.q: An adult wants to hunt deer on Saltspring Island. What does page 20 require?
options: A Gulf Islands Special Area Licence, $100,000 liability insurance unless guided, and landowner permission on private land
rb-region-1.why: Page 20, Gulf Islands Special Hunting Area: all islands in MU 1-1 except Vancouver Island. Adults must buy the licence, carry $100,000 insurance unless guided, and get permission on private land.

rb-region-1.q: How many black tailed deer bucks may you take in Region 1 in one licence year?
rb-region-1.why: Page 20: the bag limit for mule (black tailed) deer is 3, only two may be antlerless from Special Areas and only two may be bucks. Page 14 table: Region 1 bucks 2.

rb-region-4.q: You shoot a white tailed buck in MU 4-20. What may you not carry out of the CWD Management Zone?
options: The brain tissue and the spinal column, vertebrae included, but not the tail
rb-region-4.why: Page 15: a person who kills a deer, elk or moose in MUs 4-1 to 4-8 and 4-20 to 4-25 must not transport outside the zone the brain tissue or spinal column, including vertebrae, but not the tail.

rb-region-4.q: What is the deer bag limit in Region 4, before the Cranbrook Deer Hunt?
options: 2 all together: 1 mule deer, and white tails up to 2 (one buck, one antlerless)
rb-region-4.why: Page 37: the aggregate bag limit in the Kootenay Region is 2. Mule deer 1. White tailed 2, one may be antlerless and one a buck.

rb-region-4.q: When does the general 4 point mule deer buck season close in Region 4?
rb-region-4.why: Page 39: mule deer, 4-1 to 4-9 and 4-14 to 4-40, 4 point bucks, Sept 10 to Nov 10. White tailed bucks run to Nov 30.

rb-region-4.q: May you hand feed apples to deer at a Kootenay cabin far from any town?
options: Yes, if over 200 m from a dwelling
No. It is unlawful to intentionally feed or bait ungulates or turkeys anywhere in the Kootenay Region
rb-region-4.why: Page 37, Notice to Hunters: 'It is unlawful to intentionally feed or bait ungulates or turkeys in the Kootenay Region.' No distance limit is printed.

rb-region-4.q: How many turkeys may you take in Region 4 in a year?
options: 3: only one in spring and two in fall
rb-region-4.why: Page 37: the regional aggregate bag limit for turkey is 3, one in spring and two in fall. Page 39 footnote repeats it.

rb-region-6.q: 15 October, MU 6-9. A 2 point mule deer buck. Legal?
options: Yes, any buck is open 1 to 19 October
rb-region-6.why: Page 50: MUs 6-1, 6-2, 6-4 to 6-9 and 6-30, Bucks, 1 to 19 October. From 20 October it is 4 point bucks only.

rb-region-6.q: How many Haida Gwaii deer may you have in possession at one time?
rb-region-6.why: Page 49 and the page 50 footnote: in MUs 6-12 and 6-13 the bag limit is 15 but the possession limit is 5.

rb-region-6.q: Can you use a snowmobile to haul a moose out of MU 6-8 on 1 December?
options: No. In 6-8, snowmobiles may haul game only 16 December to 31 March
Yes, if you do not shoot from it
rb-region-6.why: Page 49: in MUs 6-4, 6-5, 6-6, 6-8, 6-9, 6-15 and 6-30, snowmobiles may transport wildlife, gear or hunters only from 16 December to 31 March, and may never be used to hunt.

rb-region-6.q: You shoot a cougar in MU 6-11. How long do you have to get it inspected?
rb-region-6.why: Page 17: a cougar taken in Region 6 must be submitted for inspection in the region where it was killed within 4 days.

rb-region-6.q: Haines Highway area, 10 September, MU 6-29. Which bull moose is legal?
options: Only a spike fork, tripalm or 10 point bull
rb-region-6.why: Map F39 and the page 50 + footnote: 23 to 31 August any bull; 1 September to 31 October only spike fork, tripalm or 10 point bulls.

rb-region-7a.q: 20 October, MU 7-13. A 2 point mule deer buck. Legal for an adult?
options: Yes, bucks are open in October
No. MUs 7-12 to 7-14, 7-24 and 7-25 are 4 point bucks only, 1 October to 15 November
rb-region-7a.why: Page 57: the any buck October row covers 7-2 to 7-11, 7-15 to 7-18 and others, not 7-12 to 7-14, 7-24 or 7-25. Those MUs have 4 point bucks 1 October to 15 November.

rb-region-7a.q: Which bull moose is open in the general season in Region 7A?
rb-region-7a.why: Page 57: every moose row is Spike fork Bulls.

rb-region-7a.q: 15 September, 7:00 am, MU 7-9. May you ride your ATV to your stand to hunt?
options: No. ATVs are closed for hunting 5:30 am to 9:00 am, 1 to 30 September
Only on a Forest Service Road
rb-region-7a.why: Page 56: in MUs 7-7 to 7-15 and 7-24 to 7-29, ATVs for hunting are closed 5:30 am to 9:00 am from 1 to 30 September.

rb-region-7a.q: What is the Region 7A mule deer bag limit?
rb-region-7a.why: Page 56: the bag limit for mule deer in Region 7A is 1.

rb-region-7a.q: When does coyote season open in Region 7A now?
rb-region-7a.why: Pages 55 and 57: coyote season extended to open 15 August, closing 31 March, no bag limit.

rb-region-7b.q: MU 7-20. When can you hunt moose in the general season?
rb-region-7b.why: Page 62: MUs 7-19 to 7-22, part of 7-31, 7-33, 7-35, 7-46 to 7-49 and 7-55, bulls, 25 to 26 October and 10 to 11 November.

rb-region-7b.q: Which bull moose may you shoot in a Peace general season?
options: Spike fork, tripalm or 10 point bulls only
rb-region-7b.why: Page 62 ★ footnote: open for bull moose with no more than 2 points on one antler, 3 or more points on one brow palm, or at least 10 points on one antler.

rb-region-7b.q: How many deer may you take in Region 7B in one licence year?
rb-region-7b.why: Page 61: the combined bag limit for deer in Region 7B is 2.

rb-region-7b.q: Wolf hunting at 900 m elevation on 1 July in MU 7-33. Legal?
options: Yes. Below 1,100 m there is no closed season
rb-region-7b.why: Page 62: wolf seasons Aug 1 to Mar 31 and Apr 1 to June 15, with the ▼ footnote: no closed season below 1,100 m elevation.

rb-region-7b.q: What is the possession limit for sharp tailed grouse in the Peace?
rb-region-7b.why: Page 63 prints 3 (6). Page 12: in Regions 3, 5 and 7B the sharp tailed grouse possession limit is 2 times the daily limit.

mc-mule-deer-01.q: From behind you see a big white rump and a thin white tail with only a black tip. What deer is it?
mc-mule-deer-01.why: A thin white rope tail with a black tip on a large white rump is the mule deer mark (90%, BC account). A black tail has a tail dark on top for most of its length; a white tail has a wide brown tail that flags white.

mc-mule-deer-01.q: Most yearling mule deer bucks carry how many points a side?
mc-mule-deer-01.why: The BC account says most yearling mule deer have 2 points on each side, two year olds large forks or 3 points, and older bucks 4 or more plus an eye guard (90%). Points are still a poor age guide.

mc-mule-deer-01.q: Which race of Odocoileus hemionus lives in the Fraser Valley near Mission?
mc-mule-deer-01.why: Columbian black tails live west of the Coast Range, including the Fraser Valley (90%). Sitka black tails are on the north coast and Haida Gwaii.

mc-mule-deer-01.q: About how much does a mule deer buck weigh in BC?
mc-mule-deer-01.why: The BC account gives 68 to 113 kg for bucks, up to 180 kg in peak condition (90%). Does are 50 to 75 kg.

mc-mule-deer-01.q: In MU 3-27, about how many hunter days did each mule deer take from 2020 to 2024?
mc-mule-deer-01.why: BC harvest statistics: 1,635 deer from 36,294 hunter days, about 22 days per deer (90%, computed). Plan several trips.

mc-mule-deer-02.q: Where is the heart of a broadside deer?
options: Low in the chest, just behind the front leg
In the middle of the belly
mc-mule-deer-02.why: Hunter education places the heart low, just above and slightly behind the front leg (85%). The lungs fill the chest above and around it.

mc-mule-deer-02.q: You aim at the middle of the deer's body. What do you most likely hit?
mc-mule-deer-02.why: The rumen fills the middle of the belly. Lungs sit forward, behind the shoulder. Aim up the back of the front leg, one third up (85%).

mc-mule-deer-02.q: A jaw's third cheek tooth has 3 cusps and is worn. Age?
mc-mule-deer-02.why: A 3 cusped premolar means a yearling; by 2.5 years it is replaced by a 2 cusped adult tooth (85%, Mule Deer Working Group fact sheet 35).

mc-mule-deer-02.q: How do mule deer mostly beat winter cold?
options: By picking warm, low, sheltered slopes
By migrating south to the US
mc-mule-deer-02.why: The BC habitat model says the main way is habitat choice: warm south and west aspects, gentle slopes, low elevations and Douglas fir cover (85%).

mc-mule-deer-02.q: Why can feeding hay to starving deer kill them?
options: Hay is poisonous to all deer
Their rumen microbes cannot switch foods fast enough
Hay makes them too fat to run
mc-mule-deer-02.why: Rumen bacteria are specific to foods. Fed deer can die with full stomachs (85%, Mule Deer Working Group fact sheet 2). Also, in BC, feeding wildlife has its own rules; see the Rule Book.

mc-mule-deer-03.q: It is 09:00 and the sun is on the slope where deer are bedded. Which way does your scent go?
mc-mule-deer-03.why: Sun warms the slope, warm air rises, scent drifts uphill (80%). Approach from above or the side.

mc-mule-deer-03.q: Which sound band do deer hear best?
mc-mule-deer-03.why: D'Angelo and others found best hearing at about 4 to 8 kHz, the band of zips, Velcro and metal clicks (85%).

mc-mule-deer-03.q: About how wide is a deer's field of view without turning its head?
mc-mule-deer-03.why: Penn State Deer Research gives about 310 degrees (80%). Only a small blind spot sits straight behind.

mc-mule-deer-03.q: Why does blaze orange not stand out much to a deer?
mc-mule-deer-03.why: Deer have 2 cones, blue and green, and no red cone, so orange looks dull (75 to 85%). Motion and outline still give you away.

mc-mule-deer-03.q: What does the metatarsal gland on a mule deer's hind leg do?
options: Leaves a trail scent between the toes
mc-mule-deer-03.why: The BC deer account says the metatarsal gland produces an alarm scent (90%). The interdigital glands between the toes leave the trail scent.

mc-mule-deer-04.q: A mule deer stots uphill away from you. What is your best move?
options: Get a rest and watch the next rise
mc-mule-deer-04.why: Mule deer often stop on a rise and look back (65%). Stay put on a rest, identify fully, and only take a standing broadside shot. Big old bucks often keep going.

mc-mule-deer-04.q: Who lives in a mule deer doe group?
options: Unrelated does that meet each fall
One buck and his does all year
mc-mule-deer-04.why: The BC account says clans of females related by maternal descent; bucks are not related (90%).

mc-mule-deer-04.q: Two young bucks push antlers and twist heads in October. What is it?
mc-mule-deer-04.why: The BC account says sparring between unequal bucks is not fighting and results in social bonding (90%). Serious fights happen between equal mature bucks in the rut.

mc-mule-deer-04.q: What does a hunted deer herd do compared with park deer?
options: Runs from people at greater distances
mc-mule-deer-04.why: A 2008 review found hunted hoofed animals flee people at greater distances (65%). Off trail people and dogs cause the most avoidance (85%).

mc-mule-deer-04.q: You find a spotted fawn alone in June. What do you do?
options: Leave it; the doe is nearby
mc-mule-deer-04.why: Fawns hide over 95% of the time and the doe stays a few hundred metres away (85%, Mule Deer Working Group fact sheet 26). Leave quietly.

mc-mule-deer-05.q: What mostly triggers mule deer to move down to winter range?
mc-mule-deer-05.why: Snow and cold trigger the move (85%, Monteith 2011). The rut comes later, in mid November, on the winter range.

mc-mule-deer-05.q: When are most mule deer fawns born in BC?
mc-mule-deer-05.why: The BC account says late May through June (90%); in western provinces most are born in June (85%).

mc-mule-deer-05.q: When do mule deer bucks drop their antlers?
options: January to March, old bucks first
Right after the rut in early November
mc-mule-deer-05.why: BC account: January to March, older bucks first (90%). They regrow April through August.

mc-mule-deer-05.q: April near Kamloops: where are deer easiest to see?
mc-mule-deer-05.why: The BC account names April on low, south facing grassy slopes, including the Dewdrop Range near Kamloops (90%).

options: A buck staying with one doe and keeping rivals off until she breeds
mc-mule-deer-05.why: The BC account describes courtship as a tending bond: the buck keeps other bucks away until mating or until another buck displaces him (90%).

mc-mule-deer-06.q: When are mule deer most active in late October?
mc-mule-deer-06.why: A telemetry study found peaks about 04:00 to 09:00 and 17:00 to 21:00 (85%). Midday they bed.

mc-mule-deer-06.q: A hot October afternoon. Where do you glass for bedded deer?
options: Shade, north slopes and timber edges
mc-mule-deer-06.why: On warm days beds are in shade, north timber, benches and draws (80%). On cold days, sunny south and west slopes.
