mc-mule-deer-06.q: What did a 7 year GPS study find about the moon and deer movement?
options: Deer move most at full moon
Deer stop moving at new moon
mc-mule-deer-06.why: Webb and others 2010 found moon phase had no effect on daily, night or day movement of white tails (70%). No mule deer study says otherwise.

mc-mule-deer-06.q: Clouds roll in and the wind starts swirling during your stalk. Best move?
options: Back out and wait for a steady wind
mc-mule-deer-06.why: Incoming weather kills a steady wind direction; backing out and waiting is the advice (65%, Rinella).

mc-mule-deer-06.q: Which of these has the strongest evidence for changing deer movement?
mc-mule-deer-06.why: Dawn and dusk peaks are well supported (85%). Barometer effects are weak (40%) and moon effects were not found (70% for no effect).

mc-mule-deer-07.q: What does the BC habitat model call the mule deer because it favours forest edges?
mc-mule-deer-07.why: The model calls mule deer an ecotonal species favouring high contrast forest edges with forage near escape and thermal cover (85%).

mc-mule-deer-07.q: Which slopes make the best interior winter range?
options: South and west facing, low, gentle, old Douglas fir
mc-mule-deer-07.why: Warm aspects, gentle to moderate slopes, low elevation and Douglas fir (85%, BC habitat model; 90%, BC account).

mc-mule-deer-07.q: Near Kamloops, what share of the fall and winter diet was grass in the stomach study?
mc-mule-deer-07.why: Willms 1976 found grass under 10% of the diet until spring (85%). Look for browse and forbs, not grass.

mc-mule-deer-07.q: In the Fraser Valley, which deer are you hunting?
mc-mule-deer-07.why: West of the Coast Range the deer is the Columbian black tail, the same species as the mule deer (90%). Region 2 rules apply.

mc-mule-deer-07.q: Which Hunt Map tool shades the ground you can see from a glassing seat?
options: What can I see from here
mc-mule-deer-07.why: The terrain tool "What can I see from here" works out a viewshed from your pin. Use it to choose glassing seats (Tip).

mc-mule-deer-08.q: Which end of a deer track points the way it travelled?
mc-mule-deer-08.why: The split heart shape points in the direction of travel (85%).

mc-mule-deer-08.q: You find groups of 4 prints several metres apart. What happened?
options: A mule deer stotted, likely alarmed
Two deer walked side by side
mc-mule-deer-08.why: Stotting leaves groups of 4 prints, bounds of about 2.7 to 5.2 m (60 to 80%). It usually means alarm.

mc-mule-deer-08.q: A twig end is torn and ragged. Who ate it?
mc-mule-deer-08.why: Deer have no upper front teeth, so browse looks torn (75 to 85%). Hares clip clean at about 45 degrees.

mc-mule-deer-08.q: At 08:00 on a frosty slope you find a dark green oval with no frost. What does it mean?
options: An old bed from last week
A deer got up from it very recently
mc-mule-deer-08.why: No frost in the bed while the slope is frosted means the deer lay there through the night and just left (Tip). Freeze and glass ahead.

mc-mule-deer-08.q: You lose the trail. What next?
options: Guess a direction and walk fast
Go back to the last flag and circle out
mc-mule-deer-08.why: Return to the last sure sign and circle in growing loops (Tip). That is why you flag and pin it.

mc-mule-deer-09.q: Your first trip. Which method fits a beginner best?
options: Sit and glass a feeding slope at dawn and dusk
mc-mule-deer-09.why: Sitting and glassing is quiet, gives a rested shot and teaches deer behaviour (Tip). Midday, scout for sign.

mc-mule-deer-09.q: Why stalk a bedded mule deer from above?
mc-mule-deer-09.why: Mule deer usually bed facing downhill, so coming from above is an advantage (65%, Rinella). Still check the wind and thermals.

mc-mule-deer-09.q: Which call is unlawful for deer in BC?
mc-mule-deer-09.why: Recorded or electronic calls are unlawful except for wolf, coyote, cougar, lynx, bobcat and Schedule C birds (99%, page 12). Mouth calls and rattling are allowed (95%, my reading).

mc-mule-deer-09.q: Can you use a dog to hunt deer in BC?
options: Yes, but only on a leash
mc-mule-deer-09.why: Synopsis page 12: dogs must be on a leash when used to hunt deer (99%). That includes tracking a wounded deer (90%, my reading).

mc-mule-deer-09.q: The wind turns and blows from you toward the bedded buck. What does an old hand do?
options: Back out and come back another time
mc-mule-deer-09.why: The nose cannot be fooled (chapter 3). Back out and try again with a good wind (Tip).

mc-mule-deer-10.q: A broadside mule deer. Where do you aim?
options: Up the back of the front leg, one third up the chest
mc-mule-deer-10.why: That hits both lungs and the top of the heart (85%). The middle of the body is the rumen.

mc-mule-deer-10.q: The deer hunches and walks off slowly after the shot. What do you do?
options: Mark the spot and back out for hours, longer than for a lung hit
mc-mule-deer-10.why: A hunched walk often means a gut hit (70%). Every source says wait hours; how many differs (4 to 12 hours, your call). Pushing it early loses deer.

mc-mule-deer-10.q: What do you do first when you reach your downed buck?
mc-mule-deer-10.why: Cancel the licence immediately after the kill, before you handle the deer (99%, page 11 item 1).

mc-mule-deer-10.q: What temperature should the meat reach as fast as possible?
mc-mule-deer-10.why: Below 4°C slows bacteria; 4 to 60°C is the danger zone (80%).

mc-mule-deer-10.q: In MU 3-27 on 5 November, which mule deer buck is legal?
options: A 4 point buck or better (4 tines on one antler, not counting the brow tine)
mc-mule-deer-10.why: 1 November to 10 December is a 4 point season in MUs 3-27 and 3-28 (99%, page 34). Count tines on one side, brow tine not counted (99%, page 4).

mc-white-tailed-deer-01.q: A deer bounds away low and smooth with a wide tail straight up, white underneath. Which species?
mc-white-tailed-deer-01.why: The raised white flag and smooth gallop are white tail signs. A mule deer has a thin rope tail with a black tip and stots on all 4 feet.

mc-white-tailed-deer-01.q: How do white tail antlers grow?
options: One main beam with tines rising off it
mc-white-tailed-deer-01.why: White tail tines rise off one forward sweeping main beam. Forks on forks are a mule deer pattern.

mc-white-tailed-deer-01.q: Best first clue to a buck's age on the hoof?
options: Body shape: neck, chest, belly, legs
mc-white-tailed-deer-01.why: Antlers mislead. Age shows in the body: a yearling looks like a doe with antlers, an old buck has a deep chest, sagging belly and thick neck.

mc-white-tailed-deer-01.q: Can you hunt white tails near your home in Mission (Region 2)?
options: No: the Region 2 white tail bag limit is 0
mc-white-tailed-deer-01.why: The synopsis page 14 table gives white tailed deer 0 for Region 2, and Herrling Island near Hope has no open season.

mc-white-tailed-deer-01.q: Which BC region had the most resident white tail kills in 2024?
mc-white-tailed-deer-01.why: Harvest statistics: about 3,971 in Region 4, compared with about 1,091 in Region 3 and none in Region 2.

mc-white-tailed-deer-02.q: What separates the chest from the belly and drives breathing?
mc-white-tailed-deer-02.why: The diaphragm is a sheet of muscle. Moving back it pulls air into the lungs; moving forward it pushes air out.

options: Low in the chest, near the elbows
In the middle of the belly
mc-white-tailed-deer-02.why: The heart is low between the front legs. Aim one third up the chest to take the lungs and the top of the heart.

mc-white-tailed-deer-02.q: Why can a white tail starve on a full stomach in a hard winter?
options: Its rumen microbes need time to adjust to new food
It cannot chew cud in the cold
mc-white-tailed-deer-02.why: Rumen microbes specialise. A sudden switch, for example to hay, is not digested until the right microbes build up (Montana State University Extension).
Bucks fatten through late summer, then burn their fat in the November rut and enter winter thin.

mc-white-tailed-deer-02.q: In heavily hunted Pennsylvania, how long did bucks live on average?
mc-white-tailed-deer-02.why: US Forest Service species review reports average life expectancy of about 2 years for males and 3 for females under heavy hunting.

mc-white-tailed-deer-03.q: It is 17:30 and the slopes are cooling. Which way does your scent go?
mc-white-tailed-deer-03.why: Cooling air sinks. In a valley it drains down to the river, where white tails bed. Do not sit right above them in the evening.

mc-white-tailed-deer-03.q: About how wide is a white tail's field of view?
mc-white-tailed-deer-03.why: Side set eyes give about 310 degrees. The blind spot is a narrow wedge straight behind.

mc-white-tailed-deer-03.q: Which sounds sit in a deer's best hearing band?
mc-white-tailed-deer-03.why: Deer hear best at about 4 to 8 kHz, exactly the band of zippers, Velcro, nylon and metal.

mc-white-tailed-deer-03.q: Why does blaze orange look dull to a deer?
mc-white-tailed-deer-03.why: Deer have blue and green cones only. Orange looks grey or brown. Motion is what gives you away.

mc-white-tailed-deer-03.q: A white tail heard you but cannot see or smell you. What do many hunters report it doing?
mc-white-tailed-deer-03.why: Unsure white tails often circle downwind to let the nose decide. This is a widely reported tip, not a measured fact.

mc-white-tailed-deer-04.q: A doe stares at you and stamps a front hoof. What do you do?
mc-white-tailed-deer-04.why: The stamp is a test to make you move. Any movement confirms you. Freeze.

mc-white-tailed-deer-04.q: In the Penn State collar study, what did deer do when hunting season opened?
options: Left their home range for good
Hid in refuges inside their home range
mc-white-tailed-deer-04.why: Deer reacted the day before opening and hid inside their home range, for example on a steep hillside, rather than leaving.

mc-white-tailed-deer-04.q: About what share of yearling bucks disperse from where they were born?
mc-white-tailed-deer-04.why: Pennsylvania research puts it at about 70%, mostly in October and November.

mc-white-tailed-deer-04.q: Which call is typical of a dominant buck challenging another in the rut?
mc-white-tailed-deer-04.why: Atkeson and others describe the grunt snort wheeze as characteristic of dominance interactions among bucks in the breeding season.

mc-white-tailed-deer-04.q: Which statement about old bucks is best supported?
options: Their home ranges keep growing with age
They use a small range and the thickest cover, and react fast to pressure
mc-white-tailed-deer-04.why: collar study reviews suggest mature buck ranges shrink with age, they hold in dense cover, and adult males are the hardest to kill.

mc-white-tailed-deer-05.q: When do most white tail does conceive in northern populations?
mc-white-tailed-deer-05.why: The BC account puts the rut peak in November, and Penn State gives about 13 to 17 November for most conceptions.

mc-white-tailed-deer-05.q: A doe is not bred in her first heat. What happens?
options: She comes back into heat about 28 days later
mc-white-tailed-deer-05.why: Montana State University Extension: heat lasts about 24 hours and returns at about 28 day intervals. That is the December second rut.

mc-white-tailed-deer-05.q: When do bucks drop their antlers?
mc-white-tailed-deer-05.why: Testosterone falls after the rut and antlers are cast, about January to March.

mc-white-tailed-deer-05.q: You find a spotted fawn alone in June. What do you do?
options: Leave it: the doe is nearby and returns to nurse
mc-white-tailed-deer-05.why: Does hide fawns and return only to nurse a few times a day. A lone fawn is normal.

mc-white-tailed-deer-05.q: In Region 3, when is the antlerless white tail season (2026 to 2028 synopsis)?
mc-white-tailed-deer-05.why: Region 3 page 34: antlerless white tailed deer 10 to 31 October in the listed MUs, general open season.

mc-white-tailed-deer-06.q: What predicts white tail movement best?
mc-white-tailed-deer-06.why: collar studies agree: dawn and dusk dominate, and season (the rut, winter) changes the pattern. Weather and moon effects are small and mixed.

mc-white-tailed-deer-06.q: When are white tails active most of the day?
mc-white-tailed-deer-06.why: BC account: in summer they are active at dawn and dusk, but in winter they are active most of the day.

mc-white-tailed-deer-06.q: What did the Penn State study find about deer before winter storms?
options: They fed heavily before the storm
No change before; they moved less during
mc-white-tailed-deer-06.why: Collared does through 30 winter storms showed no change before storms and moved less during them.

mc-white-tailed-deer-06.q: Your best evening sit starts when?
mc-white-tailed-deer-06.why: Be settled before the deer start moving. The last 2 hours of light are prime.

mc-white-tailed-deer-06.q: What is the main reason wind matters to a white tail hunter?
options: Wind carries your scent and covers your sound
mc-white-tailed-deer-06.why: Studies on wind and movement are mixed. Wind always decides where your scent goes.

mc-white-tailed-deer-07.q: Which landscape is classic white tail country?
options: Valley bottoms where river brush meets farm fields
mc-white-tailed-deer-07.why: The BC account: white tails prefer valley bottoms with farmland. They bed in riparian brush and feed in fields.

mc-white-tailed-deer-07.q: Which foods are white tail winter favourites in the Northwest?
mc-white-tailed-deer-07.why: In winter white tails eat mostly shrubs. Idaho lists willow, dogwood and chokecherry; US Forest Service species review adds serviceberry (saskatoon) and snowberry.

mc-white-tailed-deer-07.q: How far do white tails usually move between summer and winter range?
options: Under about 16 km, along or across the valley
50 km or more like mule deer
mc-white-tailed-deer-07.why: US Forest Service species review: migrations to winter range are usually under 16 km. The BC account describes moves up or down valleys or across them.

mc-white-tailed-deer-07.q: Which Hunt Map layer shows where you must ask permission?
mc-white-tailed-deer-07.why: Private land parcels are shown in orange. You need the owner's permission to hunt or cross.

mc-white-tailed-deer-07.q: Which MU in Region 3 led resident white tail kills from 2022 to 2024?
mc-white-tailed-deer-07.why: Harvest statistics: 3-36 led with 486, then 3-27 with 389. MU 3-45 is Wells Gray Park, closed, and 2-3 is in Region 2.

mc-white-tailed-deer-08.q: You find tight groups of 4 deer prints, all feet together, far apart. Which deer?
mc-white-tailed-deer-08.why: A stot lands all 4 feet together. White tails gallop with the hind feet landing ahead of the front feet.

mc-white-tailed-deer-08.q: What matters most at a scrape?
options: The size of the dirt patch
mc-white-tailed-deer-08.why: Ozoga showed a licking branch at about 1.2 to 1.5 m over open ground could get bucks to scrape there.

mc-white-tailed-deer-08.q: Which gland leaves scent on rubs?
mc-white-tailed-deer-08.why: The forehead gland between the antler bases is believed to be the main source of scent on rubs and licking branches.

mc-white-tailed-deer-08.q: How do you tell deer browse from hare browse?
options: Deer cut twigs clean at 45 degrees
Deer tear twigs, leaving ragged ends
mc-white-tailed-deer-08.why: Deer have no upper front teeth, so they tear. Hares cut clean at about 45 degrees.

mc-white-tailed-deer-08.q: Can your dog help find a wounded deer?
options: Yes, but only on a leash
mc-white-tailed-deer-08.why: Synopsis page 12: dogs may be used for all game, but must be on a leash when used to hunt deer.

mc-white-tailed-deer-09.q: You have permission on a hayfield edge. What is the beginner's best method?
options: Walk the middle of the field at noon
Sit a stand on the trail between bedding and the field, downwind
mc-white-tailed-deer-09.why: White tails travel that trail at dawn and dusk. Sitting downwind keeps your scent off them.

options: Cool, calm mornings from late October to mid November
mc-white-tailed-deer-09.why: Rattling copies a rut fight. Response was best on cool, calm, overcast mornings near the rut.

mc-white-tailed-deer-09.q: Where should the shooter sit when rattling with a partner?
mc-white-tailed-deer-09.why: Bucks often circle downwind to smell the fight. The shooter covers that side.

mc-white-tailed-deer-09.q: Can you use an electronic deer call in BC?
options: No: recorded or electronic calls are not allowed for deer
mc-white-tailed-deer-09.why: The synopsis allows recorded or electronic calls only for wolf, coyote, cougar, lynx, bobcat and listed birds. Hand grunt calls and rattling antlers are fine.

mc-white-tailed-deer-09.q: At the truck the wind is wrong for your plan A stand. What do you do?
options: Go to plan B or still hunt
mc-white-tailed-deer-09.why: A wrong wind educates the deer at your best spot. Have a second stand for a different wind.

mc-white-tailed-deer-10.q: A white tail stands quartering away at 120 m. Where do you aim?
options: Farther back, so the bullet exits the far shoulder
mc-white-tailed-deer-10.why: Quartering away, aim behind the near shoulder so the bullet angles through both lungs and exits the far shoulder.

mc-white-tailed-deer-10.q: The deer hunches, clamps its tail and walks off slowly. What do you do?
options: Mark the spot and wait several hours
mc-white-tailed-deer-10.why: That reaction suggests a gut hit. Back out quietly and wait hours (sources give 4 to 12; your call), then track.

mc-white-tailed-deer-10.q: What is the first thing you do when you reach your downed white tail?
mc-white-tailed-deer-10.why: Synopsis page 11 item 1: cancel the licence immediately after the kill, before you handle the deer.

mc-white-tailed-deer-10.q: What is the Region 8 white tail bag limit?
options: 2, no more than one buck and one antlerless
mc-white-tailed-deer-10.why: Region 8 page 67: 2 white tails, only one of which may be a buck and one antlerless. Region 3 allows 2, either sex.

mc-white-tailed-deer-10.q: Which evidence of sex must stay attached on a white tail doe?
options: Part of the udder and teats
mc-white-tailed-deer-10.why: Page 15: the unskinned tail plus part of the udder and teats for a doe, or a testicle or part of the penis for a buck.

mc-ducks-01.q: A brown duck in early October jumps straight up off a creek. Its wing shows a blue patch with white bars on both sides. What is it?
mc-ducks-01.why: Jumping straight up says puddle duck. Blue with white bars on both sides is the mallard speculum, and it is the same on hens and on drakes still in eclipse plumage. A gadwall shows a white square; a goldeneye is a diver with white wing blocks.

mc-ducks-01.q: Which clue stays the same all season and is the most reliable in flight?
mc-ducks-01.why: Wing feathers are replaced once a year, so the speculum does not change during the season. Drake heads are drab in eclipse plumage into fall.

mc-ducks-01.q: A duck with a long sloped head flies fast in a line with others. You already have 4 of them today. What now?
options: No shot: canvasback are limited to 4 a day
mc-ducks-01.why: That is a canvasback: long sloped profile, fast, flies in lines. The daily limit is 8 ducks, but no more than 4 canvasback, 4 pintail, 2 goldeneye and 2 harlequin.

mc-ducks-01.q: A bird with a dagger bill sits low and dives near your decoys. What is it and what do you do?
options: A merganser: it counts in your 8
A loon or a grebe: no open season, do not shoot
mc-ducks-01.why: Loons and grebes dive like ducks but have dagger or thin pointed bills. They have no open season. Mergansers have a thin red toothed bill; coots have a white chicken bill.

mc-ducks-01.q: About what share of BC's breeding ducks are in the Interior?
mc-ducks-01.why: Ducks Unlimited estimates about 1.7 million ducks breed in BC, and about 65% of them breed in the Interior, the BC Intermountain. That is your Kamloops and Okanagan country.

mc-ducks-02.q: Which way does air move through a duck's lung?
options: In and out the same way, like ours
One way, pushed through by the air sacs
It does not pass through the lung
mc-ducks-02.why: Bird lungs are stiff. The air sacs work like bellows and push air one way through the lung on both the in breath and the out breath. One gulp of air takes two breaths to pass through.

mc-ducks-02.q: How many air sacs does a bird have?
mc-ducks-02.why: Nine: four pairs (neck, front chest, rear chest, belly) plus one single sac at the base of the neck. Side pockets even reach into the hollow wing bones.

mc-ducks-02.q: A duck you hit only in the rear belly flies on. Why?
options: Ducks have no vitals there, mostly air sacs and gut
Its heart is in the rear
mc-ducks-02.why: The heart and lungs sit high and forward. The rear belly is mostly air sacs and gut, so the bird can keep flying and die later. Aim at the head and front half.

mc-ducks-02.q: What does a duck use instead of teeth?
mc-ducks-02.why: The gizzard is a thick muscle that grinds food with grit, sand and small stones. Ducks have no true crop; their gullet stretches to store food.

mc-ducks-02.q: Of 100 adult mallards alive this fall, about how many are alive next fall?
mc-ducks-02.why: Band studies put adult mallard survival at about 0.6 to 0.66 a year. That is why few wild ducks reach 5 years, even though the record is about 27.

mc-ducks-03.q: Where is a mallard's blind spot?
options: Straight behind its head, a big one
There is little or none: it sees almost all around
mc-ducks-03.why: Ducks Unlimited describes a 360 degree view for mallards. Some sources mention a tiny blind area behind the head, but you should hunt as if a duck sees everything, including straight down into your hide.

mc-ducks-03.q: What sense extra do ducks have in their colour vision?
mc-ducks-03.why: Birds have a fourth type of cone that picks up ultraviolet light. That is one reason shine and glare stand out to them.

mc-ducks-03.q: A flock is circling your spread. What is the most likely thing to make them flare?
options: A face looking up, or any movement
mc-ducks-03.why: Bird eyes are built to catch motion, and ducks look down into the hide. Keep your head down and move your eyes only until the shot is called.

mc-ducks-03.q: Where is a mallard's hearing best?
mc-ducks-03.why: A mallard hearing test found best sensitivity near 2 kHz, and duck voices sit at 1 to 3 kHz. Your calls and your clanking gear both land in that band.

mc-ducks-03.q: In a sleeping row of ducks, which ones keep one eye open most?
options: The ones at the edges, eye facing out
mc-ducks-03.why: In the study, edge birds slept with one eye open about 32% of the time, middle birds about 12%. The open eye faced out, toward danger.

mc-ducks-04.q: A raft of ducks stops feeding, stretches necks up and bunches together. What should you do?
mc-ducks-04.why: Necks up, still and bunching is the alert posture. Any more movement will flush them. Freeze, and let them settle (a tip, widely taught).

mc-ducks-04.q: What did GPS tracked mallards do in a heavily hunted area?
options: Spread out over the whole area
Sat in refuges during shooting hours, about 2 flights a day
Left the region the first day
mc-ducks-04.why: In West Tennessee, tracked mallards avoided heavily hunted areas during shooting hours and made about two flights a day between safety and food.

mc-ducks-04.q: How long should you rest a spot after hunting it?
mc-ducks-04.why: Ducks Unlimited researchers say ducks perceive sanctuary in weeks, not days, and that a spot may need a week or more of rest.

mc-ducks-04.q: Which ducks are more likely to be shot?
mc-ducks-04.why: Since Bellrose and others in 1961, studies show juveniles are more vulnerable to hunting than adults, though the gap varies by place, year and species.

mc-ducks-04.q: When are most mallard hens paired?
mc-ducks-04.why: In a California wintering study over 80% of mallard hens were paired by early December, after a courtship peak in October and November.

mc-ducks-05.q: Which ducks are usually the first to leave BC in fall?
options: Blue winged teal, shoveler and pintail
mc-ducks-05.why: Blue winged teal, shoveler and pintail leave breeding areas in August or early September. Goldeneyes, bufflehead and mergansers are among the last and go with the ice.

mc-ducks-05.q: How long is a duck flightless during the wing moult?
mc-ducks-05.why: Ducks drop all flight feathers at once after breeding. Mallards are flightless about 23 to 26 days; most waterfowl 3 to 4 weeks.

mc-ducks-05.q: About how long does a mallard hen sit on her eggs?
mc-ducks-05.why: Incubation runs 26 to 30 days, about 28. The ducklings then fly at about 50 to 60 days.

mc-ducks-05.q: What ends most duck migration through the Interior?
options: The end of the hunting season
mc-ducks-05.why: When plateau lakes and ponds ice over in late November, most ducks pack onto open valley water or move on to the coast and south.

mc-ducks-05.q: Why do drakes look drab on an early October hunt?
options: They are still in eclipse plumage after the summer moult
mc-ducks-05.why: After breeding, drakes moult into a drab eclipse plumage. Colour comes back over October and November; about 9 in 10 mallard drakes are in colour by mid November.

mc-ducks-06.q: When do mallards usually fly out to feed in fields?
mc-ducks-06.why: Mallards feed in harvested fields early in the morning and late in the afternoon, and rest on marshes and creeks at midday and at night. Under heavy pressure, feeding shifts into the dark.

mc-ducks-06.q: Which weather effect has the strongest evidence?
options: Ice and snow cover pushing ducks south
mc-ducks-06.why: A study built a weather severity index from cold and snow cover, and mallards were more likely to leave when it passed a threshold. No good study was found for the barometer alone, and full moon claims are mostly lore.

mc-ducks-06.q: What does Ducks Unlimited report about moonlit, windy nights?
options: Ducks leave to feed earlier in the evening
mc-ducks-06.why: Waterfowl generally leave to feed earlier on moonlit, windy nights than on dark, calm nights.

mc-ducks-06.q: A strong cold front with a north wind passed overnight. What does hunter lore say?
options: Hunt the morning after: new birds
mc-ducks-06.why: Hunters widely report new birds arriving behind a front on a north wind (lore, 65%). It fits the stronger evidence that cold and ice push ducks south.

mc-ducks-06.q: Where do redheads usually spend the middle of the day?
mc-ducks-06.why: Redheads raft on deep water by day and feed in the shallows morning and evening.

mc-ducks-07.q: How deep is the water puddle ducks feed in best?
mc-ducks-07.why: Dabbling ducks feed by tipping up, so they need shallow water, generally under about 30 cm. Teal and pintail like the shallowest edges. Divers use deeper open water.

mc-ducks-07.q: Which of your bases is the centre of wood duck country in BC?
options: Mission and the lower Fraser Valley
mc-ducks-07.why: The BC Breeding Bird Atlas puts the centre of wood duck abundance in the lower Fraser Valley.

mc-ducks-07.q: Where do most ducks spend the winter in BC?
options: Low, open valley water, rivers and the coast
mc-ducks-07.why: Freeze up pushes ducks onto open valley water below about 700 m, rivers like the South Thompson, and the Fraser delta and coast.

mc-ducks-07.q: On the Hunt Map, which layer shows lakes of 20 ha or more where ducks stage in fall?
mc-ducks-07.why: The Duck staging and winter waters layer shows valley lakes and wetlands of 20 ha or more used in fall and spring, plus low open water in winter. Wetlands shows smaller marshes.

mc-ducks-07.q: You find ducks on Vaseux Lake. Can you hunt them there?
options: No: it is a migratory bird sanctuary
mc-ducks-07.why: Vaseux Lake is a migratory bird sanctuary with no hunting. Always check land status and the Rule Book before you hunt a water.

mc-ducks-08.q: What does a duck track look like?
options: Three forward toes joined by webbing, tiny hind toe
mc-ducks-08.why: Ducks have three forward toes joined by web and a short hind toe that may barely print. Coots have lobed toes; deer have two pointed toes.

mc-ducks-08.q: You hear a loud, repeated quack. Who is it most likely?
mc-ducks-08.why: The loud classic quack is the mallard hen. The drake is quieter and raspier. Wigeon drakes whistle.

mc-ducks-08.q: What is the best scouting sign for ducks?
options: Where they fly and land at first and last light
mc-ducks-08.why: Ducks live on water, where sign does not last. Watching the flight line from far off tells you where they will be tomorrow.

mc-ducks-08.q: A duck falls on the water with its head up and swims. What now?
options: Shoot again at once, then mark and fetch it
mc-ducks-08.why: A head up duck is a cripple that can dive and escape. Shoot again at once, mark it against a landmark, and retrieve it. Retrieval is the law.

mc-ducks-08.q: Why are feathers common on pond edges in July and August?
options: Ducks drop all their flight feathers at once in the summer moult
mc-ducks-08.why: Ducks moult all flight feathers together after breeding and are flightless for 3 to 4 weeks, so moulting spots fill with feathers.

mc-ducks-09.q: When is the best time to scout a duck spot?
options: The evening before, from far off
mc-ducks-09.why: Watch from far away at last light to see where birds land and when. Walking the shore pushes them off.

mc-ducks-09.q: Where should the open landing pocket be in a J hook spread?
options: In front of you, inside about 25 m
mc-ducks-09.why: Ducks land into the wind in the open pocket. Keep it inside 25 m so shots are close and birds are easy to name.

mc-ducks-09.q: Why put the wind at your side instead of straight at your back?
options: Ducks then cross in front of the hide instead of staring straight at it
mc-ducks-09.why: Ducks land into the wind. With a side wind they swing in on a crossing angle, so they see less of the hide. This is a tip, not a rule.

mc-ducks-09.q: You are jump shooting a creek with your brother. What is the best approach?
options: Sneak bend to bend behind cover, rise together on a word
mc-ducks-09.why: Use cover and the bends to get close, agree who shoots which side, and rise together. Pick one bird.

mc-ducks-09.q: A duck comes in at 50 m. You can name it and are under your limit. Shoot?
options: No: it is past 35 m, let it go or let it come closer
mc-ducks-09.why: Range is one of the five yeses. Beyond about 35 m (38 yd), steel loses killing power and cripples rise. Lead shot is illegal for ducks in any case.

mc-ducks-10.q: Where should your pattern hit a duck for a clean kill?
options: The head, neck and front half
mc-ducks-10.why: The brain, spine, heart and lungs are in the head, neck and front half. The rear belly is air sacs and gut, so those hits cripple.

mc-ducks-10.q: In Tom Roster's table, about how many steel pellets should a pattern put in a 76 cm circle for teal over decoys?
mc-ducks-10.why: Small ducks need a denser pattern: 135 to 145 pellets. Big ducks like mallards need 85 to 90; medium ducks 115 to 120.

mc-ducks-10.q: A duck falls but its head is up and it starts swimming. What do you do?
options: Shoot again right away, then mark and fetch it
mc-ducks-10.why: A head up duck is a cripple that can dive and escape. Shoot again at once, mark it, and retrieve it. Retrieval is the law.

mc-ducks-10.q: What must stay on each duck until it is preserved?
options: A fully feathered wing or the head
mc-ducks-10.why: Federal and BC rules: keep one fully feathered wing or the fully feathered head on each unpreserved bird, so it can be counted and identified.

mc-ducks-10.q: Which is a sensible avian influenza habit when cleaning ducks?
options: Clean them in the kitchen while eating lunch
Wear gloves, clean outdoors, no eating, wash up
mc-ducks-10.why: United States agencies advise gloves, cleaning outdoors or in ventilated places, no eating, drinking or smoking while cleaning, washing up, and not handling sick birds.

mc-geese-01.q: A small goose with a stubby bill and a high yelp lands with Canada geese. How does it count?
options: In the same bag as Canada geese, 10 a day together
It is a young Canada goose, no limit
mc-geese-01.why: It is a cackling goose, a separate species. The federal table counts Canada and cackling geese combined, 10 a day.

mc-geese-01.q: You see a white goose with a dark grin patch on a long pink bill. What is it?
mc-geese-01.why: The grin patch marks a snow goose. A Ross's goose is smaller with a stubby bill and no grin. A swan is far bigger with all white wings.

mc-geese-01.q: An all white bird bigger than a goose flies over. Its wings have no black tips. What do you do?
options: Shoot, it is a snow goose
Let it pass: it is a swan, with no open season
Shoot only if it is alone
mc-geese-01.why: Snow and Ross's geese have black wing tips. All white wings and a bigger body mean swan. Swans have no open season.

mc-geese-01.q: Can you shoot brant at Heffley Creek or Mission?
mc-geese-01.why: District 3 has no open season for brant. District 2 opens brant only in MU 2-4 from 1 to 10 March, 3 a day. Mission is MU 2-8.

mc-geese-01.q: How do you tell a gander from a goose in a field?
options: The gander has a brown neck
You mostly cannot by colour; the gander is a bit bigger and guards and leads
mc-geese-01.why: Sexes look alike. Ganders are slightly larger and act as guards, and the gander's head toss leads the family into the air.

mc-geese-02.q: Where does a goose's heart sit?
options: In the middle of the back
Low and forward, at the base of the neck, under the keel
mc-geese-02.why: The heart sits low in the front of the body. The lungs lie against the back ribs. Both are in the front half, which is why front body and head hits kill clean.

mc-geese-02.q: How many air sacs does a bird have?
mc-geese-02.why: Birds have 9 air sacs that act as bellows, moving air one way through stiff lungs.

mc-geese-02.q: Why does a goose eat for so many hours a day?
options: It digests only about a third of the grass it eats, and grass passes in about 1.5 hours
mc-geese-02.why: Grazing geese digest about 27 to 34 percent of grass, and food passes quickly. They make up for it by eating a lot, and leave lots of droppings.

mc-geese-02.q: What does the gizzard need to work?
mc-geese-02.why: The gizzard is a muscular mill. Grit grinds the grass and grain.

mc-geese-02.q: Why steel BB for big Canada geese?
options: It is the only legal size
Thick feathers, big breast muscle and strong bones stop small pellets
mc-geese-02.why: A big goose is armoured with feathers, muscle and bone. BB carries enough energy. Non toxic shot is the law; the size is your choice.

mc-geese-03.q: Which sense do geese rely on most?
mc-geese-03.why: Waterfowl rely on sight more than any other sense. They see fine detail 2.5 to 3 times farther than people.

mc-geese-03.q: Why is there almost no safe 'behind' a feeding goose?
options: Their field of view wraps almost all the way around, with only a narrow blind spot
mc-geese-03.why: Studies found narrow blind areas and wide side vision, with a slanted sharp band that covers ground and sky at once.

mc-geese-03.q: A flock is coming in. You want to see if they are in range. What do you do?
options: Lift your head for a quick look
Watch through the blind mesh or under your hat brim and wait for the shot call
mc-geese-03.why: Movement and a pale face flare geese. Watch without moving your head; one caller says when.

mc-geese-03.q: How much does a cloudy morning delay the first flight?
mc-geese-03.why: In the Illinois study, cloud delayed the light level that triggers flight by about 15 minutes.

mc-geese-03.q: Which call is legal for geese in BC?
mc-geese-03.why: Electronic calls are banned for migratory birds in BC. Mouth calls are fine.

mc-geese-04.q: You glass a feeding flock and see several birds shaking their heads side to side with straight necks. What does it mean?
mc-geese-04.why: Head tossing is the preflight signal. The gander's toss gets the family up fastest.

mc-geese-04.q: What did GPS tagged geese do on hunting days in Pennsylvania?
options: Stayed, moved less, and flew when a threat came close
mc-geese-04.why: They stayed on the hunted areas but cut their movement, and took flight more as a threat got near.

mc-geese-04.q: How long do young geese stay with their parents?
mc-geese-04.why: Goslings stay with their parents for a full year, so fall flocks are made of families.

mc-geese-04.q: Local geese stop landing in your spread and land 200 m away. Best next move?
options: Note where they landed and set up there next time
Add more decoys in the same place
mc-geese-04.why: Geese show you where they want to be. Move to them, and change your spread so they do not learn it.

mc-geese-04.q: Which is lore, not a tested fact?
options: Geese mate in their second year
Old ganders lead flocks away while young birds break off to decoys
mc-geese-04.why: Pairing age is from Hinterland Who's Who; landing into wind is basic flight. The old gander story is hunter lore: useful, but untested.

mc-geese-05.q: How long does a goose hen sit on her eggs?
mc-geese-05.why: The hen incubates 25 to 28 days while the gander guards.

mc-geese-05.q: Why can you not find geese flying in July?
options: They moult all flight feathers at once and cannot fly for 4 to 6 weeks
mc-geese-05.why: Geese drop all flight feathers in one moult, usually June into August, and are flightless for weeks.

mc-geese-05.q: A September goose at Heffley Creek is most likely what?
options: A local bird in a family group
mc-geese-05.why: Arctic nesters reach wintering areas in October or November. September geese are mostly local families.

mc-geese-05.q: You plan a District 3 Canada goose hunt on 25 September. Open?
mc-geese-05.why: District 3 Canada and cackling geese: 8 to 20 September, then 1 October to 23 December, then 1 to 10 March.

mc-geese-05.q: On a minus 15°C morning, when should you expect geese in the field?
options: Later, often in the warmer afternoon
mc-geese-05.why: Below about minus 9°C at sunrise most geese skipped the morning flight and fed when it warmed.

mc-geese-06.q: Clear sky, mild morning. When do the first geese usually leave the roost?
mc-geese-06.why: In the Illinois study the first birds flew about 15 minutes before sunrise under clear skies, with the main flight at or just after sunrise.

mc-geese-06.q: It is minus 12°C at sunrise. What will most geese do?
options: Stay on the roost and feed later in the day
mc-geese-06.why: Below about minus 9°C at sunrise there was usually no heavy morning flight.

mc-geese-06.q: Which claim has the weakest evidence?
options: A falling barometer makes geese feed hard
Hunted geese move less on hunt days
mc-geese-06.why: No study was found for the barometer claim. The other two come from field studies.

mc-geese-06.q: A bright full moon was up all night. What should you plan?
options: A morning hunt plus an afternoon field hunt, in case they fed at night and come late
mc-geese-06.why: With a visible full moon, evening flights ran later, and hunters report night feeding. An afternoon backup is a sensible plan.

mc-geese-06.q: What are legal hours for geese?
options: One hour before sunrise to one hour after sunset
Half an hour before sunrise to half an hour after sunset
mc-geese-06.why: Migratory birds: half an hour before sunrise to half an hour after sunset. Big game hours are the one hour rule.

mc-geese-07.q: Which three things must be close together for geese?
options: Safe water, open food and a clear view
mc-geese-07.why: Geese roost on water, feed in open fields within commuting distance, and avoid cover that hides predators.

mc-geese-07.q: What do you need to hunt geese inside Mission's city limits, beyond your usual licences and the federal permit?
options: The Fraser Valley Special Area licence and $1,000,000 liability insurance
mc-geese-07.why: Map B10: all of MU 2-4 and the parts of 2-8 inside Maple Ridge, Pitt Meadows, Mission and Coquitlam need the special licence and insurance.

mc-geese-07.q: Interior lakes freeze in late November. Where do the geese go?
options: Open valley rivers and the coast
mc-geese-07.why: High water freezes first, so birds crowd onto open valley water and the coast.

mc-geese-07.q: Which Hunt Map tool helps you find a road spot to glass a field from?
options: What can I see from here
mc-geese-07.why: The viewshed tool shades what you can see from a point, so you can scout without trespassing.

mc-geese-07.q: Can you shoot geese in an Okanagan orchard without asking?
options: Yes, if there is no fence
No. Orchards and vineyards are cultivated land: you need consent
mc-geese-07.why: No hunting on cultivated land without the consent of the owner, lessee or occupant.

mc-geese-08.q: How long is a Canada goose track?
mc-geese-08.why: Canada goose prints run about 10 to 12 cm, roughly twice a duck track.

mc-geese-08.q: You find green, wet, shiny droppings thick in one corner of a field. What does it mean?
options: Geese fed there very recently: likely the X
mc-geese-08.why: Fresh droppings thick in one patch mark where the flock fed. They will likely return there.

mc-geese-08.q: What should you do when the flock is still feeding in the field you scouted?
options: Walk out to count the droppings
Wait until they leave on their own, then check the spot
Honk the horn to see how many there are
mc-geese-08.why: Bumping them teaches them the field is unsafe. Let them leave, then walk it with permission.

mc-geese-08.q: Where do you scout from if you have no permission yet?
mc-geese-08.why: Glass from public roads. Never trespass. Ask for permission after you find the field.

mc-geese-08.q: You hear high pitched yelps mixed into a flock of honkers. What are they?
mc-geese-08.why: Cackling geese call higher than Canada geese. They count in the same bag.

mc-geese-09.q: Where do you put the layout blinds in a field spread?
options: Beside the landing hole, about 9 m to the side
Far upwind behind all the decoys
mc-geese-09.why: Geese should see decoys, not blinds, as they finish. Guides put blinds about 10 yd to the side of the hole or parallel to the wind.

mc-geese-09.q: A flock turns toward you after loud calling. What now?
options: Switch to soft clucks and murmurs, then go quiet
mc-geese-09.why: Loud calling turns far birds. Once they commit, soft ground talk, then silence and stillness.

mc-geese-09.q: You cut the outboard and glide toward geese on the river. Can you shoot?
options: No. A boat still moving from its motor counts as moving
Yes, if the motor is tilted up
mc-geese-09.why: Federal s. 41 and BC rules: no hunting from a moving boat with a motor; gliding on the motor's push still counts as moving.

mc-geese-09.q: Can you hunt geese in a farmer's hay field without asking if it has no fence or sign?
mc-geese-09.why: No hunting on cultivated land without the consent of the owner, lessee or occupant, fenced or not.

mc-geese-09.q: Which goose call device is illegal in BC?
mc-geese-09.why: Electronic calls are banned for migratory birds in BC. All mouth calls are fine.

mc-geese-10.q: Which steel pellet is the all round choice for big Canada geese?
mc-geese-10.why: BB is the standard goose pellet in steel, with BBB or T for longer range. Pattern it: 60 pellets in a 76 cm circle at your longest range.

mc-geese-10.q: A goose you hit sails off and lands 300 m away. What do you do first?
options: Mark the spot with a landmark and pin, then go get it as soon as you can
mc-geese-10.why: You must kill and retrieve a wounded bird as soon as circumstances permit, and make all reasonable effort to find it.

mc-geese-10.q: Driving home, what must stay on each goose?
options: A fully feathered wing or the fully feathered head
mc-geese-10.why: Until a bird is preserved, at least one fully feathered wing or the head must stay attached so its species can be identified.

mc-geese-10.q: What daily limit applies to snow and Ross's geese at Heffley Creek?
mc-geese-10.why: District 3: snow and Ross's geese combined, 5 a day, 15 in possession.

mc-geese-10.q: What internal temperature do wildlife agencies advise for cooking game birds because of bird flu?
mc-geese-10.why: Agency advice for avian influenza is to cook game to 165°F, 74°C, inside.

mc-grouse-01.q: A ruffed grouse has a tail band broken in the middle and 1 pale dot on its rump feathers. Male or female?
mc-grouse-01.why: A broken band and a single rump dot both point to a hen. Two clues that agree make the call solid (70 to 85%).

mc-grouse-01.q: Which two feathers tell a young of the year from an adult?
options: P9 and P10, the outer flight feathers
mc-grouse-01.why: Young birds keep their juvenile P9 and P10 through the first fall: pointed and frayed. Adults show rounded tips (85%, Alaska Department of Fish and Game).

mc-grouse-01.q: You hunt near Mission. What does the Region 2 table call the blue grouse?
mc-grouse-01.why: The coast bird is the sooty grouse. Region 2 lists SOOTY (Blue); Regions 3 and 8 list DUSKY (Blue) (99%).

mc-grouse-01.q: A pale grouse with V marks on a white breast and a pointed tail flushes in MU 3-27. Can you shoot it?
options: No. Sharp tailed grouse are open only in MUs 3-30 and 3-31 in Region 3
mc-grouse-01.why: That is a sharp tailed grouse. Region 3 lists it only for MUs 3-30 and 3-31, with part of 3-30 closed (99%).

mc-grouse-01.q: A white ptarmigan in winter has a white tail. Which one is it?
mc-grouse-01.why: Only the white tailed ptarmigan has a white tail all year. Willow and rock ptarmigan keep black tails (85%).

mc-grouse-02.q: Why does a grouse flush hard and then glide?
options: Its white breast muscle gives big power but tires fast
mc-grouse-02.why: Breast meat is white, fast muscle that runs on stored sugar and fatigues quickly. Power for a burst, then a glide (70%).

mc-grouse-02.q: How does air move through a bird's lung?
options: In and out the same way, like ours
One way through, pushed by air sacs
mc-grouse-02.why: Bird lungs are rigid. Air sacs act as bellows and push air one way through the lung on both breaths (80%).

mc-grouse-02.q: You open the crop of a grouse and find kinnikinnick berries. What do you do?
mc-grouse-02.why: The crop shows what the birds are eating right now. Hunt that food (Tip, common hunter practice).

mc-grouse-02.q: What does a grouse need to make a snow roost?
options: Soft snow about 20 cm or deeper
mc-grouse-02.why: Grouse dive into soft snow. Under 20 cm of it, roosts stayed far warmer than the air (75%).

mc-grouse-02.q: With a .22 on a sitting grouse, where do you aim?
mc-grouse-02.why: Brain and spine are in the head and neck, and the breast is the meat you came for (Tip, 70%).

mc-grouse-03.q: Where is a grouse's blind spot?
mc-grouse-03.why: Eyes on the sides of the head give about 300 degrees of view. The gap is a small wedge straight behind (75%, chicken data).

mc-grouse-03.q: What gives you away first to a grouse?
mc-grouse-03.why: Grouse key on motion and hear low thumps well. No study shows they smell hunters (Tip).

mc-grouse-03.q: Why work a dog into the wind?
options: So it meets the bird's scent cone drifting downwind
So the grouse smells the dog
mc-grouse-03.why: Scent drifts downwind in a cone. A dog moving into the wind crosses it and follows it in (Tip).

mc-grouse-03.q: A ruffed grouse flushes. Where does it most likely go?
options: A short glide, usually under 90 m, often into a tree
Straight up and back down in the same spot
mc-grouse-03.why: Pennsylvania notes the glide is usually under 100 yd (90 m) (75%). Mark it and follow up.

mc-grouse-03.q: When should your gun be most ready?
mc-grouse-03.why: Hunter lore: the stop makes a hiding grouse nervous, and it flushes. Stop where you can swing (Tip).

mc-grouse-04.q: A ruffed grouse stretches its neck tall and raises its crest. What next?
options: It is about to flush: get ready
mc-grouse-04.why: A tall neck and raised crest are the classic sign a bird is about to go (hunter lore, Tip).

mc-grouse-04.q: In the Pennsylvania study, what share of birds near open roads were shot each year?
mc-grouse-04.why: 48% near open roads versus 19% farther away (75%). Walk away from the road.

mc-grouse-04.q: When do ruffed grouse families break up?
options: At about 12 weeks, in early fall
mc-grouse-04.why: Around 12 weeks the brood splits and young birds disperse, young hens about 4.8 km (75 to 80%).

mc-grouse-04.q: Why do you see more adults in the bag in December?
options: Young birds were taken earlier and the survivors include more adults
Adults only come out in snow
mc-grouse-04.why: Pennsylvania: adults were 34% of the October harvest and 57% in December (75%).

mc-grouse-04.q: A grouse flushes and glides into a fir 70 m away. Best move?
options: Mark the tree and walk straight to it, ready
mc-grouse-04.why: Most flushes are short and end in a tree. A quick, ready follow up often gives a second chance (Tip, 60 to 75%).

mc-grouse-05.q: How does a ruffed grouse make the drumming sound?
options: Beating its wings on a hollow log
Beating cupped wings against the air while standing on a log
mc-grouse-05.why: The wings never touch the log. They snap forward and back through the air (85%, Hinterland Who's Who).

mc-grouse-05.q: When do ruffed grouse usually hatch?
mc-grouse-05.why: Incubation is 23 to 24 days and hatching is usually early June (85%).

mc-grouse-05.q: What do dusky grouse do in fall?
options: Move uphill into dense conifers and eat needles
mc-grouse-05.why: Dusky and sooty grouse are upside down migrants: uphill in fall to winter in conifers (70 to 75%).

mc-grouse-05.q: In Region 3 (MU 3-27), when does the general grouse season open and close?
mc-grouse-05.why: Region 3 general: 10 September to 30 November, with a youth only season 1 to 9 September (99%, Rule Book).

mc-grouse-05.q: Why listen for drumming in April?
options: Drummers mark territories that still hold birds in fall
mc-grouse-05.why: Males hold territories for life (85%). Mapping drummers in spring shows where grouse live (Tip).

mc-grouse-06.q: What are legal hunting hours for grouse in BC?
options: 30 minutes before sunrise to 30 minutes after sunset
1 hour before sunrise to 1 hour after sunset
mc-grouse-06.why: Item 38: game other than migratory birds, 1 hour before sunrise to 1 hour after sunset (99%). The 30 minute rule is for ducks and geese.

mc-grouse-06.q: It is noon and quiet. Best plan?
options: Still hunt slowly and look up into conifers for sitting birds
mc-grouse-06.why: Midday birds rest, dust and sit in trees. Slow down and look up (Tip, 65 to 70%).

mc-grouse-06.q: What does the evidence say about grouse and the moon?
options: Full moon moves them at night
mc-grouse-06.why: No study links grouse movement to moon phase. Plan on time of day, weather and food instead.

mc-grouse-06.q: Why do grouse use road edges at dawn?
mc-grouse-06.why: Grit for the gizzard and food along the edge (75 to 85%). Know the road rules before you hunt there.

mc-grouse-06.q: A hard crust forms after a thaw and freeze. Where do grouse go?
mc-grouse-06.why: Crust blocks snow roosting, so birds move into thick conifer clumps (85%, Hinterland Who's Who).

mc-grouse-07.q: At what height are ruffed grouse most abundant in BC?
mc-grouse-07.why: BC Breeding Bird Atlas: most abundant at 750 to 1,250 m, in aspen and poplar near water (85%).

mc-grouse-07.q: What does a dusky grouse eat in winter?
mc-grouse-07.why: Dusky grouse move uphill to dense conifers and live on needles all winter (65 to 75%).

mc-grouse-07.q: Which Hunt Map layer best shows young ruffed grouse cover?
mc-grouse-07.why: Ruffed grouse use young forest under about 20 years old (75%). Cutblocks by age shows where it grows (Tip).

mc-grouse-07.q: Can you hunt sharp tailed grouse near Heffley Creek in MU 3-27?
options: No. Region 3 opens them only in MUs 3-30 and 3-31
mc-grouse-07.why: The Region 3 row lists only MUs 3-30 and 3-31 (99%).

mc-grouse-07.q: What is the core winter food of ptarmigan?
mc-grouse-07.why: Ptarmigan eat buds and twigs of low willow, alder and dwarf birch in winter (85%).

mc-grouse-08.q: What does a forest grouse track look like?
options: Three long toes forward, one short toe back, about 5 cm
A round pad with four toes
mc-grouse-08.why: Three forward toes and a short hind toe, about 5 cm long (75%).

mc-grouse-08.q: You find a pile of droppings on one spot of a big mossy log. What is it?
mc-grouse-08.why: Males drum from the same spot and leave piles of droppings there (85%, Hinterland Who's Who).

mc-grouse-08.q: A snow hole with wing prints on both sides means what?
options: The bird burst out and left
mc-grouse-08.why: Wing prints beside a hole show the take off (75%). A hole with no exit sign may still hold a bird.

mc-grouse-08.q: Caecal droppings are green. Fresh or old?
mc-grouse-08.why: They start green and turn black fast in the sun (65%).

mc-grouse-08.q: A fresh track line heads into a patch of young fir. What do you do?
options: Slow down, walk beside the line, be ready
mc-grouse-08.why: Fresh tracks mean a close bird. Slow down, keep the line readable and be ready to shoot (Tip).

mc-grouse-09.q: Is your CZ 457 .22 legal for a California quail in the Okanagan?
options: No. Rimfire is legal only for grouse, ptarmigan and turkey
mc-grouse-09.why: Page 13 note 2: rimfire for upland birds is grouse, ptarmigan or turkey only (99%).

mc-grouse-09.q: A spruce grouse sits on a branch with only sky behind it. What do you do?
options: No shot with the .22: move for a dirt backstop or pass
mc-grouse-09.why: A .22 bullet can fly over 1 km. Dirt behind the bird or no shot (Tip; safety).

mc-grouse-09.q: You see a grouse on the shoulder of a two lane public highway. What is legal?
options: Stop, get out, walk out of the road allowance, load, shoot only away from the road with a safe backstop
Shoot from the road surface with the engine off
mc-grouse-09.why: No hunting from a vehicle (item 22), no loaded gun in it (item 28), and no shooting or hunting within the road allowance, 15 m from the middle of a road under three lanes (99%).

mc-grouse-09.q: What does the Rule Book say about the road allowance on a Forest Service Road?
options: The law names two lane public roads kept by the transportation ministry or another government; an FSR likely is not one, but keep the same safe habit
mc-grouse-09.why: The page 10 rule names numbered highways and two lane or wider public roads kept by Transportation and Infrastructure. The law behind it (Closed Areas Regulation s. 12) defines the road by the ministry that maintains it, so an FSR kept by the Ministry of Forests likely does not count (85%, my reading). Items 22 and 28 apply everywhere.

mc-grouse-09.q: Which shotgun setup suits ruffed grouse in thick cover?
mc-grouse-09.why: Shots are close and fast: an open choke and small lead shot is the common choice (Tip, 60%). Lead is legal for upland birds (99%).

mc-grouse-10.q: What must stay on a grouse until you get home?
mc-grouse-10.why: Page 15: a game bird other than a migratory bird keeps one feathered wing attached while you possess or transport it (99%).

mc-grouse-10.q: Which parts of a grouse are the edible portions you must take home?
mc-grouse-10.why: Definition, page 3: for game birds, the edible portions of both breasts (99%).

mc-grouse-10.q: You shot two birds on a warm September day. Best care?
options: Pile them in a game bag in the sun
Pull crops and guts, spread them in shade, then a cooler on ice
mc-grouse-10.why: Cool fast; above 4 C is the main threat to meat; no warm piles (80%, Clemson).

mc-grouse-10.q: In Region 8 you have 3 ruffed and 2 spruce grouse today. Can you take a dusky?
options: No. Region 8 is 5 grouse a day in total
mc-grouse-10.why: Region 8 footnote: the daily aggregate for dusky, spruce and ruffed is 5 (99%).

mc-grouse-10.q: What internal temperature do food safety agencies give for game birds?
mc-grouse-10.why: Extension services citing USDA: game birds to 74 C (165 F), checked with a thermometer (80%).

mc-quail-01.q: A quail with a straight, upright plume and bold white bars on red brown sides flushes. Shoot?
options: Yes, it is a quail in Region 8
No. It is a mountain quail, and the Rule Book says no open season
mc-quail-01.why: California quail have a plume that curls forward. A straight plume and barred red sides mark a mountain quail. Region 1 prints no open season on mountain quail, and the Region 8 row is unclear, so you never shoot one.

mc-quail-01.q: Which bird has an orange face and a chestnut horseshoe on the belly?
mc-quail-01.why: The Hun has an orange face, a chestnut belly patch and rusty outer tail feathers. The chukar has a black necklace and red bill.

mc-quail-01.q: About how much does a California quail weigh?
mc-quail-01.why: Audubon gives 140 to 230 g. 540 to 765 g is a chukar; over a kilo is a cock pheasant.

mc-quail-01.q: A young of the year quail in October: what wing clue gives it away?
options: Buff tips on the upper primary coverts
mc-quail-01.why: Young quail keep buff tipped primary coverts and pointed outer flight feathers until their first full moult.

mc-quail-01.q: Why are there no quail to hunt near Mission?
options: The Fraser Valley population appears gone, and Region 2 has no quail row
They are only on Vancouver Island
mc-quail-01.why: The BC Breeding Bird Atlas found the Fraser Valley population apparently gone, and the Rule Book shows no quail row in Region 2.

mc-quail-02.q: Where are a quail's heart and lungs?
options: In the rear half, near the tail
In the front half: lungs high under the back, heart low behind the crop
mc-quail-02.why: The lungs press against the ribs on the back and the heart sits low in the chest behind the crop. Both are in the front half, which is why you want pellets in the head and front body.

mc-quail-02.q: Birds have no diaphragm. What pumps the air?
options: The ribs and breastbone moving the air sacs
mc-quail-02.why: Muscles swing the ribs and breastbone, changing body volume. That pumps the nine air sacs, which push air through the stiff lungs.

mc-quail-02.q: Why does a flushed quail usually fly only a short way?
options: Its breast muscle is mostly white fibre: fast but quick to tire
mc-quail-02.why: White fibre muscle gives a fast burst with little staying power. So quail burst, glide, land and run. Watch where they land.

mc-quail-02.q: You open a quail's crop after the hunt. What does it tell you?
options: What the covey is eating right now, so where to hunt tomorrow
mc-quail-02.why: The crop stores the last meal before grinding in the gizzard. Seeds or leaves in it point to the food patch the covey uses.

mc-quail-02.q: Most quail in a fall covey are:
options: Young of the year, because few quail live past their first birthday
mc-quail-02.why: Survival is low: few live past one year. A fall covey is mostly that year's young.

mc-quail-03.q: Which sense does a quail rely on most to spot a hunter?
mc-quail-03.why: Eyes on the sides of the head give a near full circle of view, and the covey adds many eyes and a sentinel. Smell is weak in fowl.

mc-quail-03.q: Birds hear best in which pitch band?
mc-quail-03.why: Avian hearing reviews put peak sensitivity at about 1 to 4 kHz, the same band as voices and boots on gravel.

mc-quail-03.q: What does the cock on the fence post do?
options: Watches as a sentinel and gives the alarm
mc-quail-03.why: One bird, usually a male, watches from a high perch while the covey feeds and gives alarm calls when it sees danger.

mc-quail-03.q: How far from cover do California quail usually feed?
mc-quail-03.why: California habitat records say they seldom venture more than 15 to 30 m from cover to feed. Hunt the edges.

mc-quail-03.q: Is scent control a big deal for quail?
options: Yes, quail smell hunters at 200 m
No. Smell is weak in fowl; wind matters for your noise and your dog
mc-quail-03.why: Poultry anatomy shows a weak sense of smell. Wind still carries your sound and brings scent to a dog.

mc-quail-04.q: What is the assembly call for?
options: A separated bird calling the covey back together, or a covey on the move
mc-quail-04.why: The three note chi CA go call is given when a bird is separated from the group or its mate, and before and during covey moves.

mc-quail-04.q: A covey flushes and scatters. What do the singles usually do next?
options: Land a few dozen yards off, hold tight, then call to regroup
Go straight back to the same spot in the air
mc-quail-04.why: Washington Fish and Wildlife: singles may settle a few dozen yards away and hold very tight, then call to find each other.

mc-quail-04.q: What is a quail's first answer to danger?
options: Run into cover; fly only as a last resort
mc-quail-04.why: Quail run very rapidly on the ground and fly as a last resort. Expect the flush where cover runs out.

mc-quail-04.q: You flushed a covey of Huns twice. What happens on the third approach?
mc-quail-04.why: Washington Fish and Wildlife: gray partridge flush farther on each approach. Make the first chance count.

mc-quail-04.q: How big is a typical BC fall covey?
mc-quail-04.why: The BC atlas: coveys occasionally include 100 or more, but more often fewer than 30.

mc-quail-05.q: When do California quail coveys break up into pairs?
options: March, with pairing over about 2 months
mc-quail-05.why: Coveys break up in March and it takes about 2 months for birds to sort into pairs.

mc-quail-05.q: About how many days does the hen sit on the eggs?
mc-quail-05.why: California records give 23 days; Edgewood notes 22 to 23; Audubon 18 to 23.

mc-quail-05.q: What are the Region 8 quail season and limits?
options: 1 October to 30 November, 10 a day, 30 in possession
mc-quail-05.why: Rule Book, Region 8, page 68: QUAIL, Oct 1 to Nov 30, 10 (30), MUs 8-1 to 8-15 and 8-21 to 8-26.

mc-quail-05.q: What drives a good quail hatch?
options: Rain and green growth the winter and spring before
mc-quail-05.why: California records: high numbers follow wet winters with abundant forbs.

options: Move to lower ground and south facing slopes
mc-quail-05.why: FEIS: chukar move from higher ground to lower terrain in heavy snow and onto south facing slopes in bad weather.

mc-quail-06.q: When do quail feed in fall?
options: Twice: just after dawn and late afternoon
mc-quail-06.why: In the non breeding season quail feed twice a day, morning just after dawn and late afternoon.

mc-quail-06.q: What do quail do at midday?
options: Loaf in cover, dust bathe, drink
mc-quail-06.why: Washington Fish and Wildlife: midday resting in cover, dusting and taking water in warm, dry weather.

mc-quail-06.q: A covey flushes into trees and sits there. Best move?
options: Walk away and come back in 30 to 60 minutes
mc-quail-06.why: Washington Fish and Wildlife suggests leaving and returning 30 to 60 minutes later when they may be back on the ground. Sitting birds in trees are no sport and a poor safety shot.

mc-quail-06.q: What does good evidence say about a cold front or the moon and quail?
options: Both are proven to double activity
No good quail data: treat any claim as a Tip
Quail hunt at night under a full moon
mc-quail-06.why: No quail study was found for fronts, pressure or moon. Only hot weather water use and feeding in storm breaks have decent support.

mc-quail-06.q: Late afternoon, where are chukar heading?
options: Down to the river to roost
Back up toward steeper roosting areas
mc-quail-06.why: Washington Fish and Wildlife: chukar usually begin moving back toward steeper roosting areas late in the afternoon. Be above them.

mc-quail-07.q: At what elevation are BC quail most common?
mc-quail-07.why: The BC atlas: breeding birds mostly below 750 m and most common from 250 to 500 m.

mc-quail-07.q: Which plant is the key to chukar country?
mc-quail-07.why: FEIS calls cheatgrass the key plant for chukar habitat in North America; Audubon agrees.

mc-quail-07.q: Can you hunt quail at Heffley Creek?
options: Yes, Region 3 has a quail row
No. Region 3 has chukar and partridge rows but no quail row
mc-quail-07.why: The Region 3 table has no quail row, so there is no open season. Chukar and Huns are open there.

mc-quail-07.q: Which three Hunt Map layers first for a quail trip?
options: California quail habitat, Private land, City and town limits
Duck waters, wetlands, Limited Entry zones
mc-quail-07.why: Find the habitat, see who owns it, and see where town bylaws apply.

mc-quail-07.q: Which terrain tool shows where snow melts first?
mc-quail-07.why: Slope direction shows which way ground faces. South facing slopes warm first; chukar use them after cold nights and in snow.

mc-quail-08.q: How do quail tracks usually lie on a dusty lane?
options: In one line, one foot in front of the other
mc-quail-08.why: Quail walk, so tracks fall in a single line. Three toes forward, a short hind toe that often does not show.

mc-quail-08.q: What is the white part of a bird dropping?
mc-quail-08.why: Birds pass their nitrogen waste as uric acid, the white cap on the dropping.

mc-quail-08.q: Where do California quail roost, and so where are roost piles?
options: On bare ground in the open
In dense trees or shrubs, so piles are under them
mc-quail-08.why: California quail roost in dense trees or shrubs, not on the ground. Look for droppings under thick cover near feeding areas.

mc-quail-08.q: You hear a chorus of chi CA go calls at dusk. What does it tell you?
options: A covey is gathering to roost there: hunt it next morning
The birds are leaving the valley
mc-quail-08.why: Washington Fish and Wildlife: scattered birds call at dusk as they gather to roost. Note the spot and come back at first light.

mc-quail-08.q: Which call is legal to use for quail in BC?
options: A phone playing recorded quail calls
mc-quail-08.why: Item 42, page 12: no recorded bird calls to hunt game birds. A mouth call is not recorded or electronic (95%, my reading in the Rule Book).

mc-quail-09.q: An Okanagan orchard has no sign and no fence. May you hunt its edges?
options: No. Cultivated land needs the consent of the owner, lessee or occupant
Yes, if you stay 100 m from the house
mc-quail-09.why: The Rule Book: no hunting on cultivated land without consent. An orchard is cultivated land. The 100 m rule applies on top.

mc-quail-09.q: You want to hunt quail inside Vernon city limits on a friend's acreage. Legal?
options: No. Vernon Bylaw 5399 bans discharging a firearm in the city
mc-quail-09.why: The app quotes Bylaw 5399: no discharge within the city. Firearm includes air guns. Only farmers protecting crops and bylaw officers are exempt.

mc-quail-09.q: How long should you stop on a stop and go walk?
mc-quail-09.why: Washington Fish and Wildlife: wait at least 15 or 20 seconds before moving on; hiding quail get nervous and fly.

mc-quail-09.q: Best approach to a chukar covey on a slope?
options: From above, then along the same contour
mc-quail-09.why: Chukar run uphill and fly downhill. Get above them. A .22 is not legal for chukar.

mc-quail-09.q: A quail flies straight away from you. Where do most hunters miss?
mc-quail-09.why: Washington Fish and Wildlife: most hunters shoot too high on straightaway birds. Shooting just under pays better.

mc-quail-10.q: Which load and choke suit quail best?
options: Lead 7.5 or 8 (steel 6 or 7), skeet or improved cylinder
mc-quail-10.why: Washington Fish and Wildlife: 7.5 and 8 lead are standard, steel 6 and 7; a fairly open choke suits most quail shots.

mc-quail-10.q: A bird falls into brush as a second bird flushes. What first?
options: Mark the fall, drop your hat, walk straight to it
mc-quail-10.why: Mark the first bird before you swing again. Retrieval is the law: all reasonable effort to find and bag it.

mc-quail-10.q: You breast your quail in the field. What must stay attached until home?
mc-quail-10.why: Page 15: a game bird other than a migratory bird keeps one feathered wing attached. Keep it on the breast you carry.

mc-quail-10.q: What is the Region 8 quail possession limit?
mc-quail-10.why: Region 8 page 68: 10 (30). 10 a day, 30 in possession.

mc-quail-10.q: What inside temperature makes cooked game birds safe?
mc-quail-10.why: USDA lists all poultry at 165 °F, 74 °C. The app's meat care lesson uses 74 °C for birds.

mc-moose-01.q: A big dark animal with a shoulder hump, a bell under the throat and no pale rump patch. What is it?
mc-moose-01.why: Moose have a hump, a bell and no rump patch (90%, BC account). Elk show a pale yellow rump patch.

mc-moose-01.q: Which statement about yearling bull moose is true?
options: Fewer than half are spike fork; many carry 3 points a side
mc-moose-01.why: BC studies found about 43 to 46% of yearlings are spike fork (75 to 80%). The BC account says yearlings carry 2 or 3 points a side. Count every bull.

mc-moose-01.q: The synopsis describes a cow moose as how tall at the shoulder?
mc-moose-01.why: Page 3: a cow moose is 1.8 m at shoulder height and weighs 340 to 420 kg (99%).

mc-moose-01.q: Which moose race lives around Kamloops?
mc-moose-01.why: Northwestern moose (Alces alces andersoni) cover most of BC. Shiras are in the far southeast, Alaskan in the far northwest (80 to 90%, BC account map).

mc-moose-01.q: About how many hunter days did each moose take in MU 3-27, 2020 to 2024?
mc-moose-01.why: 5,599 hunter days for 73 moose: about 77 days per moose (90%, computed from BC harvest statistics).

mc-moose-02.q: Where are a moose's heart and lungs?
options: Low in the chest, behind the front leg
In the middle of the body
mc-moose-02.why: The hump is muscle over the spine (75%). Lungs and heart sit low behind the front leg (85%). The middle of the body is the rumen.

mc-moose-02.q: What does a moose mostly eat in winter?
mc-moose-02.why: Moose are browsers and depend mainly on willow twigs in winter, up to 20 kg a day (90%, BC account).

mc-moose-02.q: In what snow depth do moose move with little or no difficulty?
mc-moose-02.why: BC account: little or no difficulty up to 40 cm, slight difficulty at 40 to 70 cm (90%).

mc-moose-02.q: When do winter tick larvae climb onto moose?
mc-moose-02.why: Larvae attach during the rut, mid September to mid October; adults engorge in March and April (85%, BC winter tick report).

mc-moose-02.q: A warm October afternoon of 16°C. Where do you expect moose?
options: Bedded in shade, timber or wet ground
mc-moose-02.why: Captive moose showed heat stress from about 14°C in summer (70%). Expect them bedded in cool cover in the heat of the day (Tip).

mc-moose-03.q: Which sense does a moose trust most?
mc-moose-03.why: Agencies describe moose eyesight as poor and smell and hearing as acute (75%). Hunters say a moose trusts its nose every time (opinion).

mc-moose-03.q: How far can a cow moose's rutting moan be heard?
mc-moose-03.why: BC account: a long, quavering moan audible for up to 3 km (90%).

mc-moose-03.q: Evening at a lake basin. Where does your scent go?
options: Down into the low ground with the cooling air
mc-moose-03.why: At evening cool air sinks and drains into valleys and wetlands (80%). Sit beside or below the swamp, not above it (Tip).

mc-moose-03.q: A moose stands and stares at you. What does it most likely mean?
mc-moose-03.why: Hunter wisdom: a staring moose has noticed you (60%, opinion). Freeze; only shoot a counted, legal, broadside bull with a clear backstop.

mc-moose-03.q: Is a moose urine lure bought in Montana legal to use in BC?
options: No, any moose part or derivative from outside BC is unlawful for hunting
mc-moose-03.why: Page 12: unlawful to use any part or derivative of a deer, elk, moose or caribou from outside BC for hunting (99%).

mc-moose-04.q: What is the only lasting social bond in moose?
options: Cow and calf, for about a year
mc-moose-04.why: BC account: the only lasting social bond is mother and calf, and it lasts only a year (90%).

mc-moose-04.q: A moose has its ears laid back and the hair on its hump raised. What do you do?
options: Step closer for a better look
Back away and get a tree between you
mc-moose-04.why: Those are warning signs before an attack (85%, Alaska Department of Fish and Game). If you see them you are far too close.

mc-moose-04.q: A moose charges. What is the usual advice?
options: Stand your ground like with a bear
Run and put a tree between you
mc-moose-04.why: Alaska Department of Fish and Game: it is usually a good idea to run from a moose; they won't chase far, and you can run around a tree faster than a moose (85%).

mc-moose-04.q: Which bulls do most of the breeding?
mc-moose-04.why: Yearlings can breed, but older bulls do most of the successful breeding (90%, BC account).

mc-moose-04.q: Why did roads and fresh cutblocks matter for BC moose declines?
options: They made moose easier for hunters and predators to find
mc-moose-04.why: BC's landscape change hypothesis: salvage logging and roads raised moose vulnerability, primarily to hunters and predators (90%).

mc-moose-05.q: When are most BC moose calves conceived?
options: Two weeks in late September and early October
mc-moose-05.why: BC account: over 80% of calves are conceived in the first heat, two weeks in late September and early October (90%).

mc-moose-05.q: When do BC moose antlers reach full size?
mc-moose-05.why: BC account: full size by early September, then the velvet dries and is rubbed off (90%).

mc-moose-05.q: Which bulls shed their antlers first?
mc-moose-05.why: Older bulls shed earliest, from mid November; by March only yearlings may still have antlers (90%, BC account).

mc-moose-05.q: Compared with deer and elk, when do moose leave high country in fall?
options: Last: they stay high much longer
mc-moose-05.why: Moose can stay on high elevation ranges much longer than elk, deer or sheep (90%, BC account).

mc-moose-05.q: In MUs 3-27 and 3-28, when is the general moose season?
mc-moose-05.why: Page 34: spike fork bulls, 1 to 15 November, bag 1 (99%).

mc-moose-06.why: GPS studies show crepuscular activity, peaking about 2 hours after sunrise and around sunset (75%). They also feed in several bouts day and night.

mc-moose-06.q: How high can a moose reach to browse?
options: Up to about 2.5 m, and it breaks taller stems down
mc-moose-06.why: BC account: twigs up to 2.5 m, and moose break branches down with their jaws (90%).

mc-moose-06.q: What is the best supported weather effect on moose?
options: Heat sends them to shade and water
mc-moose-06.why: Heat sensitivity is well studied (70%). No moose study on moon or air pressure was found: VERIFY.

mc-moose-06.q: What are the legal hunting hours for moose?
options: 1 hour before sunrise to 1 hour after sunset
mc-moose-06.why: Big game hours are 1 hour before sunrise to 1 hour after sunset (99%, legal methods).

mc-moose-06.q: Why avoid shooting a moose at last light?
options: Recovery, quartering and cooling a huge animal in the dark is hard
Moose cannot be seen at all
mc-moose-06.why: It is legal until 1 hour after sunset, but a moose is a long night of work. Shoot early enough to deal with it (Tip).

mc-moose-07.q: What does a BC moose depend on most for winter food?
mc-moose-07.why: BC account: moose depend primarily on willows for winter food (90%).

mc-moose-07.q: Near Kamloops, where should you look for moose?
options: Dry grass benches in the valley
Forested plateaus with lakes, wetlands, burns and cutblocks
mc-moose-07.why: Moose are scarce in dry southern valleys like the Thompson (90%). Look on wet, forested plateaus (85%, my reading).

mc-moose-07.q: In one BC study, which cutblocks did collared moose select?
mc-moose-07.why: 46 GPS collared moose avoided blocks under 10 years and over 30, and selected 10 to 30 year blocks (65%).

mc-moose-07.q: Is there a general open moose season near Mission (Region 2)?
mc-moose-07.why: Page 28: moose is not open near Mission (99%). Region 2 holds only 70 to 100 moose (90%).

mc-moose-07.q: Which Hunt Map layer shows the general moose pattern for a month?
mc-moose-07.why: The app has a Moose by month (general pattern) layer, plus Moose winter range, Wetlands, Burns and Cutblocks (99%, app).

mc-moose-08.q: About how long is a moose track?
mc-moose-08.why: About 13 to 15 cm, more than twice a deer track (75%). Track cards give 11 to 14 cm (85%).

mc-moose-08.q: What does winter moose dung look like?
options: Big oval pellets like pressed sawdust
mc-moose-08.why: Winter twig diet gives oval pellets like pressed sawdust; summer gives soft patties (65%).

mc-moose-08.q: A browse line at about 2 m on willows suggests which animal?
mc-moose-08.why: Moose browse lines run 1.8 to 2.4 m (65 to 85%); deer reach about 1.2 m.

options: A pawed hole a bull urinates in during the rut
mc-moose-08.why: Bull moose dig shallow pits 45 to 105 cm long and urinate in them; cows wallow in them (65 to 90%).

mc-moose-08.q: You follow fresh moose tracks. How do you walk?
options: Right on the trail, eyes down
Beside the trail, looking well ahead, wind in your face
mc-moose-08.why: Walk beside the trail and glass ahead; moose may be bedded close (Tip).

mc-moose-09.q: Which calls are legal for moose?
options: Mouth calls, hand calls and raking brush
mc-moose-09.why: Recorded or electronic calls are unlawful except for wolf, coyote, cougar, lynx and bobcat (99%, page 12). Mouth and hand calls are not recorded or electronic (95%).

mc-moose-09.q: You call with your brother. Where should the shooter sit?
options: Right beside the caller, facing away
mc-moose-09.why: Bulls often circle downwind to smell the call before they show (65%, Tip). The shooter waits on that side.

mc-moose-09.q: May you shoot a moose from your 10 ft boat while the motor pushes it?
mc-moose-09.why: Page 11: unlawful to hunt wildlife other than migratory birds from a boat being propelled by a motor (99%). And never a swimming moose.

mc-moose-09.q: Driving at dusk, why is a moose hard to see?
options: Its eyes sit above your headlights, so no eyeshine; look for a dark shape
mc-moose-09.why: A moose is tall and dark; its eyes are above the beam (70%). BC advises extra care at dawn, dusk and night (85%).

mc-moose-09.q: A young bull stands in thick willow. You cannot clearly count the tines on either antler. What do you do?
options: Wait and count again; if still not sure, no shot
mc-moose-09.why: The legal test is no more than 2 tines on one antler (99%). Old hand's rule: if you are not sure, you are not shooting (opinion).

mc-moose-10.q: A broadside moose. Where do you aim?
options: Up the back of the front leg, one third up the chest
mc-moose-10.why: Lungs and heart sit low behind the front leg (75 to 85%). The hump is muscle; the centre of the body is the rumen.

mc-moose-10.q: What is the first thing you do when you reach your downed bull?
mc-moose-10.why: Cancel the licence immediately after the kill and before handling (99%, page 11). Keep the antlers on part of the skull with the licence (99%).

mc-moose-10.q: About how much does a spike fork bull's carcass weigh (four quarters, no head, hide or organs)?
mc-moose-10.why: Central BC meat cutter records: spike fork bulls about 162 kg; adult bulls about 249 kg (75%).

mc-moose-10.q: Why skin and quarter a moose fast even on a cool day?
options: Its big body holds heat deep at the bone; meat must get below 4°C
mc-moose-10.why: The target is meat below 4°C fast (80%). A moose holds heat deep in the quarters (Tip).

mc-moose-10.q: You bought a moose licence and got nothing. What must you do?
options: Submit the Mandatory Hunter Report by 31 March
mc-moose-10.why: Page 16: every moose licence holder reports by 31 March, success or not; miss it and you cannot buy next season's licence until filed (99%).

mc-elk-01.q: Which three marks together say elk, not moose or deer?
options: Tan body, dark neck mane, cream rump patch
Grey body, big ears, black tail tip
