mc-elk-01.why: The BC elk account describes a brownish body, heavy dark mane and a yellowish white rump patch (90%). Black body and bell is a moose; big ears and black tail tip is a mule deer.

mc-elk-01.q: A two year old bull usually carries how many points a side?
mc-elk-01.why: BC account: yearlings usually spikes, two year olds 3 or 4 points a side, three year olds 4 or 5 (90%). Point count is still only a guide to age.

mc-elk-01.q: For the BC 6 point rule, how do you count?
options: At least 6 tines on one antler, brow tine included
6 tines not counting the brow tine
mc-elk-01.why: Synopsis page 3: at least six tines on one antler (99%). Unlike the mule deer 4 point rule, the brow tine counts for elk.

mc-elk-01.q: Which race of elk lives in the Lower Mainland valleys near Mission?
mc-elk-01.why: Roosevelt elk are the coastal race: Vancouver Island, the Sunshine Coast and, after translocations, Lower Mainland valleys (85 to 90%).

mc-elk-01.q: About what share of Region 8 resident elk hunters got an elk, 2020 to 2024?
mc-elk-01.why: BC harvest statistics: 560 elk from 13,427 hunter seasons, about 4.2%, or about 195 hunter days per elk (90%, computed).

options: In the middle of the belly
In the chest above the front legs, behind the shoulder
mc-elk-02.why: The lungs fill the chest behind the shoulder, above the heart (85%). The middle of the belly is the rumen.

mc-elk-02.q: Why aim behind the shoulder blade, not into it, on a big bull?
options: It can be about 6 cm thick and stop or deflect a bullet or arrow
The heart is in the shoulder
mc-elk-02.why: A bull's shoulder blade can be up to about 6 cm thick (65%). The ribs behind it are thin and the lungs lie right there.

mc-elk-02.q: Why does a bull enter winter in poor condition?
options: He barely eats during the rut but burns a lot of energy
mc-elk-02.why: BC elk account: during the rut bulls do not feed but exert a lot of energy, so they start winter in poor condition (90%).

mc-elk-02.q: An elk has 5 cheek teeth in the lower jaw. How old is it?
mc-elk-02.why: Idaho Fish and Game: calves 4 cheek teeth, yearlings 5, elk 2.5 years and older 6 (85%).

mc-elk-02.q: What do elk ivories tell you about sex?
options: Both bulls and cows have them
mc-elk-02.why: The BC account lists large rounded upper canines in both sexes (90%). They do not tell bull from cow.

mc-elk-03.q: Which elk sense ends the hunt fastest?
mc-elk-03.why: Colorado Parks and Wildlife ranks smell as the most developed sense: an elk that catches your scent leaves (75%). Eyes and ears usually only make it look.

mc-elk-03.q: At first light on a cool morning, where should you approach elk on a slope from?
options: From below, cool air sinks and carries scent downhill
mc-elk-03.why: Cool air sinks early, so your scent runs downhill away from elk above you; it reverses as the sun warms the slope (75%).

mc-elk-03.q: A cow lifts her head and stares at you. What do you do?
options: Freeze until she looks away or feeds
mc-elk-03.why: Elk check a shape with other senses before running (75%). Motion confirms you; stillness may let her go back to feeding (Tip).

mc-elk-03.q: What colours does an elk likely see well?
mc-elk-03.why: Deer family animals are dichromats: blue is clear, while reds and oranges look dull (80%). Motion and outline matter more than colour.

mc-elk-03.q: The wind keeps swirling in the timber. What is the old hand's call?
options: Back out and come another day
mc-elk-03.why: When winds swirl the elk will probably win (75%, Colorado Parks and Wildlife). Backing out keeps the herd from learning you (Tip).

mc-elk-04.q: In the Starkey trail study, which activity pushed elk the farthest?
mc-elk-04.why: Flight risk lasted beyond 1,500 m for ATVs and mountain bikes, beyond 750 m for horses, and faded past about 500 m for hikers (85%).

mc-elk-04.q: What does the BC elk account say hunted elk learn to do?
options: Become wary, secretive and nocturnal, and find protected areas
mc-elk-04.why: Quote: hunted elk become wary, secretive and nocturnal and learn the location of protective reserves (90%).

mc-elk-04.q: How long does a cow usually keep her newborn calf hidden before rejoining the group?
mc-elk-04.why: BC account: after two or three weeks the cow and calf rejoin the matriarchal group (90%).

mc-elk-04.q: At what age do most bulls actually get to breed?
mc-elk-04.why: Bulls can breed as yearlings but usually do not get a chance until they are 4 or 5 years old (90%, BC account).

mc-elk-04.q: A cow barks and the herd bunches. What happens next most often?
options: They leave, often to timber or the next drainage
mc-elk-04.why: A bark is the alarm call and the herd usually leaves (65%); heading to timber or over a ridge is hunter experience (Tip).

mc-elk-05.q: When are most cow elk bred?
mc-elk-05.why: BC elk account: most cows are bred from mid to late September; others about a month later, possibly a third in November (90%).

mc-elk-05.q: Which elk move up to summer range first?
mc-elk-05.why: Bulls migrate earliest, following the new growth; cows wait until their calves can follow (90%).

mc-elk-05.q: When do bulls drop their antlers?
options: Right after the rut in October
Late February to early April, oldest first
mc-elk-05.why: BC account: bulls drop antlers from late February to early April, and the oldest animals shed first (90%).

mc-elk-05.q: What pushes elk down to winter range in fall?
mc-elk-05.why: Autumn snowfalls push elk back to their traditional winter ranges; a few bulls may stay high (90%).

mc-elk-05.q: What are the Region 8 general seasons for elk?
options: 6 point bulls: bow only 1 to 9 Sept, then 10 Sept to 20 Oct
mc-elk-05.why: Page 68: 6 point bulls, bow only 1 to 9 September and 10 September to 20 October (99%). See the Region 8 Rule Book screen.

mc-elk-06.q: When are elk most active in the day, per the Alberta collar study?
mc-elk-06.why: Ensing and others 2014: crepuscular peaks after sunrise and at the end of evening twilight; the morning peak came almost 2 hours after first light (80%).

mc-elk-06.q: How close to cover do most elk stay?
mc-elk-06.why: A BC habitat model citing Black 1979: most elk occur within 183 m of cover (80%).

mc-elk-06.q: Where does a summer elk usually bed at midday?
options: Open south slope in the sun
Shaded north slope under dense canopy
In the middle of a meadow
mc-elk-06.why: Black Hills study: north aspects with over 54% canopy closure, cooler than random spots (75%).

mc-elk-06.q: How strong is the evidence that the moon changes elk daytime activity?
options: No elk study found; deer studies found no effect
mc-elk-06.why: No elk study tested it; deer GPS work found no moon effect (70%). Treat moon claims as Tip.

mc-elk-06.q: After a day of ATV traffic, what did Starkey elk do at sunrise and sunset?
mc-elk-06.why: Movement rates were higher at sunrise and sunset on treatment days, suggesting elk were displaced from preferred areas (85%).

mc-elk-07.q: Where do interior elk usually spend July and August?
options: Subalpine and alpine basins and avalanche tracks
mc-elk-07.why: BC account: in May and June most Rocky Mountain elk migrate to subalpine and alpine basins and avalanche tracks (90%).

mc-elk-07.q: What does 'security cover' mean for elk in the BC habitat models?
options: Vegetation that hides 90% of a standing elk at 61 m
mc-elk-07.why: Thomas 1979, cited in BC habitat models: cover that conceals 90% of a standing elk at 61 m or less (80%).

mc-elk-07.q: Is there a general open season for elk near Heffley Creek or Mission?
options: No. Regions 3 and 2 have no general open season for elk
mc-elk-07.why: Pages 34 and 28 have no elk rows (99%). Region 2 elk are taken by LEH draw; the 2026 to 2027 LEH synopsis lists no Region 3 elk hunt (95%).

mc-elk-07.q: Which slopes do elk prefer in winter and spring?
mc-elk-07.why: BC habitat model: many studies report elk prefer southern to southwestern exposures in winter and spring; snow free slopes give access to feed (80%).

mc-elk-07.q: What is the 'Elk by month' layer on the Hunt Map?
options: A general pattern of habitat zones and elevations by month, about 60%
mc-elk-07.why: The app layer note: where elk tend to be by month from studies, a general pattern, not mapped corridors (60%). The official Elk winter range layer covers only map area F.

mc-elk-08.q: About how long is an adult elk front track?
mc-elk-08.why: Field guides give 7.6 to 12.4 cm for front tracks (70%). Deer are smaller; moose longer and more pointed.

options: A muddy pit where rutting bulls urinate and roll
mc-elk-08.why: BC account and RMEF: bulls wallow and spray urine, coating themselves with scent in the rut (85 to 90%).

mc-elk-08.q: You hear splashing and grunting at a wallow in September. What does it mean?
options: A bull is in the wallow now
mc-elk-08.why: RMEF: if you hear splashing, grunting or whining at a wallow, move in quickly while the bull is busy (70%).

mc-elk-08.q: Can you tell a legal bull from its tracks?
options: No. Track sexing is unconfirmed and legality needs antlers
mc-elk-08.why: The bull front foot claim is unconfirmed (VERIFY). A 6 point bull needs 6 tines on one antler, which only your eyes can count.

mc-elk-08.q: A cow barks and you hear hooves. What sign have you just made?
options: You were detected; the herd is leaving
mc-elk-08.why: Barks are alarm calls (65%). The herd will usually leave (Tip). Note it and do not chase.

mc-elk-09.q: Which calls are legal for elk in BC?
options: Mouth calls, hand calls and bugle tubes
mc-elk-09.why: Page 12: recorded or electronic calls are unlawful except for wolf, coyote, cougar, lynx, bobcat and Schedule C birds (99%). Mouth and hand calls are not recorded or electronic.

mc-elk-09.q: In a calling setup, where does the shooter sit?
options: In front of the caller, toward the elk and on the downwind side
mc-elk-09.why: Bulls often circle downwind to check the call; the shooter in front and downwind meets him first (65%, calling guides).

mc-elk-09.q: Late October, heavy pressure. Where are the elk by day?
mc-elk-09.why: Hunted elk become wary, secretive and nocturnal (90%, BC account). Still hunt timber on a good wind or glass edges at first and last light (Tip).

mc-elk-09.q: How do you sit a wallow?
options: Downwind, screened, away from the main trail in
mc-elk-09.why: RMEF: set up downwind, screened by vegetation and away from the main trail to the wallow (70%).

mc-elk-09.q: A bull shows at 80 m. You count 5 tines on the left antler and cannot see the right. What do you do?
options: Wait until you can count 6 on one antler, or pass
mc-elk-09.why: A 6 point bull needs at least 6 tines on one antler, brow included (99%, page 3). No certain count, no shot.

mc-elk-10.q: What must you do before you move a dead elk?
mc-elk-10.why: Page 11: cancel the species licence immediately after the kill and before handling the animal (95%). In a 6 point season the antlers stay attached to part of the skull, with the licence.

mc-elk-10.q: About how much boneless meat does a bull elk give?
mc-elk-10.why: University of Wyoming: one bull gave 75 kg boneless from 181 kg field dressed; six bulls averaged 99 kg (85%).

mc-elk-10.q: You hit a bull in the lungs and he ran out of sight. How long do you wait at least?
mc-elk-10.why: Hunter Ed blog and NDA (National Deer Association) 2012: heart or lungs out of sight, about 30 minutes (70%). NDA 2023 says a few minutes with a rifle; no source says overnight. Lean longer on elk, but balance it with meat cooling in heat (Tip).

mc-elk-10.q: Which parts must come out of the field?
options: All four quarters, loins, neck and ribs
Only what you can carry in one trip
mc-elk-10.why: Page 11, edible portions: four quarters, loins, neck and ribs (99%). Make as many trips as it takes.

mc-elk-10.q: Who must file the Mandatory Hunter Report for elk, and by when?
options: Everyone who bought an elk licence, by 31 March
mc-elk-10.why: Page 16: all individuals who purchase an elk, moose or caribou species licence report by 31 March (99%). New for elk in this edition.

mc-black-bear-01.q: A big cinnamon coloured bear feeds on a slope near Kamloops. What tells you if it is a black bear?
options: Shoulder hump, face profile, ears and claws, at least 3 agreeing
mc-black-bear-01.why: Interior black bears are often brown or cinnamon (90%), so colour is useless. Use shape: no hump, straight face, tall ears, short curved claws. Idaho Fish and Game says never use one feature alone, and not colour or size (85%).

mc-black-bear-01.q: Which bear is legal to hunt in season?
mc-black-bear-01.why: Item 14, page 11: no black bear under 2 years old and no bear in its company (99%). The synopsis notice asks you to select an adult male (98%).

mc-black-bear-01.q: About how much does an adult male black bear weigh in BC?
mc-black-bear-01.why: BC account: males 80 to 300 kg, females 40 to 140 kg, 60 to 90 cm at the shoulder (90%).

mc-black-bear-01.q: Which race of black bear lives around Heffley Creek and the South Okanagan?
mc-black-bear-01.why: cinnamomum covers most of BC east of the Coast Range; larger, and brown bears are common (90%, BC account). kermodei is the north coast, carlottae Haida Gwaii.

mc-black-bear-01.q: You see a white black bear on the coast. Can you hunt it?
options: No. White and blue colour phases are never legal
mc-black-bear-01.why: Item 15, page 11: unlawful to hunt the white or blue (Glacier) colour phases of the black bear (99%).

mc-black-bear-02.q: Where do you aim on a broadside black bear?
options: Low, on the point of the elbow
Halfway up, tight behind the shoulder, near leg forward
mc-black-bear-02.why: The shot placement lesson: halfway up the body, tight behind the shoulder once the near leg steps forward, through both lungs (85%). The heart sits low and the lungs reach past the middle (70%).

mc-black-bear-02.q: Why do bears chase berries, fish and insects instead of grazing all day like deer?
options: They have one simple stomach and digest fibre poorly
mc-black-bear-02.why: Bears have a carnivore's gut but eat mostly plants, so they seek low fibre, easy to digest, concentrated food (90%, BC account).

mc-black-bear-02.q: What happens to a black bear's heart rate in the den?
options: It drops from about 50 to 55 to about 10 to 14 a minute
mc-black-bear-02.why: BC account: about 50 down to about 10 (90%). Alaska study: about 55 to about 14, with metabolism near 25% of normal (80%).

options: The hide is easier to sell
Fat and the thick hide hold heat and spoil the meat
mc-black-bear-02.why: The hide and fat insulate the meat, which speeds spoilage (75%, Maryland Department of Natural Resources). Chapter 10 has the steps.

mc-black-bear-02.q: How often does a black bear sow usually have cubs?
options: Every 2 to 3 years, starting near age 4
mc-black-bear-02.why: BC account: females usually mature at about 4 and breed every 2 to 3 years (90%). A slow birth rate is one reason sows with young are protected.

mc-black-bear-03.q: Which sense should you plan around first on a bear stalk?
mc-black-bear-03.why: A bear's nose is its strongest sense: nasal lining about 100 times ours, food smelled over 1 km away (70%). Wind in your face or across it, always (Tip).

mc-black-bear-03.q: You sit an evening berry slope. Where does your scent tend to go as the light fades?
mc-black-bear-03.why: Evening thermals slide down the slope as the air cools (80%). Set up so the sinking air carries your scent away from where the bear will come.

mc-black-bear-03.q: What does the North American Bear Center call the bear's first line of defence?
mc-black-bear-03.why: Hearing works in all directions and, in brush, carries farther than sight (70%). The nose then confirms.

options: Yes, and they see sharply up close
mc-black-bear-03.why: Bears see colour and have sharp close up vision (70%); a retina study predicts two colour channels (70%). Motion still gives you away most (Tip).

mc-black-bear-03.q: A bear stands up on its hind legs and looks your way. What is it most likely doing?
options: Trying to see and smell better
mc-black-bear-03.why: A standing bear is usually gathering information, not attacking (Tip, bear safety guidance). Freeze and let it settle.

mc-black-bear-04.q: A bear stomps, pops its jaws and woofs at you. What is it telling you?
options: It is about to hunt you
It is stressed and wants space
It is calling cubs to eat
mc-black-bear-04.why: Jaw popping, woofing, moaning, stomping and bluff charges are signs of an agitated, defensive bear (75%, WildSafeBC). Speak calmly, back away, have spray ready.

mc-black-bear-04.q: Two cubs scramble up a tree near a feeding bear. Can you shoot the big bear?
options: No. Any bear in the company of a bear under 2 is closed
Only if it is a boar
mc-black-bear-04.why: Item 14, page 11 (99%). Cubs in a tree mean the sow is close, and she is in their company.

mc-black-bear-04.q: How big is an adult boar's home range compared with a sow's?
options: Boar 25 to 150 km2, sow 5 to 25 km2
mc-black-bear-04.why: BC account (90%). Big males roam widely, especially in the June and July mating season.

mc-black-bear-04.q: At what distance does WildSafeBC say to use bear spray?
mc-black-bear-04.why: WildSafeBC: discharge at about 5 to 10 m (75%). Aim low so the cloud rises into the bear's face.

mc-black-bear-04.q: In the 2008 Alaska study, how often did spray stop black bears' undesirable behaviour?
mc-black-bear-04.why: 90% for black bears, 92% for brown bears; 98% of people carrying spray were uninjured (80%). The black bear sample was small (20 cases).

mc-black-bear-05.q: When are black bear cubs born?
options: April, as the sow leaves the den
January or February, in the den
mc-black-bear-05.why: Cubs are born in the den in January or February, at about 400 g (90%, BC account). Mating is early June to mid July; implantation is delayed to October or November.

mc-black-bear-05.q: Which bears usually come out of the den first in spring?
mc-black-bear-05.why: Near the Okanagan, males came out 4 April to 7 May and females to 22 May (80%, Gaines 2003). Sows with cubs come out last.

mc-black-bear-05.q: What are the Region 3 black bear seasons in most MUs?
options: Apr 1 to June 30 and Sept 1 to Nov 30
May 1 to June 15 and Oct 1 to Oct 31
mc-black-bear-05.why: Page 34: 1 April to 30 June and 1 September to 30 November, bag 2 (99%). MU 3-46 fall opens 20 September.

options: The fall feeding frenzy before the den
mc-black-bear-05.why: Hyperphagia is the late summer and fall feeding drive; a bear may eat up to 20,000 calories a day (70%, WildSafeBC).

mc-black-bear-05.q: In late November, which bear is most likely still out?
options: A big boar near lasting food
mc-black-bear-05.why: Sows den first and big males last (80%); some males skip denning where food lasts (75%).

mc-black-bear-06.q: When are black bears mainly active, according to WildSafeBC?
options: Mainly by day, with more night feeding near people
mc-black-bear-06.why: WildSafeBC: mainly diurnal, but may feed at night in high risk, human active areas (75%).

mc-black-bear-06.q: What are the legal hunting hours for black bear in BC?
options: 1 hour before sunrise to 1 hour after sunset
mc-black-bear-06.why: Page 11: no hunting game, except migratory birds, from 1 hour after sunset to 1 hour before sunrise (99%). No lights or infrared optics.

mc-black-bear-06.q: What does the evidence say about the moon and bear movement?
options: No good bear data found: VERIFY
Bears den at the full moon
mc-black-bear-06.why: No bear studies were found, so it is marked VERIFY. Do not plan around it.

mc-black-bear-06.q: A cutblock near the road gets lots of hunters. What do the bears likely do?
mc-black-bear-06.why: Bears near people shift feeding to night (75% WildSafeBC; 65% Massachusetts GPS study). Glass from far away or hunt the far side (Tip).

mc-black-bear-06.q: In a cool October, how long can a bear spend foraging?
options: Up to about 20 hours a day
It does not feed in fall
mc-black-bear-06.why: Hyperphagia reports describe foraging up to about 20 hours a day (65%). Keep glassing through the day in cool weather (Tip).

mc-black-bear-07.q: Where should you look for black bears in early May near Heffley Creek?
options: Low, south facing grassy slopes and road edges greening up
mc-black-bear-07.why: Spring bears feed on new green growth: grassy south facing slopes, meadows, riparian strips, avalanche chutes and burns (90%, BC account).

mc-black-bear-07.q: About how much of a black bear's diet is plants?
mc-black-bear-07.why: WildSafeBC: about 80% (75%). The BC account says vegetable matter forms the bulk, especially in spring and summer (90%).

mc-black-bear-07.q: Which cutblocks does the Hunt Map guide say feed bears?
mc-black-bear-07.why: The app's habitat guide: cutblocks 5 to 20 years old feed deer, moose, bears and grouse (app tip). Dense second growth produces little bear food (90%, BC account).

mc-black-bear-07.q: Why are coastal black bear densities higher?
mc-black-bear-07.why: BC account: coastal densities are higher because of access to spawning salmon (90%).

mc-black-bear-07.q: In Region 8, what is special about the August bear season?
options: Private land only, with the owner's permission
mc-black-bear-07.why: Page 68: August 1 to 31, restricted to private land only; hunters must obtain permission from landowners (99%).

mc-black-bear-08.q: You lay a straight edge across the top of a front bear track's pad. It crosses the toes. What made it?
mc-black-bear-08.why: Idaho Fish and Game: a black bear's toes form an arc, so the edge crosses them; on a grizzly the toes sit above the edge (80%).

mc-black-bear-08.q: How far ahead of the toe pads are black bear claw marks?
mc-black-bear-08.why: Idaho Fish and Game: black bear 1 to 2.5 inches; grizzly 2 to 4.5 inches (80%).

mc-black-bear-08.q: Scat on a trail is loose and full of berry seeds. What does it tell you?
options: A ripe berry patch is being used nearby
mc-black-bear-08.why: Scat shows what bears eat this week (Tip). Find the ripe patch and glass it at first and last light.

mc-black-bear-08.q: What does a rub tree with hair in the bark tell you about the bear's species?
options: The hair colour tells you the species
Nothing about species; colour is not ID
mc-black-bear-08.why: Both species rub and mark trees (90%, BC account). Hair colour shows coat colour, and colour is not a species clue (chapter 1).

mc-black-bear-08.q: You find a raked mound of debris, birds overhead and a smell of rot. What do you do?
options: Back away the way you came, watching behind
Sit on it for a bear
mc-black-bear-08.why: That is likely a bear cache, and bears may bed close and defend it (85%). Also, hunting bears over a carcass is unlawful (99%, item 21).

mc-black-bear-09.q: Is it legal to sit over your deer's gut pile to wait for a bear?
options: Yes, it is your own animal
No. Hunting bears with a dead animal or part of one as bait is unlawful
mc-black-bear-09.why: Item 21, page 11: unlawful to hunt bears by placing bait or by using a dead animal or part of it as bait (99%).

mc-black-bear-09.q: Can you use an electronic predator call for black bear?
options: No. Electronic calls are only allowed for wolf, coyote, cougar, lynx, bobcat and Schedule C birds
mc-black-bear-09.why: Item 41, page 12 (99%). Bear is not on the list. Mouth or hand calls are allowed, my reading (95%).

mc-black-bear-09.q: Which bear fits the synopsis description of a large adult male?
options: All legs, pointed head, big looking ears
Stocky legs, belly near the ground, round head, small looking ears, thick neck
mc-black-bear-09.why: Page 80 notice (98%): adult males have stocky legs, a massive body with the belly near the ground, a big round head, small looking ears and a thick neck.

mc-black-bear-09.q: You glass a lone bear on a berry slope. What do you do first?
options: Watch it at least 5 minutes for cubs and judge it
mc-black-bear-09.why: Be patient (98%, synopsis notice). Cubs may be hidden; a bear in the company of a cub is closed (99%).

mc-black-bear-09.q: Are unleashed dogs allowed for hunting black bear in BC?
options: Yes, page 12 allows unleashed dogs for black bear
mc-black-bear-09.why: Page 12: unleashed dogs may be used to hunt small game, lynx, bobcat, black bear or cougar (99%). Deer, elk and moose need a leash.

mc-black-bear-10.q: What is the first thing you do when you reach your dead bear?
mc-black-bear-10.why: Item 1, page 11: cancel the species licence immediately after the kill and before handling (99%).

mc-black-bear-10.q: Why must you skin a bear quickly?
options: Fat and the thick hide trap heat; meat spoils and hair slips
mc-black-bear-10.why: Alaska: skin immediately to get heat out of hide and meat; hides can slip within a day (85%). Maryland: fat and hide insulate the meat (75%).

mc-black-bear-10.q: How should you store a salted bear hide?
options: Folded skin to skin in a game bag or burlap, never plastic
mc-black-bear-10.why: Alaska: never store a hide in plastic; use game bags or burlap so it breathes (85%). Plastic makes hair slip.

mc-black-bear-10.q: Does freezing bear meat kill Trichinella?
options: No. The northern species survives freezing; cook to 71°C (160°F)
mc-black-bear-10.why: Trichinella nativa survives months or years frozen (85%, CDC). A 2005 Victoria outbreak came from bear meat that had been frozen (75%).

mc-black-bear-10.q: What may you do with the gall bladder of your legal black bear?
options: Remove it and leave it at the kill site, or dispose of the gut pile with it within 48 hours
mc-black-bear-10.why: Item 48, page 11: no possessing or trafficking bear galls; leaving the gall at the kill site, or disposing of the gut pile with it within 48 hours, is allowed (99%).

mc-skills-01.q: What is the exit pupil of a 10x42 binocular?
mc-skills-01.why: Front lens ÷ power: 42 ÷ 10 = 4.2 mm (85%, Vortex). An 8x42 gives 5.25 mm, a touch brighter at dawn.

mc-skills-01.q: Why do old hands glass from a tripod?
options: A steady view shows the tiny ear flick or tail twitch a shaky view hides
mc-skills-01.why: The movement you look for is often a tiny flick (65%, goHUNT). Shaking hands hide it.

mc-skills-01.q: Glassing order: near first or far first?
options: Near first is the only right way
Far first is the only right way
Both are taught by good hunters; it is your call
mc-skills-01.why: Kirchner (onX) looks close first; Warren (Western Hunter) picks the furthest points first before heat waves. Both agree: naked eye look, quick pass, then a slow grid (65%).

mc-skills-01.q: What should you look for on a far slope?
options: Parts: a flat back line, an ear, legs, a flicker
mc-skills-01.why: Animals are usually partly hidden. Horizontal back lines against vertical trees, ears and movement give them away (65%).

mc-skills-01.q: You want to glass from your parked truck with your rifle cased inside. What does this lesson say?
options: Hunting includes searching with a firearm, and hunting from a motor vehicle is unlawful: ask a conservation officer before relying on any reading
mc-skills-01.why: Page 3 and page 11 item 22 (99%). How they apply to glassing from a parked truck is not spelled out here, so ask a conservation officer (VERIFY). Simplest: no firearm while scouting from the truck.

mc-skills-02.q: Where do you measure a track in mud or snow?
mc-skills-02.why: Mud and snow push the rim out, so measure the floor (80%, Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife). Average 3 to 5 prints.

mc-skills-02.q: Tracks leave a bed in groups of four with long gaps. What happened?
mc-skills-02.why: Walking tracks out mean it left on its own. Bound or stot groups out mean it was spooked (80%).

mc-skills-02.q: A print has small rain pits inside it. When was it made?
mc-skills-02.why: Rain pits inside a print mean it was made before the rain. A clean print on pitted ground was made after (70%).

mc-skills-02.q: A scrape is a pawed patch of soil under what?
options: A licking branch about 1.2 to 1.5 m up
mc-skills-02.why: Bucks paw soil under an overhanging licking branch about 1.2 to 1.5 m up and mark the branch (65%). Most visits happen at night.

mc-skills-02.q: You follow a fresh deer track with your rifle 30 minutes after legal light ends. Is that legal?
options: No: following on the trail of wildlife while in possession of a firearm is hunting, and hunting hours apply
Yes, if the track is fresh
mc-skills-02.why: The definition of hunt includes following on the trail of wildlife with a firearm (95%). Hunting hours and every other rule apply.

mc-skills-03.q: At 7 a.m., before the sun reaches your slope, which way is the slope air usually moving?
options: Downhill, still draining from the night
mc-skills-03.why: Slope air drains down at night and flips up soon after the sun strikes the slope (75%, Fire Weather handbook). Before the sun hits, it is often still sinking.

mc-skills-03.q: Where should you NOT sit to glass?
options: On the windward side of a ridge
Just over the crest on the lee side
mc-skills-03.why: Just behind a crest the air can tumble back uphill in a lee eddy (70%). Your scent goes everywhere.

mc-skills-03.q: Forecast says 20 km/h. What do you likely feel at head height in the open?
mc-skills-03.why: Forecasts are for 10 m up; at 2 m wind may be only 50 to 70% of it (90%, Royal Meteorological Society). In timber, less again.

mc-skills-03.q: Is the 297 million deer receptor figure a measured fact?
options: No: it is an early 1990s estimate; experts think it may be low and no one is sure
mc-skills-03.why: Outdoor Life (2026) calls it an oft cited stat from the early 90s (65%). What matters: the deer's nose is far better than yours.

mc-skills-03.q: The wind is wrong for your planned seat on the morning of the hunt. What do old hands do?
options: Go to the B seat planned for that wind
mc-skills-03.why: Plan an A and B seat for each likely wind and never force A (Tip). No product beats a bad wind.

mc-skills-04.q: What is the difference between still hunting and stalking?
options: Still hunting is slow walking to find an animal; stalking is closing on one you have already seen
Stalking is sitting in a blind
mc-skills-04.why: Still hunting finds; stalking closes in (70%). Both are mostly standing still.

mc-skills-04.q: A buck lifts his head and stares your way mid step. What do you do?
options: Freeze, even on one leg, until he goes back to feeding
mc-skills-04.why: Movement is what deer catch best (75%). Weight back lets you freeze mid step (Tip).

mc-skills-04.q: Which colour is the worst to wear around deer?
mc-skills-04.why: Deer lack the red cone; they likely tell blue from red but not orange from green. Blue stands out (75%, National Deer Association).

options: Low ground the animal cannot see into, where you can move faster
mc-skills-04.why: Fast where it cannot see you, slow where it can (Tip). The Hunt Map's What can I see tool helps find it.

mc-skills-04.q: You and your brother stalk a deer together. Best way?
options: One moves while the other watches and signals, then swap
Both run to the next cover
mc-skills-04.why: Two shapes moving double the risk. One moves, one watches, hand signals only (Tip).

mc-skills-05.q: When are you most likely to fall from a tree stand?
options: Climbing up or down, or moving in and out of the stand
mc-skills-05.why: About 60% of falls happen climbing or at the transition into the stand (70%, Iowa DNR with Tree Stand Safety Awareness). Clip in before your feet leave the ground.

mc-skills-05.q: How does the firearm get into a tree stand?
options: Unloaded, on a haul line after you are clipped in
mc-skills-05.why: Wisconsin DNR: always use a haul line to raise and lower your unloaded firearm (80%).

mc-skills-05.q: Which call is legal for mule deer in BC?
mc-skills-05.why: Recorded or electronic calls are unlawful except for wolf, coyote, cougar, lynx, bobcat and Schedule C birds (99%, item 41). Mouth calls are not recorded or electronic (95%, my reading).

mc-skills-05.q: Coyote calling: wind in your face or crosswind?
options: Both are taught by experienced callers; it is your call. Both agree to watch the downwind side
mc-skills-05.why: Outdoor Canada (Wilson) prefers calling from downwind; Grand View (Nemnich) and Bass Pro (Wood) prefer a crosswind (65%). All agree coyotes try to come from downwind.

mc-skills-05.q: Hanging in a harness after a fall: how fast can suspension trauma become dangerous?
mc-skills-05.why: Wisconsin DNR: suspension trauma can occur in under 20 minutes and can be fatal (80%). Carry a relief strap and your phone on you.

mc-skills-06.q: With a 100 m zero and 150 gr loads, how far does your .308 drop at 300 m?
mc-skills-06.why: About 48 cm low at 300 m, 28 cm at 250 m, 13 cm at 200 m (75%, Hunt Mentor model from Federal data). That is twice a deer's vital zone.

mc-skills-06.q: A 20 km/h wind blows straight across at 250 m. About how far does the 150 gr bullet drift?
mc-skills-06.why: About 27 cm (75%). Ignored, it puts the bullet out of a 20 to 25 cm vital zone. Get closer or pass.

mc-skills-06.q: Rangefinder says 250 m on a 30 degree downhill slope. What do you hold for?
mc-skills-06.why: Flat distance = slope distance × cosine of the angle: 250 × 0.866 = 217 m (95% arithmetic). Hold for 250 and you hit high.
Hunter education ranks prone, then sitting, then kneeling, then standing (85%). Lower and more supported is steadier.

mc-skills-06.q: Snow on the ground, bright sun behind you. Your eye guess of the distance will likely be:
options: Too short: the animal looks nearer than it is
mc-skills-06.why: Bright light, the sun behind you and snow make objects seem nearer (80%, Canadian Army fieldcraft), so the real distance is farther than you think. Range it.

mc-skills-07.q: Where do you aim on a broadside deer?
options: Up the back of the near front leg, one third up the chest
mc-skills-07.why: Hunter education: find the near front leg, go up its back edge, one third up the chest. Both lungs and the top of the heart (85%).

mc-skills-07.q: A buck stands quartering toward you. What does a beginner do?
options: Shoot the centre of the chest
Wait for him to turn broadside or quartering away
mc-skills-07.why: Quartering toward means bone in the way; a bullet can deflect off the shoulder (85%). Wait for the turn (Tip).

mc-skills-07.q: Where do you aim on a moose compared with a deer?
options: Same spot behind the front leg; aim lower than the hump suggests
mc-skills-07.why: Same rule, behind the front leg one third up. The hump fools hunters into shooting above the lungs (65 to 85%).

mc-skills-07.q: A deer stands on a ridge top with sky behind it. What do you do?
mc-skills-07.why: Hunter education: do not shoot at a skylined animal (85%). Sky is never a backstop.

mc-skills-07.q: What is the honest answer to shooting through brush?
options: No bullet reliably goes through brush; a twig can throw the shot. Clear lane or no shot
mc-skills-07.why: Tests find no true brush busting bullet (70%, American Hunter). Wait for a clear lane.

mc-skills-08.q: A deer hunches up after the shot and walks off slowly. What do you do?
options: Mark the spot and back out for hours: likely a gut hit
Shoot again at it in the timber
mc-skills-08.why: Hunched back and a slow walk often mean a gut hit (70%). Every source says hours; how many differs (4 to 12 hours, your call) (70%).

mc-skills-08.q: What is the first thing to do after the shot?
options: Watch it, then mark where it stood and where you last saw it
mc-skills-08.why: Watch the reaction and mark both spots before you move. Everything looks different from over there (Tip; flagging 70%).

mc-skills-08.q: Pink, frothy blood with bubbles means?
mc-skills-08.why: Bright pink, frothy blood is a lung hit sign (65 to 70%). Dark with no bubbles suggests liver; green matter suggests gut.

mc-skills-08.q: The blood trail stops. What next?
options: Back to the last flag, circle 10 m then 20 m, then search in lanes about 10 m apart
mc-skills-08.why: Clotting often stops a trail (60%). Go back to the last sure sign, circle, then grid in lanes about 10 m apart in sight of each other (70%).

mc-skills-08.q: It is 20 minutes after legal light ended. Can you keep tracking with your rifle and a headlamp?
options: No: following on the trail with a firearm is hunting, and hunting with a light or after hours is unlawful
Yes, if your brother holds the light
mc-skills-08.why: Hunt includes following on the trail with a firearm (95%). Hunting after hours or with a light is unlawful (95%). Ask a conservation officer about tracking with no firearm (VERIFY).

mc-skills-09.q: What is the target temperature for game meat, as fast as you can?
mc-skills-09.why: Below 4°C slows bacteria; 4 to 60°C is the danger zone where they can double every 20 minutes (80%).

mc-skills-09.q: It is 15°C and sunny. Your deer is quartered. How do you carry the meat to the truck?
options: In cloth game bags, in shade, then to a cooler the same day
mc-skills-09.why: Plastic and tarps hold heat in (80%). Cloth bags let the meat breathe and form a dry crust.

mc-skills-09.q: Does the gutless method excuse you from taking the neck and rib meat?
options: No: neck, ribs, four quarters and loins all come out
mc-skills-09.why: Edible portions for big game are the neck, ribs, four quarters and loins (95%, page 3), whatever method you use.

mc-skills-09.q: What do you do with the deer's tail and evidence of sex?
options: Cut them off to save weight
Leave them naturally attached as the Rule Book says; cut around, never through
mc-skills-09.why: Deer: the unskinned tail plus the sex evidence stay naturally attached (99%, page 15, Rule Book: after the kill).

mc-skills-09.q: You must leave the carcass for the night with guts still in. Okay?
options: No: guts left in overnight spoil the meat regardless of temperature. Gut it or take the meat off
mc-skills-09.why: Alaska Department of Fish and Game: leaving guts in overnight will cause spoilage regardless of outside temperature (80%).

mc-skills-10.q: You and your brother walk side by side. A deer runs between you. What do you do?
options: No shot: the middle is a no shot zone
mc-skills-10.why: Each hunter shoots only in about 45 degrees straight ahead; the middle and behind are no shot zones (75%, hunter education).

mc-skills-10.q: A tourniquet goes on how far above a limb wound?
options: Sources differ: 5 to 8 cm or 5 to 10 cm above, heart side, never on a joint. Ask your instructor
mc-skills-10.why: American Red Cross and Stop the Bleed guides say 5 to 8 cm (70%); the 2012 Canadian Red Cross sheet says 5 to 10 cm (75%). Both: above the wound, heart side, off joints. Your call with your instructor.

mc-skills-10.q: Your partner is shivering hard, then stops shivering and gets drowsy. What does that mean?
options: Moderate hypothermia: handle gently, keep horizontal, wrap, warm the trunk, get help
mc-skills-10.why: Shivering slows or stops in moderate hypothermia (75%, Wilderness Medical Society). Shivering that stops is an emergency.

mc-skills-10.q: You realise you are lost in timber under cloud. First step?
options: Walk fast downhill to a creek
STOP: Stop, Think, Observe, Plan. Doubt means stay and call early
mc-skills-10.why: STOP (75%, AdventureSmart). Under cloud people walk in circles (75%), and creeks drop into ravines (75%, North Shore Rescue).

mc-skills-10.q: No cell signal and your brother is badly hurt. Best tool?
options: Satellite SOS: a satellite messenger or a phone with satellite SOS, from open sky
mc-skills-10.why: 911 first if any tower reaches you (75%). Where phones do not work, a satellite messenger or satellite SOS phone can reach help (65 to 85%).

mc-nav-01.q: How many ground search and rescue tasks did BC have in 2022?
mc-nav-01.why: BCSARA's 2022 Year in Review lists 1,510 ground search and rescue tasks (95%). Hiking was the biggest slice at about 41% (80%).

mc-nav-01.q: Why do hunters usually get lost?
options: They follow an animal or blood trail intently through thick brush
mc-nav-01.why: Koester's lost person research: hunters usually get lost following game through dense brush (65%). Eyes on the game, not the way back.

mc-nav-01.q: "One more ridge, we came this far." Which FACETS trap is that?
mc-nav-01.why: Consistency: being highly committed to a goal even as things get worse (80%, avalanche.org). The hunter example is my application (Tip).

mc-nav-01.q: Which of these is on BCSARA's top 10 worst things you can do?
options: Not leaving a trip plan with a trusted emergency contact
mc-nav-01.why: Number 2 on the list (95%). A trip plan tells searchers where to start and when to worry.

mc-nav-01.q: When should you call 911 if you are lost?
options: Only when it is fully dark
As soon as you know you are lost or injured
mc-nav-01.why: North Shore Rescue: dial 911 as soon as you know you're lost or injured; there is no cost for rescue (75%). Early calls find you before conditions get worse.

mc-nav-02.q: What is a backstop in the box method?
options: A big line you never cross, which tells you that you went too far
mc-nav-02.why: Baseline you walk back to, handrails on the sides, a backstop beyond the area. Hit the backstop and you know you overshot (Tip, built on orienteering catching features, 85%).

mc-nav-02.q: You leave the truck. What two things do you do first?
options: Load the rifle and start walking
Drop a Parking waypoint and note the escape bearing to the baseline
mc-nav-02.why: The pin lets the phone lead you back (99%, app). The escape bearing works when the phone dies (Tip).

mc-nav-02.q: How often should you find yourself on the map in timber?
options: Every 15 to 30 minutes, more often in timber and fog
mc-nav-02.why: Small direction errors add up without landmarks (75%, Max Planck). A rhythm catches the drift early (Tip).

mc-nav-02.q: About how fast do you walk off trail?
mc-nav-02.why: Aitken: 4 km an hour off path, 5 on roads (75%). Add an hour per 600 m of climb (Naismith, 75%).

mc-nav-02.q: You are not sure which creek fork this is. What now?
options: Walk faster to the next one
Stop. Go back to your last sure point if you can see it or follow your track
mc-nav-02.why: First doubt, full stop. Early the fix is small. North Shore Rescue: wandering usually takes you farther from your last known point (75%).

mc-nav-03.q: On a 1:50,000 map, how far is 1 cm on the ground?
mc-nav-03.why: 1:50,000 means 1 cm on the map is 50,000 cm, which is 500 m. So 2 cm is 1 km (99%, maths).

mc-nav-03.q: 20 m contour lines sit 1 mm apart on a 1:50,000 map. How steep?
mc-nav-03.why: 1 mm is 50 m on the ground. 20 m up over 50 m across is about 22 degrees (95%, my calculation).

mc-nav-03.q: Contour lines make a V where they cross a creek. Which way does the V point?
mc-nav-03.why: USGS: contours crossing a stream form a V that points upstream (95%). Water flows the other way.

mc-nav-03.q: How do you read a UTM grid reference?
mc-nav-03.why: Read right, then up: easting first, northing second (95%).

mc-nav-03.q: What is the declination near Heffley Creek in October 2026?
mc-nav-03.why: NOAA World Magnetic Model: 15.17 degrees east at Heffley Creek, 15.20 at Mission (95%). East declination: magnetic least.

mc-nav-04.q: Taking a bearing off the map, what do you do with the needle?
options: Box it in the shed first
Ignore it while on the map
mc-nav-04.why: On the map only the ring's north lines and the map's north lines matter (95%). The needle comes in when you lift the compass to walk.

mc-nav-04.q: You walked out on a bearing of 300. What is the back bearing?
You are on a long road and can see one named peak off to the side. How do you find where you are?
options: Take a bearing to the peak; where its back bearing crosses the road is you
mc-nav-04.why: On a handrail, one bearing is enough (Tip, from resection, 85%).

mc-nav-04.q: The truck is on a road 2 km away. Why aim off to one side?
options: A small error means you won't know which way to turn; aim off and you do
mc-nav-04.why: Aiming off is deliberate (85%, Little Book). At 2 km a 5 degree error is about 175 m, so aim off 200 to 300 m (Tip).

mc-nav-04.q: You forgot to set declination near Kamloops. After 1 km, about how far off are you?
mc-nav-04.why: 15 degrees of error is about 268 m per km (98%, maths).

mc-nav-05.q: How do you orient a map with a compass?
options: Turn yourself until the needle points at you
Turn the map until its north lines run with the needle
Point the map at the sun
mc-nav-05.why: Turn the map, not yourself: north lines with the needle (95%, Little Book of Orienteering Techniques).

mc-nav-05.q: In terrain association, what do you match first?
options: Big shapes: ridges, saddles, valleys, lakes
mc-nav-05.why: Big shapes are on the map and visible from far off. Small things rarely are (Tip).

mc-nav-05.q: Two of three features match, but the third is on the wrong side. What does that mean?
options: You are probably somewhere else: don't bend the map
mc-nav-05.why: If one feature does not fit, you are probably not where you think (Tip). Check with a bearing or the phone.

mc-nav-05.q: Mid October near Heffley Creek, about where does the sun rise?
mc-nav-05.why: My calculation: 103 degrees on 15 October, moving to 119 by mid November (85%). In fall it rises south of east.

mc-nav-05.q: Shadow stick: which mark is west?
mc-nav-05.why: The shadow tip moves west to east, so the first mark is west (60%). It is a rough check only.

mc-nav-06.q: No cell signal on the hill. Will the Hunt Map still show where you are?
options: Yes, the GPS dot works, and the map shows if you saved the area offline first
mc-nav-06.why: GPS needs no cell network (95%). Map tiles do, so save the area in Offline Maps at home (99%, app).

mc-nav-06.q: What does Back to start show in Go & Track?
options: Distance and heading back to where you started recording
mc-nav-06.why: For example 1.9 km, heading 214 degrees (SW); the green dot marks the start (99%, app).

mc-nav-06.q: You only dropped a truck pin, no track. How do you get a heading to it?
options: Tools, Draw and measure, Measure from your dot to the pin
mc-nav-06.why: Measure shows the distance and bearing of the leg (99% for the tool; Tip for this use).

mc-nav-06.q: What does a personal locator beacon do that a messenger does not need?
options: Sends SOS only, with no monthly plan for SOS
mc-nav-06.why: A PLB is one way SOS on 406 MHz, no plan needed for SOS (60%). A messenger texts both ways on a paid plan (65%).

mc-nav-06.q: Phone shut off at minus 5°C showing 40%. First move?
options: STOP, then warm it inside your jacket for about 15 minutes
mc-nav-06.why: Apple: cold can shut it off and it returns to normal when warm (95%). Don't charge a frozen battery (75%).

mc-nav-07.q: You realise you don't know where you are. First thing?
options: Walk faster to find a landmark
mc-nav-07.why: AdventureSmart teaches STOP (75%). Moving usually makes it harder for searchers and more dangerous for you.

mc-nav-07.q: Why do searchers want you to stay put?
options: Double the distance you wander and the search area is 4 times bigger
mc-nav-07.why: Area grows with the square of the radius (95%). Staying near your last known point keeps the search small (75%).

mc-nav-07.q: Which way do lost hunters tend to drift?
mc-nav-07.why: Koester's lost person data, via Popular Science: hunters tend to go downhill and off trail (65%). Draws can end in creeks and cliffs (75%, NSR).

mc-nav-07.q: What do you say first on a 911 call when lost?
options: Where you are: coordinates, and their format
mc-nav-07.why: Location first, then who, what happened, what you have, and your plan (Tip). Dial 911 and ask for police (75%, NSR).

mc-nav-07.q: You hear a searcher's whistle. What do you do?
options: Three whistle blasts back and stay where you are
Walk toward it fast through the timber
mc-nav-07.why: Answer searchers and stay put (70%, Hug a Tree). Three of anything means help (75%).

mc-nav-08.q: When should you decide to spend the night?
options: About an hour before dark, while you can still build
mc-nav-08.why: Shelter and wood take time and light (65% that debris shelters take hours; the 1 hour rule is a Tip).

mc-nav-08.q: A great roof over bare cold ground. What is wrong?
options: The ground pulls heat by conduction: insulate under you first
mc-nav-08.why: Insulation from the ground is the core of hypothermia prevention (75%, Wilderness Medical Society). Bed before roof.

mc-nav-08.q: How big is a Category 1 campfire in BC?
options: No bigger than 0.5 m high by 0.5 m wide
mc-nav-08.why: BC Wildfire Service: Category 1 is no larger than 0.5 by 0.5 m (80%). Check bans before every fire (80%).

mc-nav-08.q: Your brother stops shivering and gets drowsy and confused. What is it?
options: Moderate hypothermia: gentle, horizontal, wrap, warm the trunk, get help
mc-nav-08.why: In moderate hypothermia shivering slows or stops (75%, Wilderness Medical Society). It is an emergency.

mc-nav-08.q: Where should the whistle and lighters be?
options: In your pockets, so they stay with you if you drop the pack
mc-nav-08.why: The 10 essentials go on you, not in the truck (75%, AdventureSmart). Pockets go where you go (Tip).

mc-nav-09.q: Mid October near Heffley Creek, when does big game legal light end?
mc-nav-09.why: Legal hours end 1 hour after sunset (99%, Rule Book); sunset is about 18:08 (85%). The last legal hour is mostly dark: plan the walk out.

mc-nav-09.q: Which Hunt Map slope colour is avalanche terrain in snow?
mc-nav-09.why: Red is 30 to 45 degrees (99%, app). Most avalanches start on 30 to 45 degree slopes (95%).

mc-nav-09.q: What does the first 1 in 1 10 1 warn about?
options: About 1 minute of cold shock gasping
mc-nav-09.why: Cold shock: the gasp and fast breathing for about a minute (80%). A worn PFD keeps your head up through it.

mc-nav-09.q: You ride the ATV to the trailhead. How is the rifle carried?
options: Unloaded: nothing in the chamber or an attached magazine
mc-nav-09.why: A loaded firearm in or on a motor vehicle is unlawful, and an attached loaded magazine counts as loaded (98 to 99%, Rule Book).

mc-nav-09.q: A moose with ears back and hackles up comes at you. What do you do?
options: Stand your ground like with a bear
Run and put a tree between you
mc-nav-09.why: Alaska Department of Fish and Game: it is usually a good idea to run from a moose and get a tree between you (85%). Bears and cougars are different: never run (75%).

mc-nav-10.q: In the compass triangle drill you walk 0, 120 and 240 degrees. Where should you finish?
mc-nav-10.why: Three equal legs at 120 degree turns close the triangle. Finishing within about 10 m on 300 m is about 2 degrees of error (98% maths; the pass mark is a Tip).

mc-nav-10.q: In the phone drill, why put the phone away and walk the heading on the compass?
options: It saves battery, keeps your eyes up, and builds the habit for when the phone dies
The compass is more accurate than GPS
mc-nav-10.why: A track keeps the screen on (99%, app); eyes on a tree are safer than eyes on a screen (Tip).

mc-nav-10.q: During the lost scenario drill, should you dial 911 to practise?
options: No: say the script out loud, coordinates first, but do not dial
mc-nav-10.why: 911 is for real emergencies. Practise the words, not the call (Tip).

mc-nav-10.q: What is the declination to set at Heffley Creek and Mission?
mc-nav-10.why: NOAA World Magnetic Model, October 2026: 15.17 E at Heffley Creek, 15.20 E at Mission (95%).

mc-nav-10.q: Before a real hunt, which single habit from this Masterclass protects you most if everything else fails?
options: A trip plan with a call 911 if time, left with someone
mc-nav-10.why: BCSARA lists no trip plan among the 10 worst things you can do (95%). It tells searchers where and when to start.

mc-black-tailed-deer-01.q: A deer bounds off through salal. The top of its tail is dark brown almost all the way down, with a small white rump patch. What is it?
mc-black-tailed-deer-01.why: A tail dark on top for most of its length with a small rump patch is the black tail mark (90%, BC deer account). A mule deer has a thin white tail with only a black tip and a big rump patch.

mc-black-tailed-deer-01.q: MU 2-18, 25 November. A yearling with two short spikes, no forks. Legal?
options: Yes, a deer with visible bony antlers is a buck, and the 2-18 row says Bucks
mc-black-tailed-deer-01.why: Page 4: a buck bears visible bony antlers. Page 28: 2-8, 2-18 and 2-19 are Bucks rows, not 4 point rows (99%). About 90% of yearling black tails are spikes.

mc-black-tailed-deer-01.q: A deer flicks up a wide tail showing a big white flag. Where you are, what does that mean?
options: Probably a white tailed deer: no season in Region 2, no shot
A black tailed buck in alarm: shoot
mc-black-tailed-deer-01.why: A wide white flag is the white tail sign. Region 2 has no white tailed deer season (99%, pages 14 and 27). A black tail can raise its tail too (80%), so if you cannot be sure, do not shoot.

mc-black-tailed-deer-01.q: About how heavy is an adult black tailed buck?
mc-black-tailed-deer-01.why: BC deer account: 48 to 90 kg for bucks, 40 to 65 kg for does (90%). Smaller than a mule deer buck at 68 to 113 kg.

mc-black-tailed-deer-01.q: From 2020 to 2024, about how many hunter days did each deer take in MU 2-18?
mc-black-tailed-deer-01.why: Harvest statistics: 216 deer from 5,304 hunter days, about 24.6 days per deer (90%, computed). The Region 2 average was about 13.5.

mc-black-tailed-deer-02.q: It snowed hard overnight, about 50 cm up high. Where are deer more likely?
options: The middle of a big fresh clearcut
Under big conifer timber and on steep south to west slopes
mc-black-tailed-deer-02.why: A 50 cm snowfall left about 5 cm under 70% conifer cover and about 50 cm in a clearcut; walking in the clearcut cost about 500% more (90%, Nyberg and Janz). Winter range is old growth and steep south to west slopes (90%).

mc-black-tailed-deer-02.q: In spring and summer, which places do coast black tails use often?
mc-black-tailed-deer-02.why: The BC deer account: black tails make frequent use of logged habitats during spring and summer (90%).

mc-black-tailed-deer-02.q: In order U-2-006, which slope directions count as capable deer winter range?
options: 135 to 285 degrees: south east through south to west
mc-black-tailed-deer-02.why: The order defines capable winter range on warm aspects 135 to 285 degrees with slopes of 40 to 100% (95%, read directly).

mc-black-tailed-deer-02.q: About what share of deer migrate in the deep snowpack zone on the south coast?
mc-black-tailed-deer-02.why: Nyberg and Janz: about 20 to 25% migrate in the moderate zone and 70% or more in the deep zone (90%).

mc-black-tailed-deer-02.q: Which is a winter food of coast black tails?
mc-black-tailed-deer-02.why: Winter and early spring foods: Douglas fir, western redcedar, red huckleberry, salal, deer fern and tree lichens (90%). Sagebrush and bitterbrush are interior mule deer foods.

mc-black-tailed-deer-03.q: When are black tailed deer most active?
options: Near dawn and dusk, though they can move any time
mc-black-tailed-deer-03.why: WDFW: deer are most active near dawn and dusk and may be active at any time of day (80%). The rut adds daylight movement.

mc-black-tailed-deer-03.q: Sunset is 4:30 p.m. A buck steps out at 5:20 p.m. Legal to shoot?
mc-black-tailed-deer-03.why: No hunting from 1 hour after sunset to 1 hour before sunrise (99%, page 11, item 38). 4:30 plus 1 hour is 5:30 p.m. Be sure of the target in fading light.

mc-black-tailed-deer-03.q: Good security cover hides about how much of a deer at 60 m?
mc-black-tailed-deer-03.why: Research cited by Nyberg and Janz: the most effective security cover hides about 90% of a deer at 60 m or less (85%). Look for parts: an ear, a leg, a tail.

mc-black-tailed-deer-03.q: Which sense should you plan around first?
options: Smell: keep the wind in your face
mc-black-tailed-deer-03.why: Smell is the strongest deer sense (85%). Blaze orange looks dull to deer (75%); motion and noise matter more than colour.

mc-black-tailed-deer-04.q: On Vancouver Island, when did most black tailed does conceive?
mc-black-tailed-deer-04.why: Nyberg and Janz, citing Thomas 1970: most does conceive from 15 November to 5 December (90%). That window sits inside the 2-18 and 2-19 buck season, which ends 15 December (99%, page 28).

mc-black-tailed-deer-04.q: How long is a doe receptive?
mc-black-tailed-deer-04.why: Does are receptive for a short period, about a day; if not bred they cycle again 22 to 29 days later (90%).

mc-black-tailed-deer-04.q: You see a buck circling another with stiff steps, back arched, head low, tail flicking. What is it?
mc-black-tailed-deer-04.why: The BC deer account describes exactly this as a dominance display before the rut (90%). The smaller buck often bolts.

mc-black-tailed-deer-04.q: In the rut a doe walks out and keeps looking back. Best move?
options: Wait and watch behind her for a buck
mc-black-tailed-deer-04.why: Bucks tend does in the rut (90%). Waiting is a Tip. And the doe is never legal in 2-8, 2-18 or 2-19: bucks only (99%, page 28).

mc-black-tailed-deer-05.q: You watch a 300 m wide fresh cutblock at dawn. Where should most of your attention go?
options: The very centre of the cut
The band within about 100 m of the timber edges
mc-black-tailed-deer-05.why: Collared coast deer concentrated their clearcut use within 100 m of cover (90%, Nyberg and Janz). Watching the edge band is the Tip.

mc-black-tailed-deer-05.q: Your brother wants to drive the truck slowly along a spur to push deer toward you. Legal?
options: Yes, if the road is open
No. Using a motor vehicle to herd or harass wildlife is unlawful; pushes are on foot only
mc-black-tailed-deer-05.why: Page 11, item 25: unlawful to use a power boat, aircraft or motor vehicle to herd or harass wildlife (99%). Walk the push.

mc-black-tailed-deer-05.q: It is raining hard. A buck stands quartering toward you at 180 m in brush. What does the rain change?
options: Rain can erase blood fast, so only a sure shot; pass this one
mc-black-tailed-deer-05.why: Rain can erase a blood trail within about an hour (Tip). Quartering to through brush at 180 m is not a sure shot for a first season (Tip).

mc-black-tailed-deer-05.q: Why does hunting pressure barely change coast deer numbers, according to the coastal handbook?
options: There are no hunters on the coast
Coast forests hold so much security cover
Deer move to the interior in fall
mc-black-tailed-deer-05.why: Nyberg and Janz: because of the abundance of security cover in coastal ecosystems, hunting has little effect on black tailed deer herds compared with habitat and predation (90%).

mc-black-tailed-deer-05.q: You are walking the Weaver Lake FSR during the season and see a legal buck inside the 400 m band. May you shoot?
options: No, it is closed to everyone
Yes, if lawfully hunting, never on or across the road, with a safe backstop
mc-black-tailed-deer-05.why: Page 27: the discharge ban there applies unless lawfully hunting (99%; my reading 90%). Page 10: never shoot on or across a road allowance (99%).

mc-black-tailed-deer-06.q: You shoot a buck in light rain; heavier rain is forecast in an hour. It ran hard and low. What do you do?
options: Mark the spots, wait about 30 minutes, then track carefully before the rain
Go home and come back tomorrow
mc-black-tailed-deer-06.why: A hard low run often means heart or lungs (70%); about 30 minutes is the agreed wait (70%). Rain can erase blood within about an hour, so go sooner (Tip).

mc-black-tailed-deer-06.q: Your buck is down. What comes first?
mc-black-tailed-deer-06.why: Cancel the species licence immediately after the kill, before you handle the deer (99%, page 11).

mc-black-tailed-deer-06.q: It is raining and 6°C. Best way to hang the quarters?
options: In game bags, under a tarp roof with an air gap, off the ground
On the ground under the truck
mc-black-tailed-deer-06.why: No plastic or tarps on meat before it is chilled (80%, WDFW). A tarp as a roof with an air gap keeps rain off while air moves (80%). At 6°C, also add ice to get below 4°C (Tip).

mc-black-tailed-deer-06.q: Do you take a Region 2 black tailed buck to a compulsory inspection?
options: No. Region 2 compulsory inspection is for mountain goat and cougar
mc-black-tailed-deer-06.why: Page 28: Region 2 compulsory inspection covers mountain goat and cougar, not deer (99%).

mc-black-tailed-deer-06.q: Why do brushy shots matter more on a black tail?
options: The chest is small and brush can deflect the bullet
mc-black-tailed-deer-06.why: A black tail's chest is about 57 cm high (90%) and the vital zone about 20 to 25 cm (75%). Brush can deflect a bullet; find a clear lane or wait (Tip).

options: Behind the bolt handle, right side
On the left of the receiver
mc-cz457-01.why: The CZ manual's Fig. 1 and Fig. 4 show the safety behind the bolt handle on the right. The bolt catch is the part on the left.
CZ manual page 5: press the magazine catch located at the front of the magazine in a rearward direction.

mc-cz457-01.q: What does closing the bolt do?
options: Feeds a cartridge into the chamber and cocks the striker
mc-cz457-01.why: CZ manual page 6: pushing the bolt forward and turning it down inserts the cartridge into the chamber and cocks the striker mechanism.

mc-cz457-01.q: Which part does the Criminal Code treat as the firearm itself?
mc-cz457-01.why: Criminal Code s. 2: a firearm includes any frame or receiver of a barrelled weapon.

mc-cz457-01.q: A Varmint MTR has a match chamber. What does CZ recommend?
options: Match ammunition; non standard high power or longer cartridges are not recommended
mc-cz457-01.why: CZ manual page 5: match chambers are cut to the CIP minimum, so match ammunition is recommended and non standard ammunition is not.

mc-cz457-02.q: The safety is pushed back and a white dot shows. What state is the rifle in?
options: Safety ON: the trigger is locked
mc-cz457-02.why: CZ manual page 7: shift the safety backward until the white dot is uncovered; this locks the trigger mechanism. It says nothing about whether the rifle is loaded.

mc-cz457-02.q: Can you open the bolt to unload with the safety ON?
mc-cz457-02.why: CZ lists pulling the bolt out even with the safety engaged as a feature for safe unloading (manual page 4).

mc-cz457-02.q: The cocking indicator is flush with the plug. The rifle is:
options: Not cocked; it may still have a round in the chamber, so PROVE it
mc-cz457-02.why: The indicator only shows whether the striker is cocked (manual page 7). Only PROVE tells you it is unloaded.

options: Keep it pointed safe and wait 30 seconds
mc-cz457-02.why: CZ rule 19: a hangfire fires within 30 seconds, so hold it pointed in a safe direction and wait, then eject and examine the cartridge.

mc-cz457-02.q: Walking back to the truck, what must be true before the CZ goes in?
options: Magazine out of the rifle and chamber empty
mc-cz457-02.why: BC item 28 bans a loaded firearm in or on a vehicle, and loaded includes a cartridge in a detachable magazine attached to the rifle (synopsis pages 3 and 11).

mc-cz457-03.q: Loading the magazine, where does each cartridge go first?
options: On the follower with the base just ahead of the lips, then pressed down and back
mc-cz457-03.why: CZ manual page 5: place the cartridge with the base just forward of the retaining lips, then press it down and back until it touches the rear edge.
CZ manual page 6: remove the magazine, then open the bolt and check the cartridge has been extracted. Opening the bolt first would feed another round on closing.

mc-cz457-03.q: Is a 10 round magazine legal in your CZ 457 .22 LR?
options: No, 5 is the limit for all rifles
Yes: the 5 round rule is for semi automatic centre fire firearms and excludes rimfire magazines
mc-cz457-03.why: SOR/98-462 Part 4 s. 3(1)(a)(ii) limits magazines for semi automatic firearms; s. 3(2)(a)(i) excludes magazines for rimfire firearms (95%, my reading).

mc-cz457-03.q: The chamber is empty but the magazine is in the rifle. Can it ride in the truck?
options: No: a cartridge in an attached detachable magazine makes it loaded under BC law
mc-cz457-03.why: Synopsis page 3 defines a loaded firearm to include a detachable magazine inside or attached to the firearm. Item 28 bans loaded firearms in or on vehicles.

mc-cz457-04.q: At what distance does CZ zero the CZ 457 iron sights?
mc-cz457-04.why: CZ manual page 8: the sights have been zeroed at 50 m in the factory.

mc-cz457-04.q: Which sight adjusts elevation on the CZ 457?
options: The front sight, with its pair of screws
mc-cz457-04.why: CZ manual page 8: rear sight for windage, front sight for elevation using the pair of front screws (Fig. 9). The rear slider also sets range marks from 25 to 200 m.

mc-cz457-04.q: What does the scope mount onto?
options: The 11 mm dovetail on the receiver, or a Weaver rail
mc-cz457-04.why: CZ manual page 8: install the scope on the 11 mm dovetail using mounts, or via a Weaver rail.

mc-cz457-04.q: Your group is 3.6 cm low at 50 m. Quarter MOA clicks. About how many clicks up?
mc-cz457-04.why: A quarter MOA click is about 0.36 cm at 50 m. 3.6 / 0.36 = 10.

mc-cz457-04.q: Why finish the zero at 50 m, not 25 m?
options: Iron sights only work at 50 m
A 50 m zero keeps the bullet within about 1.5 cm from 15 to 55 m
mc-cz457-04.why: The Hunt Mentor model shows a 50 m zero is dead on from 15 to 55 m (75%), the range most grouse shots happen at.

mc-cz457-05.q: What dot size at 50 m matches a deer's 20 cm vital zone at 200 m?
mc-cz457-05.why: 20 cm x 50 / 200 = 5 cm. Same angle, a quarter of the distance, a quarter of the size.

mc-cz457-05.q: In the cold shot game, which shot counts?
options: Only the first shot of the day
mc-cz457-05.why: The deer gets your first, cold shot. The game trains that one (Tip).

mc-cz457-05.q: What does a snap cap do in the flinch game?
options: Shows a flinch when the striker falls and nothing fires
mc-cz457-05.why: With no shot, any dip of the muzzle is your flinch. CZ also names snap caps for dry training (manual page 5).

mc-cz457-05.q: A paper grouse is pinned high on a tree with sky behind. In the grouse walk you:
options: Call no shot and score the call
Shoot only with a head shot
mc-cz457-05.why: No earth behind, no shot. CZ rule 15: know what is behind the target; a bullet can carry hundreds of metres.

mc-cz457-06.q: Which of these may you hunt with your CZ .22 in BC?
mc-cz457-06.why: Page 13 note 2: rimfire for grouse, ptarmigan or turkey only among game birds. Ducks: shotgun or class D bow only.
Page 28: the hare season covers MUs 2-5 to 2-19 only.

mc-cz457-06.q: You walk a strip within 150 m of Highway 7 east of Mission. Can you shoot a grouse with the .22?
options: No. It is shot only: shotgun, no rifle
mc-cz457-06.why: The Closed Areas Regulation makes that strip shot only (99%, via the Region 2 lesson).

mc-cz457-06.q: What is the Region 2 daily limit for grouse (sooty, ruffed, spruce together)?
mc-cz457-06.why: Page 28: 10 a day, 30 in possession, all three kinds together.

mc-cz457-06.q: Latest legal time to shoot a grouse?
mc-cz457-06.why: Item 38, page 11: no hunting game except migratory birds from one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise.

mc-cz457-07.q: From which end does the CZ manual say to put the rod in?
mc-cz457-07.why: CZ manual page 10: rod and brush go in from the chamber to prevent wear or damage to the muzzle.

mc-cz457-07.q: Can you use bore solvent on the bolt and trigger?
options: No: it can stay in joints and cause corrosion
mc-cz457-07.why: CZ manual page 10: never use the bore cleaning agent on other parts; it can remain in the joints and cause corrosion.

mc-cz457-07.q: Your CZ got rained on but you did not shoot it. Clean it?
options: Yes: CZ says clean it if it gets wet
mc-cz457-07.why: CZ manual page 9 lists if you get your rifle wet as a time to clean.

mc-cz457-07.q: What does CZ say to do right before shooting a stored rifle?
options: Add more oil to the bore
Pull a dry patch through the barrel
mc-cz457-07.why: CZ manual page 10: before shooting always pull through the barrel with a dry patch.

mc-cz457-08.q: How far does CZ say you should strip the CZ 457 for routine care?
mc-cz457-08.why: CZ manual page 9: magazine out, safety off, open the bolt, press the bolt catch and pull the bolt out. No further disassembly; anything more goes to a gunsmith.
The manual's Fig. 10 shows the bolt catch on the left of the receiver.

mc-cz457-08.q: What torque does CZ give for the stock screws?
mc-cz457-08.why: CZ manual page 9: tighten stock screws 73 and 74 to 3.5 Nm.

mc-cz457-08.q: After putting the bolt back, what is the safety check?
options: Cycle the bolt and safety on the empty rifle: it must not fire
mc-cz457-08.why: CZ manual page 7: open and close the bolt repeatedly and move the safety on and off on the unloaded rifle; it must not discharge.

mc-cz457-09.q: What holds a CZ 457 barrel in the receiver?
options: Two barrel screws at the front of the receiver
mc-cz457-09.why: The parts list shows Barrel Screw (2x), and the all4shooters test describes two front screws that retain the barrel.

mc-cz457-09.q: Which change can make your CZ a prohibited firearm?
options: Cutting it so the barrel is under 457 mm
mc-cz457-09.why: Criminal Code s. 84: a rifle adapted by sawing, cutting or any other alteration to under 660 mm, or with a barrel under 457 mm, is a prohibited firearm.

mc-cz457-09.q: Screw A on the CZ trigger sets:
mc-cz457-09.why: CZ manual page 7: set screws A (pull) and B (travel after firing), with the stock removed; screw C in the trigger sets travel before firing.

mc-cz457-09.q: What is the standard trigger's adjustable range?
mc-cz457-09.why: CZ manual page 7: standard trigger 8 to 15 N, set at the factory to 11.1 to 14 N.

mc-cz457-09.q: After any trigger adjustment, what must you do?
options: The safety check: cycle the bolt and safety on the unloaded rifle; it must not fire
mc-cz457-09.why: CZ manual page 7 gives that safety check and says the rifle must not discharge during it.

mc-cz457-10.q: Can you legally fit a suppressor to a threaded CZ 457 in Canada?
options: No: a device to muffle or stop the sound of a firearm is a prohibited device

mc-cz457-10.q: What do scope rings for the CZ 457 need to fit?
options: An 11 mm dovetail (or a Weaver rail if one is fitted)
mc-cz457-10.why: CZ manual page 8: the scope goes on the 11 mm dovetail on the receiver or via a Weaver rail.

mc-cz457-10.q: Which upgrade comes first in this course's order?
options: An ammo test with 3 or 4 kinds
mc-cz457-10.why: A .22 often shoots one brand far better than another; finding it costs a few boxes (Tip).

mc-cz457-10.q: Your friend offers a thermal scope for grouse season. In BC:
options: Illegal to use or even possess on a hunting trip
mc-cz457-10.why: Synopsis page 11, item 39: it is unlawful to use or possess infrared optics on a hunting expedition.

mc-shotgun-01.q: What are the first three things you do every time you handle a shotgun?
options: Point it safe, finger off the trigger, check it is unloaded
mc-shotgun-01.why: Muzzle safe, finger off and outside the guard, then open the action and prove it empty. Every chapter starts here.

mc-shotgun-01.q: Which part is your rear sight on a shotgun?
options: Your eye, looking along the rib
mc-shotgun-01.why: There is no rear sight. Your eye sits behind the rib and does that job, so fit matters.

mc-shotgun-01.q: You want a handier duck gun. Can you saw 6 inches off the barrel?
options: No: under 457 mm barrel or 660 mm overall makes it prohibited, and a semi auto under 470 mm is restricted. Ask a gunsmith, buy a shorter barrel made for it
Yes, if it stays over 660 mm overall
mc-shotgun-01.why: Criminal Code s. 84(1). Never cut a gun. Buy a factory barrel of a legal length instead.

mc-shotgun-01.q: How many shells may your pump or semi auto hold for ducks?
mc-shotgun-01.why: Migratory Birds Regulations s. 37(1)(c): three in magazine and chamber combined, with a one piece plug.

mc-shotgun-02.q: On a Remington 870, what does a showing red band on the safety mean?
mc-shotgun-02.why: Remington: red band hidden is safe. Red band showing means the gun will fire when the trigger is pulled.

mc-shotgun-02.q: The fore end will not come back on a cocked 870. What do you do?
options: Push the action bar lock, then pull it back
mc-shotgun-02.why: The fore end is locked when the gun is cocked. The action bar lock frees it.

mc-shotgun-02.q: Under stress you pull the fore end only half way. What happens?
options: Short stroke: the next shell may not feed and the gun jams
mc-shotgun-02.why: Rack it fully back and fully forward, every time.

mc-shotgun-02.q: You unloaded the magazine. Is the gun empty?
options: Not until you have also cleared the chamber and looked and felt both
Only if the safety is on
mc-shotgun-02.why: The chamber shell comes out first. Then look and feel the chamber and magazine. Count what came out.

mc-shotgun-03.q: What works the action in an inertia semi auto?
options: Recoil compresses a spring in the bolt, which then cycles it
mc-shotgun-03.why: Stoeger M3000: the bolt moves about 4 mm against a stiff spring under recoil; the spring then drives the bolt back.

mc-shotgun-03.q: Your inertia gun will not cycle light target loads. Why?
options: Inertia needs enough recoil; Stoeger's minimum is 1 oz, 3 dram loads
mc-shotgun-03.why: No recoil, no cycle. Use the maker's minimum load.

mc-shotgun-03.q: Should you oil the A300 gas piston and cylinder?
options: No: clean them, wipe dry; Beretta says they must not be lubricated
mc-shotgun-03.why: Oil collects residue there. Clean and dry.

mc-shotgun-03.q: How many shells does an A300 hold as shipped?
options: 3: two in the magazine plus one chambered
mc-shotgun-03.why: Beretta fits a reducer at the factory. That matches the 3 shell rule for ducks and geese.

mc-shotgun-04.q: On a Citori, when can you change which barrel fires first?
mc-shotgun-04.why: Browning: barrel selection can be made only when the safety is in the on safe position.

mc-shotgun-04.q: Your second barrel will not fire. Most likely cause?
options: You did not let the trigger go fully forward between shots
mc-shotgun-04.why: With a single trigger the mechanism resets only when the trigger returns fully forward. Gloves make it worse.

mc-shotgun-04.q: How should you close a loaded over under?
options: Lift the stock up to the barrels so the muzzles stay pointed down
Swing the barrels up to the stock
mc-shotgun-04.why: Keep the muzzles in a safe direction. Bring the stock up instead.

mc-shotgun-04.q: Why not leave fired hulls in the chambers?
options: Moisture can sweat out of plastic hulls and rust the chambers
mc-shotgun-04.why: Browning warns plastic hulls can sweat moisture onto the chamber walls.

mc-shotgun-05.why: Smaller gauge number, bigger bore. 12 gauge is about 18.5 mm, 20 gauge about 15.6 mm.

mc-shotgun-05.q: Your barrel says 3 in. Which shells are safe?
mc-shotgun-05.why: Never use a shell longer than the chamber stamped on the barrel.

mc-shotgun-05.q: A shot sounds weak and the recoil is soft. What now?
options: Stop, unload, check the barrel for something stuck
mc-shotgun-05.why: Remington: a weak shot can mean an obstruction. Firing again can burst the barrel.

mc-shotgun-05.q: Why keep 20 gauge shells away from a 12 gauge?
options: A 20 can slide into the 12 barrel and stick, and the next 12 shell can burst it

mc-shotgun-06.q: What is the standard pattern test?
options: Count holes in a duck decoy
Percent of pellets in a 30 in (76 cm) circle at 40 yd (37 m)
mc-shotgun-06.why: Trulock's standard: 30 in circle around the densest part, at 40 yd. Then repeat at your real range.

mc-shotgun-06.q: A Browning tube has three notches. What does it shoot with steel?
mc-shotgun-06.why: Three notches is modified for lead. Browning's chart says it patterns full with steel.

mc-shotgun-06.q: Where do you draw the 30 in circle?
options: Around the densest part of the pattern
mc-shotgun-06.why: Trulock: around the densest part. Where that sits versus the aim mark tells you about fit.

mc-shotgun-06.q: How many sheets per choke and shell?
mc-shotgun-06.why: One sheet can mislead. Five and an average give the real number.

mc-shotgun-06.q: Why clean and oil the choke threads?
options: Dirty dry threads can seize the tube in the barrel
mc-shotgun-06.why: Browning warns a tube can seize if the threads are not cleaned and oiled.

mc-shotgun-07.q: On a duck hunt you find one lead grouse shell in your coat. Legal?
options: No: s. 38(1) bans possessing shot other than non toxic shot in the hunting area
Yes, if you do not shoot it
mc-shotgun-07.why: Possession counts, not just use. Empty your pockets before the marsh.

mc-shotgun-07.q: Which shot is legal for ducks?
options: Steel, bismuth, tungsten or tin types
mc-shotgun-07.why: Only non toxic shot listed by the federal rules: steel, bismuth, tungsten types and tin.
TSS is about 18 g/cm3, lead about 11, bismuth about 9.7, steel about 7.8.

mc-shotgun-07.q: Is lead legal for ruffed grouse in BC?
options: Yes, unless a local restriction applies
mc-shotgun-07.why: The lead ban covers ducks, geese, coots and snipe, not upland birds. Some places, like the Delta dykes, ban lead for any purpose.

mc-shotgun-08.q: In a good mount, what moves?
options: Your head drops to the stock
The stock comes up to your cheek, then back to the shoulder
mc-shotgun-08.why: Gun to the face. Your head stays still so your eye stays the rear sight.
Start on the bird, match its speed, pull ahead and fire while moving.

mc-shotgun-08.q: You lift your head to see the bird fall. Where did the shot go?
mc-shotgun-08.why: Raising your eye is like raising a rear sight: the gun shoots high.

mc-shotgun-08.q: What do all three lead methods share?
options: The gun stops at the shot
The gun keeps moving through and after the shot
mc-shotgun-08.why: Stopping the swing is the classic miss behind.

mc-shotgun-09.q: Three of you walk a field in a line. A bird flies back between you and your neighbour. What do you do?
options: Let it go: between and behind the line is a no shot zone
mc-shotgun-09.why: Shoot only in your slice ahead. Never between or behind the line.

mc-shotgun-09.q: In a boat, the motor is pushing you to the blind. Your gun is:
mc-shotgun-09.why: BC: no loaded firearm in a boat while the motor is moving it. Federal: no hunting ducks from a moving motor boat.

mc-shotgun-09.q: Snow went into your muzzle when you slipped. What now?
options: Unload, look from the breech, push it out with a rod
Fire a shot to clear it
mc-shotgun-09.why: Remington: never shoot an obstruction out. It can burst the barrel.

mc-shotgun-09.q: How do you hand your shotgun to your brother?
options: Action open, proven empty, muzzle safe, and he checks it too
mc-shotgun-09.why: Open and empty, and both of you check. Every time.

mc-shotgun-10.q: Which grouse setup suits thick cover?
mc-shotgun-10.why: Shots are close and fast. An open choke and small shot is the common pick. Lead is legal for grouse.

mc-shotgun-10.q: Why put your farthest decoy at 35 m?
options: It is an honest range marker: inside it you shoot, past it you watch
mc-shotgun-10.why: Eyes misjudge range on birds. A ranged decoy keeps steel shots inside a killing pattern.

mc-shotgun-10.q: Do you need the plug in for grouse in BC?
options: Yes: BC requires the plug for pumps and semi autos for all hunting except slugs on big game
mc-shotgun-10.why: Page 12 of the synopsis. Leave the plug in all season.

mc-shotgun-11.q: What is the first step of every field strip?
options: Point it safe, finger off, unload and prove it empty
