mc-shotgun-11.why: All four manuals start with an unloaded, checked gun. Ammunition out of the room.

mc-shotgun-11.q: Should you oil the Beretta A300 piston and gas cylinder?
options: No: clean and wipe them; Beretta says they must not be lubricated
mc-shotgun-11.why: Oil there collects residue. Clean, dry, and check the piston glides freely.

mc-shotgun-11.q: Where does an over under get grease?
options: Hinge pin recess, barrel lugs and forearm bracket
mc-shotgun-11.why: Browning: those fitted surfaces must always have a film of grease. Not oil poured into the action.

mc-shotgun-11.q: On an M3000, what must you check when the bolt goes back together?
options: The inertia spring is seated between head and bolt
mc-shotgun-11.why: Stoeger warns the inertia spring must be in place. Then do the unloaded function check.

mc-shotgun-12.q: Which action is the softest shooting with heavy 3 in steel loads?
mc-shotgun-12.why: Gas spreads the recoil. That is why the lean is a gas semi auto for a duck gun.

mc-shotgun-12.q: Why try a gun in your hunting jacket?
options: A thick jacket changes length of pull and the mount
mc-shotgun-12.why: Fit it the way you will hunt in October rain.

mc-shotgun-12.q: Buying privately. What must happen before the transfer?
options: The seller gets a reference number from the Registrar using your licence details
You register the shotgun with BC
mc-shotgun-12.why: Firearms Act s. 23: a reference number for the transfer, after checking your licence.

mc-shotgun-12.q: A used gun's choke tube will not come out. What does that tell you?
options: It is extra tight, which is good
It may be seized: a gunsmith job and a reason to walk away or pay less
mc-shotgun-12.why: Seized chokes come from dirty dry threads or steel through the wrong tube. Expensive to fix.

mc-sks-01.q: You shake the cleaned SKS bolt and hear nothing. What now?
options: Clean the firing pin channel again; still silent means a gunsmith
Oil it heavily so the pin slides
mc-sks-01.why: A free floating pin should move freely. A pin stuck forward by old grease can cause a slam fire (70%). Clean again, then a gunsmith if it is still stuck.

options: A shot fired by the trigger very fast
The rifle firing as the bolt closes, without the trigger
A misfire that goes off later
mc-sks-01.why: A firing pin stuck forward can hit the primer as the bolt slams shut, so the rifle fires with no trigger press (70%).

mc-sks-01.q: With dummy rounds, 6 go into your fixed magazine. What does that mean?
options: The 5 round limit has failed: do not use it, see a gunsmith
mc-sks-01.why: A magazine for a semi automatic centrefire rifle that holds more than 5 is a prohibited device (99%, SOR/98-462 Part 4). Do not use it; have it fixed by a gunsmith.

mc-sks-01.q: The RCMP table warns not to confuse your Type 56 SKS with what?
options: The Chinese Type 56 AK, a prohibited AK-47 copy
mc-sks-01.why: Both carry the Chinese name Type 56. The AK is prohibited; the standard Type 56 SKS is non restricted (99%, FRT).

mc-sks-01.q: What is the SKS legal class on 23 October 2026?
mc-sks-01.why: The RCMP Firearms Reference Table, valid 19 October 2026, lists the standard Type 56 SKS as non restricted (99%). A federal review is under way, so check each season.

mc-sks-02.q: Which way is SAFE on the SKS safety?
options: Rearward and down against the guard
Pushed through from left to right
mc-sks-02.why: TC 9-56: apply the safety by rotating it forward and upward. Rearward and down, parallel to the trigger, is fire (95%).

mc-sks-02.q: What does the SKS safety block?
mc-sks-02.why: It places a block behind the trigger (95%, TC 9-56). It does not stop a stuck firing pin, so a slam fire is still possible (Tip).

mc-sks-02.q: You open the magazine and 5 rounds drop out. Is the rifle unloaded?
options: No, the chamber can still hold a round
Only if the safety is on
mc-sks-02.why: The magazine and the chamber are separate. The manual's unload uses the operating handle to clear the chamber, then a look (95%).

mc-sks-02.q: Function check: safety ON, press the trigger. The hammer falls. What now?
options: Stop: the safety failed, see a gunsmith
mc-sks-02.why: With the safety on, the hammer should not go forward (95%, TC 9-56). If it does, the rifle is unsafe until a gunsmith fixes it.

mc-sks-02.q: Why does the bolt stay open after the last shot?
options: A nib on the magazine platform lifts the bolt catch
mc-sks-02.why: When the last round feeds, a nib on the magazine platform forces the catch up and it holds the bolt open (95%, TC 9-56).

mc-sks-03.q: Where does the stripper clip go?
options: Into the clip guides at the front of the bolt carrier
mc-sks-03.why: TC 9-56: insert a stripper clip into the clip guides at the top front of the bolt carrier, with the bolt open (95%).

mc-sks-03.q: You opened the magazine and took out all rounds. Next step?
options: Close the magazine, pull the handle back to eject any chambered round, then look
mc-sks-03.why: The manual's unload clears the chamber with the operating handle, then you inspect magazine, chamber and receiver (95%).

mc-sks-03.q: In the truck, which is legal?
options: Chamber empty, 5 in the fixed magazine
One in the chamber, safety on
mc-sks-03.why: Item 28 bans live ammunition in the breech or in a magazine attached to the firearm in a vehicle (99%). The SKS magazine is always attached, so it must be empty.

mc-sks-03.q: Click, no bang while hunting. First?
options: Keep the muzzle safe and wait, then clear it
mc-sks-03.why: A hang fire can go off late. Keep it pointed safe and wait (Tip; Tikka asks for one minute), then use the manual's drill (95%).

mc-sks-03.q: How many rounds may your SKS magazine hold?
options: Any number if the chamber is empty
mc-sks-03.why: A magazine for a semi automatic centrefire long gun may hold no more than 5 (99%, SOR/98-462 Part 4; RCMP).

mc-sks-04.q: The rear sight slide sits on the 3. What range is that?
mc-sks-04.why: The numbers are hundreds of metres (95%, TC 9-56). 3 is 300 m.

mc-sks-04.q: Your group hits low. Which way do you move the front post?
mc-sks-04.why: Move the front sight opposite to the miss: a lower post makes the rifle hit higher (85%; TC 9-56 describes turning the post to raise the strike).

mc-sks-04.q: Your group hits left. Front sight?
mc-sks-04.why: Move the front sight opposite to the miss. Hits left: drift the front sight left, and the hits move right (85%).

mc-sks-04.q: What is the first mark on the leaf for?
options: A battle setting for up to 300 m
mc-sks-04.why: TC 9-56: the first character on the leaf is a battle sight setting for ranges up to 300 m (95%).

mc-sks-04.q: Which ammunition do you zero with?
options: The exact hunting load you will use
mc-sks-04.why: Different loads hit in different places (85%). Zero with the soft point you hunt with.

mc-sks-05.q: Why do corrosive primers cause rust?
options: They leave salt that pulls water from the air
They contain acid in the powder
mc-sks-05.why: Fired chlorate primers leave potassium chloride, a salt that attracts moisture (65%). Moisture plus steel is rust.

options: Water based cleaning, then dry and oil
mc-sks-05.why: Water dissolves the salt; oil does not (65%). Then dry fully and oil, because water left behind rusts too.

mc-sks-05.q: Can you hunt deer with surplus full metal jacket 7.62x39?
options: No, it is illegal in BC
mc-sks-05.why: Synopsis page 12: it is unlawful to hunt with a rifle using a full metal jacketed non expanding bullet (99%).

mc-sks-05.q: Which parts need cleaning after corrosive ammunition?
options: Bore, bolt face, carrier, gas tube and piston
mc-sks-05.why: Residue reaches the bolt, carrier and gas system too (Tip; the manual cleans all parts, 95%).

mc-sks-05.q: Where is the SKS cleaning rod?
options: Under the barrel, freed by unlocking the bayonet
mc-sks-05.why: TC 9-56: unlock the bayonet, let it hang, free the rod head from the front sight base and pull the rod out (95%). The tool kit is in the butt.

mc-sks-06.q: What comes off first in the SKS field strip, after unloading?
options: The top cover, after turning the cover pin up and out
mc-sks-06.why: TC 9-56: rotate the receiver cover pin vertical and pull it out, then remove the cover to the rear (95%).

mc-sks-06.q: Which way does the recoil spring assembly go back in?
options: Stepped end first, into the bolt carrier
mc-sks-06.why: Insert the driving spring assembly, stepped end first, into the bolt carrier (95%, TC 9-56).

mc-sks-06.q: Before the trigger group catch will press, the safety must be:
mc-sks-06.why: The safety must be in the safe position before the catch can be depressed (95%, TC 9-56).

mc-sks-06.q: Where does the extractor sit when you put the bolt in?
mc-sks-06.why: Place the bolt with the extractor to the right front, about 10 mm from the rear wall (95%, TC 9-56).

mc-sks-06.q: How far does the manual say to strip the SKS?
options: Field strip only: no further disassembly is necessary or desirable
mc-sks-06.why: TC 9-56: no further disassembly is necessary or desirable (95%). Deeper work is for a gunsmith.

mc-sks-07.q: About where does the 123 gr 7.62x39 load drop below 1,000 ft lb?
mc-sks-07.why: Hornady lists 1,136 ft lb at 100 yd and 842 at 200 yd; the line crosses 1,000 near 146 yd, about 134 m (75%, computed).

mc-sks-07.q: Is the 7.62x39 legal for deer in BC?
options: Yes: deer may be hunted with a centrefire rifle, with expanding bullets
mc-sks-07.why: Page 13 allows a centrefire rifle for deer and sets no calibre minimum; page 12 bans full metal jacket bullets (99%).

mc-sks-07.q: Does BC require a magazine plug in a semi automatic rifle?
options: No, the plug rule is for shotguns; the federal 5 round magazine limit applies
mc-sks-07.why: The page 12 plug rule names pump, repeating and auto loading shotguns (99%). Your SKS magazine falls under the federal 5 round limit (99%).

mc-sks-07.q: Your 5 shots at 100 m spread wider than a 15 cm plate. Your deer range?
options: Shorter, until you can keep all 5 in the plate
mc-sks-07.why: The plate test is a Tip: your limit is the distance where you can keep every shot in the vital zone.

mc-sks-07.q: You hunt near Harrison Mills on the lowland flats. Can you carry the SKS there to hunt?
mc-sks-07.why: Harrison Mills and Nicomen lowland: no rifles (99%, Closed Areas Regulation, via the Harrison lesson). Hunt deer in the hills.

mc-sks-08.q: A friend offers to cut your SKS barrel to 400 mm. What would it become?
options: Prohibited: the RCMP table lists a cut 400 mm SKS as prohibited
mc-sks-08.why: FRT record 2387: a 400 mm cut barrel is prohibited under s. 84(1) prohibited firearm (b)(ii), a rifle cut so its barrel is under 457 mm (99%).

mc-sks-08.q: Why is a 419 mm SKS restricted even if made that way?
options: It is a semi automatic centrefire with a barrel under 470 mm
mc-sks-08.why: Criminal Code s. 84(1) restricted firearm (b): semi automatic centrefire, barrel under 470 mm (99%).

mc-sks-08.q: You pry out the rivet so the fixed magazine takes 10. What is it now?
options: A prohibited device, and altering it is an offence
mc-sks-08.why: A semi automatic centrefire magazine holding more than 5 is prohibited (99%, SOR/98-462 Part 4), and altering a magazine above its lawful capacity is a Criminal Code offence since C-21 (95%, RCMP).

mc-sks-08.q: Which stock would make the SKS restricted?
options: A fixed wood stock of the same length
A folding stock that lets it fire under 660 mm
mc-sks-08.why: s. 84(1) restricted firearm (c): designed or adapted to fire when reduced under 660 mm by folding, telescoping or otherwise (99%).

mc-sks-08.q: A suppressor for the SKS is:
options: Legal with a PAL (Possession and Acquisition Licence)
mc-sks-08.why: s. 84(1): a device designed or intended to muffle or stop the sound or report of a firearm is a prohibited device (99%).

mc-tikka-01.q: Where is the safety catch on your T3x Arctic?
options: Left side, by the bolt stop
Right side, just behind the bolt handle
In front of the trigger guard
mc-tikka-01.why: The Tikka manual: the safety catch is on the side of the receiver just behind the bolt handle (page 8). The button in front of the trigger guard is the magazine release.

mc-tikka-01.q: What do you press to take the bolt out?
options: The bolt stop on the left side
mc-tikka-01.why: Lift the handle, press the bolt stop (bolt release) and pull the bolt fully out (Tikka manual pages 8 and 13).

mc-tikka-01.q: How does Canadian law measure a rifle barrel?
options: From the front of the stock to the muzzle
From the muzzle to and including the chamber, without muzzle devices
mc-tikka-01.why: Criminal Code s. 84(2): muzzle to and including the chamber, not counting parts that reduce flash or recoil.

mc-tikka-01.q: Your factory Arctic barrel is how long?
mc-tikka-01.why: Sako lists 508 mm for the Arctic in .308. 457 mm is the legal line for an altered rifle. Measure yours, chamber included.

mc-tikka-01.q: Before the first shot from a new Tikka, the manual says to push a dry patch through the bore from:
mc-tikka-01.why: Page 7: wipe the oil from the barrel with a dry patch starting from the breech end.

mc-tikka-02.q: Your Arctic is cocked and the safety is ON. You want to unload. First move?
options: Push the safety forward, muzzle pointed safe
mc-tikka-02.why: Safety ON locks the bolt closed. The manual's unloading starts with the safety forward, red dot showing, muzzle safe.

mc-tikka-02.q: In what order does the manual unload the rifle?
options: Bolt back to pull the live round, then magazine out
mc-tikka-02.why: Page 10: lift and pull back to extract the round, then remove the magazine, then check, close and decock. Keep the bolt back until the magazine is out.

mc-tikka-02.q: Your empty, uncocked rifle sits with the safety forward. Is something wrong?
options: No. That is the transport position; the safety only goes ON when cocked
mc-tikka-02.why: Figure 7, position 2: unloaded, uncocked, safety OFF is the transport position. The safety can only be engaged when the rifle is cocked.

options: Keep the muzzle safe, wait at least one minute, then unload with extreme care
mc-tikka-02.why: Tikka manual pages 10 and 19. A slow ignition can still fire.

mc-tikka-02.q: Is your 10 round Tikka bolt action magazine under the 5 round limit for long gun magazines?
options: Yes, all rifle magazines are limited to 5
No. The 5 round limit is for magazines designed for semi automatic firearms
mc-tikka-02.why: SOR/98-462 Part 4 s. 3 limits magazines designed for semi automatic firearms. A bolt action magazine is not on that list (my reading, 90%). Never alter one.

mc-tikka-03.q: Your 3 shot group is low. Which way do you turn the Arctic front elevation screw?
options: Clockwise: the post goes down and the shots go up
Neither: elevation is on the drum
mc-tikka-03.why: Tikka manual page 11: clockwise moves the bead down and the point of impact up.

mc-tikka-03.q: Your group centre is 3.5 cm left at 100 m. How many windage clicks?
mc-tikka-03.why: One click is about 7 mm at 100 m. 3.5 ÷ 0.7 = 5 clicks.

mc-tikka-03.q: What must you never do to the rear sight drum?
options: Turn it to the 100 m step
Open the screw in its centre
mc-tikka-03.why: The manual warns the centre screw holds spring loaded parts that fly out and ruin the sight.

mc-tikka-03.q: Where should your eye focus with a peep sight?
mc-tikka-03.why: Tip, widely taught: look through the peep and keep the front post sharp. Your eye centres the post in the ring.

mc-tikka-03.q: The manual's first step to get the sights near the target is:
options: Bolt out, look through the bore at a target 25 to 30 m away
mc-tikka-03.why: Page 12: bore sight at about 25 to 30 m, then final sighting in at 100 to 150 m.

mc-tikka-04.q: Why can a scope be hard to fit on your Arctic?
options: The rear sight drum sits behind a short rail, under where the scope passes
mc-tikka-04.why: The drum is fixed right behind the Picatinny rail. The scope must clear it, or you take the drum off by the manual's steps.

mc-tikka-04.q: Where does the ring screw torque number come from?
options: Your ring maker's sheet or product page
mc-tikka-04.why: The Tikka manual gives no ring torque and says to follow the mount maker. Leupold BackCountry ring tops: 28 in lb; Vortex Pro ring screws: 18 in lb.

mc-tikka-04.q: What torque do the Tikka receiver screws take with a metal trigger guard?
mc-tikka-04.why: Tikka manual page 13: 7 Nm with metal trigger guards, max 5 Nm with plastic ones.

mc-tikka-04.q: You set eye relief. Which power?
options: Highest power, where eye relief is shortest
mc-tikka-04.why: Eye relief often shrinks as power goes up (Vortex). Set it on top power and check prone and sitting.

mc-tikka-04.q: Your group is 2.9 cm left at 100 m. With 1/4 MOA clicks, about how many clicks right?
mc-tikka-04.why: One 1/4 MOA click is about 0.73 cm at 100 m. 2.9 ÷ 0.73 is about 4.

mc-tikka-05.q: What should be in the chamber for dry fire practice?
options: A snap cap with a spring loaded primer
A dummy round with an empty primer pocket
mc-tikka-05.why: Tikka manual page 9: snap caps cushion the firing pin. Dummy rounds are for loading practice and do not protect it.

mc-tikka-05.q: Your rifle is on a pack for a prone shot. What touches the pack?
options: The fore end of the stock
mc-tikka-05.why: Tip: the Arctic barrel is free floating. Pressure on it can shift the shot. Rest the fore end.

mc-tikka-05.q: Where can a bipod attach on your Tikka?
mc-tikka-05.why: Tikka manual page 16: the front sling swivel stud can also be used to fasten a bipod.

mc-tikka-05.q: In the plate test, what is your range from a position?
options: The last distance with 5 of 5 hits
mc-tikka-05.why: Tip: only a distance where you put every shot in the plate counts.

mc-tikka-05.q: You fired and the deer stands. You do not need a second shot after all. Then:
options: Safety ON, muzzle safe, finger away
Unload by firing in the air
mc-tikka-05.why: Tikka manual page 10: if you do not plan a second shot, engage the safety, keep the muzzle safe and fingers away from the trigger.

mc-tikka-06.q: Which bullet is unlawful for hunting deer in BC?
mc-tikka-06.why: The synopsis: it is unlawful to hunt with a full metal jacketed non expanding bullet, or a tracer, incendiary or explosive bullet.

mc-tikka-06.q: Where is your rifle's calibre marked?
options: On the side of the barrel
mc-tikka-06.why: Tikka manual page 9. Match it with the headstamp and the box.

mc-tikka-06.q: Which ammunition does Tikka say never to shoot?
mc-tikka-06.why: Page 9: do not ever shoot steel jacketed bullets. Also nothing over 10 years old, and reloads void the warranty.

mc-tikka-06.q: You change from a 150 gr load to a 165 gr load. Then:
mc-tikka-06.why: Every load hits a different spot. Zero with the load you hunt with.

mc-tikka-06.q: About how much does a black tailed buck weigh?
mc-tikka-06.why: BC deer account: black tailed bucks 48 to 90 kg, does 40 to 65 kg. A 150 to 165 gr .308 expanding bullet is plenty.

mc-tikka-07.q: Which way does the cleaning rod go through your Tikka?
options: Breech to muzzle, through a rod guide, in the bullet direction
mc-tikka-07.why: Tikka manual page 18: use a rod guide and clean only in the direction of bullet movement.

mc-tikka-07.q: Before the first shot after cleaning, the chamber should be:
mc-tikka-07.why: Leave a thin coat of oil for storage, but the manual says remember to wipe it dry before shooting.

mc-tikka-07.q: Stripping the T3x bolt: when do you remove the screwdriver from the gap?
options: Right after the shroud comes off
Not until you are ready to put the shroud back on
mc-tikka-07.why: Page 13: IMPORTANT, do not remove the screwdriver tip until you are ready to reassemble the bolt shroud.

mc-tikka-07.q: What is the lowest trigger weight Tikka allows?
mc-tikka-07.why: Page 15: for safety, do not reduce trigger weight below 11 N (2.5 lb). Factory is 13 to 15 N.

mc-tikka-07.q: Which three spots get light grease?
options: Locking lugs, cocking cam, cocking piece head

mc-tikka-08.q: You got home soaked. Where does the rifle spend the night?
options: Out of the case, drying in warm, dry air, then cleaned
mc-tikka-08.why: Tikka: dry it in a warm, dry place without a protective cover, and do not store it in leather or fabric, which hold moisture.

mc-tikka-08.q: Why clean oil out of the bolt before a cold hunt?
options: Tikka says oil inside the bolt matters most in cold or harsh weather
mc-tikka-08.why: Page 13: if oil may have got into the bolt, clean it to keep it working smoothly, particularly in cold or harsh weather.

mc-tikka-08.q: You slipped and the muzzle went into snow. Next?
options: Fire a shot to clear it
Unload, bolt out, look through the bore
mc-tikka-08.why: Firing with an obstruction can cause serious injury. Any obstruction is a gunsmith job (page 9).

mc-tikka-08.q: Which is lawful home storage for your rifle?
options: Unloaded, with the bolt removed, ammunition not readily at hand
Unloaded, ammunition in the stock pouch
mc-tikka-08.why: SOR/98-209 s. 5(1): unloaded and locked, or bolt removed, or locked up; ammunition not readily at hand unless locked.

mc-tikka-08.q: A gadget for cold hands that Tikka sells:
mc-tikka-08.why: Tikka manual page 17: the oversized bolt knob pushes over the original and locks with a screw. Thermal optics are banned on the hunt.

mc-tikka-09.q: What should you buy first for your Arctic?
options: A scope, good rings and a torque driver
mc-tikka-09.why: The biggest real gain in dawn light and at range. The factory trigger is already good, and a brake replaces your front sight.

mc-tikka-09.q: Is a suppressor legal for your rifle in Canada?
options: No. It is a prohibited device
mc-tikka-09.why: Criminal Code s. 84(1): a device designed or intended to muffle or stop the sound of a firearm is a prohibited device.

mc-tikka-09.q: You stack a third length of pull spacer. You also need:
mc-tikka-09.why: Tikka manual page 15: more than two spacers need longer screws. Do not overtighten them.

mc-tikka-09.q: Why skip a muzzle brake on the Arctic for now?
options: It replaces the front sight on the muzzle thread and adds noise
mc-tikka-09.why: The Arctic front sight sits on the muzzle thread (manual page 11). Brakes are not named in s. 84, but they cost you the irons and your hearing.

mc-tikka-09.q: Where can a bipod go on your stock?
mc-tikka-09.why: Tikka manual page 16: the front sling swivel stud can also hold a bipod.

mc-tikka-10.q: First shots at the range with a new sight setup: where?
options: 25 to 30 m to get on paper, then 100 m
Straight to 100 m without bore sighting
mc-tikka-10.why: Tikka manual page 12: bore sight at about 25 to 30 m, then final sighting in at 100 to 150 m.

mc-tikka-10.q: Who needs eye and ear protection at the bench?
options: You and everyone close to you
mc-tikka-10.why: Page 10: wear protective glasses and earplugs and make sure persons close to you are protected too.

mc-tikka-10.q: What is the cold bore bull for?
options: Your first shot from a cold, clean barrel next time, like a hunting shot
mc-tikka-10.why: Tip: the first shot of the day is the one that counts on a hunt. Learn where it goes.

mc-tikka-10.q: The bolt gets sticky and a primer looks flattened and leaking. You:
options: Stop shooting and have the rifle checked
mc-tikka-10.why: Tikka manual page 19: any cartridge malfunction such as a punctured primer or a changed sound: stop shooting immediately and see an authorised gunsmith.

mc-tikka-10.q: What goes on the zero card?
options: Load and lot, zero distance and date, clicks, plate test limits
The serial number of the scope
mc-tikka-10.why: Tip: everything you need to repeat your zero and know your limits.

fw-rules-01.q: Your deer tag from September is cancelled and the meat is in the freezer. Must it come on your November grouse hunt?
options: Yes. Carry every species licence from this licence year, cancelled or not
fw-rules-01.why: Page 5 and item 52 on page 12: carry all species licences, cancelled and uncancelled, while hunting.

fw-rules-01.q: You buy a cougar licence at the counter on Monday morning. When is it valid?
fw-rules-01.why: Page 8: cougar, bobcat, lynx, caribou, goat, sheep and wolverine licences are not valid until 2 days after the date of issue.

fw-rules-01.q: You shoot a buck but your brother still has an open tag and you do not. What is legal?
options: He cancels his tag on it
Only you can tag it, with your own licence. With no licence, you have a problem to self report
fw-rules-01.why: Item 2, page 11: never use another person's licence or transfer any licence. Page 18 gives the self report steps for a kill you cannot legally tag.

fw-rules-01.q: You hunt ducks inside the District of Mission in MU 2-8. What do you need on top of your BC licence and federal permit?
options: The Fraser Valley Special Area licence and $1,000,000 liability insurance
fw-rules-01.why: Map B10, page 29: hunting in MU 2-4, and in 2-8 inside Mission and the other listed municipalities, needs the special licence and the insurance.

fw-rules-01.q: It is 5 April. Is last October's hunting licence good for spring bear?
options: No. All hunting and species licences expire 31 March
fw-rules-01.why: Page 8: all hunting and species licences expire 31 March. The licence year runs 1 April to 31 March (page 3).

fw-rules-02.q: Your rifle's chamber is empty but the clipped in magazine holds 3 rounds. You climb on the ATV. Legal?
options: No. A magazine attached to the firearm with live rounds counts, and item 28 bans that on any vehicle
Yes, if the safety is on
fw-rules-02.why: Page 3 defines loaded to include a detachable magazine attached to the firearm. Item 28 bans live ammunition in the breech or attached magazine in or on a motor vehicle.

fw-rules-02.q: Grouse hunting with your pump 12 gauge. Does the plug matter?
options: No, plugs are a duck rule
Yes. Page 12 requires a plug holding no more than 2 cartridges to hunt with a pump, repeating or auto loading shotgun
fw-rules-02.why: Page 12 applies to hunting in general. The only unplugged exception is slugs only for big game where shotguns are allowed.

fw-rules-02.q: A California quail covey runs ahead of you. Which firearm is legal?
fw-rules-02.why: Page 13 notes 2 and 3: rimfire only for grouse, ptarmigan or turkey; centrefire only for grouse or ptarmigan. Quail take shotgun, air rifle or bow.

fw-rules-02.q: You will paddle your kayak, no motor, to a duck marsh. Can the shotgun be loaded in it while you hunt?
options: Yes. The exemption covers hunting from a boat with no motor or one its motor is not propelling
fw-rules-02.why: Firearm Violence Prevention Act s. 4(1) bans a loaded firearm in a boat from 1 October 2026; the Designation and Exemption Regulation s. 18 exempts hunting from a boat with no motor, or one the motor is not propelling.

fw-rules-02.q: Which load is legal for a deer with your 12 gauge?
options: No. 1 Buck or larger, or a slug
fw-rules-02.why: Page 13 note 1: 20 gauge or larger with No. 1 Buck or larger. Page 12 allows slugs where shotguns are allowed for big game.

fw-rules-03.q: 20 October, MU 3-28. Can you use the quad only to haul your deer to the truck?
options: No. The ATV for hunting closure bans transporting wildlife too, 1 September to 10 December
fw-rules-03.why: Page 10 lists transporting wildlife as a hunting use; page 33 closes ATVs for hunting in 3-28 from 1 September to 10 December.

fw-rules-03.q: How far from the middle of a 2 lane public road before you may shoot?
options: Past 15 m, or past the line of private or cultivated land if that is closer
fw-rules-03.why: Page 10: the road allowance runs 15 m either side of the middle of a road with less than three lanes, or to private or cultivated land, whichever comes first.

fw-rules-03.q: A grouse 200 m off the Coquihalla between Hope and Kamloops. Shotgun with shot, outside the road allowance?
options: Legal. Only single projectiles are banned in that 400 m band
fw-rules-03.why: Page 10: on the listed routes a single projectile is banned within 400 m of the road allowance; a shotgun using shot only is permitted.

fw-rules-03.q: No closure sign at the gate, but the regulation lists a closure. Which wins?
fw-rules-03.why: Page 10: where signs and the regulation disagree, the regulation is the final authority. Page 33: recognizing closures is the hunter's job, sign or not.

fw-rules-03.q: Can you run your boat toward a raft of ducks so they fly past your brother?
options: Yes, if you do not shoot from the boat
No. Item 25 bans using a power boat to herd or harass wildlife
fw-rules-03.why: Item 25, page 11: it is unlawful to use a power boat, aircraft, motor vehicle or other mechanical device to herd or harass wildlife.

fw-rules-04.q: The farmer says you may hunt quail 60 m from his occupied house. Legal?
options: No. Page 10 bans hunting or shooting within 100 m of a dwelling, and permission is not an exemption
fw-rules-04.why: Page 10: the only exemption is the owner, occupier or employee slaughtering livestock.

fw-rules-04.q: A Crown grazing lease has no cattle on it today. Can you hunt it without asking?
options: No. Leased land is subject to the Trespass Act whether or not livestock are present
fw-rules-04.why: Page 9, new note this edition: leased land is subject to the Trespass Act regardless of livestock.

fw-rules-04.q: A No Shooting Area lies on your route. What may you use there?
options: A bow or crossbow, unless the region restricts it
fw-rules-04.why: Page 10: No Shooting Areas are open to bows, crossbows included, unless specifically restricted. A No Hunting Area bans hunting by any method.

fw-rules-04.q: You shoot a legal buck in season, but on posted private land you did not ask about. What is the problem?
options: Item 19: killing wildlife while committing another offence, such as trespass, is unlawful
fw-rules-04.why: Item 19, page 11 names wildlife taken while trespassing on private property as an example.

fw-rules-04.q: A BC Park is closed to hunting. Where may your shotgun be?
options: Only inside a vehicle, unless a park officer authorizes otherwise
fw-rules-04.why: Page 9: when a park is closed to hunting, possession is only allowed within a vehicle or with a park officer's authorization.

fw-rules-05.q: Sunrise is 7:20. When may you first shoot a duck? A deer?
fw-rules-05.why: Items 37 and 38: migratory birds from 30 minutes before sunrise; other game from 1 hour before sunrise.

fw-rules-05.q: Region 3, MU 3-27. A covey of quail. Is there a season?
options: Yes, all upland birds are open
No. Region 3 has no quail row, and no row means no season
fw-rules-05.why: Page 34 prints no quail row for Region 3; page 5 says open seasons are only those defined in the synopsis.

fw-rules-05.q: Your thermal monocular stays in the pack and is never used. Legal?
options: No. Item 39 bans possessing infrared optics on a hunting expedition
fw-rules-05.why: Item 39, page 11: use or possession on the trip is the offence.

fw-rules-05.q: A cell trail camera sends deer photos to your phone in mid October. Can you use it to hunt?
options: No. Wireless cameras may not be used for hunting from 1 August to 10 December
fw-rules-05.why: Item 30, page 11 (Region 1 has its own rule).

fw-rules-05.q: You live at Heffley Creek. Can you put out grain for deer 50 m from your house?
options: No. Region 3 bans intentionally feeding or baiting ungulates within 200 m of a dwelling
fw-rules-05.why: Page 33, new this edition: no intentional baiting or feeding of ungulates within 200 m of a dwelling, school yard or playground in Region 3.

fw-rules-06.q: A mule deer buck shows 3 tines plus a brow tine on his best side. 4 point?
options: No. The brow tine is excluded for mule deer
fw-rules-06.why: Page 4: at least four tines, excluding the brow tine, on one antler.

fw-rules-06.q: 2 November, MU 3-27. A 2 point a side mule deer buck. Legal?
options: No. From 1 November to 10 December only 4 point bucks are open
fw-rules-06.why: Page 34: any buck 1 to 31 October only; 4 point bucks 1 November to 10 December.

fw-rules-06.q: You took a mule deer buck at Heffley Creek. Can you take another mule deer buck in the Okanagan the same licence year?
options: No. Only 1 mule deer buck from Regions 3 to 8 combined
fw-rules-06.why: Page 14: only 1 of your 3 deer may be a mule deer buck from Regions 3, 4, 5, 6, 7A, 7B and 8 combined.

fw-rules-06.q: A male fawn with small furry bumps. Buck or antlerless?
fw-rules-06.why: Page 3: skin or hair covered bumps of male fawns and calves are not antlers, so he is antlerless.

fw-rules-06.q: A deer is swimming across the lake, unwounded. Can you shoot it from shore?
options: No. Big game may not be hunted while swimming unless already wounded

fw-rules-07.q: On a duck hunt you shoot only steel, but a box of lead grouse shells rides in your boat. Legal?
options: Yes, you did not shoot lead
No. Possessing shot other than non toxic shot in the hunting area is an offence
Yes, if the box is closed
fw-rules-07.why: s. 38(1)(a) and note 4, page 13: possession or use of other shot is prohibited when hunting migratory game birds.

fw-rules-07.q: You have 3 pintails and 5 mallards. A pintail comes in. Can you shoot it?
options: No. That makes 9 ducks, over the daily 8
Yes, if you give one away
fw-rules-07.why: Page 12: 8 ducks in aggregate; restricted species count inside the 8. At 8 you stop (s. 44).

fw-rules-07.q: Plucked but unfrozen ducks from three weekends sit in your fridge. Do they count?
options: Yes. Unpreserved birds count toward the possession limit of 24, home included
fw-rules-07.why: Page 12: possession limit applies at all times, including at a residence. A bird is preserved once plucked and frozen, cooked and so on (s. 1).
Table 1 item 2: District 2 ducks open the Saturday after the first Monday in October, 10 October in 2026. District 3 opened 8 September.

fw-rules-07.q: You cut the outboard and glide toward ducks. When may you shoot?
options: Only once the boat has stopped moving from the motor's push
fw-rules-07.why: Item 24, s. 41(4) and BC Hunting Regulation s. 17(1.2): a boat still moving from motion its motor gave it counts as moving.

fw-rules-08.q: Your deer is down. When do you cancel the species licence?
options: Immediately after the kill, before you handle the animal

fw-rules-08.q: Driving a mule deer home whole. What must stay naturally attached?
options: The unskinned tail and the evidence of sex
fw-rules-08.why: Page 15: deer keep the unskinned tail AND the evidence of sex attached until home and butchered, at a meat cutter, or inspected.

fw-rules-08.q: You bought a moose licence and never saw a moose. Report?
options: Yes. Every elk, moose or caribou licence buyer files the Mandatory Hunter Report by 31 March
fw-rules-08.why: Page 16. Missing it is an offence and blocks next season's licence and LEH application.

fw-rules-08.q: Your truck hits a deer. Can you take it home for meat?
options: No. Big game killed by accident or collision may not be possessed; report it

fw-rules-08.q: A game check is set up on the highway. You have no game. Must you stop?
options: Yes. All hunters, with or without game, must stop and report

fw-rules-09.q: A neighbour offers to fix your roof in return for half a deer. Legal?
options: No. Trading wildlife meat for anything of value, or offering to, is trafficking
fw-rules-09.why: Item 7, page 11, and the page 4 definition: buy, sell, trade or distribute for gain or consideration, or offer to.

fw-rules-09.q: You drive your brother's deer meat to his house. What paper do you need?
options: A Record of Receipt with the six details
fw-rules-09.why: Page 15: for an animal taken by another person, carry a Record of Receipt (form on page 14).

fw-rules-09.q: You give a friend 6 ducks. Whose possession limit do they count against?
fw-rules-09.why: Federal s. 46(5): a gift counts in the receiver's possession once accepted.

fw-rules-09.q: How long do you keep the cancelled licence for a deer?
options: Until the animal has been consumed
fw-rules-09.why: Page 7: keep all documents under which an animal was taken until it has been consumed.

fw-rules-09.q: You shot a mule deer in Alberta. What may come back into BC?
options: Meat of the quarters, loins, neck and ribs, and a cleaned hide, antlers and skull plate

fw-rules-10.q: A co worker offers $100 and a share of the meat if you take him deer hunting. Legal without a licence?
options: No. Accompanying and assisting a hunter for compensation or reward is guiding and needs a licence
Yes if he has his own tag
fw-rules-10.why: Page 11: it is unlawful to act as a guide for compensation or reward unless licensed. He could be charged as a party too.

fw-rules-10.q: Your 9 year old nephew wants to shoot a grouse under your eye. Legal?
options: No. No one under 10 may hunt, and allowing it is an offence

fw-rules-10.q: Your 14 year old on a youth licence takes a white tailed deer. Whose bag does it count in?
fw-rules-10.why: Page 6: wildlife taken under a youth or initiation licence is included in the bag limit of the supervising licensed adult.

fw-rules-10.q: What does accompany mean for supervising?
options: Able to see them without binoculars and talk without amplification

fw-rules-10.q: This is your first year with a federal duck permit. Can you take a 15 year old with a free youth permit duck hunting as the accompanying adult?
options: No. The adult must hold a permit now and have held one in a previous year

fw-grandpa-01.q: What does the A in ACTS stand for?
fw-grandpa-01.why: ACTS: Assume every firearm is loaded, Control the muzzle, Trigger finger off, See that it is unloaded by proving it safe (85%).

fw-grandpa-01.q: You must cross a barbed wire fence alone. What is the taught method?
options: Keep it loaded with the safety on
Unload, lay it under with the muzzle away, cross, check the barrel
Hand it over the top, loaded, by the barrel
fw-grandpa-01.why: Hunter education teaches: unload, place it across or under with the muzzle pointed away, cross away from it, then check the barrel for mud or snow (85%).

fw-grandpa-01.q: In New York, 1989 to 1995, what share of hunters shot after being mistaken for game were NOT wearing orange?
fw-grandpa-01.why: 117 of 125 (94%) wore no hunter orange (90%, US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention).

fw-grandpa-01.q: You fall into 6 degree lake water. Roughly how long do you have for useful movement?
fw-grandpa-01.why: Cold Water Boot Camp's 1, 10, 1: about 1 minute of cold shock, about 10 minutes of useful movement, up to about 1 hour before you pass out (85%).

fw-grandpa-01.q: A shape moves in the brush at dusk. It might be a deer. What do you do?
options: Wait for a clear view; if still unsure, no shot
fw-grandpa-01.why: Never shoot at a sound or a movement. In low light, pass the shot (85%, Texas hunter education). If you are not sure, you are not shooting.

fw-grandpa-02.q: Why does a red sunset often mean dry weather tomorrow?
options: The sun is hotter in the evening
High pressure with dry air is coming from the west
fw-grandpa-02.why: Dust trapped under high pressure scatters blue light and leaves red. A red sunset means the high is arriving from the west, where most weather comes from (75%, Met Office).

fw-grandpa-02.q: What did Penn State find about moon phase and doe movement?
fw-grandpa-02.why: GPS collared does in three Pennsylvania forests: moon phase had an insignificant effect (85%). Dawn and dusk stayed the main pattern.

fw-grandpa-02.q: It is 15 minutes before sunrise on a cold, calm slope. Which way is the air most likely moving?
fw-grandpa-02.why: Cold air sinks. Until the sun warms the slope, air usually keeps sliding downhill (75 to 80%).

fw-grandpa-02.q: Penn State GPS data on windy days found deer moved:
options: Less by day and less by night
More by day, less by night
fw-grandpa-02.why: Both sexes moved more on windy days and less on windy nights, even at light wind (80%, Penn State Deer Forest blog).

fw-grandpa-02.q: What sets the timing of the deer rut?
fw-grandpa-02.why: Fetal aging studies found breeding dates stay steady year to year regardless of moon or weather; day length is the main trigger (70%).

fw-grandpa-03.q: In the Penn State study, how far from a road did hunters actually get on average, at most?
fw-grandpa-03.why: GPS showed an average farthest distance of 0.84 km, while hunters reported 2.23 km (80%). 73% stayed within 0.5 km (85%).

fw-grandpa-03.q: What do you look for when glassing timber?
options: A flat line, an ear flick, a tail or a patch of white
fw-grandpa-03.why: Most of the bush is vertical, so a horizontal back line stands out, as do ear and tail flicks (70%). Look for pieces, not a whole deer.

fw-grandpa-03.q: Montana elk under hunting pressure chose:
options: Large forest patches with hiding cover away from open roads
fw-grandpa-03.why: Weber and others: elk selected areas away from open roads with large patches of forest and hiding cover (80%).

fw-grandpa-03.q: A cold, clear October morning. Where do you glass first for bedded mule deer?
fw-grandpa-03.why: Temperature and canopy drive bed choice (85%). Cold morning, look to the sun (opinion).

fw-grandpa-03.q: Why ask the farmer even if you think the answer is no?
options: It is required on Crown land
Most landowners surveyed said yes when asked first, and they know where animals move
fw-grandpa-03.why: 88% of surveyed Idaho landowners allow hunting when asked first (80%). The farmer also knows the crossings. BC access rules are in the Rule Book.

fw-grandpa-04.q: Hunter education's still hunting rule of thumb is:
options: Walk 10 times more than you stand
Stand at least 10 times longer than you walk
fw-grandpa-04.why: Spend at least 10 times longer still and observing than walking (85%, hunter education).

fw-grandpa-04.q: You need to see over a ridge into the next basin. What do you do?
options: Walk along the top for the best view
Come up below the crest and peek over slowly
fw-grandpa-04.why: A human outline on the skyline spooks game (85%). Approach from below and peek.

fw-grandpa-04.q: A doe stares straight at you from 80 m. What now?
options: Wave to see what she does
Freeze until she looks away or drops her head
fw-grandpa-04.why: Movement is what deer catch (85%). When it stares, you are a stump; move only when its head is down.

fw-grandpa-04.q: In one South Carolina collar study, how long did bucks avoid a stand area after one sit?
fw-grandpa-04.why: About 3 days, shot or not (60%, secondary report). Rotate stands and save the best one.

fw-grandpa-04.q: While still hunting, where should your eyes be at each stop?
options: Ahead and to the sides, into the cover
fw-grandpa-04.why: Hunter education: look into the forest, not down at the ground (85%).

fw-grandpa-05.q: For a 4 point buck rule, how do you count?
options: Count one antler, not the brow tine, and count it twice
fw-grandpa-05.why: A 4 point buck has at least 4 tines on one antler, not counting the brow tine (99%, synopsis page 4). Count one side twice, then decide.

fw-grandpa-05.q: Do you need to cut off the tarsal glands to save the meat?
options: No; removal is unnecessary and can spread taint with your knife or hands
fw-grandpa-05.why: Ohio's field dressing guide calls it a misconception; removal is unnecessary and can contaminate the meat (90%).

fw-grandpa-05.q: Which colour stands out most to a deer?
fw-grandpa-05.why: Deer see blue well and cannot tell orange from green (85%, National Deer Association).

fw-grandpa-05.q: A white tail flags and bounds away at 70 m. What do you do?
options: Let it go and watch where it stops
Whistle and shoot when it stops in thick brush
fw-grandpa-05.why: A running deer is a poor shot. A flag is a goodbye; only shoot a still, clear animal (tradition, Tip).

fw-grandpa-05.q: Why read the body before the antlers when judging age?
options: Antler points are not a reliable age guide
fw-grandpa-05.why: BC's mule deer account: the number of antler points is not a reliable way to determine age (90%).

fw-grandpa-06.q: A cow moose with a calf lays her ears back and walks toward you. What do you do?
options: Back away and put a tree or vehicle between you
Walk between them for a photo
fw-grandpa-06.why: Moose injure more people than bears in Alaska (65%); cows guard calves. Never get between a cow and calf; back off.

fw-grandpa-06.q: A legal bull stands knee deep at the lake edge. Grandpa's advice?
options: Wait for it to step onto dry ground
fw-grandpa-06.why: A moose is too heavy to drag out of water (opinion, 60%). Wait for dry ground. Boat and swimming moose rules are in the Rule Book.

fw-grandpa-06.q: What kills Trichinella in bear meat?
fw-grandpa-06.why: The northern species survives freezing for months or years; cook to 71 °C (160 °F) (90%, US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention).

fw-grandpa-06.q: A bear with big looking ears and long legs walks out. What does that suggest?
options: A young bear or a sow
fw-grandpa-06.why: Young bears and sows look big eared and leggy; big boars look small eared with thick legs (opinion, 60 to 70%). Watch for cubs too.

fw-grandpa-06.q: Why avoid spooking an elk herd you plan to hunt tomorrow?
options: Elk always come back in an hour
Pressured elk may leave the drainage, some over 10 km
fw-grandpa-06.why: In one Montana study some elk moved more than 10 km in the first days of the season (65%).

fw-grandpa-07.q: The wind blows from the north. Where do you want it relative to your blind?
options: At your back, so ducks land into it facing you
fw-grandpa-07.why: Ducks land into the wind. With the wind at your back they come in facing you over the hole (85%, Ducks Unlimited).

fw-grandpa-07.q: How far in front of the blind should the landing hole be, by Ducks Unlimited's sweet spot?
fw-grandpa-07.why: Twenty yards is the sweet spot; farther can put birds out of range when shooting starts (80%).

fw-grandpa-07.q: A flock comes straight at you, low. Do you call?
options: No, stay quiet and still; call to tails, not faces
fw-grandpa-07.why: Call only at tails and wingtips, not at ducks flying toward you (70%, Field and Stream, Ducks Unlimited callers).

fw-grandpa-07.q: A covey of quail bursts at your feet. What is the taught method?
options: Pick one bird, shoot, then pick a second
Wait for them to land and shoot on the ground
fw-grandpa-07.why: Kentucky's wildlife agency: pick a single bird, shoot, pick a second, shoot, then mark the down birds (85%).

fw-grandpa-07.q: You used lead #4 for ducks. Under the common rule of thumb, which steel size?
fw-grandpa-07.why: Steel is lighter, so go about 2 sizes larger (75%). Lead #4 becomes steel #2. Pattern to check.

fw-grandpa-08.q: Your deer hunched and walked off slowly after the shot, and you suspect a gut hit. What do all the sources agree on?
options: Back out for hours, longer than for a lung hit
fw-grandpa-08.why: Every source says hours for a gut hit; how many differs: Hunter Ed blog 6 to 8 or overnight, NDA (National Deer Association) 2012 4 to 6, NDA 2023 10 to 12 (70%). Your call. Pushing it early loses it.

fw-grandpa-08.q: You see bone chips and no blood at the hit site. What does the National Deer Association advise?
options: Track at once and be ready for a follow up shot
Assume a miss and go home
fw-grandpa-08.why: Bone fragments suggest a non lethal leg hit; start tracking immediately and look for a follow up shot (85%).

fw-grandpa-08.q: A buck drops instantly at the shot. What now?
options: Reload, watch it, approach from its back side ready to shoot
fw-grandpa-08.why: Spine shock can wear off within about a minute (85%, bowhunter education). Down is not dead.

fw-grandpa-08.q: Where do you walk when following a blood trail?
fw-grandpa-08.why: Walk beside the trail so you can read it again; flag the last blood (85%, National Deer Association; app opinion).

fw-grandpa-08.q: What does 'aim small, miss small' mean?
options: Pick one small spot, not the whole animal
fw-grandpa-08.why: A small aiming point keeps your misses close to it. The saying's origin is uncertain (Tip).

fw-grandpa-09.q: What carcass temperature does Penn State Extension aim for, quickly?
fw-grandpa-09.why: Quickly cool the carcass to 35 to 40 °F (3 to 4 °C) to prevent bacterial growth (90%).

fw-grandpa-09.q: Should you cut the deer's throat to bleed it?
options: No; removing heart and lungs does a better job
fw-grandpa-09.why: Ohio's field dressing guide calls throat cutting a popular misconception (90%).

fw-grandpa-09.q: How long should a home hunter hang venison, by Penn State Extension?
options: 2 to 3 days at most, at 4 °C or below
fw-grandpa-09.why: Two to three days at most at 40 °F (4 °C) or below; for sausage, aging is not necessary (90%).

fw-grandpa-09.why: Wet cotton loses its insulating air pockets and dries slowly; wool keeps some warmth when wet (70%).

fw-grandpa-09.q: How far from your sleeping area should food and meat be in bear country, by Alberta's BearSmart?
fw-grandpa-09.why: At least 100 m from your sleeping area, with anything bloody outside the camp area (80%).

fw-grandpa-10.q: The Boone and Crockett Club's fair chase rests on which three ideas?
fw-grandpa-10.why: Fair chase is the ethical, sportsmanlike and lawful pursuit of free ranging wild game, with a fair chance to escape (85%).

fw-grandpa-10.q: You find a farm gate open on the way in. What do you do?
options: Leave it open, as you found it
fw-grandpa-10.why: Leave gates the way you found them unless the owner says otherwise (80%, Idaho Fish and Game). Cattle may need that gate open for water.

fw-grandpa-10.q: Last year a rancher said yes. This year?
options: Ask again and confirm days, species and who may come
Only ask if you see the rancher
fw-grandpa-10.why: Never assume last year's permission still applies; get it in writing (80%, Idaho Fish and Game).

fw-grandpa-10.q: You see someone shooting deer at night from a truck. What do you do?
options: Block the road and confront them
Note details from a safe place and call the RAPP line
fw-grandpa-10.why: Never confront a suspect; record date, time, place, vehicle and call RAPP (Report All Poachers and Polluters), 1 877 952 7277 (95%).

fw-grandpa-10.q: Where does BC's licence conservation surcharge go?
fw-grandpa-10.why: Surcharges on hunting, angling, trapping and guiding licences are dedicated to the Habitat Conservation Trust Foundation, started in 1981 (80%).
